ORC:2903.21.heading: EXAMPLE – AGGRAVATED MENACING 2903.21 ORC
ORC:2903.21.text: _____________ did knowingly cause another, to wit: (VICTIM’S NAME), to believe that (OFFENDER’S NAME) would cause serious physical harm to (said other, said other’s unborn, said other’s property or a member of said other’s immediate family) because of (his or her) (race or color or religion or national origin), to wit: (DESCRIBE REASON FOR BELIEF), in violation of Section 2927.12(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2903.21.notes: NOTE: Originally, Aggravated Menacing is a misdemeanor of the first degree; however, it becomes a felony of the fifth degree under Ethnic Intimidation.

ORC:2903.211.heading: MENACING BY STALKING 2903.211(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2903.211.text: _____________ did, engage in a pattern of conduct, to wit: (DESCRIBE PATTERN OF CONDUCT WHICH CAUSED THE VICTIM TO BELIEVE THE DEFENDANT WOULD CAUSE (him/her or his/her family or household member) PHYSICAL HARM INCLUDING THE DATES SUCH CONDUCT OCCURRED), which knowingly caused another, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM), to believe that the offender would cause physical harm to said other person or a family or household member of said other person, in violation of Section 2903.211(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2903.211.notes: NOTE: See Menacing by Stalking listed in Section 2903.211(B)(2)(a). NOTE: In addition to any other basis for the other person’s belief that the offender will cause physical harm to the other person or the other person’s family or household member, the other person’s belief may be based on words or conduct of the offender that are directed at or identify a corporation, association, or other organization that employs the other person or to which the other person belongs. PATTERN OF CONDUCT – two or more actions or incidents closely related in time, whether or not there has been a prior conviction based on any of those action or incidents, or two or more actions or incidents closely related in time, whether or not there has been a prior conviction based on any of those actions or incidents, directed at one or more persons employed by or belonging to the same corporation, association, or other organization. Actions or incidents that prevent, obstruct, or delay the performance by a public official, firefighter, rescuer, or emergency medical services person of any authorized act within the public official’s, firefighter’s, rescuer’s, emergency facility person’s, or emergency medical services person’s official capacity, or the posting of messages, use of intentionally written or verbal graphic gestures, or receipt of information or data through the use of any form of written communication or an electronic method of remotely transferring information, including but not limited to, a computer, computer network, computer program, computer system, or telecommunications device, may constitute a “pattern of conduct.” ORGANIZATION – includes an entity that is a governmental employer. FAMILY OR HOUSEHOLD MEMBER – has the same definition as used in ORC 2919.25 (DV).

ORC:2903.211.heading: MENACING BY STALKING 2903.211(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2903.211.text: _____________ did, engage in a pattern of conduct, to wit: (DESCRIBE PATTERN OF CONDUCT WHICH CAUSED (the victim or a family or household member of the victim) MENTAL DISTRESS INCLUDING THE DATES SUCH CONDUCT OCCURRED), which knowingly caused another, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM), mental distress, to wit: (DESCRIBE MENTAL DISTRESS CAUSED), in violation of Section 2903.211(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2903.211.notes: NOTE: See Menacing by Stalking listed in Section 2903.211(B)(2)(a). NOTE: The other person’s mental distress may be based on words or conduct of the offender that are directed at or identify a corporation, association, or other organization that employs the other person or to which the other person belongs, in addition to any other basis. FAMILY OR HOUSEHOLD MEMBER – has the same definition as used in ORC 2919.25 (DV). MENTAL DISTRESS – any mental illness or condition that involves some temporary substantial incapacity or mental illness or condition that would normally require psychiatric treatment, psychological treatment, or other mental health services, whether or not any person requested or received psychiatric treatment, psychological treatment, or other mental health services.

ORC:2903.211.heading: MENACING BY STALKING 2903.211(A)(2)(a) ORC
ORC:2903.211.variant: VIOLATE (A)(1) THROUGH USE OF COMMUNICATION DEVICE – M1
ORC:2903.211.text: _____________ did, through the use of (any form of written communication or any electronic method of remotely transferring information, including, but not limited to, any computer, computer network, computer program, computer system, or telecommunication device) (post a message or use any intentionally written or verbal graphic gesture), to wit: (DESCRIBE COMMUNICATION AND MEANS OF TRANSMISSION) with purpose to engage in a pattern of conduct, to wit: (DESCRIBE PATTERN OF CONDUCT WHICH CAUSED THE VICTIM TO BELIEVE THE DEFENDANT WOULD CAUSE (him or /her or his/her family or household member) (physical harm or mental distress) INCLUDING THE DATES SUCH CONDUCT OCCURRED), which knowingly caused another, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM), (physical harm or mental distress), to wit: (DESCRIBE PHYSICAL HARM OR MENTAL DISTRESS CAUSED), in violation of Section 2903.211(A)(2)(a) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2903.211.notes: NOTE: See Menacing by Stalking listed in Section 2903.211(B)(2)(a). NOTE: In addition to any other basis for the other person’s belief that the offender will cause physical harm to the other person or the other person’s family or household member, the other person’s belief or mental distress may be based on words or conduct of the offender that are directed at or identify a corporation, association, or other organization that employs the other person or to which the other person belongs. FAMILY OR HOUSEHOLD MEMBER – has the same definition as used in ORC 2919.25 (DV).

ORC:2903.211.heading: MENACING BY STALKING 2903.211(A)(2)(b) ORC
ORC:2903.211.variant: URGE/INCITE ANOTHER TO VIOLATE (A)(1) THROUGH USE OF COMMUNICATION DEVICE – M1
ORC:2903.211.text: _____________ did, through the use of (any form of written communication or any electronic method of remotely transferring information, including, but not limited to, any computer, computer network, computer program, computer system, or telecommunication device) (post a message or use any intentionally written or verbal graphic gesture), to wit: (DESCRIBE COMMUNICATION AND MEANS OF TRANSMISSION) with purpose to (urge or incite) another, to wit: (DESCRIBE SAID OTHER) to engage in a pattern of conduct, to wit: (DESCRIBE PATTERN OF CONDUCT WHICH CAUSED THE VICTIM TO BELIEVE THE DEFENDANT WOULD CAUSE (him or /her or his/her family or household member) (physical harm or mental distress) INCLUDING THE DATES SUCH CONDUCT OCCURRED), which knowingly caused another, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM), (physical harm or mental distress), to wit: (DESCRIBE PHYSICAL HARM OR MENTAL DISTRESS CAUSED), in violation of Section 2903.211(A)(2)(b) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2903.211.notes: NOTE: See Menacing by Stalking listed in Section 2903.211(B)(2)(a). NOTE: In addition to any other basis for the other person’s belief that the offender will cause physical harm to the other person or the other person’s family or household member, the other person’s belief or mental distress may be based on words or conduct of the offender that are directed at or identify a corporation, association, or other organization that employs the other person or to which the other person belongs. FAMILY OR HOUSEHOLD MEMBER – has the same definition as used in ORC 2919.25 (DV).

ORC:2903.211.heading: MENACING BY STALKING 2903.211(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2903.211.text: _____________ did, with a sexual motivation, engage in a pattern of conduct, to wit: (DESCRIBE PATTERN OF CONDUCT WHICH CAUSED THE VICTIM TO BELIEVE THE DEFENDANT WOULD CAUSE (him/her or his/her family or household member) (physical harm or mental distress) INCLUDING THE DATES SUCH CONDUCT OCCURRED), which knowingly caused another, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM), (physical harm or mental distress), to wit: (DESCRIBE PHYSICAL HARM OR MENTAL DISTRESS CAUSED), in violation of Section 2903.211(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2903.211.notes: NOTE: See Menacing by Stalking listed in Section 2903.211(B)(2)(a). NOTE: Sexual Motivation means a purpose to gratify the sexual needs or desires of the offender. NOTE: In addition to any other basis for the other person’s belief that the offender will cause physical harm to the other person or the other person’s family or household member, the other person’s belief or mental distress may be based on words or conduct of the offender that are directed at or identify a corporation, association, or other organization that employs the other person or to which the other person belongs. FAMILY OR HOUSEHOLD MEMBER – has the same definition as used in ORC 2919.25 (DV).

ORC:2903.211.heading: MENACING BY STALKING 2903.211(B)(2)(a) ORC
ORC:2903.211.text: _____________ did, engage in a pattern of conduct, to wit: (DESCRIBE PATTERN OF CONDUCT WHICH CAUSED THE VICTIM TO BELIEVE THE DEFENDANT WOULD CAUSE (him/her or his/her family or household member) PHYSICAL HARM INCLUDING THE DATES SUCH CONDUCT OCCURRED), which knowingly caused another, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM), to believe that the offender would cause physical harm to said other person or a family or household member of said other person, and having been previously convicted of or pleaded guilty to a violation of this section or a violation of Section 2911.211, to wit: (NAME OFFENSE, COURT OF CONVICTION, DATE, AND CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2903.211(B)(2)(a) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2903.211.notes: NOTE: In addition to any other basis for the other person’s belief that the offender will cause physical harm to the other person or the other person’s family or household member, the other person’s belief may be based on words or conduct of the offender that are directed at or identify a corporation, association, or other organization that employs the other person or to which the other person belongs. FAMILY OR HOUSEHOLD MEMBER – has the same definition as used in ORC 2919.25 (DV).

ORC:2903.211.heading: MENACING BY STALKING 2903.211(B)(2)(a) ORC
ORC:2903.211.text: _____________ did, engage in a pattern of conduct, to wit: (DESCRIBE PATTERN OF CONDUCT WHICH CAUSED (the victim or a family or household member of the victim) MENTAL DISTRESS INCLUDING THE DATES SUCH CONDUCT OCCURRED), which knowingly caused another, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM), mental distress, to wit: (DESCRIBE MENTAL DISTRESS CAUSED), and having been previously convicted of or pleaded guilty to a violation of this section or a violation of Section 2911.211, to wit: (NAME OFFENSE, COURT OF CONVICTION, DATE, AND CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2903.211(B)(2)(a) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2903.211.notes: NOTE: The other person’s mental distress may be based on words or conduct of the offender that are directed at or identify a corporation, association, or other organization that employs the other person or to which the other person belongs, in addition to any other basis. FAMILY OR HOUSEHOLD MEMBER – has the same definition as used in ORC 2919.25 (DV). MENTAL DISTRESS – any mental illness or condition that involves some temporary substantial incapacity or mental illness or condition that would normally require psychiatric treatment, psychological treatment, or other mental health services, whether or not any person requested or received psychiatric treatment, psychological treatment, or other mental health services.

ORC:2903.211.heading: MENACING BY STALKING 2903.211(B)(2)(a) ORC
ORC:2903.211.text: _____________ did, with sexual motivation, engage in a pattern of conduct, to wit: (DESCRIBE PATTERN OF CONDUCT WHICH CAUSED THE VICTIM TO BELIEVE THE DEFENDANT WOULD CAUSE (him/her or his/her family or household member) (physical harm or mental distress) INCLUDING THE DATES SUCH CONDUCT OCCURRED), which knowingly caused another, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM), (physical harm or mental distress), to wit: (DESCRIBE PHYSICAL HARM OR MENTAL DISTRESS CAUSED), having been previously convicted of this section or a violation of Section 2911.211, to wit: (NAME OFFENSE, COURT OF CONVICTION, DATE, AND CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2903.211(B)(2)(a) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2903.211.notes: NOTE: In addition to any other basis for the other person’s belief that the offender will cause physical harm to the other person or the other person’s family or household member, the other person’s belief or mental distress may be based on words or conduct of the offender that are directed at or identify a corporation, association, or other organization that employs the other person or to which the other person belongs. NOTE: MENACING BY STALKING is a felony of the fourth degree if any of the following apply: 2903.211(B)(2)(b): In committing the offense, the offender made a threat of physical harm to or against the victim or as a result of an offense committed under (A)(2) or (3) of this section, a third person induced by the offender’s posted message made a threat of physical harm to or against the victim – a felony of the fourth degree. 2903.211(B)(2)(c): In committing the offense, the offender trespassed on the land or premises where the victim lives, is employed, or attends school, or as a result of an offense committed under division (A)(2) or (3) of this section, a third person induced by the offender’s posted message trespassed on the land or premises where the victim lives, is employed, or attends school – a felony of the fourth degree. 2903.211(B)(2)(d): The victim of the offense is a minor – a felony of the fourth degree. 2903.211(B)(2)(e): The offender has a history of violence toward the victim or any other person or a history of other violent acts toward the victim or any other person – a felony of the fourth degree. 2903.211(B)(2)(f): While committing the offense under division (A)(1) of this section or a violation of division (A)(3) of this section based on conduct in violation of division (A)(1), the offender had a deadly weapon on or about the offender’s person or under the offender’s control – a felony of the fourth degree. 2903.211(B)(2)(g): At the time of the commission of the offense, the offender was the subject of a protection order issued under Section 2903.213 or 2903.214 of the Revised Code, regardless of whether the person to be protected under the order is the victim of the offense or another person – a felony of the fourth degree. 2903.211(B)(2)(h): In committing the offense, the offender caused serious physical harm to the premises at which the victim resides, to the real property on which that premises is located, or to any personal property located on that premises or as a result of an offense committed under (A)(2) or (A)(3) of this section, a third person induced by the offender’s posted message, caused serious physical harm to that premises, real property or any personal property on that premises – a felony of the fourth degree. 2903.211(B)(2)(i): Prior to committing the offense, the offender had been determined to represent a substantial risk of physical harm to others as manifested by evidence of then-recent homicidal or other violent behavior, evidence of then-recent threats that placed another in reasonable fear of violent behavior and serious physical harm, or other evidence of then-present dangerousness – a felony of the fourth degree. 2903.211(B)(3): If the victim of the offense is an officer or employee of a public children services agency or a private child placing agency and the offense relates to the officer’s or employee’s performance or anticipated performance of official responsibilities or duties – a felony of the fifth degree – OR – If the offender previously has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to an offense of violence, the victim of that prior offense was an officer or employee of a public children services agency or private child placing agency, and that prior offense related to the officer’s or employee’s performance or anticipated performance of official responsibilities or duties – a felony of the fourth degree. PATTERN OF CONDUCT – two or more actions or incidents closely related in time, whether or not there has been a prior conviction based on any of those action or incidents, or two or more actions or incidents closely related in time, whether or not there has been a prior conviction based on any of those actions or incidents, directed at one or more persons employed by or belonging to the same corporation, association, or other organization. Actions or incidents that prevent, obstruct, or delay the performance by a public official, firefighter, rescuer, or emergency medical services person of any authorized act within the public official’s, firefighter’s, rescuer’s, emergency facility person’s, or emergency medical services person’s official capacity, or the posting of messages, use of intentionally written or verbal graphic gestures, or receipt of information or data through the use of any form of written communication or an electronic method of remotely transferring information, including but not limited to, a computer, computer network, computer program, computer system, or telecommunications device, may constitute a “pattern of conduct.” MENTAL DISTRESS – any mental illness or condition that involves some temporary substantial incapacity or mental illness or condition that would normally require psychiatric treatment, psychological treatment, or other mental health services, whether or not any person requested or received psychiatric treatment, psychological treatment, or other mental health services.

ORC:2903.216.heading: ILLEGAL USE OF TRACKING DEVICE OR APPLICATION 2903.216(B) (1) ORC
ORC:2903.216.variant: INSTALL ON PROPERTY WITHOUT CONSENT – M1
ORC:2903.216.text: _____________ did install a (tracking device or tracking application) on another’s property without the other person’s consent, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME AND PROPERTY), in violation of Section 2903.216(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2903.216.heading: ILLEGAL USE OF TRACKING DEVICE OR APPLICATION 2903.216(B) (1) ORC
ORC:2903.216.variant: INSTALL ON PROPERTY WITHOUT CONSENT – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F4
ORC:2903.216.text: _____________ did install a (tracking device or tracking application) on another’s property without the other person’s consent, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME AND PROPERTY), having been previously convicted of violating Section (2903.211 or 2903.216) of the Ohio Revised Code, to wit: (NAME COURT, CASE NUMBER, AND DATE OF CONVICTION), in violation of Section 2903.216(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2903.216.heading: ILLEGAL USE OF TRACKING DEVICE OR APPLICATION 2903.216(B) (1) ORC
ORC:2903.216.variant: INSTALL ON PROPERTY WITHOUT CONSENT – SUBJECT OF A PROTECTION ORDER – F4
ORC:2903.216.text: _____________ did install a (tracking device or tracking application) on another’s property without the other person’s consent, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME AND PROPERTY), while being the subject of a protection order issued under Section (2903.213 or 2903.214) of the Ohio Revised Code, to wit: (NAME COURT AND DATE OF PROTECTION ORDER), in violation of Section 2903.216(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2903.216.heading: ILLEGAL USE OF TRACKING DEVICE OR APPLICATION 2903.216(B) (1) ORC
ORC:2903.216.variant: INSTALL ON PROPERTY WITHOUT CONSENT – SUBSTANTIAL RISK OF PHYSICAL HARM TO OTHERS – F4
ORC:2903.216.text: _____________ did install a (tracking device or tracking application) on another’s property without the other person’s consent, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME AND PROPERTY), having been previously found to be a substantial risk of physical harm to others, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2903.216(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2903.216.heading: ILLEGAL USE OF TRACKING DEVICE OR APPLICATION 2903.216(B) (1) ORC
ORC:2903.216.variant: INSTALL ON PROPERTY WITHOUT CONSENT – HISTORY OF VIOLENCE TOWARDS VICTIM – F4
ORC:2903.216.text: _____________ did install a (tracking device or tracking application) on another’s property without the other person’s consent, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME AND PROPERTY), having a history of (violence or other violent acts) towards the victim, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2903.216(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2903.216.heading: ILLEGAL USE OF TRACKING DEVICE OR APPLICATION 2903.216(B) (1) ORC
ORC:2903.216.text: _____________ did cause a (tracking device or tracking application) to track the (position or movement) of (another or another’s property) without the other person’s consent, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME AND CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2903.216(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2903.216.heading: ILLEGAL USE OF TRACKING DEVICE OR APPLICATION 2903.216(B) (1) ORC
ORC:2903.216.variant: TRACK POSITION OR MOVEMENT – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F4
ORC:2903.216.text: _____________ did cause a (tracking device or tracking application) to track the (position or movement) of (another or another’s property) without the other person’s consent, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME AND CIRCUMSTANCES), having been previously convicted of violating Section (2903.211 or 2903.216) of the Ohio Revised Code, to wit: (NAME COURT, CASE NUMBER, AND DATE OF CONVICTION), in violation of Section 2903.216(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2903.216.heading: ILLEGAL USE OF TRACKING DEVICE OR APPLICATION 2903.216(B) (1) ORC
ORC:2903.216.variant: TRACK POSITION OR MOVEMENT – SUBJECT OF A PROTECTION ORDER – F4
ORC:2903.216.text: _____________ did cause a (tracking device or tracking application) to track the (position or movement) of (another or another’s property) without the other person’s consent, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME AND CIRCUMSTANCES), while being the subject of a protection order issued under Section (2903.213 or 2903.214) of the Ohio Revised Code, to wit: (NAME COURT AND DATE OF PROTECTION ORDER), in violation of Section 2903.216(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2903.216.heading: ILLEGAL USE OF TRACKING DEVICE OR APPLICATION 2903.216(B) (1) ORC
ORC:2903.216.variant: TRACK POSITION OR MOVEMENT – SUBSTANTIAL RISK OF PHYSICAL HARM TO OTHERS – F4
ORC:2903.216.text: _____________ did cause a (tracking device or tracking application) to track the (position or movement) of (another or another’s property) without the other person’s consent, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME AND CIRCUMSTANCES), having been previously found to be a substantial risk of physical harm to others, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2903.216(B) (1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2903.216.heading: ILLEGAL USE OF TRACKING DEVICE OR APPLICATION 2903.216(B) (1) ORC
ORC:2903.216.variant: TRACK POSITION OR MOVEMENT – HISTORY OF VIOLENCE TOWARDS VICTIM – F4
ORC:2903.216.text: _____________ did cause a (tracking device or tracking application) to track the (position or movement) of (another or another’s property) without the other person’s consent, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME AND CIRCUMSTANCES), having a history of (violence or other violent acts) towards the victim, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2903.216(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2903.216.heading: ILLEGAL USE OF TRACKING DEVICE OR APPLICATION 2903.216(B) (1) ORC
ORC:2903.216.text: _____________ did fail (to remove or ensure the removal) of a (tracking device or tracking application) after the other person revoked consent, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME AND CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2903.216(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2903.216.heading: ILLEGAL USE OF TRACKING DEVICE OR APPLICATION 2903.216(B) (1) ORC
ORC:2903.216.variant: AFTER REVOKED CONSENT – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F4
ORC:2903.216.text: _____________ did fail (to remove or ensure the removal) of a (tracking device or tracking application) after the other person revoked consent, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME AND CIRCUMSTANCES), having been previously convicted of violating Section (2903.211 or 2903.216) of the Ohio Revised Code, to wit: (NAME COURT, CASE NUMBER, AND DATE OF CONVICTION), in violation of Section 2903.216(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2903.216.heading: ILLEGAL USE OF TRACKING DEVICE OR APPLICATION 2903.216(B) (1) ORC
ORC:2903.216.variant: AFTER REVOKED CONSENT – SUBJECT OF A PROTECTION ORDER – F4
ORC:2903.216.text: _____________ did fail (to remove or ensure the removal) of a (tracking device or tracking application) after the other person revoked consent, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME AND CIRCUMSTANCES), while being the subject of a protection order issued under Section (2903.213 or 2903.214) of the Ohio Revised Code, to wit: (NAME COURT AND DATE OF PROTECTION ORDER), in violation of Section 2903.216(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2903.216.heading: ILLEGAL USE OF TRACKING DEVICE OR APPLICATION 2903.216(B) (1) ORC
ORC:2903.216.variant: AFTER REVOKED CONSENT – SUBSTANTIAL RISK OF PHYSICAL HARM TO OTHERS – F4
ORC:2903.216.text: _____________ did fail (to remove or ensure the removal) of a (tracking device or tracking application) after the other person revoked consent, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME AND CIRCUMSTANCES), having been previously found to be a substantial risk of physical harm to others, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2903.216(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2903.216.heading: ILLEGAL USE OF TRACKING DEVICE OR APPLICATION 2903.216(B) (1) ORC
ORC:2903.216.variant: AFTER REVOKED CONSENT – HISTORY OF VIOLENCE TOWARDS VICTIM – F4
ORC:2903.216.text: _____________ did fail (to remove or ensure the removal) of a (tracking device or tracking application) after the other person revoked consent, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME AND CIRCUMSTANCES), having a history of (violence or other violent acts) towards the victim, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2903.216(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2903.22.heading: MENACING 2903.22 ORC (CCC 2303.22)
ORC:2903.22.variant: CAUSE ANOTHER TO BELIEVE PHYSICAL HARM WILL BE DONE – M4
ORC:2903.22.text: _____________ did knowingly cause another, to wit: (VICTIM’S NAME), to believe that (STATE NAME OF OFFENDER), would cause physical harm to (said other person, said others unborn, said others property, or a member of said others immediate family), to wit: (DESCRIBE REASON FOR BELIEF), in violation of Section 2903.22 of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2903.22.notes: NOTE: In addition to any other basis for the other person’s belief that the offender will cause physical harm to the other person or the other person’s mental distress, the other person’s belief or mental distress may be based on words or conduct of the offender that are directed at or identify a corporation, association, or other organization that employs the other person or to which the other person belongs. NOTE: If the offender had a firearm or dangerous ordnance on or about the offender’s person or under the offender’s control at the time of the commission of the offense in violation of the Columbus City Code, the firearm or dangerous ordnance shall be seized and is subject to forfeiture under Chapter 2981 of the Ohio Revised Code. Refer to the complaint language cited in Chapter 2927 of the Criminal Complaint Manual.

ORC:2903.22.heading: MENACING 2903.22 ORC (CCC 2303.22)
ORC:2903.22.variant: CAUSE ANOTHER TO BELIEVE PHYSICAL HARM WILL BE DONE – OFFICER OR EMPLOYEE OF CHILDREN SERVICES AGENCY – M1
ORC:2903.22.text: _____________ did knowingly cause another, to wit: (VICTIM’S NAME), to believe that (STATE NAME OF OFFENDER), would cause physical harm to (said other person, said others unborn, said others property, or a member of said others immediate family), to wit: (DESCRIBE REASON FOR BELIEF), being an officer or employee of a (public children services agency or a private child placing agency), to wit: (NAME AGENCY) and the offense relates to the officer’s or employee’s performance or anticipated performance of official responsibilities or duties, to wit: (DESCRIBE PERFORMANCE OR RESPONSIBILITIES), in violation of Section 2903.22 of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2903.22.notes: NOTE: In addition to any other basis for the other person’s belief that the offender will cause physical harm to the other person or the other person’s mental distress, the other person’s belief or mental distress may be based on words or conduct of the offender that are directed at or identify a corporation, association, or other organization that employs the other person or to which the other person belongs. NOTE: If the offender had a firearm or dangerous ordnance on or about the offender’s person or under the offender’s control at the time of the commission of the offense in violation of the Columbus City Code, the firearm or dangerous ordnance shall be seized and is subject to forfeiture under Chapter 2981 of the Ohio Revised Code. Refer to the complaint language cited in Chapter 2927 of the Criminal Complaint Manual.

ORC:2903.22.heading: MENACING 2903.22 ORC (CCC 2303.22)
ORC:2903.22.variant: CAUSE ANOTHER TO BELIEVE PHYSICAL HARM WILL BE DONE – OFFICER OR EMPLOYEE OF CHILDREN SERVICES AGENCY – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F4
ORC:2903.22.text: _____________ did knowingly cause another, to wit: (VICTIM’S NAME), to believe that (STATE NAME OF OFFENDER), would cause physical harm to (said other person, said others unborn, said others property, or a member of said others immediate family), to wit: (DESCRIBE REASON FOR BELIEF), being an officer or employee of a (public children services agency or a private child placing agency), to wit: (NAME AGENCY) and the offense relates to the officer’s or employee’s performance or anticipated performance of official responsibilities or duties, to wit: (DESCRIBE PERFORMANCE OR RESPONSIBILITIES), having previously been convicted of or pleaded guilty to an offense of violence, to wit: (NAME OF OFFENSE, SECTION NUMBER, COURT, AND DATE OF CONVICTION), in violation of Section 2903.22 of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2903.22.notes: NOTE: In addition to any other basis for the other person’s belief that the offender will cause physical harm to the other person or the other person’s mental distress, the other person’s belief or mental distress may be based on words or conduct of the offender that are directed at or identify a corporation, association, or other organization that employs the other person or to which the other person belongs. NOTE: If the offender had a firearm or dangerous ordnance on or about the offender’s person or under the offender’s control at the time of the commission of the offense in violation of the Columbus City Code, the firearm or dangerous ordnance shall be seized and is subject to forfeiture under Chapter 2981 of the Ohio Revised Code. Refer to the complaint language cited in Chapter 2927 of the Criminal Complaint Manual.

ORC:2903.22.heading: MENACING 2903.22(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2903.22.variant: DISPLAY DEADLY WEAPON – EMERGENCY SERVICE RESPONDER – M1
ORC:2903.22.text: _____________ did knowingly place or attempt to place an emergency service responder, to wit: (VICTIM’S NAME AND PROFESSION), in reasonable fear of physical harm or death by displaying a deadly weapon, to wit: (DESCRIBE DEADLY WEAPON), the person knows or reasonably should know that the other person is an emergency service responder, AND it is the person’s specific purpose to engage in the specified conduct against an emergency service responder, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of 2903.22(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2903.22.notes: NOTE: “Emergency service responder” means any law enforcement officer, first responder, emergency medical technician-basic, emergency medical technician-intermediate, emergency medical technician-paramedic, firefighter, or volunteer firefighter. NOTE: The deadly weapon displayed does not need to be operable. NOTE: If the offender previously has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to an offense of violence, the victim of that prior offense was an officer or employee of a public children services agency or private child placing agency or an emergency service responder, and that prior offense related to the officer’s or employee’s performance or anticipated performance of official responsibilities or duties or to the responder’s performance of the responder’s official duties, the charge is a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2903.22.heading: MENACING 2903.22(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2903.22.variant: DISPLAY DEADLY WEAPON – FAMILY OR HOUSEHOLD MEMBER OR CO-WORKER OF EMERGENCY SERVICE RESPONDER – M1
ORC:2903.22.text: _____________ did knowingly place or attempt to place another who is a (family or household member or co-worker) of an emergency service responder, to wit: (VICTIM’S NAME AND DESCRIBE RELATIONSHIP TO EMERGENCY SERVICE RESPONDER), in reasonable fear of physical harm or death by displaying a deadly weapon, to wit: (DESCRIBE DEADLY WEAPON), the person knows or reasonably should know that the other person is a (family or household member or co-worker) of an emergency service responder, AND it is the person’s specific purpose to engage in the specified conduct against a (family or household member or co-worker) of an emergency service responder, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of 2903.22(A) (2) of the Ohio Revised code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2903.22.notes: NOTE: “Emergency service responder” means any law enforcement officer, first responder, emergency medical technician-basic, emergency medical technician-intermediate, emergency medical technician-paramedic, firefighter, or volunteer firefighter. NOTE: The deadly weapon displayed does not need to be operable. NOTE: If the offender previously has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to an offense of violence, the victim of that prior offense was an officer or employee of a public children services agency or private child placing agency or an emergency service responder, and that prior offense related to the officer’s or employee’s performance or anticipated performance of official responsibilities or duties or to the responder’s performance of the responder’s official duties, the charge is a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2903.31.heading: HAZING 2903.31(B)(1) ORC (CCC 2303.31(B)(1))
ORC:2903.31.text: _____________ did recklessly participate in the hazing of another, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON AND DESCRIBE ACT OF HAZING), in violation of Section 2903.31(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.
ORC:2903.31.notes: NOTE: “Hazing,” as defined in 2903.31(A) ORC, means doing any act or coercing another, including the victim; to do any act of initiation in any student or other organization; or any act to continue or reinstate membership in or affiliation with any student or other organization that causes or creates a substantial risk of causing mental or physical harm to any person, including coercing another to consume alcohol or a drug of abuse, as defined in 3719.011 ORC.

ORC:2903.31.heading: HAZING 2903.31(B)(2) ORC (CCC 2303.31(B)(2))
ORC:2903.31.text: _____________ did, being the (administrator, employee, faculty member, teacher, consultant, alumnus, or volunteer) of a (primary, secondary, or post-secondary school or any other educational institution, public or private), to wit: (NAME OF PERSONNEL and NAME OF INSTITUTION), recklessly permit the hazing of a person associated with the organization, to wit: (NAME OR DESCRIBE PERSON AND DESCRIBE THE HAZING ACT), in violation of Section 2903.31(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.
ORC:2903.31.notes: NOTE: See definition of hazing listed in Section 2903.31(B)(1).

ORC:2903.31.heading: HAZING 2903.31(C)(1) ORC
ORC:2903.31.variant: PARTICIPATE IN – COERCED CONSUMPTION OF ALCOHOL OR DRUGS RESULTING IN SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM – F3
ORC:2903.31.text: _____________ did recklessly participate in the hazing of another which included the coerced consumption of alcohol or drugs of abuse, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON AND DESCRIBE ACT OF HAZING) and which resulted in serious physical harm to another person, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM), in violation of Section 2903.31 (C)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2903.31.notes: NOTE: See definition of hazing listed in Section 2903.31(B)(1).

ORC:2903.31.heading: HAZING 2903.31(C)(2) ORC
ORC:2903.31.variant: SCHOOL PERSONNEL PERMITTING – COERCED CONSUMPTION OF ALCOHOL OR DRUGS RESULTING IN SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM – F3
ORC:2903.31.text: _____________ did, being an (administrator, employee, faculty member, teacher, consultant, alumnus, or volunteer) of an organization (primary, secondary, post-secondary school or any other educational institution, public or private) to wit: (NAME OF PERSONNEL and NAME OF INSTITUTION) recklessly permit the hazing of a person associated with the organization, which included the coerced consumption of alcohol or drugs of abuse, to wit: (NAME OR DESCRIBE PERSON AND DESCRIBE THE HAZING ACT), and which resulted in serious physical harm to another, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM), in violation of Section 2903.31(C)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2903.31.notes: NOTE: See definition of hazing listed in Section 2903.31(B)(1).

ORC:2903.32.heading: FEMALE GENITAL MUTILATION 2903.32(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2903.32.variant: KNOWINGLY CIRCUMCISE LABIA OR CLITORIS OF MINOR – F2
ORC:2903.32.text: _____________ did knowingly (circumcise, excise, or infibulate) any part of the (labia majora, labia minora, or clitoris) of another person who is under the age of eighteen, to wit: (STATE NAME AND AGE OF VICTIM AND DESCRIBE WHAT WAS DONE TO THEM), in violation of Section 2903.32(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2903.32.heading: FEMALE GENITAL MUTILATION 2903.32(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2903.32.variant: KNOWINGLY TRANSPORT MINOR TO A FACILITY FOR PURPOSE OF FACILITATING CIRCUMCISION – F2
ORC:2903.32.text: _____________ did knowingly transport a minor, to wit: (STATE NAME AND AGE OF VICTIM) to a facility or location, to wit: (STATE NAME OF FACILITY AND/OR ADDRESS OF LOCATION) for the purpose of facilitating the commission of an offense prohibited by ORC 2903.32(A)(1), by means of (DESCRIBE HOW VICTIM WAS TRANSPORTED AND WHAT WAS DONE TO THEM), in violation of 2903.32(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2903.32.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to a procedure performed for medical purposes if the act is performed by a physician (as authorized under ORC 4731) or licensed health care professional (as authorized under ORC Title 47) and the act is within the scope of the actor’s license. NOTE: None of the following are defenses to a violation of this section: cultural or ritual necessity; consent of the minor; or consent of the parent or guardian of the minor. DEFINITIONS 2903.34 ABUSE – knowingly cause physical harm or recklessly causing serious physical harm to a person by physical contact with the person or by the inappropriate use of a physical or chemical restraint, medication, or isolation on the person. GROSS NEGLECT – knowingly failing to provide a person with any treatment, care, goods, or service that is necessary to maintain the health or safety of the person when the failure results in physical harm or serious physical harm to the person. NEGLECT – recklessly failing to provide a person with any treatment, care, goods, or service that is necessary to maintain the health or safety of the person when the failure results in serious physical harm to the person. INAPPROPRIATE USE OF A PHYSICAL OR CHEMICAL RESTRAINING, MEDICATION, OR ISOLATION – the use of physical or chemical restraint, medication, or isolation as punishment, for staff convenience, excessively, as a substitute for treatment, or in quantities that preclude habilitation and treatment.

ORC:2903.34.heading: PATIENT ABUSE 2903.34(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2903.34.text: _____________ did, being the (owner or operator or administrator or an agent of or an employee of) a care facility, to wit: (NAME AND ADDRESS OF FACILITY), commit abuse against a resident or patient of the facility, to wit: (NAME RESIDENT OR PATIENT AND DESCRIBE ABUSE), in violation of Section 2903.34(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2903.34.heading: PATIENT ABUSE 2903.34(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2903.34.text: _____________ did, being the (owner or operator or administrator or an agent of or an employee of) a care facility, to wit: (NAME AND ADDRESS OF FACILITY), commit abuse against a resident or patient of the facility, to wit: (NAME RESIDENT OR PATIENT AND DESCRIBE ABUSE), and, having been previously convicted of or pleaded guilty to, any violation of this section, to wit: (NAME OFFENSE, SECTION, DATE, AND COURT), in violation of Section 2903.34(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2903.34.heading: GROSS PATIENT NEGLECT 2903.34(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2903.34.text: _____________ did, being the (owner or operator or administrator or an agent of or an employee of) a care facility, to wit: (NAME AND ADDRESS OF FACILITY), commit gross neglect against a resident or patient of the facility, to wit: (NAME RESIDENT OR PATIENT AND DESCRIBE GROSS NEGLECT), in violation of Section 2903.34(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2903.34.heading: GROSS PATIENT NEGLECT 2903.34(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2903.34.variant: COMMIT GROSS NEGLECT – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F5
ORC:2903.34.text: _____________ did, being the (owner or operator or administrator or an agent of or an employee of) a care facility, to wit: (NAME AND ADDRESS OF FACILITY), commit gross neglect against a resident or patient of the facility, to wit: (NAME RESIDENT OR PATIENT AND DESCRIBE GROSS NEGLECT), and, having been previously convicted of or pleaded guilty to, any violation of this section, to wit: (NAME OFFENSE, SECTION, DATE, AND COURT), in violation of Section 2903.34(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2903.34.heading: PATIENT NEGLECT 2903.34(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2903.34.text: _____________ did, being the (owner or operator or administrator or an agent of or an employee of) a care facility, to wit: (NAME AND ADDRESS OF FACILITY), commit neglect against a resident or patient of the facility, to wit: (NAME RESIDENT OR PATIENT AND DESCRIBE NEGLECT), in violation of Section 2903.34(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2903.34.heading: PATIENT NEGLECT 2903.34(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2903.34.text: _____________ did, being the (owner or operator or administrator or an agent of or an employee of) a care facility, to wit: (NAME AND ADDRESS OF FACILITY), commit neglect against a resident or patient of the facility, to wit: (NAME RESIDENT OR PATIENT AND DESCRIBE NEGLECT), and, having been previously convicted of or pleaded guilty to, any violation of this section, to wit: (NAME OFFENSE, SECTION, DATE, AND COURT), in violation of Section 2903.34(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2903.34.notes: DEFINITIONS 2903.341 NOTE: As used in this section: 1. DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES CARETAKER – means any developmental disabilities employee or any person who assumes the duty to provide for the care and protection of a person with a developmental disability on a voluntary basis, by contract, through receipt of payment for care and protection, as a result of a family relationship, or by order of a court of competent jurisdiction. cause physical harm or recklessly causing serious physical harm to a person by physical contact with the person or by the inappropriate use of a physical or chemical restraint, medication, or isolation on the person. 2. DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES CARETAKER – includes a person who is an employee of a care facility and a person who is an employee of an entity under contract with a provider. “Developmental disabilities caretaker” does not include a person who owns, operates, or administers a care facility or who is an agent of a care facility unless that person also personally provides care to a person with a developmental disability. 3. DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES EMPLOYEE – has the same meaning as in ORC 5123.50. 4. DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITY – has the same meaning as in ORC 5123.01.

ORC:2903.341.heading: PATIENT ENDANGERMENT 2903.341(B) ORC
ORC:2903.341.variant: SUBSTANTIAL RISK CREATED BY DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES CARETAKER – M1
ORC:2903.341.text: _____________ did, being a developmental disabilities caretaker, create a substantial risk to the health or safety of a person with a developmental disability, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM AND DESCRIBE RISK CREATED), in violation of Section 2903.341(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2903.341.heading: PATIENT ENDANGERMENT 2903.341(B) ORC
ORC:2903.341.variant: SUBSTANTIAL RISK CREATED BY DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES CARETAKER – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F4
ORC:2903.341.text: _____________ did, being a developmental disabilities caretaker, create a substantial risk to the health or safety of a person with a developmental disability, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM AND DESCRIBE RISK CREATED), and having been previously convicted of or pleaded guilty to a violation of this section, to wit: (NAME OFFENSE, COURT OF CONVICTION, DATE, AND CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2903.341(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2903.341.heading: PATIENT ENDANGERMENT 2903.341(B) ORC
ORC:2903.341.variant: SUBSTANTIAL RISK CREATED BY DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES CARETAKER – RESULTING IN SERIOUS HARM – F3
ORC:2903.341.text: _____________ did, being a developmental disabilities caretaker, create a substantial risk to the health or safety of a person with a developmental disability, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM AND DESCRIBE RISK CREATED), which did result in serious physical harm to the person with a developmental disability, to wit: (DESCRIBE RESULTING HARM) , in violation of Section 2903.341(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2903.341.heading: PATIENT ENDANGERMENT 2903.341(C) ORC
ORC:2903.341.variant: OWNER, OPERATOR, ADMINISTRATOR, OR AGENT – M1
ORC:2903.341.text: _____________ did, being the (owner, operator, administrator, or agent) of a care facility (condoned or knowingly permitted) any conduct by a developmental disabilities caretaker who is (employed by or under the control of) the (owner, operator, administrator, or agent), to wit: (NAME OF CARETAKER, NAME AND ADDRESS OF FACILITY), to create a substantial risk to the health or safety of a person with a developmental disability, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM AND DESCRIBE RISK CREATED), who is under the care of the (owner, operator, administrator, or agent), in violation of Section 2903.341(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2903.341.heading: PATIENT ENDANGERMENT 2903.341(C) ORC
ORC:2903.341.variant: OWNER, OPERATOR, ADMINISTRATOR, OR AGENT – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F4
ORC:2903.341.text: _____________ did, being the (owner, operator, administrator, or agent) of a care facility (condoned or knowingly permitted) any conduct by a developmental disabilities caretaker who is (employed by or under the control of) the (owner, operator, administrator, or agent), to wit: (NAME OF CARETAKER, NAME AND ADDRESS OF FACILITY), to create a substantial risk to the health or safety of a person with a developmental disability, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM AND DESCRIBE RISK CREATED), who is under the care of the (owner, operator, administrator, or agent), and having been previously convicted of or pleaded guilty to a violation of this section, to wit: (NAME OFFENSE, COURT OF CONVICTION, DATE, AND CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2903.341(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2903.341.heading: PATIENT ENDANGERMENT 2903.341(C) ORC
ORC:2903.341.variant: OWNER, OPERATOR, ADMINISTRATOR, OR AGENT – SERIOUS HARM CAUSED – F3
ORC:2903.341.text: _____________ did, being the (owner, operator, administrator, or agent) of a care facility (condoned or knowingly permitted) any conduct by a developmental disabilities caretaker who is (employed by or under the control of) the (owner, operator, administrator, or agent), to wit: (NAME OF CARETAKER, NAME AND ADDRESS OF FACILITY), to create a substantial risk to the health or safety of a person with a developmental disability, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM AND DESCRIBE RISK CREATED), who is under the care of the (owner, operator, administrator, or agent), which did result in serious physical harm to the person with a developmental disability, to wit: (DESCRIBE RESULTING HARM), in violation of Section 2903.341(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2903.35.heading: FILING A FALSE PATIENT ABUSE COMPLAINT 2903.35 ORC
ORC:2903.35.text: _____________ did knowingly (make or swear to the truth of a previously made or affirm to the truth of a previously made) false statement, alleging a violation of Section 2903.34 of the Ohio Revised Code, to wit: (DESCRIBE STATEMENT), when the statement was made for the purpose to incriminate another, to wit: (STATE OTHER’S NAME), in violation of Section 2903.35 of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2905.01.heading: KIDNAPPING 2905.01(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2905.01.variant: FOR RANSOM OR HOSTAGE – F1
ORC:2905.01.text: _____________ did, by (force, or threat of force, or deception), to wit: (DESCRIBE), (remove another from the place where that person was found or restrain the liberty of another), to wit: (STATE MANNER AND VICTIM’S NAME), with purpose to be held (for ransom or as a shield or as a hostage), in violation of Section 2905.01(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the first degree.
ORC:2905.01.notes: Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking. NOTE: This offense is a felony of the second degree if the person is released unharmed in a safe place).

ORC:2905.01.heading: KIDNAPPING 2905.01(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2905.01.variant: CHILD UNDER 13 OR MENTAL INCOMPETENT FOR RANSOM OR HOSTAGE – F1
ORC:2905.01.text: _____________ did (remove another from the place where that person was found or restrain the liberty of another), to wit: (STATE MANNER AND VICTIM’S NAME), who was (under 13 years of age, to wit: (STATE AGE) or mentally incompetent), with purpose to be held (for ransom or as a shield or as a hostage), in violation of Section 2905.01(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the first degree.
ORC:2905.01.notes: If the victim is less than 13 years of age, add the following at the end of the complaint for SEXUAL MOTIVATION: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense with a sexual motivation. Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking. NOTE: This offense is a felony of the second degree if the person is released unharmed in a safe place).

ORC:2905.01.heading: KIDNAPPING 2905.01(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2905.01.variant: FACILITATE A FELONY OR FLIGHT THEREAFTER – F1
ORC:2905.01.text: _____________ did, by (force, or threat of force, or deception), to wit: (DESCRIBE), (remove another from the place where that person was found or restrain the liberty of another), to wit: (STATE MANNER AND VICTIM’S NAME), with purpose to facilitate (the commission of a felony or flight after the commission of a felony), to wit: (NAME FELONY OFFENSE AND GIVE SECTION NUMBER), in violation of Section 2905.01(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the first degree.
ORC:2905.01.notes: Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking. NOTE: This offense is a felony of the second degree if the person is released unharmed in a safe place.

ORC:2905.01.heading: KIDNAPPING 2905.01(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2905.01.variant: CHILD UNDER 13 OR MENTAL INCOMPETENT FACILITATE A FELONY OR FLIGHT THEREAFTER – F1
ORC:2905.01.text: _____________ did (remove another from the place where that person was found or restrain the liberty of another), to wit: (STATE MANNER AND VICTIM’S NAME) who was, (under 13 years of age, to wit: (STATE AGE) or mentally incompetent), with purpose to facilitate (the commission of a felony or flight after the commission of a felony), to wit: (NAME FELONY OFFENSE AND GIVE SECTION NUMBER), in violation of Section 2905.01(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the first degree.
ORC:2905.01.notes: If the victim is less than 13 years of age, add the following at the end of the complaint for SEXUAL MOTIVATION: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense with a sexual motivation. ORC:2905.11.text: _____________ did, with purpose to (compel or attempt to compel another) against the person’s will to perform any act or refrain from performing any act, to wit: (DESCRIBE ACT), (threaten to release, exhibit, or distribute), to wit: (DESCRIBE) the private images of another, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME), in violation of Section 2905.11(D)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2905.11.notes: NOTE: If the offender has a previous conviction or pleaded guilty to a violation of section (D) of this section, or if the offense involves sexual extortion of a victim under the age of eighteen, an elderly person, or a disabled adult, sexual extortion is a felony of the second degree. ORC:2905.32.heading: TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS 2905.32(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2905.32.variant: INVOLUNTARY SERVITUDE OR COMPELLED TO ENGAGE IN SEXUAL ACTIVITY FOR HIRE – F1
ORC:2905.32.text: _____________ did knowingly (recruit, lure, entice, isolate, harbor, transport, provide, obtain, or maintain, or knowingly attempt to recruit, lure, entice, isolate, harbor, transport, provide, obtain, or maintain), another person, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME), if the person will be subjected to (involuntary servitude or be compelled to engage in sexual activity for hire, engage in a performance that is obscene, sexually oriented, or nudity oriented, or be a model or participant in the production of material that is obscene, sexually oriented, or nudity oriented), to wit: (DESCRIBE OFFENSE), in violation of Section 2905.32(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the first degree.
ORC:2905.32.notes: NOTE: “Involuntary servitude” means being compelled to perform labor or services for another against one’s will. NOTE: For a prosecution under division (A)(1) of this section, the element “compelled” does not require that the compulsion be openly displayed or physically exerted. The element “compelled” has been established if the state proves that the victim’s will was overcome by force, fear, duress, intimidation, or fraud. NOTE: In a prosecution under this section, proof that the defendant engaged in sexual activity with any person, or solicited sexual activity with any person, whether or not for hire, without more, does not constitute a violation of this section. NOTE: A prosecution for a violation of this section does not preclude a prosecution of a violation of any other section of the Revised Code. One or more acts, a series of acts, or a course of behavior that can be prosecuted under this section or any other section of the Revised Code may be prosecuted under this section, the other section of the Revised Code, or both sections. However, if an offender is convicted of or pleads guilty to a violation of this section and also is convicted of or pleads guilty to any other offense based on the same conduct involving the same victim that was the basis of the violation of this section, the two offenses are allied offenses of similar import under section 2941.25 of the Revised Code.

ORC:2907.02.heading: RAPE 2907.02(A)(1)(a) ORC
ORC:2907.02.text: _____________ did engage in sexual conduct, to wit: (DESCRIBE TYPE OF CONDUCT) with another, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME) for the purpose of (preventing resistance by the victim or substantially impairing the victim’s judgment or control) the offender administered (surreptitiously or by force or by threat of force or by deception) a (drug or intoxicant), to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT AND NAME THE ITEM), to the victim, in violation of Section 2907.02(A)(1)(a) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the first degree.

ORC:2907.03.heading: SEXUAL BATTERY 2907.03(A)(1) ORC

ORC:2907.03.text: _____________ did engage in sexual activity, to wit: (DESCRIBE TYPE OF ACTIVITY) with another, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME), by knowingly coercing said victim to submit by means that would prevent resistance by a person of ordinary resolution, to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT), in violation of Section 2907.03(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the _____________ degree.
ORC:2907.03.notes: NOTE: If the sexual activity involved is sexual conduct, sexual battery in violation of Section 2907.03 is a felony of the third degree. If the other person, or one of the other persons, is thirteen years of age or over and less than eighteen years of age, sexual battery is a felony of the second degree. NOTE: If the sexual activity involved is sexual contact, sexual battery in violation of Section 2907.03 is a felony of the fifth degree. If the other person, or one of the other persons, is less than eighteen years of age, sexual battery in violation of Section 2907.03 is a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2907.04.text: _____________ did, being (eighteen years of age or over eighteen years of age), to wit: (STATE OFFENDER’S AGE), engage in sexual conduct, to wit: (DESCRIBE TYPE OF CONDUCT) with another, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM) (knowing or being reckless in knowing) said victim being thirteen years of age or older, but less than sixteen years of age, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S AGE) and the offender previously having been convicted of or pleaded guilty to a violation of Section 2907.02, 2907.03 or 2907.04 of the Ohio Revised Code or a violation of former 2907.12 of the Ohio Revised Code, to wit: (STATE SECTION, OFFENSE, COURT AND DATE OF CONVICTION), in violation of Section 2907.04(B)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
