ORC:2913.021.text: _____________ did, with purpose to deprive (elderly person, a disabled adult, an active duty service member, or spouse of an active duty service member), to wit: (STATE THE OWNER’S NAME AND AGE OR CLASS STATUS OR DISABILITY), of mail valued at (STATE AMOUNT), knowingly (obtain or exert) control over mail by deception, to wit: (DESCRIBE DECEPTION), in violation of Section 2913.021(B)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree:
ORC:2913.021.notes: – VALUE $1,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the fourth degree. NOTE: “Mail” means any letter, card, parcel, or other material, along with its contents, that is received, accepted for delivery, delivered or left for collection by a postal service, including the United States Postal Service, a common carrier, or a private delivery service.

ORC:2913.021.heading: THEFT OF MAIL 2913.021(B)(4) ORC
ORC:2913.021.text: _____________ did, with purpose to deprive the owner, to wit: (STATE THE OWNER’S NAME), of mail valued at (STATE AMOUNT), knowingly (obtain or exert) control over mail by threat, to wit: (DESCRIBE THREAT), in violation of Section 2913.021(B)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree:
ORC:2913.021.notes: – VALUE $7,500.00 OR MORE, a felony of the fourth degree. NOTE: “Mail” means any letter, card, parcel, or other material, along with its contents, that is received, accepted for delivery, delivered or left for collection by a postal service, including the United States Postal Service, a common carrier, or a private delivery service.

ORC:2913.021.heading: THEFT OF MAIL 2913.021(B)(4) ORC
ORC:2913.021.variant: BY THREAT – VICTIM IS MEMBER OF PROTECTED CLASS – F5
ORC:2913.021.text: _____________ did, with purpose to deprive (elderly person, a disabled adult, an active duty service member, or spouse of an active duty service member), to wit: (STATE THE OWNER’S NAME AND AGE OR CLASS STATUS OR DISABILITY), of mail valued at (STATE AMOUNT), knowingly (obtain or exert) control over mail by threat, to wit: (DESCRIBE THREAT), in violation of Section 2913.021(B)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree:
ORC:2913.021.notes: – VALUE $1,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the fourth degree. NOTE: “Mail” means any letter, card, parcel, or other material, along with its contents, that is received, accepted for delivery, delivered or left for collection by a postal service, including the United States Postal Service, a common carrier, or a private delivery service.

ORC:2913.021.heading: THEFT OF MAIL 2913.021(B)(5) ORC
ORC:2913.021.text: _____________ did, with purpose to deprive the owner, to wit: (STATE THE OWNER’S NAME), of mail valued at (STATE AMOUNT), knowingly (obtain or exert) control over mail by intimidation, to wit: (DESCRIBE INTIMIDATION), in violation of Section 2913.021(B)(5) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree:
ORC:2913.021.notes: – VALUE $7,500.00 OR MORE, a felony of the fourth degree. NOTE: “Mail” means any letter, card, parcel, or other material, along with its contents, that is received, accepted for delivery, delivered or left for collection by a postal service, including the United States Postal Service, a common carrier, or a private delivery service.

ORC:2913.021.heading: THEFT OF MAIL 2913.021(B)(5) ORC
ORC:2913.021.variant: BY INTIMIDATION – VICTIM IS MEMBER OF PROTECTED CLASS – F5
ORC:2913.021.text: _____________ did, with purpose to deprive (elderly person, a disabled adult, an active duty service member, or spouse of an active duty service member), to wit: (STATE THE OWNER’S NAME AND AGE OR CLASS STATUS OR DISABILITY), of mail valued at (STATE AMOUNT), knowingly (obtain or exert) control over mail by intimidation, to wit: (DESCRIBE INTIMIDATION), in violation of Section 2913.021(B)(5) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree:
ORC:2913.021.notes: – VALUE $1,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the fourth degree. NOTE: “Mail” means any letter, card, parcel, or other material, along with its contents, that is received, accepted for delivery, delivered or left for collection by a postal service, including the United States Postal Service, a common carrier, or a private delivery service.

ORC:2913.03.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF A VEHICLE 2913.03(A) ORC (CCC 2313.03(A))
ORC:2913.03.text: _____________ did knowingly (use or operate) (an aircraft or a motor vehicle or a motorcycle or a motor boat or a motor-propelled vehicle), to wit: (DESCRIBE THE VEHICLE), without the consent of the (owner or person authorized to give consent), to wit: (STATE PERSON’S NAME), in violation of Section 2913.03(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2913.03.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF A VEHICLE 2913.03(A) ORC
ORC:2913.03.variant: VICTIM IS AN ELDERLY PERSON OR DISABLED ADULT
ORC:2913.03.text: _____________ did knowingly, with purpose to deprive (an elderly person or a disabled adult), to wit: (STATE PERSON’S NAME AND AGE OR DISABILITY), use or operate (an aircraft or a motor vehicle or a motorcycle or a motor boat or a motor-propelled vehicle), to wit: (DESCRIBE THE VEHICLE), without the consent of the (elderly person, disabled adult, or person authorized to give consent), to wit: (STATE PERSON’S NAME), a felony of the fifth degree or if the victim incurs a loss as a result of the violation, (STATE AMOUNT), in violation of Section 2913.03(A) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.03.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $37,500.00, a felony of the third degree. – VALUE $37,500.00 OR MORE, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2913.03.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF A VEHICLE 2913.03(B) ORC
ORC:2913.03.variant: REMOVED VEHICLE FROM STATE – RETAINED FOR 48 HOURS – F5
ORC:2913.03.text: _____________ did knowingly (use or operate) (an aircraft or a motor vehicle or a motor boat or a motor propelled vehicle), to wit: (DESCRIBE THE VEHICLE), without the consent of the (owner or person authorized to give consent), to wit: (NAME OF PERSON) and (having removed said vehicle from the State of Ohio or having kept possession of said vehicle for more than 48 hours), in violation of Section 2913.03(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.03.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF A VEHICLE 2913.03(B) ORC
ORC:2913.03.variant: REMOVED VEHICLE FROM STATE – RETAINED FOR 48 HOURS – VICTIM IS AN ELDERLY PERSON OR DISABLED ADULT
ORC:2913.03.text: _____________ did knowingly, with purpose to deprive (an elderly person or a disabled adult), to wit: (STATE PERSON’S NAME AND AGE OR DISABILITY), use or operate (an aircraft or a motor vehicle or a motorcycle or a motor boat propelled vehicle), to wit: (DESCRIBE THE VEHICLE), without the consent of the (elderly person, disabled adult or person authorized to give consent), to wit: (STATE PERSON’S NAME) and (having removed said vehicle from the State of Ohio or having kept possession of said vehicle for more than 48 hours), a felony of the fifth degree or if the victim incurs a loss as a result of the violation, (STATE AMOUNT), in violation of Section 2913.03(B) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.03.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $37,500.00, a felony of the third degree. – VALUE $37,500.00 OR MORE, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2913.04.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF PROPERTY 2913.04(A) ORC (CCC 2313.04(A))
ORC:2913.04.text: _____________ did knowingly (use or operate) the property of another, to wit: (DESCRIBE PROPERTY) without the consent of the owner or the person authorized to give consent, to wit: (STATE PERSON’S NAME), in violation of Section 2913.04(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.04.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF PROPERTY 2913.04(A) ORC
ORC:2913.04.variant: WITH PURPOSE OF DEVISING OR EXECUTING A SCHEME – PROPERTY VALUE
ORC:2913.04.text: _____________ did knowingly (use or operate) the property of another, to wit: (DESCRIBE PROPERTY) without the consent of the owner or the person authorized to give consent, to wit: (STATE PERSON’S NAME), and the unauthorized use of the property is committed for the purpose of (devising or executing) a scheme to defraud or to obtain property or services, valued at, to wit: (STATE AMOUNT) in violation of Section 2913.04(A) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.04.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.04.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF PROPERTY 2913.04(A) ORC
ORC:2913.04.variant: VICTIM IS AN ELDERLY PERSON OR DISABLED ADULT
ORC:2913.04.text: _____________ did knowingly, with purpose to deprive (an elderly or a disabled person), to wit: (STATE PERSON’S NAME AND AGE OR DISABILITY) (use or operate) the property of another, valued at (STATE AMOUNT) to wit: (DESCRIBE PROPERTY) without the consent of either the (elderly person or disabled adult or person authorized to give consent), to wit: (STATE PERSON’S NAME), in violation of Section 2913.04(A) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.04.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $37,500.00, a felony of the third degree. – VALUE $37,500.00 OR MORE, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2913.04.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF COMPUTER, CABLE OR TELECOMMUNICATION PROPERTY 2913.04(B) ORC
ORC:2913.04.text: _____________ did knowingly (gain access to or attempt to gain access to or cause access to be gained to) a (computer or computer system or computer network or cable service or cable system or telecommunications device or telecommunications service or information service), to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER, CABLE, OR TELECOMMUNICATIONS PROPERTY AND DESCRIBE ATTEMPT OR METHOD OF ACCESS) without the consent of (the owner or person authorized to give consent), to wit: (STATE PERSON’S NAME), in violation of Section 2913.04(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.04.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF COMPUTER, CABLE OR TELECOMMUNICATION PROPERTY 2913.04(B) ORC
ORC:2913.04.variant: GAIN ACCESS WITHOUT CONSENT – PROPERTY VALUE – PURPOSE TO DEFRAUD OR COMMIT OTHER CRIMINAL OFFENSE
ORC:2913.04.text: _____________ did knowingly (gain access to or attempt to gain access to or cause access to be gained to) a (computer or computer system or computer network or cable service or cable system or telecommunications device or telecommunications service or information service) valued at (VALUE OF PROPERTY OR SERVICES), to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER, CABLE OR TELECOMMUNICATION PROPERTY AND DESCRIBE ATTEMPT OR METHOD OF ACCESS), without the consent of (the owner or the person authorized to give consent), to wit: (STATE PERSON’S NAME), for the purpose of (devising or executing a scheme to defraud or to obtain property or services OR for obtaining money, property, or services by false or fraudulent pretenses OR for committing another criminal offense), to wit: (DESCRIBE FRAUD OR CRIMINAL OFFENSE), in violation of Section 2913.04(B) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.04.notes: – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.04.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF COMPUTER, CABLE OR TELECOMMUNICATION PROPERTY 2913.04(B) ORC
ORC:2913.04.variant: GAIN ACCESS WITHOUT CONSENT – LOSS TO VICTIM – PURPOSE TO DEFRAUD OR COMMIT OTHER CRIMINAL OFFENSE
ORC:2913.04.text: _____________ did knowingly (gain access to or attempt to gain access to or cause access to be gained to) a (computer or computer system or computer network or cable service or cable system or telecommunications device or telecommunications service or information service), to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER, CABLE OR TELECOMMUNICATION PROPERTY AND DESCRIBE ATTEMPT OR METHOD OF ACCESS), without the consent of (the owner or the person authorized to give consent), to wit: (STATE PERSON’S NAME), for the purpose of (devising or executing a scheme to defraud or to obtain property or services or for obtaining money, property, or services by false or fraudulent pretenses or for committing another criminal offense), to wit: (DESCRIBE FRAUD OR CRIMINAL OFFENSE), and causing a loss to said person, to wit: (DESCRIBE LOSS AND VALUE), in violation of Section 2913.04(B) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.04.notes: – LOSS BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – LOSS $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.04.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF COMPUTER, CABLE OR TELECOMMUNICATION PROPERTY 2913.04(B) ORC
ORC:2913.04.variant: GAIN ACCESS WITHOUT CONSENT – PROPERTY VALUE – VICTIM IS AN ELDERLY PERSON OR DISABLED ADULT
ORC:2913.04.text: _____________ did knowingly (gain access to or attempt to gain access to or cause access to be gained to) a (computer or computer system or computer network or cable service or cable system or telecommunications device or telecommunications service or information service) valued at (VALUE OF PROPERTY OR SERVICES), to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER, CABLE OR TELECOMMUNICATION PROPERTY AND DESCRIBE ATTEMPT OR METHOD OF ACCESS), without the consent of (the owner or the person authorized to give consent), to wit: (STATE PERSON’S NAME), an elderly person or disabled adult, to wit: (AGE OR DISABILITY), in violation of Section 2913.04(B) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.04.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $37,500.00, a felony of the third degree. – VALUE $37,500.00 OR MORE, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2913.04.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF COMPUTER, CABLE OR TELECOMMUNICATION PROPERTY 2913.04(B) ORC
ORC:2913.04.variant: GAIN ACCESS WITHOUT CONSENT – LOSS TO VICTIM – VICTIM IS AN ELDERLY PERSON OR DISABLED ADULT
ORC:2913.04.text: _____________ did knowingly (gain access to or attempt to gain access to or cause access to be gained to) a (computer or computer system or computer network or cable service or cable system or telecommunications device or telecommunications service or information service), to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER, CABLE OR TELECOMMUNICATION PROPERTY AND DESCRIBE ATTEMPT OR METHOD OF ACCESS), without the consent of (the owner or the person authorized to give consent), to wit: (STATE PERSON’S NAME), an elderly person or disabled adult, to wit: (AGE OR DISABILITY), causing a loss to said (elderly person or disabled adult), to wit: (DESCRIBE LOSS AND VALUE), in violation of Section 2913.04(B) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.04.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $37,500.00, a felony of the third degree. – VALUE $37,500.00 OR MORE, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2913.04.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF COMPUTER, CABLE OR TELECOMMUNICATION PROPERTY 2913.04(B) ORC
ORC:2913.04.variant: GAIN ACCESS BEYOND THE SCOPE OF CONSENT – F5
ORC:2913.04.text: _____________ did knowingly (gain access to or attempt to gain access to or cause access to be gained to) a (computer or computer system or computer network or cable service or cable system or telecommunications device or telecommunications service or information service), to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER, CABLE OR TELECOMMUNICATION PROPERTY AND DESCRIBE ATTEMPT OR METHOD OF ACCESS), beyond the scope of the (expressed or implied) consent of (the owner or the person authorized to give consent), to wit: (STATE NAME OF OWNER OR AGENT AND STATE THE LIMIT OF VIOLATOR’S ACCESS) in violation of Section 2913.04(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.04.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF COMPUTER, CABLE OR TELECOMMUNICATION PROPERTY 2913.04(B) ORC
ORC:2913.04.variant: GAIN ACCESS BEYOND THE SCOPE OF CONSENT – PROPERTY VALUE – PURPOSE TO DEFRAUD OR COMMIT OTHER CRIMINAL OFFENSE
ORC:2913.04.text: _____________ did knowingly (gain access to or attempt to gain access to or cause access to be gained to) a (computer or computer system or computer network or cable service or cable system or telecommunications device or telecommunications service or information service) valued at (VALUE OF PROPERTY OR SERVICES), to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER, CABLE OR TELECOMMUNICATION PROPERTY AND DESCRIBE ATTEMPT OR METHOD OF ACCESS), beyond the scope of the (expressed or implied) consent of (the owner or the person authorized to give consent), to wit: (STATE NAME OF OWNER OR AGENT AND STATE THE LIMIT OF VIOLATOR’S ACCESS), for the purpose of (devising or executing a scheme to defraud or to obtain property or services OR for obtaining money, property, or services by false or fraudulent pretenses OR for committing another criminal offense), to wit: (DESCRIBE FRAUD OR CRIMINAL OFFENSE), in violation of Section 2913.04(B) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.04.notes: – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.04.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF COMPUTER, CABLE OR TELECOMMUNICATION PROPERTY 2913.04(B) ORC
ORC:2913.04.variant: GAIN ACCESS BEYOND THE SCOPE OF CONSENT – LOSS TO VICTIM – PURPOSE TO DEFRAUD OR COMMIT OTHER CRIMINAL OFFENSE
ORC:2913.04.text: _____________ did knowingly (gain access to or attempt to gain access to or cause access to be gained to) a (computer or computer system or computer network or cable service or cable system or telecommunications device or telecommunications service or information service), to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER, CABLE OR TELECOMMUNICATION PROPERTY AND DESCRIBE ATTEMPT OR METHOD OF ACCESS), beyond the scope of the (expressed or implied) consent of (the owner or the person authorized to give consent), to wit: (STATE NAME OF OWNER OR AGENT AND STATE THE LIMIT OF VIOLATOR’S ACCESS), for the purpose of (devising or executing a scheme to defraud or to obtain property or services OR for obtaining money, property, or services by false or fraudulent pretenses OR for committing another criminal offense), to wit: (DESCRIBE FRAUD OR CRIMINAL OFFENSE), and causing a loss to said person, to wit: (DESCRIBE LOSS AND VALUE), in violation of Section 2913.04(B) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.04.notes: – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.04.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF COMPUTER, CABLE OR TELECOMMUNICATION PROPERTY 2913.04(B) ORC
ORC:2913.04.variant: GAIN ACCESS BEYOND THE SCOPE OF CONSENT – PROPERTY VALUE – VICTIM IS AN ELDERLY PERSON OR DISABLED ADULT
ORC:2913.04.text: _____________ did knowingly (gain access to or attempt to gain access to or cause access to be gained to) a (computer or computer system or computer network or cable service or cable system or telecommunications device or telecommunications service or information service) valued at (VALUE OF PROPERTY OR SERVICES), to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER, CABLE OR TELECOMMUNICATION PROPERTY AND DESCRIBE ATTEMPT OR METHOD OF ACCESS), beyond the scope of the (expressed or implied) consent of (the owner or the person authorized to give consent), an (elderly person or disabled adult), to wit: (STATE NAME OF OWNER OR AGENT, AGE OR DISABILITY, AND STATE THE LIMIT OF VIOLATOR’S ACCESS), in violation of Section 2913.04(B) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.04.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $37,500.00, a felony of the third degree. – VALUE $37,500.00 OR MORE, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2913.04.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF COMPUTER, CABLE OR TELECOMMUNICATION PROPERTY 2913.04(B) ORC
ORC:2913.04.variant: GAIN ACCESS BEYOND THE SCOPE OF CONSENT – LOSS TO VICTIM – VICTIM IS AN ELDERLY PERSON OR DISABLED ADULT
ORC:2913.04.text: _____________ did knowingly (gain access to or attempt to gain access to or cause access to be gained to) a (computer or computer system or computer network or cable service or cable system or telecommunications device or telecommunications service or information service), to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER, CABLE OR TELECOMMUNICATION PROPERTY AND DESCRIBE ATTEMPT OR METHOD OF ACCESS), beyond the scope of the (expressed or implied) consent of (the owner or the person authorized to give consent), an (elderly person or disabled adult), to wit: (STATE NAME OF OWNER OR AGENT, AGE OR DISABILITY, AND STATE THE LIMIT OF VIOLATOR’S ACCESS), causing a loss to said (elderly person or disabled adult), to wit: (DESCRIBE LOSS AND VALUE), in violation of Section 2913.04(B) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.04.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $37,500.00, a felony of the third degree. – VALUE $37,500.00 OR MORE, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2913.04.heading: UNAUTHORIZED ACCESS TO LEADS 2913.04(C) ORC
ORC:2913.04.variant: GAIN ACCESS WITHOUT CONSENT OR BEYOND THE SCOPE OF CONSENT OR DISSEMINATE INFORMATION FROM LEADS – F5
ORC:2913.04.text: _____________ did knowingly (gain access to or attempt to gain access to, cause access to be granted to or disseminate information gained from access to) the law enforcement automated database system created pursuant to section 5503.10 of the Ohio Revised Code (without the consent of or beyond the scope of the express or implied consent of) the chair of the law enforcement automated data system steering committee, to wit: (DESCRIBE WHAT DONE WITH THE ACCESS TO LEADS), in violation of Section 2913.04(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.04.heading: UNAUTHORIZED ACCESS TO OHLEG 2913.04(D) ORC
ORC:2913.04.variant: GAIN ACCESS WITHOUT CONSENT OR BEYOND THE SCOPE OF CONSENT OR DISSEMINATE INFORMATION FROM OHLEG – F5
ORC:2913.04.text: _____________ did knowingly (gain access to or attempt to gain access to, cause access to be granted to or disseminate information gained from access to) the Ohio law enforcement gateway established and operated pursuant to section 109.57 of the Ohio Revised Code (without the consent of or beyond the scope of the express or implied consent of) the superintendent of the bureau of criminal identification and investigation, to wit: (DESCRIBE WHAT DONE WITH THE ACCESS TO OHLEG), in violation of Section 2913.04(D) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.041.heading: POSSESSION OF UNAUTHORIZED CABLE TELEVISION DEVICE 2913.041(A) ORC
ORC:2913.041.text: _____________ did knowingly possess any device, including any (instrument, apparatus, computer chip, equipment, decoder, descrambler, converter, software, or other device) specially (adapted, modified or remanufactured) for gaining access to cable television service, to wit: (DESCRIBE ACCESS) without securing authorization from or paying the required compensation to the owner or operator (NAME OWNER OR OPERATOR) of the system that provides the cable television service, in violation of Section 2913.041(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2913.041.notes: NOTE: It is a separate violation of this section with regard to each device that is sold, distributed, manufactured, or possession in violation of A or B of this section.

ORC:2913.041.heading: SALE OF UNAUTHORIZED CABLE TELEVISION DEVICE 2913.041(B) ORC
ORC:2913.041.text: _____________ did knowingly sell, distribute, or manufacture any device, including any (instrument, apparatus, computer chip, equipment, decoder, descrambler, converter, software, or other device) specially (adapted, modified or remanufactured) for gaining access to cable television service, to wit: (DESCRIBE ACCESS) without securing authorization from or paying the required compensation to the owner or operator (NAME OWNER OR OPERATOR) of the system that provides the cable television service, in violation of Section 2913.041(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2913.041.notes: NOTE: It is a separate violation of this section with regard to each device that is sold, distributed, manufactured or possession in violation of A or B of this section.

ORC:2913.05.heading: TELECOMMUNICATIONS FRAUD 2913.05(A) ORC
ORC:2913.05.text: _____________, having devised a scheme to defraud, did knowingly (disseminate, transmit, or cause to be disseminated or transmitted) by means of a (wire, radio, satellite, telecommunication, telecommunications device, or telecommunications service) to wit: (DESCRIBE FRAUD), any (writing, data, sign, signal, picture, sound or image) with purpose to execute or otherwise further the scheme to defraud in violation of Section 2913.05(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2913.05.notes: NOTE: If the victim is an elderly person, disabled adult, active duty service member, or spouse of an active duty service member, violation of this section is a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.05.heading: TELECOMMUNICATIONS FRAUD 2913.05(A) ORC
ORC:2913.05.text: _____________, having devised a scheme to defraud, did knowingly (disseminate, transmit, or cause to be disseminated or transmitted) by means of a (wire, radio, satellite, telecommunication, telecommunications device, or telecommunications service) valued at, to wit: (DESCRIBE FRAUD AND VALUE OF BENEFIT), any (writing, data, sign, signal, picture, sound or image) with purpose to execute or otherwise further the scheme to defraud in violation of Section 2913.05(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2913.05.notes: – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,50000, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the third degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $150,000.00 AND $1,000,000.00, a felony of the second degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the first degree. NOTE: Violations of this section and violations of sections 2913.02, 2913.04, 2913.11, 2913.21, 2913.42, 2913.43, or 2921.13 may aggregate if within same course of conduct when determining the penalty.

ORC:2913.06.heading: UNLAWFUL USE OF TELECOMMUNICATIONS DEVICE 2913.06(A) ORC
ORC:2913.06.text: _____________ did knowingly (manufacture, possess, deliver, offer to deliver, or advertise) a counterfeit telecommunications device, to wit: (DESCRIBE UNLAWFUL USE AND DEVICE), with purpose to use it criminally in violation of Section 2913.06(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.06.heading: UNLAWFUL USE OF TELECOMMUNICATIONS DEVICE 2913.06(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.06.variant: AVOID LAWFUL CHARGE OF SERVICE – F5
ORC:2913.06.text: _____________ did knowingly (manufacture, possess, deliver, offer to deliver, or advertise) a counterfeit telecommunications device with purpose to use that device or allow that device to be used by another person or knowing or having reason to know that another person may use that device, to wit: (DESCRIBE USE AND DEVICE), while obtaining or attempting to obtain a telecommunications service or information service with purpose to avoid a lawful charge for that service or aid or cause another to obtain or attempt to obtain telecommunications services or information services with purpose to avoid a lawful charge for that service, in violation of Section 2913.06(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.06.heading: UNLAWFUL USE OF TELECOMMUNICATIONS DEVICE 2913.06(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2913.06.text: _____________ did knowingly (manufacture, possess, deliver, offer to deliver, or advertise) a counterfeit telecommunications device with purpose to use that device or allow that device to be used by another person or knowing or having reason to know that another person may use that device, to wit: (DESCRIBE USE), to conceal the existence, place of origin, or destination of a telecommunications service or information service, in violation of Section 2913.06(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.07.heading: MOTION PICTURE PIRACY 2913.07(B) ORC
ORC:2913.07.text: _____________ did knowingly operate an audiovisual recording function of a device in a facility in which a motion picture is being shown, to wit: (DESCRIBE OFFENSE INCLUDING DEVICE, FACILITY AND MOTION PICTURE), without the written consent of the (owner or lessee of the facility or licensor of the motion picture), to wit: (STATE NAME), in violation of Section 2913.07(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2913.07.heading: MOTION PICTURE PIRACY 2913.07(B) ORC
ORC:2913.07.text: _____________ did knowingly operate an audiovisual recording function of a device in a facility in which a motion picture is being shown, to wit: (DESCRIBE OFFENSE INCLUDING DEVICE, FACILITY AND MOTION PICTURE), without the written consent of the (owner or lessee of the facility or licensor of the motion picture), to wit: (STATE NAME), and having been previously convicted of motion picture piracy on (STATE DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT) (CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2913.07(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.11.heading: PASSING BAD CHECKS 2913.11(B) ORC
ORC:2913.11.variant: AMOUNT OF CHECK – TO SINGLE VENDOR OR PERSON
ORC:2913.11.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud (STATE VICTIM’S NAME), (issue or transfer or cause to be issued or cause to be transferred) a (check or negotiable instrument) payable in an amount of (STATE AMOUNT), dated (STATE DATE) drawn on (NAME OF BANK) to the order of (NAME PERSON), (knowing said (check or negotiable instrument) will be dishonored OR knowing that a person has ordered or will order stop payment on said (check or negotiable instrument), to wit: (DESCRIBE STOP PAYMENT)), in violation of Section 2913.11(B) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.11.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.11.heading: PASSING BAD CHECKS 2913.11(B) ORC
ORC:2913.11.variant: AMOUNT OF CHECK – TO MULTIPLE VENDORS OR PERSONS
ORC:2913.11.text: _____________ did, with a purpose to defraud (STATE VICTIMS’ NAMES), (issue or transfer or cause to be issued or cause to be transferred) a (check or negotiable instrument) payable in an amount of (STATE AMOUNT) dated (STATE DATE) drawn on (NAME OF BANK) to the order of (NAME PERSONS), (knowing said (check or negotiable instrument) will be dishonored OR knowing that a person has ordered or will order stop payment on said (check or negotiable instrument), to wit: (DESCRIBE STOP PAYMENT)), in violation of Section 2913.11(B) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.11.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,500.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,500.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.21.heading: MISUSE OF CREDIT CARDS 2913.21(A)(1) ORC (CCC 2313.21(A)(1))
ORC:2913.21.text: _____________ did practice deception for the purpose of procuring the issuance of a credit card, to wit: (DESCRIBE CARD AND COMPANY) and said credit card is issued in reliance upon the deception, to wit: (DESCRIBE DECEPTION), in violation of Section 2913.21(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2913.21.heading: MISUSE OF CREDIT CARDS 2913.21(A)(2) ORC (CCC 2313.21(A)(2))
ORC:2913.21.variant: BUYING OR SELLING CREDIT CARD – M1
ORC:2913.21.text: _____________ did knowingly (buy or sell) a credit card, to wit: (DESCRIBE CARD AND COMPANY), (from or to) (NAME OF SELLER OR PURCHASER) who was not the issuer, in violation of Section 2913.21(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2913.21.heading: MISUSE OF CREDIT CARDS 2913.21(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2913.21.variant: MISUSE BY A PUBLIC SERVANT – M1
ORC:2913.21.text: _____________ did while being an (officer, employee, or appointee of a political subdivision) or (as a public servant as defined in ORC 2921.01), to wit: (STATE JOB/CLASSIFICATION) knowingly misuse a credit card held by a political subdivision, to wit: (DESCRIBE CARD, COMPANY, POLITICAL SUBDIVISION AND HOW MISUSED), in violation of Section 2913.21(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2913.21.heading: MISUSE OF CREDIT CARDS 2913.21(B)(1) ORC (CCC 2313.21(B)(1))
ORC:2913.21.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud, obtain control over a credit card, to wit: (DESCRIBE CARD AND COMPANY) from (NAME OF VICTIM) as security for debt, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES OF HOW CARD WAS OBTAINED), in violation of Section 2913.21(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2913.21.heading: MISUSE OF CREDIT CARDS 2913.21(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.21.variant: SECURITY FOR DEBT – VICTIM IS AN ELDERLY PERSON OR DISABLED ADULT
ORC:2913.21.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud, obtain control over a credit card, to wit: (DESCRIBE CARD AND COMPANY) from (an elderly person or disabled adult), to wit: (NAME OF PERSON AND AGE OR DISABILITY) as security for debt in the amount of (STATE AMOUNT), to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES OF HOW CARD WAS OBTAINED), without the consent of the (elderly person or disabled adult or person authorized to give consent), to wit: (NAME OF PERSON), in violation of Section 2913.21(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.21.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $37,500.00, a felony of the third degree. – VALUE $37,500.00 OR MORE, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2913.21.heading: MISUSE OF CREDIT CARDS 2913.21(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2913.21.variant: OBTAIN PROPERTY/SERVICES WITH EXPIRED OR ILLEGAL CARD
ORC:2913.21.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud, obtain (property or services), to wit: (DESCRIBE ITEM OR ITEMS), being valued at (STATE AMOUNT) by the use of a credit (card or cards), to wit: (DESCRIBE CARD OR CARDS AND COMPANY OR COMPANIES INCLUDING ACCOUNT NUMBERS), in (one transaction or several transactions conducted within 90 days of each other), to wit: (STATE DATES), (knowing or having reasonable cause to believe) that the said (card or cards) had been (expired or revoked or obtained in violation of the law or retained in violation of the law or used in violation of the law), in violation of Section 2913.21(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code.
ORC:2913.21.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. (CCC 2313.21(B)(2)). – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.21.heading: MISUSE OF CREDIT CARDS 2913.21(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2913.21.variant: OBTAIN PROPERTY/SERVICES WITH EXPIRED OR ILLEGAL CARD – VICTIM IS AN ELDERLY PERSON OR DISABLED ADULT
ORC:2913.21.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud (an elderly person or a disabled adult), to wit: (NAME OF PERSON AND AGE OR DISABILITY), obtain (property or services), to wit: (DESCRIBE ITEM OR ITEMS), being valued at (STATE AMOUNT) by the use of a credit (card or cards) to wit: (DESCRIBE CARD OR CARDS AND COMPANY OR COMPANIES, INCLUDING ACCOUNT NUMBERS), in (one transaction or several transactions conducted within 90 days of each other), to wit: (STATE DATES), (knowing or having reasonable cause to believe) that the said (card or cards) had been (expired or revoked or obtained in violation of the law or retained in violation of the law), in violation of Section 2913.21(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.21.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $37,500.00, a felony of the third degree. – VALUE $37,500.00 OR MORE, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2913.21.heading: MISUSE OF CREDIT CARDS 2913.21(B)(3) ORC
ORC:2913.21.variant: FURNISH PROPERTY/SERVICES FOR CARD USED IN VIOLATION OF LAW
ORC:2913.21.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud, furnish (property or services), to wit: (DESCRIBE ITEM OR ITEMS), being valued at (STATE AMOUNT) by the use of a credit (card or cards), to wit: (DESCRIBE CARD OR CARDS AND COMPANY OR COMPANIES INCLUDING ACCOUNT NUMBERS), in (one transaction or several transactions conducted within 90 days of each other), to wit: (STATE DATES), knowing that the said (card or cards) had been used in violation of the law, in violation of Section 2913.21(B)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code.
ORC:2913.21.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. (CCC 2313.21(B)(3)). – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.21.heading: MISUSE OF CREDIT CARDS 2913.21(B)(4) ORC
ORC:2913.21.variant: FALSELY REPRESENT – PROPERTY/SERVICES FURNISHED TO CARD ISSUER
ORC:2913.21.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud, (represent or cause to be represented) to the issuer of a credit card, to wit: (DESCRIBE CARD AND COMPANY), that (property or services), to wit: (DESCRIBE ITEM OR ITEMS), being valued at (STATE AMOUNT) had been furnished in (one transaction or several transactions conducted within 90 days of each other), to wit: (STATE DATES), knowing that such (representation or representations) (was or were) false, in violation of Section 2913.21(B)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code
ORC:2913.21.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. (CCC 2313.21(B)(4)). – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.21.heading: MISUSE OF CREDIT CARDS 2913.21(C) ORC (CCC 2313.21(C))
ORC:2913.21.variant: POSSESS CARD TO VIOLATE SECTION – M1
ORC:2913.21.text: _____________ did (receive or possess or control or dispose of) a credit card, to wit: (DESCRIBE CARD AND COMPANY), with purpose to violate Section 2913.21 of the Ohio Revised Code in the following manner, to wit: (STATE SPECIFIC VIOLATION OF 2913.21 AND THE LANGUAGE OF THE PARTICULAR SECTION APPLICABLE), in violation of Section 2913.21(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2913.21.notes: DEFINITIONS 2913.30(B) ACCESS DEVICE – Means any debit or credit card representing a monetary security or retail amount by any financial institution, including a bank, savings bank, savings and loan association, credit union, or business entity. OBLIGATION OR OTHER SECURITY – Means an instrument recognized as currency or legal tender or that is issued by the United States treasury, including bills, coins, bonds, or checks.

ORC:2913.30.heading: COUNTERFEITING 2913.30(B)(1)
ORC:2913.30.variant: FALSELY MAKE AN OBLIGATION OR SECURITY – F4
ORC:2913.30.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud or knowing that the person was facilitating a fraud, (falsely make, forge, counterfeit or alter) any (obligation or other security) of the United States, by means of (DESCRIBE TYPE OF SECURITY AND HOW IT WAS FORGED OR ALTERED), in violation of Section 2913.30(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.30.heading: COUNTERFEITING 2913.30(B)(2)
ORC:2913.30.variant: PASS, UTTER, SELL ANY COUNTERFEIT OBLIGATION OR SECURITY – F4
ORC:2913.30.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud or knowing that the person was facilitating a fraud, (pass, utter, sell, purchase, conceal, or transfer) any counterfeit (obligation or other security) of the United States, by means of (DESCRIBE TYPE OF SECURITY AND HOW IT WAS UTTERED/PASSED/ TRANSFERRED etc.), in violation of Section 2913.30(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.30.heading: COUNTERFEITING 2913.30(B)(3)
ORC:2913.30.variant: POSSESS WITH PURPOSE TO UTTER A COUNTERFEIT SECURITY – F4
ORC:2913.30.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud or knowing that the person was facilitating a fraud, (possess with purpose to utter) any (obligation or other security) of the United States, knowing that the (obligation or other security) has been counterfeited, by means of (DESCRIBE TYPE OF SECURITY, HOW POSSESSED AND KNOWLEDGE OF COUNTERFEIT), in violation of Section 2913.30(B)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.30.heading: COUNTERFEITING 2913.30(B)(4)
ORC:2913.30.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud or knowing that the person was facilitating a fraud, (falsely make, forge, counterfeit, alter, or knowingly possess) any access device, to wit: (DESCRIBE TYPE OF ACCESS DEVICE AND HOW IT WAS ALTERED/POSSESSED, ETC.), without authorization of the issuer, in violation of Section 2913.30(B)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.30.heading: COUNTERFEITING 2913.30(B)(5)
ORC:2913.30.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud or knowing that the person was facilitating a fraud, (directly or indirectly) use a scanning device to (read, obtain, memorize, or store) (temporarily or permanently) information encoded on an access device, to wit: (DESCRIBE TYPE OF SCANNING DEVICE), without the permission of the (authorized user, financial institution, or merchant), in violation of Section 2913.30(B)(5) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.30.heading: COUNTERFEITING 2913.30(B)(6)
ORC:2913.30.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud or knowing that the person was facilitating a fraud, (directly or indirectly) use an encoding device to place information encoded on an access device onto a different device, to wit: (DESCRIBE TYPE OF ENCODING DEVICE), without the permission of the (authorized user, financial institution, or merchant), in violation of Section 2913.30(B)(6) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.31.heading: FORGERY 2913.31(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.31.text: _____________ did, (with purpose to defraud or knowing he was facilitating a fraud) forge a writing, to wit: (STATE AND DESCRIBE TYPE OF WRITING), of another, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM) without (his or her) authority, in violation of Section 2913.31(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.31.heading: EXAMPLE FOR SALES CHECK:
ORC:2913.31.text: _____________ did, knowing he was facilitating a fraud, forge a writing, to wit: A MACY’S SALES CHECK, number _______, signed in the name of another, to wit: John Doe, without his authority, in violation of Section 2913.31(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.31.heading: EXAMPLE FOR A CHECK:
ORC:2913.31.text: _____________ did, knowing he was facilitating a fraud, forge a writing, to wit: a check to the order of $_______, drawn upon the NATIONAL CITY BANK, and signed in the name of another, to wit: John Doe, without his authority, in violation of Section 2913.31(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.31.heading: FORGERY 2913.31(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.31.variant: WITHOUT CONSENT – VICTIM IS AN ELDERLY PERSON OR DISABLED ADULT – F5
ORC:2913.31.text: _____________ did, (with purpose to defraud or knowing he was facilitating a fraud) forge a writing, to wit: (STATE AND DESCRIBE TYPE OF WRITING), of another, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM) without (his or her) authority, in violation of Section 2913.31(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.31.heading: FORGERY 2913.31(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.31.text: _____________ did, (with purpose to defraud or knowing he was facilitating a fraud) forge a writing, to wit: (STATE AND DESCRIBE TYPE OF WRITING), of another, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM) without (his or her) authority, which resulted in the loss of (property or services), to wit: (DESCRIBE LOSS), to said victim, in violation of Section 2913.31(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code.
ORC:2913.31.notes: – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $37,500.00, a felony of the third degree. – VALUE $37,500.00 OR MORE, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2913.31.heading: FORGERY 2913.31(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2913.31.text: _____________ did, (with purpose to defraud or knowing he was facilitating a fraud) forge a writing, to wit: (STATE TYPE OF WRITING) so that the said writing purported (to be genuine when it was in fact spurious or to be the act of another, to wit: (NAME OF PERSON) who did not authorize the act or to have been executed at a time different from what was in fact the case, or to have been executed at a place different from what was in fact the case or to have been executed with terms different from what was in fact the case or to be a copy of an original when no such original existed), to wit: (STATE DETAILS), in violation of Section 2913.31(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.31.heading: EXAMPLE FOR A CHECK:
ORC:2913.31.text: _____________ did, knowing he was facilitating a fraud, forge a writing, to wit: a check to the order of John Jones, drawn on the OHIO NATIONAL BANK and signed in the name of John Doe, so that the said check purported to be genuine when it was in fact spurious, to wit: the check was not actually signed by John Doe or with his authority, in violation of Section 2913.31(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.31.heading: FORGERY 2913.31(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2913.31.text: _____________ did, (with purpose to defraud or knowing he was facilitating a fraud) forge a writing, to wit: (STATE TYPE OF WRITING) so that the said writing purported (to be genuine when it was in fact spurious or to be the act of another, to wit: (NAME OF PERSON) who did not authorize the act or to have been executed at a time different from what was in fact the case, or to have been executed at a place different from what was in fact the case or to have been executed with terms different from what was in fact the case or to be a copy of an original when no such original existed), to wit: (STATE DETAILS), which did result in the loss of (services or property), to wit: (DESCRIBE LOSS), to said victim, in violation of Section 2913.31(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code.
ORC:2913.31.notes: – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.31.heading: FORGERY 2913.31(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2913.31.variant: SPURIOUS WRITING – VICTIM IS AN ELDERLY PERSON OR DISABLED ADULT
ORC:2913.31.text: _____________ did, (with purpose to defraud or knowing (he or she) was facilitating a fraud) (an elderly person or a disabled adult), to wit: (NAME OF PERSON AND AGE OR DISABILITY) without (his or her) authority, forge a writing, to wit: (STATE TYPE OF WRITING) so that the said writing purported (to be genuine when it was in fact spurious or to be the act of another, to wit: (NAME OF PERSON) who did not authorize the act or to have been executed at a time different from what was in fact the case, or to have been executed at a place different from what was in fact the case or to have been executed with terms different from what was in fact the case or to be a copy of an original when no such original existed), to wit: (STATE DETAILS), in violation of Section 2913.31(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree or if the (elderly person or disabled adult) suffers a loss, to wit: (STATE AMOUNT) the charge is as follows:
ORC:2913.31.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $37,500.00, a felony of the third degree. – VALUE $37,500.00 OR MORE, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2913.31.heading: FORGERY 2913.31(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2913.31.variant: UTTER/POSSESS TO UTTER A FORGED WRITING – F5
ORC:2913.31.text: _____________ did, (with purpose to defraud or knowing that he was facilitating a fraud) (utter or possess with the purpose to utter) a writing, to wit: (DESCRIBE TYPE OF WRITING) which he knows to have been forged, to wit: (DESCRIBE FORGERY), in violation of Section 2913.31(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.31.heading: FORGERY 2913.31(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2913.31.variant: UTTER/POSSESS TO UTTER A FORGED WRITING
ORC:2913.31.text: _____________ did, (with purpose to defraud or knowing that he was facilitating a fraud) (utter or possess with the purpose to utter) a writing, to wit: (DESCRIBE TYPE OF WRITING) which he knows to have been forged, to wit: (DESCRIBE FORGERY), which did result in the loss of (services or property), to wit: (DESCRIBE LOSS), to said victim, in violation of Section 2913.31(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code.
ORC:2913.31.notes: – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.31.heading: FORGERY 2913.31(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2913.31.variant: UTTER/POSSESS TO UTTER A FORGED WRITING – VICTIM IS AN ELDERLY PERSON OR DISABLED ADULT
ORC:2913.31.text: _____________ did, (with purpose to defraud or knowing that (he or she) was facilitating a fraud) (an elderly person or a disabled adult), to wit: (NAME OF PERSON AND AGE OR DISABILITY) without (his or her) authority, (utter or possess with the purpose to utter) a writing, to wit: (DESCRIBE TYPE OF WRITING) which (he or she) knows to have been forged, to wit: (DESCRIBE FORGERY), in violation of Section 2913.31(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree or if the (elderly person or disabled adult) suffers a loss, to wit: (STATE AMOUNT) the charge is as follows:
ORC:2913.31.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $37,500.00, a felony of the third degree. – VALUE $37,500.00 OR MORE, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2913.31.heading: FORGERY/IDENTIFICATION CARD 2913.31(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.31.text: _____________ did knowingly forge an identification card, to wit: (STATE AND DESCRIBE TYPE OF WRITING), of another, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM) without (his or her) authority, in violation of Section 2913.31(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2913.31.notes: NOTE: Identification card means: a card that includes personal information or characteristics of an individual, a purpose of which is to establish he identity of the bearer described on the card, whether the words “identity,” “identification,” “identification card,” or other similar words appear on the card.

ORC:2913.31.heading: FORGERY/IDENTIFICATION CARD 2913.31(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2913.31.text: _____________ did knowingly (sell or distribute) a card that purports to be an identification card, knowing it to have been forged, to wit: (STATE AND DESCRIBE TYPE OF IDENTIFICATION CARD), in violation of Section 2913.31(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2913.31.notes: NOTE: Identification card means: a card that includes personal information or characteristics of an individual, a purpose of which is to establish he identity of the bearer described on the card, whether the words “identity,” “identification,” “identification card,” or other similar words appear on the card.

ORC:2913.32.heading: CRIMINAL SIMULATION 2913.32(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.32.text: _____________ did, (with purpose to defraud or knowing he was facilitating a fraud) (make or alter) an object, to wit: (DESCRIBE OBJECT) so that the said object appeared to have a value because of (antiquity or rarity or curiosity or source or authorship) when in fact the said object did not possess such value, to wit: (DESCRIBE DECEPTION), in violation of Section 2913.32(A) (1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2913.32.heading: CRIMINAL SIMULATION 2913.32(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.32.text: _____________ did, (with purpose to defraud or knowing he was facilitating a fraud) (make or alter) an object, to wit: (DESCRIBE OBJECT) so that the said object appeared to have a value because of (antiquity or rarity or curiosity or source or authorship) when in fact the said object did not possess such value, to wit: (DESCRIBE DECEPTION), which did result in a loss to the victim, to wit: (DESCRIBE LOSS), in violation of Section 2913.32(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code.
ORC:2913.32.notes: – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

DEFINITIONS 2913.40(A) The following terms are defined for purposes of Section 2913.40: STATEMENT OR REPRESENTATION – any oral, written, electronic, electronic impulse, or magnetic communication that is used to identify an item of goods or a service for which reimbursement may be made under the medicaid program or that states income and expense and is or may be used to determine a rate of reimbursement under the medicaid program. PROVIDER – any person who has signed a provider agreement with the department of medicaid to provide goods or services pursuant to the medicaid program or any person who has signed an agreement with a party to such a provider agreement under which the person agrees to provide goods or services that are reimbursable under the medicaid program. PROVIDER AGREEMENT – an agreement which is between a medicaid provider and the department of medicaid and provides for the medicaid provider to provide medicaid services to medicaid recipients and complies with 42 C.F.R. 431.107(b). RECIPIENT – any individual who receives goods or services from a provider under the medicaid program. RECORDS – any medical, professional, financial, or business records relating to the treatment or care of any recipient, to goods or services provided to any recipient, or to rates paid for goods or services provided to any recipient and any records that are required by the rules of the medicaid director to be kept for the medicaid program.

ORC:2913.40.heading: MEDICAID FRAUD 2913.40(B) ORC
ORC:2913.40.variant: FALSE STATEMENT FOR THE REIMBURSEMENT – VALUE OF SERVICES

ORC:2913.40.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.40.text: _____________ did, (with purpose to commit fraud or knowing he was facilitating a fraud), (charge or solicit or accept or receive) (property or money or consideration), valued at (STATE AMOUNT), to wit: (DESCRIBE CHARGE OR ACCEPTANCE AND CONSIDERATION INVOLVED) which was for (goods or services) provided under the medicaid program, to wit: (DESCRIBE), and which was contrary to the terms of such agreement and in addition to the amount of reimbursement under the medicaid program and provider agreement including goods and services and any cost-sharing expenses authorized by Revised Code 5162.20 or rules adopted by the medicaid director regarding the medicaid program, in violation of Section 2913.40(C)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2913.401.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to failure to disclose a transfer of property that occurred during the period beginning sixty months before submission of the application or document and ending on the date the application or document was submitted and that was made to an irrevocable trust a portion of which is not distributable to the applicant for or the recipient of medicaid or to a revocable trust. CCC:2313.41.heading: DEFRAUDING A LIVERY OR HOSTELRY 2313.41(A)(2) CCC
CCC:2313.41.variant: USING DECEPTION TO INDUCE A HOSTELRY – M1
CCC:2313.41.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud or knowing that he or she was facilitating a fraud, engage in accommodations at a (hotel or motel or inn or campground or hostelry), to wit: (NAME OF ESTABLISHMENT AND ADDRESS), by means of, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES OF DEFRAUDING), in violation of Section 2313.41(A)(2) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2913.42.heading: TAMPERING WITH RECORDS 2913.42(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.42.text: _____________ did, knowing he was without privilege to do so, and (with purpose to defraud or knowing he was facilitating a fraud), (falsify, destroy, remove, conceal, alter, deface or mutilate) any (writing, computer software, data, or record), to wit: (DESCRIBE WRITING OR COMPUTER SOFTWARE OR DATA OR COMPUTER DATA RECORD AND WHAT WAS DONE), in violation of Section 2913.42(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2913.42.heading: TAMPERING WITH RECORDS 2913.42(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.42.variant: DESTROY OR CONCEAL A WILL – F5
ORC:2913.42.text: _____________ did, knowing he was without privilege to do so, and (with purpose to defraud or knowing he was facilitating a fraud), (falsify, destroy, remove, conceal, alter, deface or mutilate) an unrevoked will, to wit: (DESCRIBE WILL AND WHAT WAS DONE WITH IT), in violation of Section 2913.42(A) (1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.42.heading: TAMPERING WITH RECORDS 2913.42(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.42.variant: DESTROY OR CONCEAL DATA OR COMPUTER SOFTWARE – VALUE INVOLVED IN OFFENSE
ORC:2913.42.text: _____________ did, knowing he was without privilege to do so, and (with purpose to defraud or knowing he was facilitating a fraud), (falsify, destroy, remove, conceal, alter, deface or mutilate) (computer software or data), to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER SOFTWARE OR DATA AND WHAT WAS DONE), and the victim of the offense incurred a loss (NAME OF VICTIM) to wit: (STATE VALUE OF THE DATA OR COMPUTER SOFTWARE LOSS) involved in the offense in violation of Section 2913.42(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.42.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.42.heading: TAMPERING WITH RECORDS 2913.42(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.42.variant: DESTROY OR CONCEAL RECORDS – PURPOSE DEVISING A SCHEME – F3
ORC:2913.42.text: _____________ did, knowing he was without privilege to do so and the offense was committed for the purpose of (devising or executing) a scheme to defraud, and (with purpose to defraud or knowing he was facilitating a fraud), (falsify, destroy, remove, conceal, alter, deface or mutilate) any (computer software or data), to wit: (DESCRIBE WRITING OR COMPUTER SOFTWARE OR DATA OR COMPUTER DATA RECORD AND WHAT WAS DONE), in violation of Section 2913.42(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.42.heading: TAMPERING WITH RECORDS 2913.42(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.42.variant: DESTROY OR CONCEAL RECORDS – TO OBTAIN PROPERTY OR SERVICES WITH VALUED LOSS TO VICTIM – F3
ORC:2913.42.text: _____________ did, knowing he was without privilege to do so and (with purpose to defraud or knowing he was facilitating a fraud), (falsify, destroy, remove, conceal, alter, deface or mutilate) any (writing or record), to wit: (DESCRIBE WRITING OR COMPUTER SOFTWARE OR DATA OR COMPUTER DATA RECORD AND WHAT WAS DONE), and the offense was committed in order to obtain property or services and the value of the (property, services, or the loss) to the victim is $7,500.00 or more, to wit: (STATE AMOUNT) in violation of Section 2913.42(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.42.heading: TAMPERING WITH RECORDS 2913.42(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.42.variant: DESTROY OR CONCEAL A GOVERNMENT RECORD – F3
ORC:2913.42.text: _____________ did, knowing he was without privilege to do so, and (with purpose to defraud or knowing he was facilitating a fraud), (falsify, destroy, remove, conceal, alter, deface or mutilate) any (writing, data, computer software, or record) kept by or belonging to a (local, state, or federal government entity) to wit: (DESCRIBE WRITING, DATA, COMPUTER SOFTWARE, OR RECORD AND WHAT WAS DONE WITH IT), in violation of Section 2913.42(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.42.heading: TAMPERING WITH RECORDS 2913.42(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2913.42.text: _____________ did, knowing he was without privilege to do so, and (with purpose to defraud or knowing he was facilitating a fraud), utter a (writing, data, computer software, or record), to wit: (DESCRIBE WRITING OR RECORD), knowing such to have been tampered with by being (falsified, removed, concealed, altered, defaced or mutilated), to wit: (DESCRIBE WHAT WAS DONE), in violation of Section 2913.42(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2913.42.heading: TAMPERING WITH RECORDS 2913.42(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2913.42.text: _____________ did, knowing he was without privilege to do so, and (with purpose to defraud or knowing he was facilitating a fraud), utter an unrevoked will, to wit: (DESCRIBE WILL), knowing such to have been tampered with by being (falsified, destroyed, removed, concealed, altered, defaced or mutilated), to wit: (DESCRIBE WHAT WAS DONE) in violation of Section 2913.42(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.42.heading: TAMPERING WITH RECORDS 2913.42(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2913.42.text: _____________ did, knowing he was without privilege to do so and (with purpose to defraud or knowing he was facilitating a fraud) utter any (writing or record kept by or belonging to a (local, state or federal) government agency, to wit: (DESCRIBE WRITING OR RECORD AND GOVERNMENTAL AGENCY), knowing such to have been tampered with by being falsified, destroyed, removed, concealed, altered, defaced or mutilated), to wit: (DESCRIBE WHAT WAS DONE), in violation of Section 2913.42(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.421.heading: ILLEGALLY TRANSMITTING MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAIL MESSAGES 2913.421(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.421.variant: RELAY OR RETRANSMIT MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAILS WITH INTENT TO DECEIVE OR MISLEAD – F5
ORC:2913.421.text: _____________ did knowingly use a computer to (relay or retransmit) multiple commercial email messages (to or from) a computer in Ohio, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), with the intent to deceive or mislead (recipients or an email service provider) as to the origin of those messages, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2913.421(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.421.heading: ILLEGALLY TRANSMITTING MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAIL MESSAGES 2913.421(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.421.variant: RELAY OR RETRANSMIT MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAILS WITH INTENT TO DECEIVE OR MISLEAD – USE OF AUTOMATED MEANS THAT GENERATES EMAIL ADDRESSES – F4
ORC:2913.421.text: _____________ did knowingly use a computer to (relay or retransmit) multiple commercial email messages (to or from) a computer in Ohio, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), with the intent to deceive or mislead (recipients or an email service provider) as to the origin of those messages, and said offender knowingly assisted in the violation through the (provision or selection) of email addresses obtained using an automated means that generates possible electronic mail addresses by combining names, letters, or numbers into numerous permutations, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2913.421(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.421.heading: ILLEGALLY TRANSMITTING MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAIL MESSAGES 2913.421(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.421.variant: RELAY OR RETRANSMIT MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAILS WITH INTENT TO DECEIVE OR MISLEAD – USE OF WEBSITE OR SERVICE WITH NOTICE THAT OPERATOR WILL NOT TRANSFER EMAIL ADDRESS – F4
ORC:2913.421.text: _____________ did knowingly use a computer to (relay or retransmit) multiple commercial email messages (to or from) a computer in Ohio, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), with the intent to deceive or mislead (recipients or an email service provider) as to the origin of those messages, and said offender knowingly assisted in the violation through the (provision or selection) of email addresses obtained using an automated means from an (internet web site or proprietary online service) operated by another person, to wit: (NAME), that included, at the time the email addresses were obtained, a notice stating that said operator will not transfer addresses maintained by that (web site or online service) to any other party for the purposes of initiating the transmission of, or enabling others to initiate the transmission of, email messages, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2913.421(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.421.heading: ILLEGALLY TRANSMITTING MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAIL MESSAGES 2913.421(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.421.variant: RELAY OR RETRANSMIT MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAILS WITH INTENT TO DECEIVE OR MISLEAD – OFFENDER COMMITTED VIOLATION WITH THREE OR MORE PERSONS – F4
ORC:2913.421.text: _____________ did, with 3 or more persons with respect to whom the offender was the organizer or leader, knowingly use a computer to (relay or retransmit) multiple commercial email messages (to or from) a computer in Ohio, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), with the intent to deceive or mislead (recipients or an email service provider) as to the origin of those messages, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION INCLUDING OTHER PERSONS), in violation of Section 2913.421(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code ,a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.421.heading: ILLEGALLY TRANSMITTING MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAIL MESSAGES 2913.421(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.421.variant: RELAY OR RETRANSMIT MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAILS WITH INTENT TO DECEIVE OR MISLEAD – AT LEAST $1,000.00 LOSS TO VICTIMS OR $1,000.00 OF PROPERTY OR SERVICE OBTAINED DURING ONE YEAR – F4
ORC:2913.421.text: _____________ did knowingly use a computer to (relay or retransmit) multiple commercial email messages (to or from) a computer in Ohio, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), with the intent to deceive or mislead (recipients or an email service provider) as to the origin of those messages, and (causing an aggregate loss of at least $1,000.00 to (a victim or victims), to wit: (NAME VICTIM(S)) OR said offender obtaining at least $1,000.00 of property or services as a result of this violation) within a one year period, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION INCLUDING AMOUNT AND TIME PERIOD), in violation of Section 2913.421(B) (1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.421.heading: ILLEGALLY TRANSMITTING MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAIL MESSAGES 2913.421(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.421.variant: RELAY OR RETRANSMIT MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAILS WITH INTENT TO DECEIVE OR MISLEAD – 250 EMAILS IN 24 HOURS, 2,500 EMAILS WITHIN 30 DAYS OR 25,000 EMAILS WITHIN 1 YEAR – F4
ORC:2913.421.text: _____________ did knowingly use a computer to (relay or retransmit) at least (250 commercial email messages within 24 hours or 2,500 commercial email messages within 30 days or 25,000 commercial email messages within 1 year) (to or from) a computer in Ohio, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), with the intent to deceive or mislead (recipients or an email service provider) as to the origin of those messages, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION INCLUDING NUMBER OF EMAILS AND TIME PERIOD), in violation of Section 2913.421(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.421.heading: ILLEGALLY TRANSMITTING MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAIL MESSAGES 2913.421(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.421.variant: RELAY OR RETRANSMIT MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAILS WITH INTENT TO DECEIVE OR MISLEAD – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F3
ORC:2913.421.text: _____________ did knowingly use a computer to (relay or retransmit) multiple commercial email messages (to or from) a computer in Ohio, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), with the intent to deceive or mislead (recipients or an email service provider) as to the origin of those messages, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), and having been previously convicted of violating this section on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT) (CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2913.421(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.421.heading: ILLEGALLY TRANSMITTING MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAIL MESSAGES 2913.421(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2913.421.variant: FALSIFY HEADER INFORMATION IN MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAILS – F5
ORC:2913.421.text: _____________ did knowingly and materially falsify header information in multiple commercial email messages sent (to or from) a computer in Ohio, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), and purposely initiate the transmission of those messages, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2913.421(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.421.heading: ILLEGALLY TRANSMITTING MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAIL MESSAGES 2913.421(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2913.421.variant: FALSIFY HEADER INFORMATION IN MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAILS – USE OF AUTOMATED MEANS THAT GENERATES EMAIL ADDRESSES – F4

ORC:2913.421.heading: ILLEGALLY TRANSMITTING MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAIL MESSAGES 2913.421(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2913.421.variant: FALSIFY HEADER INFORMATION IN MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAILS – OFFENDER COMMITTED VIOLATION WITH THREE OR MORE PERSONS – F4
ORC:2913.421.text: _____________ did, with three or more persons with respect to whom the offender was the organizer or leader, knowingly and materially falsify header information in multiple commercial email messages sent (to or from) a computer in Ohio, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), and purposely initiate the transmission of those messages, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION INCLUDING OTHER PERSONS), in violation of Section 2913.421(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.421.variant: FALSIFY HEADER INFORMATION IN MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAILS – AT LEAST $1,000.00 LOSS TO VICTIMS OR $1,000.00 OF PROPERTY OR SERVICE OBTAINED DURING ONE YEAR – F4

ORC:2913.421.heading: ILLEGALLY TRANSMITTING MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAIL MESSAGES 2913.421(B)(2) ORC

ORC:2913.421.text: _____________ did knowingly and materially falsify header information in at least (250 commercial email messages within 24 hours or 2,500 commercial email messages within 30 days or 25,000 commercial email messages within one year) sent (to or from) a computer in Ohio, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), and purposely initiate the transmission of those messages, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION INCLUDING NUMBER OF EMAILS AND TIME PERIOD), in violation of Section 2913.421(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.421.text: _____________ did knowingly and materially falsify header information in multiple commercial email messages sent (to or from) a computer in Ohio, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), and purposely initiate the transmission of those messages, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), and having been previously convicted of violating this section on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT) (CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2913.421(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.421.heading: ILLEGALLY TRANSMITTING MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAIL MESSAGES 2913.421(B)(3) ORC
ORC:2913.421.variant: FALSE REGISTRATION OF FIVE OR MORE EMAIL ACCOUNTS OR ONLINE USER ACCOUNTS OR TWO OR MORE DOMAIN NAMES – F5
ORC:2913.421.text: _____________ did knowingly register, using information that materially falsifies the identity of the actual registrant, for (five or more (email accounts or online user accounts) or two or more domain names) and purposely initiate the transmission of multiple commercial email messages (to or from) a computer in Ohio, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), from (one or any combination) of those (accounts or domain names), to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2913.421(B)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2913.421.variant: FALSE REGISTRATION OF FIVE OR MORE EMAIL ACCOUNTS OR ONLINE USER ACCOUNTS OR TWO OR MORE DOMAIN NAMES – USE OF AUTOMATED MEANS THAT GENERATES EMAIL ADDRESSES – F4
