ORC:2913.421.heading: ILLEGALLY TRANSMITTING MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAIL MESSAGES 2913.421(B)(4) ORC
ORC:2913.421.variant: FALSELY REPRESENT THE RIGHT TO USE FIVE OR MORE IP ADDRESSES – USE OF AUTOMATED MEANS THAT GENERATES EMAIL ADDRESSES – F4
ORC:2913.421.text: _____________ did knowingly falsely represent the right to use five or more internet protocol addresses, and purposely initiate the transmission of multiple commercial email messages (to or from) a computer in Ohio, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), from those addresses, and said offender knowingly assisted in the violation through the (provision or selection) of email addresses obtained using an automated means that generates possible electronic mail addresses by combining names, letters, or numbers into numerous permutations, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2913.421(B)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.421.heading: ILLEGALLY TRANSMITTING MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAIL MESSAGES 2913.421(B)(4) ORC
ORC:2913.421.variant: FALSELY REPRESENT THE RIGHT TO USE FIVE OR MORE IP ADDRESSES – USE OF WEBSITE OR SERVICE WITH NOTICE THAT OPERATOR WILL NOT TRANSFER EMAIL ADDRESS – F4
ORC:2913.421.text: _____________ did knowingly falsely represent the right to use five or more internet protocol addresses, and purposely initiate the transmission of multiple commercial email messages (to or from) a computer in Ohio, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), from those addresses, and said offender knowingly assisted in the violation through the (provision or selection) of email addresses obtained using an automated means from an (internet web site or proprietary online service) operated by another person, to wit: (NAME), that included, at the time the email addresses were obtained, a notice stating that said operator will not transfer addresses maintained by that (web site or online service) to any other party for the purposes of initiating the transmission of, or enabling others to initiate the transmission of, email messages, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2913.421(B)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.421.heading: ILLEGALLY TRANSMITTING MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAIL MESSAGES 2913.421(B)(4) ORC
ORC:2913.421.variant: FALSELY REPRESENT THE RIGHT TO USE 5 OR MORE IP ADDRESSES – OFFENDER COMMITTED VIOLATION WITH 3 OR MORE PERSONS – F4
ORC:2913.421.text: _____________ did, with three or more persons with respect to whom the offender was the organizer or leader, knowingly falsely represent the right to use five or more internet protocol addresses, and purposely initiate the transmission of multiple commercial email messages (to or from) a computer in Ohio, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), from those addresses, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION INCLUDING OTHER PERSONS), in violation of Section 2913.421(B)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.421.heading: ILLEGALLY TRANSMITTING MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAIL MESSAGES 2913.421(B)(4) ORC
ORC:2913.421.variant: FALSELY REPRESENT THE RIGHT TO USE FIVE OR MORE IP ADDRESSES – AT LEAST $1,000.00 LOSS TO VICTIMS OR $1,000.00 OF PROPERTY OR SERVICE OBTAINED DURING 1 YEAR – F4
ORC:2913.421.text: _____________ did knowingly falsely represent the right to use five or more internet protocol addresses, and purposely initiate the transmission of multiple commercial email messages (to or from) a computer in Ohio, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), from those addresses, and (causing an aggregate loss of at least $1,000.00 to (a victim or victims), to wit: (NAME VICTIM(S)) OR said offender obtaining at least $1,000.00 of property or services as a result of this violation) within a one year period, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION INCLUDING AMOUNT AND TIME PERIOD), in violation of Section 2913.421(B)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.421.heading: ILLEGALLY TRANSMITTING MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAIL MESSAGES 2913.421(B)(4) ORC
ORC:2913.421.variant: FALSELY REPRESENT THE RIGHT TO USE 5 OR MORE IP ADDRESSES – 250 EMAILS IN 24 HOURS, 2,500 EMAILS WITHIN 30 DAYS OR 25,000 EMAILS WITHIN 1 YEAR – F4
ORC:2913.421.text: _____________ did knowingly falsely represent the right to use five or more internet protocol addresses, and purposely initiate the transmission of at least (250 commercial email messages within 24 hours or 2,500 commercial email messages within 30 days or 25,000 commercial email messages within 1 year) (to or from) a computer in Ohio, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), from those addresses, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION INCLUDING NUMBER OF EMAILS AND TIME PERIOD), in violation of Section 2913.421(B)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.421.heading: ILLEGALLY TRANSMITTING MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAIL MESSAGES 2913.421(B)(4) ORC
ORC:2913.421.variant: FALSELY REPRESENT THE RIGHT TO USE 5 OR MORE IP ADDRESSES – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F3
ORC:2913.421.text: _____________ did knowingly falsely represent the right to use five or more internet protocol addresses, and purposely initiate the transmission of multiple commercial email messages (to or from) a computer in Ohio, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), from those addresses, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), and having been previously convicted of violating this section on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT) (CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2913.421(B)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.421.heading: UNAUTHORIZED ACCESS OF COMPUTER 2913.421(D)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.421.variant: UNAUTHORIZED ACCESS TO TRANSMIT MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAILS – F4
ORC:2913.421.text: _____________ did knowingly access a computer, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), without authorization and purposely initiate the transmission of multiple commercial email messages from or through said computer which were sent (to or from) a computer in Ohio, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2913.421(D)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2913.421.heading: UNAUTHORIZED ACCESS OF COMPUTER 2913.421(D)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.421.variant: UNAUTHORIZED ACCESS TO TRANSMIT MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL EMAILS – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F3
ORC:2913.421.text: _____________ did knowingly access a computer, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), without authorization and purposely initiate the transmission of multiple commercial email messages from or through said computer which were sent (to or from) a computer in Ohio, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMPUTER), to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), and having been previously convicted of violating this section on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT) (CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2913.421(D)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.43.heading: SECURING WRITINGS BY DECEPTION 2913.43 ORC
ORC:2913.43.text: _____________ did, by deception, (cause another, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM), to execute a writing, to wit: (DESCRIBE WRITING) (which disposed of property or which encumbered property or by which a pecuniary obligation was incurred), being valued at (STATE AMOUNT), to wit: (DESCRIBE PROPERTY OR PECUNIARY OBLIGATION AND DECEPTION), in violation of Section 2913.43 of the Ohio Revised Code.
ORC:2913.43.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.43.heading: SECURING WRITINGS BY DECEPTION 2913.43 ORC
ORC:2913.43.variant: VICTIM IS AN ELDERLY PERSON/DISABLED ADULT/ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBER/SPOUSE OF ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBER – SUFFERS A LOSS
ORC:2913.43.text: _____________ did, by deception, cause (an elderly person/disabled adult/ active duty service member/spouse of an active duty service member), to wit: (NAME OF PERSON AND AGE OR DISABILITY OR DESCRIBE CLASS TO WHICH PERSON BELONGS), to execute a writing, to wit: (DESCRIBE WRITING) (which disposed of property or which encumbered property or by which a pecuniary obligation was incurred), being valued at (STATE AMOUNT), to wit: (DESCRIBE PROPERTY OR PECUNIARY OBLIGATION AND DECEPTION), in violation of Section 2913.43 of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.43.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $37,500.00, a felony of the third degree. – VALUE $37,500.00 OR MORE, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2913.44.heading: PERSONATING AN OFFICER 2913.44(A) ORC (CCC 2313.44(A))
ORC:2913.44.text: _____________ did, (with purpose to defraud or knowing he was facilitating a fraud), personate (a law enforcement officer, or governmental inspector, or government investigator, or government agent), to wit: (DESCRIBE OFFICER OR AGENT PERSONATED AND GIVE DETAILS OF IMPERSONATION), in violation of Section 2913.44(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2913.44.notes: NOTE: Also see Section 2921.51 ORC, Impersonation of Officer.

ORC:2913.44.heading: PERSONATING AN OFFICER 2913.44(A) ORC (CCC 2313.44(A))
ORC:2913.44.variant: TO INDUCE ANOTHER TO PURCHASE PROPERTY OR SERVICES – M1
ORC:2913.44.text: _____________ did, with purpose to induce another, to wit: (NAME OF PERSON), to purchase (property or services), to wit: (DESCRIBE ITEM), personate (a law enforcement officer or a government inspector or a government investigator or a government agent), to wit: (DESCRIBE OFFICER OR AGENT PERSONATED AND GIVE DETAILS OF IMPERSONATION), in violation of Section 2913.44(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2913.441.heading: UNAUTHORIZED DISPLAY OF LAW ENFORCEMENT EMBLEM ON MOTOR VEHICLE 2913.441(A) ORC
ORC:2913.441.text: _____________ did, without being entitled to do, knowingly display the emblem of (a law enforcement agency or an organization of law enforcement officers), to wit: (DESCRIBE THE EMBLEM AND THE ORGANIZATION IT REPRESENTED), on a motor vehicle, to wit: (DESCRIBE VEHICLE), in violation of Section 2913.441(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor.

ORC:2913.45.heading: DEFRAUDING CREDITORS 2913.45(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.45.variant: DESTROY OR CONVEY PROPERTY – PROPERTY VALUE
ORC:2913.45.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud a creditor, to wit: (NAME OF CREDITOR), (remove or conceal or destroy or encumber or convey or deal with) said person’s property, to wit: (DESCRIBE PROPERTY AND WHAT WAS DONE), and the value of said property being (STATE VALUE), in violation of Section 2913.45(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.45.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. (CCC 2313.45(A)(1)) – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.45.heading: DEFRAUDING CREDITORS 2913.45(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2913.45.variant: MISREPRESENTATION TO APPOINTED FIDUCIARY – PROPERTY VALUE
ORC:2913.45.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud (his or her) creditor, to wit: (NAME OF CREDITOR), (misrepresent or refuse to disclose) to a fiduciary, to wit: (NAME OF FIDUCIARY) who was appointed to (administer or manage) the (affairs or estate) of the said (NAME OF DEFENDANT), the (existence or amount or location) of (property or information regarding property) belonging to the said (NAME OF DEFENDANT) and which (he or she) was legally required to furnish to the said fiduciary, and the value of said property being, to wit: (STATE VALUE), in violation of Section 2913.45(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.45.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. (CCC 2313.45(A)(2)) – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree. DEFINITIONS 2913.46 The following terms are defined for purposes of Section 2913.46 ORC: ELECTRONICALLY TRANSFERRED BENEFIT – The transfer of supplemental nutrition assistance program benefits or WIC program benefits through the use of an access device. WIC PROGRAM BENEFITS – Money, coupons, delivery verification receipts, other documents, food, or other property received directly or indirectly pursuant to section 17 of the “Child Nutrition Act of 1966,” as amended. ACCESS DEVICE – Any card, plate, code, account number, or other means of access that can be used, alone or in conjunction with another access device, to obtain payments, allotments, benefits, money, goods, or other things of value or that can be used to initiate a transfer of funds pursuant to section 5101.33 of the Revised Code and the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 or any supplemental food program administered by any department of this state or any county or local agency pursuant to section 17 of the “Child Nutrition Act of 1966,”. An “access device” may include any electronic debit card or other means authorized by section 5101.33 of the Revised Code. AGGREGATE VALUE OF SUPPLEMENTAL NUTRITION ASSISTANCE PROGRAM BENEFITS, WIC PROGRAM BENEFITS, AND ELECTRONICALLY TRANSFERRED BENEFITS INVOLVED IN THE VIOLATION – The total face value of any supplemental nutrition assistance program benefits, plus the total face value of WIC program coupons or delivery verification receipts, plus the total value of other WIC program benefits, plus the total value of any electronically transferred benefit or other access device, involved in the violation. TOTAL VALUE OF ANY ELECTRONICALLY TRANSFERRED BENEFIT OR OTHER ACCESS DEVICE – The total value of the payments, allotments, benefits, money, goods, or other things of value that may be obtained, or the total value of funds that may be transferred, by use of any electronically transferred benefit or other access device at the time of violation. NOTE: If supplemental nutrition assistance program benefits, WIC program benefits, or electronically transferred benefits or other access devices of various values are used, transferred, bought, acquired, altered, purchased, possessed, presented for redemption, or transported in violation of this section over a period of twelve months, the course of conduct may be charged as one offense and the values of supplemental nutrition assistance program benefits, WIC program benefits, or any electronically transferred benefits or other access devices may be aggregated in determining the degree of the offense.

ORC:2913.46.heading: ILLEGAL USE OF SUPPLEMENTAL NUTRITION OR WIC PROGRAM BENEFITS 2913.46(B) ORC
ORC:2913.46.text: _____________ did knowingly (possess or buy or sell or use or alter or accept or transfer) (supplemental nutrition assistance program benefits or WIC program benefits or any electronically transferred benefit) having a face value of (STATE AMOUNT) in a manner not authorized by the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 or section 17 of the Child Nutrition Act of 1966, as amended, to wit: (DESCRIBE WHAT WAS DONE WITH THE BENEFITS AND THE BENEFITS INVOLVED), in violation of Section 2913.46(B) of the Ohio Revised Code.
ORC:2913.46.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the third degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2913.46.heading: ILLEGAL USE OF SUPPLEMENTAL NUTRITION OR WIC PROGRAM BENEFITS 2913.46(C)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.46.variant: EMPLOYEE PERMITTED TO ILLEGALLY EXCHANGE ITEMS FOR SNAP/WIC BENEFITS
ORC:2913.46.text: _____________ did, being an organization, to wit: (DESCRIBE ORGANIZATION), knowingly allow an (employee or agent), to wit: (DESCRIBE EMPLOYEE), to (sell or transfer or trade) certain (items or services), to wit: (DESCRIBE WHAT WAS ALLOWED AND THE ITEMS RECEIVED) in exchange for supplemental nutrition assistance program benefits or WIC program benefits or electronically transferred benefit which had a face value of (STATE AMOUNT), and which purchase was prohibited by the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 or section 17 of the Child Nutrition Act of 1966, in violation of Section 2913.46(C)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code.
ORC:2913.46.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the third degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2913.46.heading: ILLEGAL USE OF SUPPLEMENTAL NUTRITION OR WIC PROGRAM BENEFITS 2913.46(C)(2) ORC
ORC:2913.46.variant: ALLOW EMPLOYEE TO SELL SNAP/WIC BENEFITS
ORC:2913.46.text: _____________ did, being an organization, to wit: (DESCRIBE ORGANIZATION), negligently allow an employee, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMPLOYEE), to (sell or transfer or exchange) (supplemental nutrition benefits or WIC benefits or any electronically transferred benefit) valued at (STATE AMOUNT) for something of value, to wit: (DESCRIBE ITEM), in violation of Section 2913.46(C)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code.
ORC:2913.46.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the third degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2913.47.heading: INSURANCE FRAUD 2913.47(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.47.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud or knowing that he or she was facilitating a fraud, present to, or cause to be presented to, an insurer, any written or oral statement that is part of, or in support of, (an application for insurance or a claim for payment pursuant to a policy or a claim for any other benefit pursuant to a policy), to wit: (DESCRIBE APPLICATION OR CLAIM), knowing that the statement or any part of the statement, was false or deceptive, to wit: (DESCRIBE FALSE OR DECEPTIVE STATEMENT), in violation of Section 2913.47(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.47.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.47.heading: INSURANCE FRAUD 2913.47(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2913.47.variant: AID OR ABET FALSE OR DECEPTIVE STATEMENT
ORC:2913.47.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud or knowing that he or she was facilitating a fraud, (assist or aid or abet or solicit or procure or conspire) with another to prepare or make any written or oral statement that was intended to be presented to an insurer as part of, or in support of an application for insurance, a claim for payment pursuant to a policy, or a claim for any other benefit pursuant to a policy, knowing that the statement, or any part of the statement, was false or deceptive, to wit: (DESCRIBE FALSE OR DECEPTIVE STATEMENT AND ALLEGE AMOUNT IN COMPLAINT LANGUAGE), in violation of Section 2913.47(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.47.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $ $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.48.heading: WORKERS’ COMPENSATION FRAUD 2913.48(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.48.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud or knowing that the person was facilitating a fraud, receive workers’ compensation benefits to which the person was not entitled, to wit: (STATE BENEFITS AND DESCRIBE FALSE STATEMENT RECEIVED), in violation of Section 2913.48(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.48.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.48.heading: WORKERS’ COMPENSATION FRAUD 2913.48(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2913.48.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud or knowing that the person was facilitating a fraud, make or present or cause to be made or presented a false or misleading statement with the purpose to secure payment for goods or services rendered under Chapter 4121, 4123, 4127, or 4131, of the Ohio Revised Code or to secure workers’ compensation benefits, to wit: (DESCRIBE PAYMENTS SECURED FOR BENEFITS OR GOODS OR SERVICES AND DESCRIBE FALSE STATEMENT), in violation of Section 2913.48(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.48.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.48.heading: WORKERS’ COMPENSATION FRAUD 2913.48(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2913.48.variant: ALTER, FALSIFY, DESTROY, CONCEAL, OR REMOVE RECORD OR DOCUMENT
ORC:2913.48.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud or knowing that the person was facilitating a fraud, (alter or falsify or destroy or conceal or remove) any record or document, to wit: (DESCRIBE DOCUMENT AND HOW IT WAS ALTERED, DESTROYED, CONCEALED, REMOVED, OR FALSIFIED) that was necessary to fully establish the validity of any claim filed with, or necessary to establish the nature and validity of all goods and services for which reimbursement or payment was received or was requested from, the bureau of workers’ compensation or a self-insuring employer under Chapter 4121, 4123, 4127 or 4131 of the Ohio Revised Code, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE AGENCY OR EMPLOYER WHERE THE CLAIM WAS FILED), in violation of Section 2913.48(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.48.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.48.heading: WORKERS’ COMPENSATION FRAUD 2913.48(A)(4) ORC
ORC:2913.48.variant: ALTER, FALSIFY, DESTROY, CONCEAL, OR REMOVE RECORD OR DOCUMENT
ORC:2913.48.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud or knowing that the person was facilitating a fraud, enter into (an agreement or conspiracy) to defraud the bureau or a self-insuring employer by making or presenting or causing to be made or presented a false claim for workers’ compensation benefits, to wit: (DESCRIBE FALSE CLAIM AND WITH WHICH AGENCY IT WAS FILED), in violation of Section 2913.48(A)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.48.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.48.heading: WORKERS’ COMPENSATION FRAUD 2913.48(A)(5) ORC
ORC:2913.48.variant: FALSE STATEMENT NECESSARY TO DETERMINE PREMIUM OR ASSESSMENT
ORC:2913.48.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud or knowing that the person was facilitating a fraud, (make or present or cause to be made or presented) a false statement concerning (manual codes, classification of employees, payroll, paid compensation, or number of personnel) when information of that nature is necessary to determine the actual workers’ compensation premium or assessment owed to the bureau by an employer, to wit: (DESCRIBE FALSE STATEMENT AND VALUE OF UNPAID PREMIUM OR ASSESSMENT), in violation of Section 2913.48(A)(5) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.48.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.48.heading: WORKERS’ COMPENSATION FRAUD 2913.48(A)(6) ORC
ORC:2913.48.variant: ALTER, FORGE OR CREATE FALSE BWC CERTIFICATE
ORC:2913.48.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud or knowing that the person was facilitating a fraud, (alter, forge, or create) a workers’ compensation certificate to falsely show current or correct workers’ compensation coverage, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION AND VALUE OF UNPAID PREMIUM OR ASSESSMENT), in violation of Section 2913.48(A)(6) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.48.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2913.48.heading: WORKERS’ COMPENSATION FRAUD 2913.48(A)(7) ORC
ORC:2913.48.variant: FAIL TO SECURE REQUIRED BWC COVERAGE
ORC:2913.48.text: _____________ did, with purpose to defraud or knowing that the person was facilitating a fraud, fail to (secure or maintain) workers’ compensation coverage as required by Revised Code Chapter 4123 with the intent to defraud the bureau of workers’ compensation, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION AND VALUE OF UNPAID PREMIUM OR ASSESSMENT), in violation of Section 2913.48(A)(7) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2913.48.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the third degree. DEFINITION 2913.49 The following term is defined for purposes of Section 2913.49: PERSONAL IDENTIFYING INFORMATION – Includes, but is not limited to, the following: the name, address, telephone number, driver’s license, driver’s license number, commercial driver’s license, commercial driver’s license number, state identification card, state identification card number, social security card, social security number, birth certificate, place of employment, employee identification number, mother’s maiden name, demand deposit account number, savings account number, money market account number, mutual fund account number, other financial account number, personal identification number, password, or credit card number of a living or dead individual. NOTE: It is not a defense to a charge under this section that the person whose personal identifying information was obtained, possessed, used, created, or permitted to be used was deceased at the time of the offense.

ORC:2913.49.heading: IDENTITY FRAUD 2913.49(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2913.49.variant: INTENT TO FRAUDULENTLY OBTAIN CREDIT, PROPERTY OR SERVICES
ORC:2913.49.text: _____________ did, without the express or implied consent of another person, to wit: (NAME OF PERSON), use, obtain, or possess any personal identifying information of said other person with the intent to hold (himself or herself) out to be said other person, to wit: (DESCRIBE OFFENSE), in violation of Section 2913.49(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code:

ORC:2915.02.notes: NOTE: Exemptions follow. EXEMPTIONS FOR SECTION 2915.02 ORC This section does not apply to any of the following: (1) Conduct in connection with gambling expressly permitted by law; (2) Games of chance, if all of the following apply: (a) The games of chance are not craps for money or roulette for money. (b) The games of chance are conducted by a charitable organization that is, and has received from the Internal Revenue Service a determination letter that is currently in effect, stating that the organization is exempt from federal income taxation under Section 501(a) and described in 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Service Code. (c) The games of chance are conducted at festivals of the charitable organization that are conducted not more than a total of five days a calendar year, and are conducted on premises owned by the charitable organization for a period of no less than one year immediately preceding the conducting of the games of chance, on premises leased from a governmental unit, or on premises that are leased from a veteran’s or fraternal organization and that have been owned by the lessor veteran’s or fraternal organization for a period of no less than one year immediately preceding the conducting of the games of chance. A charitable organization shall not lease premises from a veteran’s or fraternal organization to conduct a festival described above if the veteran’s or fraternal organization already has leased the premises four times during the preceding year to charitable organizations for that purpose. If a charitable organization leases premises from a veteran’s or fraternal organization to conduct a festival described above, the charitable organization shall not pay a rental rate for the premises per day of the festival that exceeds the rental rate per bingo session that a charitable organization may pay under Revised Code 2915.09(B)(1) when it leases premises from another charitable organization to conduct bingo games. (d) All of the money or assets received from the games of chance after deduction only of prizes paid out during the conduct of the games of chance are used by, or given, donated, or otherwise transferred to, any organization that is described in Subsection 509(a)(1), 509(a)(2), or 509(a)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code and is either a governmental unit or an organization that is tax exempt under Subsection 501(a) and described in Subsection 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code; (3) The games of chance are not conducted during, or within ten hours of, a bingo game conducted for amusement purposes only pursuant to Section 2915.12 of the Revised Code. No person shall receive any commission, wage, salary, reward, tip, donation, gratuity, or other form of compensation, directly or indirectly, for operating or assisting in the operation of any game of chance. (4) Any tag fishing tournament operated under a permit issued under Section 1533.92 of the Revised Code, as “tag fishing tournament” is defined in Section 1531.01 of the Revised Code; (5) Bingo conducted by a charitable organization that holds a license issued under Section 2915.08 of the Revised Code.

ORC:2915.09.heading: ILLEGALLY CONDUCTING A BINGO GAME 2915.09(B)(1) ORC

ORC:2915.09.text: _____________, a charitable organization that conducted bingo, described in Revised Code 2915.01(O)(1), to wit: (DATE, TIME AND LOCATION OF BINGO), did fail to conduct the bingo game on premises that are owned by the charitable organization, on premises that are owned by another charitable organization and leased from that charitable organization for a rental rate not in excess of the lesser of $600.00 per bingo session or 45% of the gross receipts of the bingo session, on premises that are leased from a person other than a charitable organization for a rental rate that is not more than is customary and reasonable for premises that are similar in location, size, and quality but not in excess of $450.00 per bingo session, or on premises that are owned by a person other than a charitable organization, that are leased from that person by another charitable organization, and that are subleased from that other charitable organization by the charitable organization for a rental rate not in excess of $450.00 per bingo session, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2915.09(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor.
ORC:2915.09.notes: NOTE: This section does not prohibit a bingo licensed charitable organization or a game operator from giving any person an instant bingo ticket as a prize. NOTE: A charitable organization that, prior to December 6, 1977, has entered into written agreements for the lease of premises it owns to another charitable organization or other charitable organizations for the conducting of bingo sessions so that more than two bingo sessions are conducted per calendar week on the premises, and a person that is not a charitable organization and that, prior to December 6, 1977, has entered into written agreements for the lease of premises it owns to charitable organizations for the conducting of more than two bingo sessions per calendar week on the premises, may continue to lease the premises to those charitable organizations, provided that no more than four sessions are conducted per calendar week, that the lessor organization or person has notified the attorney general in writing of the organizations that will conduct the sessions and the days of the week and the times of the day on which the sessions will be conducted, that the initial lease entered into with each organization that will conduct the sessions was filed with the attorney general prior to December 6, 1977, and that each organization that will conduct the sessions was issued a license to conduct bingo games by the attorney general prior to December 6, 1977. NOTE: This section does not apply to a bingo game conducted for amusement only pursuant to Revised Code 2915.12.

ORC:2915.09.text: _____________, a charitable organization that conducted bingo described in Revised Code 2915.01(O)(1), to wit: (DATE, TIME AND LOCATION OF BINGO), did (pay a bingo game operator for operating a bingo session that is conducted by the charitable organization OR pay a bingo game operator for preparing, selling, or serving food or beverages at the site of a bingo session that is conducted by the charitable organization OR permit an auxiliary unit or society of the charitable organization to pay a bingo game operator who prepares, sells, or serves food or beverages at a bingo session conducted by the charitable organization OR permit an auxiliary unit or society of the charitable organization to prepare, sell, or serve food or beverages at a bingo session conducted by the charitable organization, if the auxiliary unit or society pays bingo game operators who prepare, sell, or serve the food or beverages), to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), and having been previously convicted of violating this section on (DATE) in (NAME OF COURT) (CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2915.09(C)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2915.09.notes: NOTE: This section does not prohibit a bingo licensed charitable organization or a game operator from giving any person an instant bingo ticket as a prize. NOTE: This section does not apply to a bingo game conducted for amusement only pursuant to Revised Code 2915.12.

ORC:2915.09.heading: ILLEGALLY CONDUCTING A BINGO GAME 2915.09(C)(11) ORC
ORC:2915.09.variant: ILLEGAL USE OF ELECTRONIC BINGO AID – MM
ORC:2915.09.text: _____________, a charitable organization that conducted bingo described in Revised Code 2915.01(O)(1), to wit: (DATE, TIME AND LOCATION OF BINGO), did use or permit the use of electronic bingo aids not exempted by Revised Code 2915.09(C)(11), to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2915.09(C)(11) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor.
ORC:2915.09.notes: NOTE: Electronic bingo aids are permitted under the following circumstances: 1. For any single participant, not more than ninety bingo faces can be played using an electronic bingo aid or aids. 2. The charitable organization shall provide a participant using an electronic bingo aid with corresponding paper bingo cards or sheets. 3. The total price of bingo faces played with an electronic bingo aid shall be equal to the total price of the same number of bingo faces played with a paper bingo card or sheet sold at the same bingo session but without an electronic bingo aid. 4. An electronic bingo aid cannot be part of an electronic network other than a network that includes only bingo aids and devices that are located on the premises at which the bingo is being conducted or be interactive with any device not located on the premises at which the bingo is being conducted. 5. An electronic bingo aid cannot be used to participate in bingo that is conducted at a location other than the location at which the bingo session is conducted and at which the electronic bingo aid is used. 6. An electronic bingo aid cannot be used to provide for the input of numbers and letters announced by a bingo caller other than the bingo caller who physically calls the numbers and letters at the location at which the bingo session is conducted and at which the electronic bingo aid is used. NOTE: This section does not prohibit a bingo licensed charitable organization or a game operator from giving any person an instant bingo ticket as a prize. NOTE: This section does not apply to a bingo game conducted for amusement only pursuant to Revised Code 2915.12.

ORC:2915.09.text: _____________, a bingo game operator, did receive or accept compensation for (conducting bingo or providing work or labor at the site of bingo) during a bingo session, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), and having been previously convicted of violating this section on (DATE) in (NAME OF COURT) (CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2915.09(D)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2915.09.notes: NOTE: This section does not prohibit a bingo licensed charitable organization or a game operator from giving any person an instant bingo ticket as a prize. NOTE: This section does not prohibit an employee of a fraternal organization, veteran’s organization, or sporting organization from selling instant bingo tickets or cards to the organization’s members or invited guests, as long as no portion of the employee’s compensation is paid from any receipts of bingo. NOTE: This section does not apply to a bingo game conducted for amusement only pursuant to Revised Code 2915.12.

ORC:2915.092.heading: ILLEGAL CONDUCT OF A RAFFLE 2915.092(B) ORC
ORC:2915.092.text: _____________ did conduct a raffle drawing that is (for profit or not for profit), when the exemption in Revised Code 2915.092 does not apply, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2915.092(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2915.092.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to the following: 1. A charitable organization, a public school, a chartered nonpublic school, a community school, or a veteran’s organization, fraternal organization, or sporting organization that is exempt from federal income taxation under subsection 501(a) and is described in subsection 501(c)(3),(4),(7),(8),(10) or (19) of the Internal Revenue Code may conduct a raffle to raise money for the organization or school and does not need a license to conduct bingo in order to conduct a raffle drawing that is not for profit. 2. A charitable organization that is described above, but that is not also described in subsection 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code, conducts a raffle, the charitable organization shall distribute at least 50% of the net profit from the raffle to a charitable purpose described in Revised Code 2915.01(V) or to a department or agency of the federal government, the state, or any political subdivision. NOTE: This section does not apply to a bingo game conducted for amusement only pursuant to Revised Code 2915.12.

ORC:2917.01.heading: INCITING TO VIOLENCE 2917.01(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2917.01.variant: CLEAR AND PRESENT DANGER OF VIOLENCE – F3
ORC:2917.01.text: _____________ did, knowingly engage in conduct designed to urge or incite another, to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT AND PERSONS BEING URGED), to commit a felony offense of violence, to wit: (STATE SPECIFIC OFFENSE OF VIOLENCE AND SECTION NUMBER), under circumstances which created a clear and present danger that any offense of violence will be committed, to wit: (DESCRIBE DANGER), in violation of Section 2917.01(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2917.01.heading: INCITING TO VIOLENCE 2917.01(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2917.01.variant: CLEAR AND PRESENT DANGER OF VIOLENCE – M1
ORC:2917.01.text: _____________ did, knowingly engage in conduct designed to urge or incite another, to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT AND PERSONS BEING URGED), to commit a misdemeanor offense of violence, to wit: (STATE SPECIFIC OFFENSE OF VIOLENCE AND SECTION NUMBER), under circumstances which created a clear and present danger of that any offense of violence will be committed, to wit: (DESCRIBE DANGER), in violation of Section 2917.01(A) (1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2917.01.heading: INCITING TO VIOLENCE 2917.01(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2917.01.text: _____________ did, knowingly engage in conduct designed to urge or incite another, to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT AND PERSONS BEING URGED), to commit a felony offense of violence, to wit: (STATE SPECIFIC OFFENSE OF VIOLENCE AND SECTION NUMBER) and this conduct proximately resulted in the commission of an offense of violence, to wit: (STATE THE SPECIFIC OFFENSE OF VIOLENCE COMMITTED AND SECTION NUMBER), in violation of Section 2917.01(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2917.01.heading: INCITING TO VIOLENCE 2917.01(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2917.01.text: _____________ did, knowingly engage in conduct designed to urge or incite another, to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT AND PERSONS BEING URGED), to commit a misdemeanor offense of violence, to wit: (STATE SPECIFIC OFFENSE OF VIOLENCE AND SECTION NUMBER) and this conduct proximately resulted in the commission of an offense of violence, to wit: (STATE THE SPECIFIC OFFENSE OF VIOLENCE COMMITTED AND SECTION NUMBER), in violation of Section 2917.01(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2917.02.heading: AGGRAVATED RIOT 2917.02(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2917.02.text: _____________ did participate with four or more others in a course of disorderly conduct violating ORC Section 2917.11 to wit: (DESCRIBE GROUP AND CONDUCT), with purpose to (commit or facilitate the commission of) a felony, to wit: (STATE SPECIFIC FELONY AND SECTION NUMBER), in violation of Section 2917.02(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2917.02.heading: AGGRAVATED RIOT 2917.02(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2917.02.text: _____________ did participate with four or more others in a course of disorderly conduct violating ORC Section 2917.11 to wit: (DESCRIBE GROUP AND CONDUCT), with purpose to (commit or facilitate the commission of) an offense of violence, to wit: (STATE SPECIFIC OFFENSE OF VIOLENCE AND SECTION NUMBER), in violation of Section 2917.02(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2917.02.heading: AGGRAVATED RIOT 2917.02(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2917.02.variant: ACCUSED HAS A DEADLY WEAPON OR DANGEROUS ORDNANCE – F5
ORC:2917.02.text: _____________ did participate with four or more others in a course of disorderly conduct violating ORC Section 2917.11 to wit: (DESCRIBE GROUP AND CONDUCT), and did (have on (his or her) person or have about (his or her) person or have under (his or her) control or use or intend to use) a (deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance), to wit: (STATE TYPE OF WEAPON OR ORDNANCE), in violation of Section 2917.02(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2917.02.heading: AGGRAVATED RIOT 2917.02(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2917.02.variant: PARTICIPANT HAS DEADLY WEAPON OR DANGEROUS ORDNANCE – F5
ORC:2917.02.text: _____________ did participate with four or more others in a course of disorderly conduct violating Section 2917.11 to wit: (DESCRIBE GROUP AND CONDUCT), and had knowledge that a participant with (him or her) (had on (his or her) person or had about (his or her) person or had under (his or her) control or used or intended to use) a (deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance), to wit: (STATE PERSON AND DESCRIBE TYPE OF WEAPON OR ORDNANCE), in violation of Section 2917.02(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2917.02.heading: AGGRAVATED RIOT 2917.02(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2917.02.variant: INMATE TO COMMIT A FELONY – F4
ORC:2917.02.text: _____________ did, being an inmate in a detention facility, to wit: (NAME OF FACILITY) participate with four or more others in a course of disorderly conduct violating ORC Section 2917.11 to wit: (DESCRIBE GROUP AND CONDUCT), with purpose to (commit or facilitate the commission of) a felony, to with: (STATE SPECIFIC FELONY AND SECTION NUMBER), in violation of Section 2917.02(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2917.02.heading: AGGRAVATED RIOT 2917.02(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2917.02.variant: AN INMATE ACCUSED HAS A DEADLY WEAPON OR DANGEROUS ORDNANCE – F4
ORC:2917.02.text: _____________ did, being an inmate in a detention facility, to wit: (NAME OF FACILITY) participate with four or more others in a course of disorderly conduct violating ORC Section 2917.11 to wit: (DESCRIBE GROUP AND CONDUCT), and did (have on (his or her) person or have about (his or her) person or have under (his or her) control or use or intend to use) a (deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance), to wit: (STATE TYPE OF WEAPON OR ORDNANCE), in violation of Section 2917.02(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2917.02.heading: AGGRAVATED RIOT 2917.02(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2917.02.variant: AN INMATE PARTICIPANT HAS DEADLY WEAPON OR DANGEROUS ORDNANCE – F4
ORC:2917.02.text: _____________ did, being an inmate in a detention facility, to wit: (NAME OF FACILITY) participate with four or more others in a course of disorderly conduct violating Section 2917.11 to wit: (DESCRIBE GROUP AND CONDUCT), and had knowledge that a participant with him (had on (his or her) person or had about (his or her) person or had under (his or her) control or used or intended to use) a (deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance), to wit: (STATE PERSON AND DESCRIBE TYPE OF WEAPON OR ORDNANCE), in violation of Section 2917.02(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2917.02.heading: AGGRAVATED RIOT 2917.02(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2917.02.text: _____________ did, being an inmate in a detention facility, to wit: (NAME OF FACILITY) participate with four or more others in a course of disorderly conduct violating ORC Section 2917.11 to wit: (DESCRIBE GROUP AND CONDUCT), with purpose to (commit or facilitate the commission of) an offense of violence, to wit: (STATE SPECIFIC OFFENSE OF VIOLENCE AND SECTION NUMBER), in violation of Section 2917.02(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2917.03.heading: RIOT 2917.03(A)(1) ORC (CCC 2317.03(A)(1))
ORC:2917.03.text: _____________ did participate with four or more others in a course of disorderly conduct in violation of Section 2917.11, to wit: (DESCRIBE GROUP AND CONDUCT), with purpose to (commit or facilitate the commission of) another misdemeanor, to wit: (STATE SPECIFIC MISDEMEANOR AND SECTION NUMBER), in violation of Section 2917.03(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.03.notes: NOTE: Disorderly Conduct may not be the underlying misdemeanor offense in this violation.

ORC:2917.03.heading: RIOT 2917.03(A)(2) ORC (CCC 2317.03(A)(2))
ORC:2917.03.variant: TO INTIMIDATE A PUBLIC OFFICIAL – M1
ORC:2917.03.text: _____________ did participate with four or more others in a course of disorderly conduct in violation of Section 2917.11, to wit: (DESCRIBE GROUP AND CONDUCT), with purpose to intimidate a (public official or public employee), to wit: (STATE NAME AND POSITION), into (taking or refraining from) official action, to wit: (STATE ACTION), in violation of Section 2917.03(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2917.03.heading: RIOT 2917.03(A)(2) ORC (CCC 2317.03(A)(2))
ORC:2917.03.variant: TO HINDER A GOVERNMENT FUNCTION – M1
ORC:2917.03.text: _____________ did participate with four or more others in a course of disorderly conduct in violation of Section 2917.11, to wit: (DESCRIBE GROUP AND CONDUCT), with purpose to (hinder or impede or obstruct) a function of government, to wit: (STATE FUNCTION), in violation of Section 2917.03(A) (2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2917.03.heading: RIOT 2917.03(A)(3) ORC (CCC 2317.03(A)(2))
ORC:2917.03.text: _____________ did participate with four or more others in a course of disorderly conduct in violation of Section 2917.11, to wit: (DESCRIBE GROUP AND CONDUCT), with purpose to (hinder or impede or obstruct) the orderly process of (administration or instruction) at an educational institution, to wit: (STATE NAME), in violation of Section 2917.03(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2917.03.heading: RIOT 2917.03(A)(3) ORC (CCC 2317.03(A)(3))
ORC:2917.03.text: _____________ did participate with four or more others in a course of disorderly conduct in violation of Section 2917.11, to wit: (DESCRIBE GROUP AND CONDUCT), with purpose to (interfere with or disrupt) lawful activities at an educational institution, to wit: (STATE ACTIVITIES AND NAME INSTITUTION), in violation of Section 2917.03(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2917.03.heading: RIOT 2917.03(B) ORC (CCC 2317.03(A)(1))
ORC:2917.03.text: _____________ did participate with four or more others, to wit: (DESCRIBE GROUP), with purpose to do an act with unlawful (force or violence), to wit: (STATE ACT), even though such act may otherwise be lawful, in violation of Section 2917.03(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2917.04.heading: FAILURE TO DISPERSE 2917.04(A) ORC (CCC 2317.04(A))
ORC:2917.04.text: _____________ did knowingly fail to obey the order of a (law enforcement officer or public official), to wit: (STATE NAME AND TITLE/POSITION), to disperse from an area, to wit: (DESCRIBE LOCATION) where five or more persons were participating in a course of disorderly conduct in violation of (Section 2917.11 of the Ohio Revised Code or Section 2317.11 of the Columbus City Code), to wit: (DESCRIBE GROUP AND CONDUCT) and there are other persons in the vicinity whose presence creates the likelihood of physical harm to persons or property or of serious public inconvenience, annoyance, or alarm, to wit: (DESCRIBE OTHER PERSONS AND THE HARM OR INCONVENIENCE), in violation of Section 2917.04(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor.

ORC:2917.04.heading: FAILURE TO DISPERSE 2917.04(A) ORC (CCC 2317.04(A))
ORC:2917.04.text: _____________ did knowingly fail to obey the order of a (law enforcement officer or public official), to wit: (STATE NAME AND TITLE/POSITION), to disperse from an area, to wit: (DESCRIBE LOCATION) where five or more persons were participating in a course of disorderly conduct in violation of (Section 2917.11 of the Ohio Revised Code or Section 2317.11 of the Columbus City Code), to wit: (DESCRIBE GROUP AND CONDUCT) and there are other persons in the vicinity whose presence creates the likelihood of serious physical harm to persons, to wit: (DESCRIBE OTHER PERSONS AND THE LIKELIHOOD OF SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM), in violation of Section 2917.04(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2917.04.heading: FAILURE TO DISPERSE 2917.04(A) ORC (CCC 2317.04(A))
ORC:2917.04.variant: SCENE OF A FIRE, ACCIDENT, DISASTER, RIOT OR EMERGENCY – M4
ORC:2917.04.text: _____________ did knowingly fail to obey the order of a (law enforcement officer or public official), to wit: (STATE NAME AND TITLE/POSITION), to disperse from the scene of a (fire, accident, disaster, riot or emergency), to wit: (DESCRIBE SCENE) where five or more persons were participating in a course of disorderly conduct in violation of (Section 2917.11 of the Ohio Revised Code or Section 2317.11 of the Columbus City Code), to wit: (DESCRIBE GROUP AND CONDUCT) and there are other persons in the vicinity whose presence creates the likelihood of physical harm to persons or property or of serious public inconvenience, annoyance, or alarm, to wit: (DESCRIBE OTHER PERSONS AND THE HARM OR INCONVENIENCE) in violation of Section 2917.04(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2917.11.heading: DISORDERLY CONDUCT 2917.11(A)(1) ORC (CCC 2317.11(A)(1))
ORC:2917.11.text: _____________ did, recklessly cause (inconvenience or annoyance or alarm) to another, to wit: (NAME PERSON), by engaging in (fighting or threatening harm to persons or threatening harm to property or engaging in violent behavior or engaging in turbulent behavior), to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT), in violation of Section 2917.11(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor or in violation of Section 2317.11(A)(1) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2917.11.notes: NOTE: Under Columbus City Code a conviction of this section that occurs on city owned property, in a school building, on school premises, or within 1,000 feet of the boundaries of school premises will result in a mandatory 10 days imprisonment.

ORC:2917.11.heading: DISORDERLY CONDUCT 2917.11(A)(2) ORC (CCC 2317.11(A)(2))
ORC:2917.11.text: _____________ did, recklessly cause (inconvenience, annoyance, or alarm) to another, to wit: (NAME PERSON), by (making unreasonable noise or offensively course utterance, gesture, or display, or communicating unwarranted and grossly abusive language to any person), to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT), in violation of Section 2917.11(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor or in violation of Section 2317.11(A)(2) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2917.11.heading: DISORDERLY CONDUCT 2917.11(A)(3) ORC (CCC 2317.11(A)(3))
ORC:2917.11.text: _____________ did, recklessly cause (inconvenience or annoyance or alarm) to another, to wit: (STATE NAME), by (insulting or taunting or challenging) said person under circumstances where such conduct was likely to provoke a violent response, to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT), in violation of Section 2917.11(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor or in violation of Section 2317.11(A)(3) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2917.11.notes: NOTE: Under Columbus City Code a conviction of this section that occurs on city owned property, in a school building, on school premises, or within 1,000 feet of the boundaries of school premises will result in a mandatory 10 days imprisonment.

ORC:2917.11.heading: DISORDERLY CONDUCT 2917.11(A)(4) ORC (CCC 2317.11(A)(4))
ORC:2917.11.text: _____________ did, recklessly cause (inconvenience, annoyance, or alarm) to another, to wit: (STATE NAME) by (hindering or preventing) the movement of persons on a (public street, road, highway, or right of way or to, from, within, or upon public or private property) so as to interfere with the rights of others and by any act which serves no lawful and reasonable purpose, to wit: (DESCRIBE DEFENDANT’S ACTION AND HOW VICTIM WAS HINDERED OR PREVENTED), in violation of Section 2917.11(A)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor or in violation of Section 2317.11(A)(4) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2917.11.heading: DISORDERLY CONDUCT 2917.11(A)(5) ORC (CCC 2317.11(A)(5))
ORC:2917.11.variant: RISK OF HARM TO PERSONS OR PROPERTY OR PRIVATE PROPERTY – M4
ORC:2917.11.text: _____________ did, recklessly cause (inconvenience or annoyance or alarm) to another, to wit: (STATE NAME), by creating a condition which (was physically offensive to persons or presented a risk of physical harm to persons or presented a risk of physical harm to property), to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDITION), by an act which served no lawful and reasonable purpose to (himself or herself), to wit: (DESCRIBE ACTION), in violation of Section 2917.11(A)(5) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor or in violation of Section 2317.11(A)(5) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2917.11.notes: NOTE: Under City Code a conviction of this section that occurs on city owned property, in a school building, on school premises, or within 1,000 feet of the boundaries of school premises will result in a mandatory 10 days imprisonment.

ORC:2917.11.heading: DISORDERLY CONDUCT 2917.11(B)(1) ORC (CCC 2317.11(B)(1))
ORC:2917.11.text: _____________ did, while voluntarily intoxicated and (in a public place or in the presence of two or more persons), to wit: (DESCRIBE LOCATION), engage in conduct which was likely (to be offensive or to cause inconvenience or to cause annoyance or to cause alarm) to persons of ordinary sensibilities, to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT), which effect (he or she) should have realized but for being intoxicated, in violation of Section 2917.11(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor or in violation of Section 2317.11(B)(1) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2917.11.notes: NOTE: If the offender has previously been convicted of three or more violations of ORC 2917.11(B), a violation of ORC 2917.11(B) is a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2917.11.heading: DISORDERLY CONDUCT 2917.11(B)(2) ORC (CCC 2317.11(B)(2))
ORC:2917.11.variant: INTOXICATED – RISK OF HARM TO PERSONS OR PROPERTY – M4
ORC:2917.11.text: _____________ did, while voluntarily intoxicated, (engage in conduct or create a condition) which presented a risk of physical harm (to himself or to another or to the property of another), to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT OR CONDITION), in violation of Section 2917.11(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor or in violation of Section 2317.11(B)(2) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2917.11.notes: NOTE: If the offender has previously been convicted of three or more violations of ORC 2917.11(B), a violation of ORC 2917.11(B) is a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2917.12.heading: DISTURBING A LAWFUL MEETING 2917.12(A)(1) ORC (CCC 2317.12(A) (1))
ORC:2917.12.text: _____________ did, with purpose to (prevent or disrupt) a lawful (meeting or procession or gathering), to wit: (DESCRIBE MEETING AND LOCATION) do an act which (obstructed or interfered) with the due conduct of such (meeting or procession or gathering), to wit: (DESCRIBE ACT AND HOW IT SIGNIFICANTLY OBSTRUCTED OR INTERFERED WITH THE MEETING), in violation of Section 2917.12(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2917.12.notes: NOTE: The courts have ruled that in order for this section to be applicable the act of interference must have a significant effect upon the conduct of the meeting. NOTE: Disturbing a lawful meeting is a misdemeanor of the first degree if the violation is committed with the intent to disturb or disquiet any assemblage of people met for religious worship at a tax-exempt place of worship (i.e., a church, mosque, temple, etc.), regardless of whether the conduct is within the place at which the assemblage is held or is on the property on which that place is located, and disturbs the order and solemnity of the assemblage; OR the violation is committed with the intent to prevent, disrupt, or interfere with a virtual meeting or gathering of people for religious worship through use of a computer, computer system, telecommunications device, other electronic device or system, or in any other manner. If either of these circumstances apply, include the elements in the body of the complaint.

ORC:2917.12.heading: DISTURBING A LAWFUL MEETING 2917.12(A)(2) ORC (CCC 2317.12(A) (2))
ORC:2917.12.text: _____________ did, with purpose to (prevent or disrupt) a lawful (meeting or procession or gathering), to wit: (DESCRIBE MEETING AND LOCATION), make an (utterance or gesture or display), to wit: (DESCRIBE ACT), which outraged the sensibilities of the group, in violation of Section 2917.12(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2917.12.notes: NOTE: Disturbing a lawful meeting is a misdemeanor of the first degree if the violation is committed with the intent to disturb or disquiet any assemblage of people met for religious worship at a tax-exempt place of worship (i.e., a church, mosque, temple, etc.), regardless of whether the conduct is within the place at which the assemblage is held or is on the property on which that place is located, and disturbs the order and solemnity of the assemblage; OR the violation is committed with the intent to prevent, disrupt, or interfere with a virtual meeting or gathering of people for religious worship through use of a computer, computer system, telecommunications device, other electronic device or system, or in any other manner. If either of these circumstances apply, include the elements in the body of the complaint.

ORC:2917.13.heading: MISCONDUCT AT AN EMERGENCY 2917.13(A)(1) ORC (CCC 2317.13(A) (1))
ORC:2917.13.text: _____________ did knowingly hamper the lawful operations of (a law enforcement officer, firefighter, rescuer, medical person, emergency medical services person, or an authorized person), to wit: (DESCRIBE HAMPERING, CONDUCT AND OFFICIAL), engaged in (his or her) duties at the scene of (a fire or an accident or a disaster or a riot or an emergency) to wit: (DESCRIBE EMERGENCY AND LOCATION), in violation of Section 2917.13(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2917.13.heading: MISCONDUCT AT AN EMERGENCY 2917.13(A)(1) ORC (CCC 2317.31(A) (1))
ORC:2917.13.variant: HAMPER OPERATIONS – RISK OF HARM – M1
ORC:2917.13.text: _____________ did knowingly hamper the lawful operation of (a law enforcement officer, firefighter, rescuer, medical person, emergency medical services person, or an authorized person), to wit: (DESCRIBE HAMPERING, CONDUCT AND OFFICIAL), engaged in (his or her) duties at the scene of (a fire or an accident or a disaster or a riot or an emergency) to wit: (DESCRIBE EMERGENCY AND LOCATION), and by doing so did create a risk of physical harm to (persons or property), to wit: (DESCRIBE RISK AND PERSONS OR PROPERTY), in violation of Section 2917.13(A)(1) of Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2917.13.heading: MISCONDUCT AT AN EMERGENCY 2917.13(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2917.13.variant: HAMPER LAWFUL ACTIVITIES OF EMERGENCY FACILITIES PERSON – M4
ORC:2917.13.text: _____________ did knowingly hamper the lawful activities of any emergency facility person, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE HAMPERING, CONDUCT AND OFFICIAL), who is engaged in (his or her) duties in an emergency facility, to wit: (DESCRIBE DUTIES AND FACILITY), in violation of Section 2917.13(A) (2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2917.13.notes: NOTE: “Emergency facility personnel” means any of the following: – Any of the following individuals who perform services in the ordinary course of their professions in an emergency facility: – Physicians authorized under Chapter 4731 of the Ohio Revised Code to practice medicine and surgery or osteopathic medicine and surgery; – Registered nurses and licensed practical nurses licensed under Chapter 4723 of the Ohio Revised Code; – Physician assistants authorized to practice under Chapter 4730 of the Ohio Revised Code; – Health care workers; – Clerical staffs. – Any individual who is a security officer performing security services in an emergency facility; – Any individual who is present in an emergency facility, who was summoned to the facility by any “emergency facility personnel” described above. NOTE: “Emergency facility” means a hospital emergency department or any other facility that provides emergency medical services. NOTE: “Hospital” has the same meaning as in Section 3727.01 of the Ohio Revised Code. NOTE: “Health care worker” means an individual, other than an “emergency facility personnel” described above, who provides medical or other health-related care or treatment in an emergency facility, including medical technicians, medical assistants, orderlies, aides, or individuals acting in similar capacities.

ORC:2917.13.heading: MISCONDUCT AT AN EMERGENCY 2917.13(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2917.13.variant: HAMPER LAWFUL ACTIVITIES OF EMERGENCY FACILITIES PERSON – RISK OF PHYSICAL HARM – M1
ORC:2917.13.text: _____________ did knowingly hamper the lawful activities of any emergency facility person, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE HAMPERING, CONDUCT AND OFFICIAL), who is engaged in (his or her) duties in an emergency facility, to wit: (DESCRIBE DUTIES AND FACILITY), and by doing so did create a risk of physical harm to (persons or property), to wit: (DESCRIBE RISK AND PERSONS OR PROPERTY), in violation of Section 2917.13(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.13.notes: NOTE: “Emergency facility personnel” means any of the following: – Any of the following individuals who perform services in the ordinary course of their professions in an emergency facility: – Physicians authorized under Chapter 4731 of the Ohio Revised Code to practice medicine and surgery or osteopathic medicine and surgery; – Registered nurses and licensed practical nurses licensed under Chapter 4723 of the Ohio Revised Code; – Physician assistants authorized to practice under Chapter 4730 of the Ohio Revised Code; – Health care workers; – Clerical staffs. – Any individual who is a security officer performing security services in an emergency facility; – Any individual who is present in an emergency facility, who was summoned to the facility by any “emergency facility personnel” described above. NOTE: “Emergency facility” means a hospital emergency department or any other facility that provides emergency medical services. NOTE: “Hospital” has the same meaning as in Section 3727.01 of the Ohio Revised Code. NOTE: “Health care worker” means an individual, other than an “emergency facility personnel” described above, who provides medical or other health-related care or treatment in an emergency facility, including medical technicians, medical assistants, orderlies, aides, or individuals acting in similar capacities.

ORC:2917.13.heading: MISCONDUCT AT AN EMERGENCY 2917.13(A)(3) ORC (CCC 2317.13(A) (2))
ORC:2917.13.variant: FAILURE TO OBEY LAWFUL ORDER – M4
ORC:2917.13.text: _____________ did knowingly fail to obey the lawful order of a law enforcement officer, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE ORDER, NAME THE OFFICER, AND HOW THE ORDER WAS DISOBEYED) who was engaged in (his or her) duties (at the scene of or in connection with) a (fire or accident or disaster or riot or emergency), to wit: (DESCRIBE THE EMERGENCY AND THE LOCATION), in violation of Section 2917.13(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2917.13.heading: MISCONDUCT AT AN EMERGENCY 2917.13(A)(3) ORC (CCC 2317.13(A) (2))
ORC:2917.13.variant: FAILURE TO OBEY LAWFUL ORDER – RISK OF PHYSICAL HARM – M1
ORC:2917.13.text: _____________ did knowingly fail to obey the lawful order of a law enforcement officer, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE ORDER, HOW THE ORDER WAS DISOBEYED AND NAME THE OFFICER), who was engaged in (his or her) duties (at the scene of or in connection with) a (fire or accident or disaster or riot or emergency), to wit: (DESCRIBE THE EMERGENCY AND LOCATION), and by doing so did create a risk of physical harm to (persons or property), to wit: (DESCRIBE THE RISK AND THE PERSONS OR PROPERTY) in violation of Section 2917.13(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2917.14.heading: UNLAWFULLY IMPEDING PUBLIC PASSAGE OF EMERGENCY SERVICE RESPONDER 2917.14(A) ORC
ORC:2917.14.variant: PREVENTED EMERGENCY VEHICLE FROM ACCESSING HIGHWAY OR STREET – M1
ORC:2917.14.text: _____________ did, without privilege to do so, recklessly obstruct any (highway, street, sidewalk, or any other public passage) in such a manner as to render the (highway, street, sidewalk, or passage) impassable without unreasonable inconvenience or hazard, and the obstruction prevented an emergency vehicle from accessing a highway or street, and upon receipt of a (request or order) from an emergency service responder (to remove or cease the obstruction), the person refused to (remove or cease the obstruction), to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2917.14(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.14.notes: NOTE: Nothing in this section limits an officer from charging multiple offenses arising from the conduct that gave rise to this offense. NOTE: “Emergency service responder” means any law enforcement officer, first responder, emergency medical technician-basic, emergency medical technician-intermediate, emergency medical technician-paramedic, firefighter, or volunteer firefighter.

CCC:2317.14.heading: PUBLIC URINATION/DEFECATION CCC 2317.14(A)(1)
CCC:2317.14.variant: URINATE/DEFECATE ON PUBLIC SIDEWALK, STREET, PARK, ALLEY, OR YARD – MM
CCC:2317.14.text: _____________ did (urinate or defecate) on any (sidewalk, street, park, alley, or yard) that is publicly owned or open to the public for use, to wit: (DESCRIBE LOCATION AND BEHAVIOR), in violation of Section 2317.14(A)(1) of the Columbus City Code, a minor misdemeanor.
CCC:2317.14.notes: NOTE: The following affirmative defenses apply to this section: 1. A person proves that the act of urination/defecation was due to a verified medical condition that rendered the act beyond the person’s bodily control, or 2. A person proves both of the following: a. The person had the express consent of the owner of the property to use the property for the purposes of urinating/defecating. b. The person took reasonable precautions to be obscured from public view while urinating/defecating.

DEFINITIONS 2913.21 ORC As used in Section 2913.21, Telecommunication and Telecommunications Device have the same meaning as defined Section 2913.01(X)(Y): TELECOMMUNICATION – means the origination, emission, dissemination, transmission, or reception of data, images, signals, sounds, or other intelligence or equivalence of intelligence of any nature over any communications system by any method, including, but not limited to, a fiber optic, electronic, magnetic, optical, digital, or analog method. TELECOMMUNICATIONS DEVICE – means any instrument, equipment, machine, or other device that facilitates telecommunication, including, but not limited to, a computer, computer network, computer chip, computer circuit, scanner, telephone, cellular telephone, pager, personal communications device, transponder, receiver, radio, modem, or device that enables the use of a modem.

ORC:2917.21.heading: TELECOMMUNICATIONS HARASSMENT 2917.21(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2917.21.variant: WITH PURPOSE TO ABUSE, INTIMIDATE, OR HARASS ANOTHER – M1
ORC:2917.21.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a telecommunication or cause a telecommunication to be made or permit a telecommunication to be made on a telecommunications device controlled by (him or her)) to another, to wit: (STATE NAME OR PLACE CALLED), when the caller, to wit: (NAME CALLER), makes the telecommunication for the purpose of (harassing, intimidating, or abusing) a person at the premises to which the telecommunication is made, to wit: (DESCRIBE DETAILS OF THE TELECOMMUNICATION), in violation of Section 2917.21(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.21.notes: NOTE: Actual communication does not have to take place to commit this offense.

ORC:2917.21.heading: TELECOMMUNICATIONS HARASSMENT 2917.21(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2917.21.variant: WITH PURPOSE TO ABUSE, INTIMIDATE, OR HARASS ANOTHER – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F5
ORC:2917.21.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a telecommunication or cause a telecommunication to be made or permit a telecommunication to be made on a telecommunications device controlled by (him or her)) to another, to wit: (STATE NAME OR PLACE CALLED), when the caller, to wit: (NAME CALLER), makes the telecommunication for the purpose of (harassing, intimidating, or abusing) a person at the premises to which the telecommunication is made, to wit: (DESCRIBE DETAILS OF THE TELECOMMUNICATION), and having been previously convicted of the same (person or recipient or premise) violating Section 2917.21 of the Ohio Revised Code on (DATE, TIME AND RECIPIENT OF PREVIOUS TELECOMMUNICATION), in violation of Section 2917.21(A) (1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2917.21.notes: NOTE: Actual communication does not have to take place to commit this offense.

ORC:2917.21.heading: TELECOMMUNICATIONS HARASSMENT 2917.21(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2917.21.variant: SUGGESTING SEXUAL ACTIVITY AND BEING TOLD NOT TO CALL/ CONTACT – M1
ORC:2917.21.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a telecommunication or cause a telecommunication to be made or permit a telecommunication to be made on the telecommunications device controlled by (him or her)) to another, to wit: (STATE NAME OR PLACE CALLED/CONTACTED), when the caller, to wit: (NAME CALLER), (describes or suggests or requests or proposes) that someone engage in sexual activity to wit: (STATE PERTINENT CONTENTS OF TELECOMMUNICATION), and the caller (is or has been) told not to call/ contact the premises, to wit: (DESCRIBE NOTICE NOT TO CONTACT), in violation of Section 2917.21(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2917.21.heading: TELECOMMUNICATIONS HARASSMENT 2917.21(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2917.21.variant: SUGGESTING SEXUAL ACTIVITY AND BEING TOLD NOT TO CALL/ CONTACT – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F5
ORC:2917.21.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a telecommunication or cause a telecommunication to be made or permit a telecommunication to be made on a telecommunications device controlled by the violator) to another, to wit: (STATE NAME OR PLACE CALLED/CONTACTED), when the caller, to wit: (NAME CALLER), (describes or suggests or requests or proposes) that someone engage in sexual activity, to wit: (STATE PERTINENT CONTENTS OF TELECOMMUNICATION), and the caller (is or has been) told not to call/ contact the premises, to wit: (DESCRIBE NOTICE NOT TO CONTACT), and having previously called/contacted the same (person or recipient or premise) violating Section 2917.21 of the Ohio Revised Code on (DATE, TIME AND RECIPIENT OF PREVIOUS TELECOMMUNICATION), in violation of Section 2917.21(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2917.21.heading: TELECOMMUNICATIONS HARASSMENT 2917.21(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2917.21.variant: THREATENING SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM – M1
ORC:2917.21.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a telecommunication or cause a telecommunication to be made or permit a telecommunication to be made on a telecommunications device controlled by the violator) to another, to wit: (STATE NAME OR PLACE CALLED/CONTACTED), when the caller, to wit: (NAME CALLER), knowingly caused the person called/contacted to believe that (he or she) will cause serious physical harm to the (person or property) of (the person called/contacted or a member of the immediate family of the person called/contacted, to wit: (DESCRIBE PERTINENT PORTIONS OF THE TELECOMMUNICATION INCLUDING DETAILS OF THREATS), in violation of Section 2917.21(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2917.21.heading: TELECOMMUNICATIONS HARASSMENT 2917.21(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2917.21.variant: THREATENING SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM, PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F5
ORC:2917.21.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a telecommunication or cause a telecommunication to be made or permit a telecommunication to be made on a telecommunications device controlled by the violator) to another, to wit: (STATE NAME OR PLACE CALLED/CONTACTED), when the caller, to wit: (NAME CALLER), knowingly caused the person called/contacted to believe that (he or she) will cause serious physical harm to the (person or property), of (the person called/contacted or a member of the immediately family of the person called/contacted), to wit: (DESCRIBE PORTIONS OF TELECOMMUNICATION INCLUDING DETAILS OF THREATS) and having previously called/contacted the same (person or recipient or premise) violating Section 2917.21 of the Ohio Revised Code on (DATE, TIME AND RECIPIENT OF PREVIOUS TELECOMMUNICATION), in violation of Section 2917.21(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2917.21.heading: TELECOMMUNICATIONS HARASSMENT 2917.21(A)(4) ORC
ORC:2917.21.variant: THREATENS DAMAGE TO PROPERTY CONNECTED TO PERSON CALLED/CONTACTED – M1
ORC:2917.21.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a telecommunication or cause a telecommunication to be made or permit a telecommunication to be made on a telecommunications device controlled by the violator) to another, to wit: (STATE NAME OR PLACE CALLED/CONTACTED), when the caller, to wit: (NAME CALLER), knowingly states (he or she) intends to (cause damage to or destroy) (public or private) property, to wit: (DESCRIBE PERTINENT PORTIONS OF THE TELECOMMUNICATION AND DESCRIPTION OF PROPERTY THREATENED), which (is owned by or is resided in by or is worked in by or is insured by or is protected by or at time of destruction will be near to or at time of destruction will contain) (the recipient of the telecommunication or a family member of the recipient of the telecommunication or person residing at the premises receiving the telecommunication), to wit: (DESCRIBE PARTICULAR CIRCUMSTANCES INCLUDING PERSON INVOLVED AND CONNECTION WITH THREATENED PROPERTY), in violation of Section 2917.21(A)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.21.notes: NOTE: If a violation of Section 2917.21(A)(4) results in economic harm, the economic harm caused must be alleged in the affidavit. The charge is as follows: – VALUE between $1,000.00 and $7,500.00, Telecommunications Harassment, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE between $7,500.00 and $150,000.00, Telecommunications Harassment, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE at more than $150,000.00, Telecommunications Harassment, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2917.21.heading: TELECOMMUNICATIONS HARASSMENT 2917.21(A)(4) ORC
ORC:2917.21.variant: THREATENED DAMAGE TO PROPERTY CONNECTED TO PERSON CALLED/CONTACTED, PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F5

ORC:2917.21.notes: NOTE: If a violation of Section 2917.21(A)(4) results in economic harm, the economic harm caused must be alleged in the affidavit. The charge is as follows: – VALUE between $1,000.00 and $7,500.00, Telecommunications Harassment, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE between $7,500.00 and $150,000.00, Telecommunications Harassment, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE at more than $150,000.00, Telecommunications Harassment, a felony of the third degree. DEFINITIONS 2917.21 ORC NOTE: Divisions (A)(5) to (A)(11) and (B)(2) of Section 2917.21 do not apply to a person who, while employed or contracted by a newspaper, magazine, press association, news agency, news wire service, cable channel or cable operator, or radio or television station, is gathering, processing, transmitting, compiling, editing, or disseminating information for the general public within the scope of the person’s employment in that capacity or the person’s contractual authority in that capacity.
