ORC:2917.21.variant: CALLING/CONTACTING AFTER BEING TOLD NOT TO – M1
ORC:2917.21.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a telecommunication or cause a telecommunication to be made or permit a telecommunication to be made on a telecommunications device controlled by the violator) to another, to wit: (STATE NAME OR PLACE CALLED/CONTACTED), when the caller, to wit: (NAME CALLER), knowingly made the telecommunication to (the recipient of the telecommunication or a person at the premises called/contacted or the premises called/contacted) and had been previously told not to call/contact (the premises or a person at the premises) by (the recipient of the call/contact or a person at the premises) to wit: (DESCRIBE THE PARTICULAR FACTS ADVISING AGAINST THE TELECOMMUNICATION), in violation of Section 2917.21(A)(5) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2917.21.heading: TELECOMMUNICATIONS HARASSMENT 2917.21(A)(7) ORC
ORC:2917.21.variant: WITHOUT A LAWFUL BUSINESS PURPOSE – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F5
ORC:2917.21.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a telecommunication or cause a telecommunication to be made or permit a telecommunication to be made on a telecommunications device controlled by the violator) to another, to wit: (STATE NAME OR PLACE CALLED/CONTACTED), when the caller, to wit: (NAME CALLER), knowingly interrupts the telecommunication service of any person without a lawful business purpose, to wit: (DESCRIBE PERSON AND INTERRUPTION), and having previously been convicted of violating Section 2917.21 of the Ohio Revised Code on (DATE, TIME AND RECIPIENT OF PREVIOUS TELECOMMUNICATION, COURT AND CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2917.21(A)(7) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2917.21.heading: TELECOMMUNICATIONS HARASSMENT 2917.21(A)(9) ORC
ORC:2917.21.variant: MAKE FALSE STATEMENT TO ABUSE, THREATEN, INTIMIDATE, OR HARASS ANOTHER – M1
ORC:2917.21.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a telecommunication or cause a telecommunication to be made or permit a telecommunication to be made on a telecommunications device controlled by the violator) to another, to wit: (STATE NAME OR PLACE CALLED/CONTACTED), when the caller, to wit: (NAME CALLER), knowingly makes any false statement concerning the (death, injury, illness, disfigurement, reputation, indecent conduct, or criminal conduct) of the (recipient/family or household member of the recipient) with purpose to (abuse, threaten, intimidate, or harass) the recipient, to wit: (DESCRIBE STATEMENT, RECIPIENT, AND DETAILS OF THE COMMUNICATION), in violation of Section 2917.21(A)(9) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2917.21.heading: TELECOMMUNICATIONS HARASSMENT 2917.21(A)(11) ORC

ORC:2917.21.heading: TELECOMMUNICATIONS HARASSMENT 2917.21(B)(1) ORC

ORC:2917.21.heading: TELECOMMUNICATIONS HARASSMENT 2917.21(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2917.21.variant: POSTING ON INTERNET TO ABUSE, THREATEN, OR HARASS ANOTHER – M1
ORC:2917.21.text: ____________ did knowingly post a (text, audio statement, or image) on an internet (web site or web page), to wit: (DESCRIBE WHAT WAS POSTED AND WHERE) for the purpose of (abusing, threatening, or harassing) another person, to wit: (DESCRIBE PERSON AND PURPOSE), in violation of Section 2917.21(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2917.21.heading: TELECOMMUNICATIONS HARASSMENT 2917.21(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2917.21.variant: POSTING ON INTERNET TO ABUSE, THREATEN, OR HARASS ANOTHER – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F5
ORC:2917.21.text: ____________ did knowingly post a (text, audio statement, or image) on an internet (web site or web page), to wit: (DESCRIBE WHAT WAS POSTED AND WHERE) for the purpose of (abusing, threatening, or harassing) another person, to wit: (DESCRIBE PERSON AND PURPOSE), and having been previously convicted of violating Section 2917.21 of the Ohio Revised Code on (DATE, TIME AND RECIPIENT OF PREVIOUS TELECOMMUNICATION, COURT AND CASE NUMBER) in violation of Section 2917.21(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2917.21.notes: DEFINITIONS 2917.211(B) ORC As used in this section: 1. “Disseminate” means to post, distribute, or publish on a computer device, computer network, web site, or other electronic device or medium of communication. 2. “Image” means a photograph, film, videotape, digital recording, or other depiction or portrayal of a person. 3. “Interactive computer service” has the meaning defined in the “Telecommunications Act of 1996,” 47 U.S.C. 230, as amended. 4. “Internet provider” means a provider of internet service, including all of the following: a. Broadband service, however defined or classified by the federal communications commission; b. Information service or telecommunications service, both as defined in the “Telecommunications Act of 1996,” 47 U.S.C. 153, as amended; c. Internet protocol-enabled services, as defined in Section 4927.01 of the Revised Code. 5. “Mobile service” and “telecommunications carrier” have the meanings defined in 47 U.S.C. 153, as amended. 6. “Cable service provider” has the same meaning as in Section 1332.01 of the Revised Code. 7. “Direct-to-home satellite service” has the meaning defined in 47 U.S.C. 303, as amended. 8. “Video service provider” has the same meaning as in Section 1332.21 of the Revised Code. 9. “Sexual act” means any of the following: a. Sexual activity; b. Masturbation; c. An act involving a bodily substance that is performed for the purpose of sexual arousal or gratification; d. Sado-masochistic abuse.

ORC:2917.21.heading: EXAMPLE – TELECOMMUNICATIONS HARASSMENT 2917.21 ORC
ORC:2917.21.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a telecommunication or cause a telecommunication to be made or permit a telecommunication to be made on a telecommunications device controlled by the violator) to another, to wit: (STATE NAME OR PLACE CALLED/CONTACTED), when the caller, to wit (NAME CALLER), knowingly caused the person called/contacted to believe that (he or she) will cause serious physical harm to the (person or property) of (the person called/contacted or a member of the immediate family of the person called/contacted), because of (his or her) (race or color or religion or national origin), to wit: (DESCRIBE PERTINENT PORTIONS OF THE TELECOMMUNICATION INCLUDING DETAILS OF THREATS), in violation of Section 2927.12(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2917.211.heading: DISSEMINATION OF CERTAIN IMAGES 2917.211(B) ORC
ORC:2917.211.variant: DISSEMINATION OF PRIVATE SEXUAL IMAGE WITHOUT CONSENT – F5
ORC:2917.211.text: ____________ did knowingly disseminate a private sexual image, to wit: (DESCRIBE WHAT KIND OF IMAGE AND HOW IT WAS DISSEMINATED) of another person, to wit: (STATE NAME) who is (STATE AGE OF VICTIM), who can be identified from (the image or information displayed in connection with the image by the offender) by means of (state how victim can be identified), and the victim is (in a state of nudity or engaged in sexual act), to wit: (DESCRIBE), and the image was disseminated without consent from the victim and with intent to harm said victim, by means of (STATE HARM), in violation of Section 2917.211(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2917.211.notes: NOTE: For prior convictions of Section 2917.211, a sexually oriented offense, or a child victim-oriented offense, the charge is a felony of the fourth degree. – Prior convictions must be included in the complaint. The court of conviction, date of conviction, case number, and code section of each prior conviction should be written in the complaint language. NOTE: See exceptions in Section 2917.211(E) of the Revised Code.

ORC:2917.211.notes: NOTE: For prior convictions of Section 2917.211, a sexually oriented offense, or a child victim-oriented offense, the charge is a felony of the third degree. – Prior convictions must be included in the complaint. The court of conviction, date of conviction, case number, and code section of each prior conviction should be written in the complaint language. NOTE: See exceptions in Section 2917.211(E) of the Revised Code.

ORC:2917.211.heading: DISSEMINATION OF CERTAIN IMAGES 2917.211(D) ORC

ORC:2917.211.text: ____________ did, in order to (harass, extort, threaten) or cause (physical, emotional, reputational, or economic) harm, knowingly (create or solicit) a fabricated sexual image with the intent to distribute, to wit: (DESCRIBE KIND OF IMAGE AND CIRCUMSTANCES), of another person, to wit: (STATE NAME), and the image was disseminated without consent from the victim, in violation of Section 2917.211(D) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2917.211.notes: NOTE: For prior convictions of Section 2917.211, a sexually oriented offense, or a child victim-oriented offense, the charge is a felony of the third degree. – Prior convictions must be included in the complaint. The court of conviction, date of conviction, case number, and code section of each prior conviction should be written in the complaint language. NOTE: See exceptions in Section 2917.211(E) of the Revised Code. DEFINITIONS 2917.31, 2917.32, AND 2917.33 ORC WEAPON OF MASS DESTRUCTION – means any of the following in Sections 2917.31, 2917.32, and 2917.33: 1. Any weapon that is designed or intended to cause death or serious physical harm through the release, dissemination, or impact of toxic or poisonous chemicals, or their precursors; 2. Any weapon involving a disease organism or biological agent; 3. Any weapon that is designed to release radiation or radioactivity at a level dangerous to human life; 4. Any of the following, except to the extent that the item or device in question is expressly excepted from the definition of “destructive device” pursuant to 18 USC 921(a)(4) and regulations issued under that section: a. Any explosive, incendiary, or poison gas bomb, grenade, rocket having a propellant charge of more than four ounces, missile having an explosive or incendiary charge of more than one-quarter ounce, mine, or similar device; b. Any combination of parts either designed or intended for use in converting any item or device into any item or device described in section 4.a. above and from which an item or device described in that section may be readily assembled.

ORC:2917.31.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to authorized fire or emergency drills.

ORC:2917.31.heading: INDUCING PANIC 2917.31(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2917.31.variant: BY COMMITTING AN OFFENSE – WMD – F4
ORC:2917.31.text: _____________ did (cause the evacuation of a public place or cause serious public inconvenience or cause serious public alarm), to wit: (DESCRIBE LOCATION AND WHAT INCONVENIENCE WAS CAUSED), by committing an offense pertaining to a purported, threatened, or actual use of a weapon of mass destruction, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE SPECIFIC OFFENSE AND SECTION NUMBER), with reckless disregard that its commission would cause serious public (inconvenience or alarm), in violation of Section 2917.31(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2917.31.notes: NOTE: See definition of weapon of mass destruction listed at beginning of Section 2917.31.

ORC:2917.31.heading: INDUCING PANIC 2917.31(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2917.31.variant: BY COMMITTING AN OFFENSE – WMD AND PHYSICAL HARM TO PERSON – F3
ORC:2917.31.text: _____________ did (cause the evacuation of a public place or cause serious public inconvenience or cause serious public alarm), to wit: (DESCRIBE LOCATION AND WHAT INCONVENIENCE WAS CAUSED), by committing an offense pertaining to a purported, threatened, or actual use of a weapon of mass destruction, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE SPECIFIC OFFENSE AND SECTION NUMBER), with reckless disregard that its commission would cause serious public (inconvenience or alarm), and which did result in physical harm to a person, to wit: (DESCRIBE HARM AND NAME OF PERSON), in violation of Section 2917.31(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2917.31.notes: NOTE: See definition of weapon of mass destruction listed at beginning of Section 2917.31.

ORC:2917.31.heading: INDUCING PANIC 2917.31(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2917.31.variant: BY COMMITTING AN OFFENSE – WMD AND ECONOMIC HARM OVER $100,000.00 – F3
ORC:2917.31.text: _____________ did (cause the evacuation of a public place or cause serious public inconvenience or cause serious public alarm), to wit: (DESCRIBE LOCATION AND WHAT INCONVENIENCE WAS CAUSED), by committing an offense pertaining to a purported, threatened, or actual use of a weapon of mass destruction, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE SPECIFIC OFFENSE AND SECTION NUMBER), with reckless disregard that its commission would cause serious public (inconvenience or alarm), and causing economic harm valued at (STATE AMOUNT), in violation of Section 2917.31(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2917.31.notes: NOTE: See definition of weapon of mass destruction listed at beginning of Section 2917.31.

ORC:2917.32.heading: MAKING FALSE ALARMS 2917.32(A)(1) ORC (CCC 2317.32(A)(1))
ORC:2917.32.text: _____________ did (initiate or circulate) a (report or warning) of an (alleged or impending) (fire or explosion or crime or catastrophe), to wit: (DESCRIBE REPORT), knowing that such (report or warning) was false and likely to cause public (inconvenience or alarm), in violation of Section 2917.32(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.32.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to authorized fire or emergency drills.

ORC:2917.32.heading: MAKING FALSE ALARMS 2917.32(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2917.32.variant: FALSE REPORT OF CATASTROPHE – ECONOMIC HARM
ORC:2917.32.text: _____________ did (initiate or circulate) a (report or warning) of an (alleged or impending) (fire or explosion or crime or catastrophe), to wit: (DESCRIBE REPORT), knowing that such (report or warning) was false and likely to cause public (inconvenience or alarm), and causing economic harm valued at (STATE AMOUNT), in violation of Section 2917.32(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2917.32.notes: – VALUE between $1,000.00 and $7,500.00, Making False Alarms, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE between $7,500.00 and $150,000.00, Making False Alarms, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE at more than $150,000.00, Making False Alarms, a felony of the third degree. NOTE: This section does not apply to authorized fire or emergency drills.

ORC:2917.32.heading: MAKING FALSE ALARMS 2917.32(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2917.32.variant: FALSE REPORT OF CATASTROPHE – WMD – F3
ORC:2917.32.text: _____________ did (initiate or circulate) a (report or warning) of an (alleged or impending) (fire or explosion or crime or catastrophe), pertaining to a purported, threatened, or actual use of a weapon of mass destruction, to wit: (DESCRIBE REPORT), knowing that such (report or warning) was false and likely to cause public (inconvenience or alarm), in violation of Section 2917.32(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2917.32.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to authorized fire or emergency drills. NOTE: See definition of weapon of mass destruction listed at beginning of Section 2917.31.

ORC:2917.32.heading: MAKING FALSE ALARMS 2917.32(A)(2) ORC (CCC 2317.32(A)(2))
ORC:2917.32.variant: TRANSMITTING FALSE EMERGENCY REPORT TO PUBLIC/PRIVATE EMERGENCY ORGANIZATION – M1
ORC:2917.32.text: _____________ did knowingly cause a false alarm of a (fire or emergency) to be transmitted, to wit: (DESCRIBE ALARM AND HOW TRANSMITTED), (to or within) a (public or private) organization, to wit: (NAME OF SPECIFIC ORGANIZATION), which deals with emergencies involving a risk of physical harm to (person or property), in violation of Section 2917.32(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.32.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to authorized fire or emergency drills.

ORC:2917.32.heading: MAKING FALSE ALARMS 2917.32(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2917.32.variant: TRANSMITTING FALSE EMERGENCY REPORT TO PUBLIC/PRIVATE EMERGENCY ORGANIZATION – ECONOMIC HARM
ORC:2917.32.text: _____________ did knowingly cause a false alarm of a (fire or emergency) to be transmitted, to wit: (DESCRIBE ALARM AND HOW TRANSMITTED), (to or within) a (public or private) organization, to wit: (NAME OF SPECIFIC ORGANIZATION), which deals with emergencies involving risk of physical harm to (person or property), and causing economic harm valued at (STATE AMOUNT), in violation of Section 2917.32(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2917.32.notes: – VALUE between $1,000.00 and $7,500.00, Making False Alarms, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE between $7,500.00 and $150,000.00, Making False Alarms, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE at more than $150,000.00, Making False Alarms, a felony of the third degree. NOTE: This section does not apply to authorized fire or emergency drills.

ORC:2917.32.heading: MAKING FALSE ALARMS 2917.32(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2917.32.variant: TRANSMITTING FALSE EMERGENCY REPORT TO PUBLIC/PRIVATE EMERGENCY ORGANIZATION – WMD – F3
ORC:2917.32.text: _____________ did knowingly cause a false alarm of a (fire or emergency) pertaining to a purported, threatened, or actual use of a weapon of mass destruction to be transmitted, to wit: (DESCRIBE ALARM AND HOW TRANSMITTED), (to or within) a (public or private) organization, to wit: (NAME OF SPECIFIC ORGANIZATION), which deals with emergencies involving risk of physical harm to (person or property), in violation of Section 2917.32(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2917.32.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to authorized fire or emergency drills. NOTE: See definition of weapon of mass destruction listed at beginning of Section 2917.31.

ORC:2917.32.heading: MAKING FALSE ALARMS 2917.32(A)(3) ORC (CCC 2317.32(A)(3))
ORC:2917.32.text: _____________ did report to a law enforcement agency, to wit: (NAME AGENCY), an (offense or incident), to wit: (DESCRIBE REPORT), which is within the concern of the said agency and knowing that the (offense or incident) did not occur, in violation of Section 2917.32(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.32.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to authorized fire or emergency drills.

ORC:2917.32.heading: MAKING FALSE ALARMS 2917.32(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2917.32.variant: TO LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCY – ECONOMIC HARM
ORC:2917.32.text: _____________ did report to a law enforcement agency, to wit: (NAME AGENCY), an (offense or incident), to wit: (DESCRIBE REPORT), which is within the course of the said agency and knowing that the (offense or incident) did not occur, and causing economic harm valued at (STATE AMOUNT), in violation of 2917.32(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2917.32.notes: – VALUE between $1,000.00 and $7,500.00, Making False Alarms, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE between $7,500.00 and $150,000.00, Making False Alarms, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE at more than $150,000.00, Making False Alarms, a felony of the third degree. NOTE: This section does not apply to authorized fire or emergency drills.

ORC:2917.32.heading: MAKING FALSE ALARMS 2917.32(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2917.32.variant: TO LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCY – WMD – F3
ORC:2917.32.text: _____________ did report to a law enforcement agency, to wit: (NAME AGENCY), an (offense or incident) pertaining to a purported, threatened, or actual use of a weapon of mass destruction, to wit: (DESCRIBE REPORT), which is within the concern of the said agency and knowing that the (offense or incident) did not occur, in violation of Section 2917.32(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2917.32.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to authorized fire or emergency drills. NOTE: See definition of weapon of mass destruction listed at beginning of Section 2917.31.

ORC:2917.32.heading: MAKING FALSE ALARMS 2917.32(A)(4) ORC
ORC:2917.32.variant: FALSE REPORT OF CATASTROPHE – CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE FACILITY – M1
ORC:2917.32.text: _____________ did (initiate or circulate) a (report or warning) of an (alleged or impending) (fire, explosion, crime, or other catastrophe), to wit: (DESCRIBE REPORT), knowing that the (report or warning) was false and likely to impede the operation of a critical infrastructure facility, in violation of Section 2917.32(A) (4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.32.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to authorized fire or emergency drills. NOTE: “Critical infrastructure” has the same meaning as defined in ORC 2911.21(F)(4).

ORC:2917.321.heading: SWATTING 2917.321(B) ORC
ORC:2917.321.text: _____________ did, by means of a (telecommunications device or telecommunications service), report or cause to be reported false or misleading information to a (law enforcement agency, emergency service provider, or public safety answering point), knowing the information to be false or misleading, to wit: (DESCRIBE FALSE OR MISLEADING STATEMENT), with reckless disregard as to whether the report may cause bodily harm to any individual as a direct result of an emergency response to the report, and under circumstances where the report is reasonably likely to cause an emergency response from (a law enforcement agency, emergency service provider, or public safety answering point), and the report does cause an emergency response, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMERGENCY RESPONSE), in violation of Section 2917.321(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2917.321.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to any person conducting an authorized emergency drill.

ORC:2917.321.heading: SWATTING 2917.321(B) ORC
ORC:2917.321.variant: REPORT MISLEADING INFORMATION – CAUSE SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM – F2
ORC:2917.321.text: _____________ did, by means of a (telecommunications device or telecommunications service), report or cause to be reported false or misleading information to a (law enforcement agency, emergency service provider, or public safety answering point), knowing the information to be false or misleading, to wit: (DESCRIBE FALSE OR MISLEADING STATEMENT), with reckless disregard as to whether the report may cause bodily harm to any individual as a direct result of an emergency response to the report, and under circumstances where the report is reasonably likely to cause an emergency response from (a law enforcement agency, emergency service provider, or public safety answering point), and the report does cause an emergency response, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMERGENCY RESPONSE),and the offender’s violation of this section resulted in serious physical harm to another, to wit: (NAME OF VICTIM AND DESCRIBE SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM), in violation of Section 2917.321(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2917.321.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to any person conducting an authorized emergency drill.

ORC:2917.33.heading: UNLAWFUL POSSESSION OR USE OF A HOAX WEAPON OF MASS DESTRUCTION 2917.33(A) ORC
ORC:2917.33.text: _____________ did, without privilege to do so, (manufacture, possess, sell, deliver, display, use, threaten to use, attempt to use, conspire to use, or make readily accessible to others) a hoax weapon of mass destruction with the intent to deceive or otherwise mislead one or more persons into believing that the hoax weapon of mass destruction will cause (terror, bodily harm, or property damage), to wit: (DESCRIBE OFFENSE INCLUDING HOAX WMD), in violation of Section 2917.33(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2917.33.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to any member or employee of the armed forces of the United States, a governmental agency of this state, another state, or the United States, or a private entity, to whom all of the following apply: 1. The member or employee otherwise is engaged in lawful activity within the scope of the member’s or employee’s duties or employment. 2. The member or employee otherwise is duly authorized or licensed to manufacture, possess, sell, deliver, display, or otherwise engage in activity as described in division (A) of this section. 3. The member or employee is in compliance with applicable federal and state law. NOTE: “Hoax weapon of mass destruction” means any device or object that by its design, construction, content, or characteristics appears to be, appears to constitute, or appears to contain, or is represented as being, constituting, or containing, a weapon of mass destruction and to which either of the following applies: 1. It is, in fact, an inoperative facsimile, imitation, counterfeit, or representation of a weapon of mass destruction that does not meet the definition of a weapon of mass destruction. 2. It does not actually contain or constitute a weapon, biological agent, toxin, vector, or delivery system. NOTE: See definition of weapon of mass destruction listed at beginning of Section 2917.31.

CCC:2317.33.heading: IMPROPER USE OF 9–1–1 TELEPHONE SYSTEM CCC 2317.33
CCC:2317.33.text: _____________ did knowingly use the telephone number of the 9–1–1 (with the knowledge that no emergency exists or for non-emergency telephone calls, to wit: (DESCRIBE NATURE OF KNOWLEDGE AND CALL), in violation of Section 2317.33 of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2917.40.heading: CONCERT TICKET SALE 2917.40(B)(1)(a) ORC
ORC:2917.40.variant: SALE NON-RESERVED SEAT FOR LIVE PERFORMANCE – M1
ORC:2917.40.text: _____________ did (sell or offer to sell or offer in return for a donation) a ticket to (NAME PERSON TO WHOM OFFER WAS MADE), that is not numbered and does not correspond to a specific seat for admission to a live entertainment performance, to wit: (DESCRIBE PERFORMANCE INCLUDING LOCATION AND DATE) for which more than 8,000 tickets are offered to the public and held in a restricted area, in violation of Section 2917.40(B)(1)(a) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.40.notes: NOTE: Before filing this offense, consult Section 2917.40 for definitions and exemptions. Also if physical harm is suffered as a result of violating this section, the court may consider imprisonment.

ORC:2917.40.heading: CONCERT TICKET SALE 2917.40(B)(1)(a) ORC
ORC:2917.40.variant: SALE NON-RESERVED SEAT FOR LIVE PERFORMANCE PHYSICAL HARM TO PERSON – M1
ORC:2917.40.text: _____________ did (sell or offer to sell or offer in return for a donation) a ticket to (NAME PERSON TO WHOM OFFER WAS MADE) that is not numbered and does not correspond to a specific seat for admission to a live entertainment performance, to wit: (DESCRIBE PERFORMANCE INCLUDING LOCATION AND DATE), for which more than 8,000 tickets are being offered to the public and held in restricted area and in which physical harm is suffered by a person, incident to the performance, to wit: (STATE NAME AND CIRCUMSTANCES UNDER WHICH HARM WAS SUSTAINED), in violation of Section 2917.40(B)(1)(a) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.40.notes: NOTE: Before filing this offense, consult Section 2917.40 for definitions and exemptions. Also if physical harm is suffered as a result of violating this section, the court may consider imprisonment.

ORC:2917.40.heading: CONCERT TICKET SALE 2917.40(B)(1)(b) ORC
ORC:2917.40.variant: SALE NON-RESERVED SEAT FOR CONCERT – M1
ORC:2917.40.text: _____________ did (sell or offer to sell or offer in return for a donation) a ticket to (NAME PERSON TO WHOM OFFER WAS MADE), that is not numbered and does not correspond to a specific seat for admission to a concert, to wit: (DESCRIBE CONCERT INCLUDING LOCATION AND DATE), for which more than 3,000 tickets are offered to the public, in violation of Section 2917.40(B)(1) (b) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.40.notes: NOTE: Before filing this offense, consult Section 2917.40 for definitions and exemptions. Also if physical harm is suffered as a result of violating this section, the court may consider imprisonment.

ORC:2917.40.heading: CONCERT TICKET SALE 2917.40(B)(1)(b) ORC
ORC:2917.40.variant: SALE NON-RESERVED SEAT FOR CONCERT PHYSICAL HARM TO PERSON – M1
ORC:2917.40.text: _____________ did (sell or offer to sell or offer in return for a donation) a ticket to (NAME PERSON TO WHOM OFFER WAS MADE), that is not numbered and does not correspond to a specific seat for admission to a concert, to wit: (DESCRIBE CONCERT INCLUDING LOCATION AND DATE), for which more than 3,000 tickets are offered to the public and in which physical harm is suffered by a person, incident to the concert, to wit: (STATE NAME AND CIRCUMSTANCES UNDER WHICH HARM WAS SUSTAINED), in violation of Section 2917.40(B)(1)(b) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.40.notes: NOTE: Before filing this offense, consult Section 2917.40 for definitions and exemptions. Also if physical harm is suffered as a result of violating this section, the court may consider imprisonment.

ORC:2917.40.heading: ADVERTISE CONCERT 2917.40(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2917.40.text: _____________ did advertise (a live entertainment performance for which more than 8,000 tickets are being offered to the public without reserved seating or a concert for which more than 3,000 tickets are being offered to the public without reserved seating), to wit: (DESCRIBE PERFORMANCE OR CONCERT AND DATES INCLUDING LOCATION), and said advertisement did not contain the words “Reserved Seats Only,” in violation of Section 2917.40(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.40.notes: NOTE: Before filing this offense, consult Section 2917.40 for definitions and exemptions. Also if physical harm is suffered as a result of violating this section, the court may consider imprisonment.

ORC:2917.40.heading: ADVERTISE CONCERT 2917.40(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2917.40.text: _____________ did advertise (a live entertainment performance for which more than 8,000 tickets are being offered to the public without reserved seating or a concert for which more than 3,000 tickets are being offered to the public without reserved seating), to wit: (DESCRIBE PERFORMANCE OR CONCERT AND DATES, INCLUDING LOCATION), and said advertisement did not contain the words “Reserved Seats Only,” and in which physical harm is suffered by a person, incident to the (performance or concert) to wit: (STATE NAME AND CIRCUMSTANCES UNDER WHICH HARM WAS SUSTAINED), in violation of Section 2917.40(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.40.notes: NOTE: Before filing this offense, consult Section 2917.40 for definitions and exemptions. Also if physical harm is suffered as a result of violating this section, the court may consider imprisonment.

ORC:2917.40.heading: MAINTAIN ENTRANCES TO LIVE PERFORMANCE 2917.40(C) ORC
ORC:2917.40.text: _____________ did, being the person who (owns or operates) a restricted entertainment area, to wit: (DESCRIBE AREA AND LOCATION), fail to properly open, maintain and staff the number of entrances designated by a public official, to wit: (DESCRIBE NUMBER OF ENTRANCES DESIGNATED TO BE OPEN AND WHO MADE DESIGNATION), for a minimum of 90 minutes prior to the scheduled start of a live entertainment performance, to wit: (DESCRIBE PERFORMANCE INCLUDING DATES AND TIMES), which is to be held in the said restricted entertainment area and for which more than 3,000 tickets are being (sold or offered for sale or offered in return for donations), in violation of Section 2917.40(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.40.notes: NOTE: Before filing this offense, consult Section 2917.40 for definitions and exemptions. Also if physical harm is suffered as a result of violating this section, the court may consider imprisonment.

ORC:2917.40.heading: MAINTAIN ENTRANCES TO LIVE PERFORMANCE 2917.40(C) ORC
ORC:2917.40.text: _____________ did, being the person who (owns or operates) a restricted entertainment area, to wit: (DESCRIBE AREA AND LOCATION), fail to properly open, maintain and staff the number of entrances designated by a public official, to wit: (DESCRIBE NUMBER OF ENTRANCES DESIGNATED TO BE OPEN AND WHO MADE DESIGNATION), for a minimum of 90 minutes prior to the scheduled start of a live entertainment performance, to wit: (DESCRIBE PERFORMANCE INCLUDING DATES AND TIMES), which is to be held in the said restricted entertainment area and for which more than 3,000 tickets are being (sold or offered for sale or offered in return for donations), and in which physical harm is suffered by a person, incident to the performance, to wit: (STATE NAME AND CIRCUMSTANCES UNDER WHICH HARM WAS SUSTAINED), in violation of Section 2917.40(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.40.notes: NOTE: Before filing this offense, consult Section 2917.40 for definitions and exemptions. Also if physical harm is suffered as a result of violating this section, the court may consider imprisonment.

ORC:2917.40.heading: CONTRACT FOR LIVE PERFORMANCE NOT IN COMPLIANCE WITH LAW 2917.40(F) ORC
ORC:2917.40.text: _____________ did enter into a contract with (NAME PERSON OR COMPANY) for a live entertainment performance, to wit: (DESCRIBE PERFORMANCE INCLUDING DATES, TIMES AND LOCATION), and the said contract did not comply with the provisions and requirements set down in Section 2917.40 of the Ohio Revised Code, to wit: (DESCRIBE WHAT TERMS WERE OMITTED), in violation of Section 2917.40(F) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.40.notes: NOTE: Before filing this offense, consult Section 2917.40 for definitions and exemptions. Also if physical harm is suffered as a result of violating this section, the court may consider imprisonment.

ORC:2917.40.heading: CONTRACT FOR A LIVE PERFORMANCE NOT IN COMPLIANCE WITH LAW 2917.40(F) ORC
ORC:2917.40.text: _____________ did enter into a contract with (NAME PERSON OR COMPANY) for a live entertainment performance, to wit: (DESCRIBE PERFORMANCE INCLUDING DATES, TIMES AND LOCATION), and the said contract did not comply with the provisions and requirements set down in Section 2917.40 of the Ohio Revised Code, to wit: (DESCRIBE WHAT TERMS WERE OMITTED), and in which physical harm was suffered by a person, incident to the performance, to wit: (STATE NAME AND CIRCUMSTANCES UNDER WHICH HARM WAS SUSTAINED), in violation of Section 2917.40(F) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.40.notes: NOTE: Before filing this offense, consult Section 2917.40 for definitions and exemptions. Also if physical harm is suffered as a result of violating this section, the court may consider imprisonment. DEFINITIONS 2917.41 ORC For purposes of Section 2917.41: PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM – means any of the following: A county transit system (306.01 - 306.13 ORC); a regional transit authority (306.30 - 306.71 ORC); or a regional transit commission (306.80 - 306.90 ORC).

ORC:2917.41.heading: MISCONDUCT INVOLVING A PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM 2917.41(A) ORC (CCC 2317.41(B))
ORC:2917.41.text: _____________ did evade the payment of a known fare for a public transportation system, to wit: (DESCRIBE HOW FARE WAS EVADED, FARE AND SYSTEM INVOLVED), in violation of Section 2917.41(A) of the Ohio Revised Code , a misdemeanor of the fourth degree or in violation of Section 2317.41(B) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.41.notes: NOTE: See definition of public transportation system listed at beginning of Section 2917.41.

ORC:2917.41.heading: MISCONDUCT INVOLVING A PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM 2917.41(B) ORC (CCC 2317.41(C))
ORC:2917.41.text: _____________ did alter a (transfer or pass or ticket or token) of a public transportation system, to wit: (DESCRIBE ALTERATION OF ITEM AND SYSTEM INVOLVED), with the purpose of (evading the payment of a fare to or defrauding) the transportation system, in violation of Section 2917.41(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree or in violation of Section 2317.41(C) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.41.notes: NOTE: See definition of public transportation system listed at beginning of Section 2917.41.

ORC:2917.41.heading: MISCONDUCT INVOLVING A PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM 2917.41(C)(1) ORC (CCC 2317.41(L)(1))
ORC:2917.41.text: _____________ did while in (a facility or a vehicle) of a public transportation system, to wit: (DESCRIBE LOCATION AND SYSTEM), play a sound equipment without the proper use of a private earphone, to wit: (DESCRIBE EQUIPMENT AND MANNER USED), in violation of Section 2917.41(C)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor or in violation of Section 2317.41(L)(1) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.41.notes: NOTE: See definition of public transportation system listed at beginning of Section 2917.41.

ORC:2917.41.heading: MISCONDUCT INVOLVING A PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM 2917.41(C)(2) ORC (CCC 2317.41(L)(2))
ORC:2917.41.variant: SMOKE OR EAT OR DRINK WHERE PROHIBITED – M1
ORC:2917.41.text: _____________ did while in (a facility or a vehicle) of a public transportation system, to wit: (DESCRIBE LOCATION AND SYSTEM), (smoke or eat or drink) in an area clearly marked prohibiting such, in violation of Section 2917.41(C)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor or in violation of Section 2317.41(L)(2) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.41.notes: NOTE: See definition of public transportation system listed at beginning of Section 2917.41.

ORC:2917.41.heading: MISCONDUCT INVOLVING A PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM 2917.41(C)(3) ORC (CCC 2317.41(L)(3))
ORC:2917.41.text: _____________ did (while in a facility of a public transportation system or a vehicle of a public transportation system), to wit: (DESCRIBE LOCATION), expectorate upon a person, facility, or vehicle to wit: (NAME PERSON, IF APPLICABLE AND DESCRIBE CONDUCT), in violation of Section 2917.41(C)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor or in violation of Section 2317.41(L)(3) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.41.notes: NOTE: See definition of public transportation system listed at beginning of Section 2917.41.

ORC:2917.41.heading: MISCONDUCT INVOLVING A PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM 2917.41(D) ORC (CCC 2317.41(D))
ORC:2917.41.variant: MARK OR DRAW ON VEHICLE OR FACILITY – M1
ORC:2917.41.text: _____________ did (write or deface or draw or mark) on any (facility, property, seats, vehicle, or walls) of a public transportation system, to wit: (DESCRIBE ACT, FACILITY OR VEHICLE INVOLVED AND THE TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM INCLUDING LOCATION), in violation of Section 2917.41(D) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the third degree or in violation of Section 2317.41(D) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.41.notes: NOTE: See definition of public transportation system listed at beginning of Section 2917.41.

ORC:2917.41.heading: MISCONDUCT INVOLVING A PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM 2917.41(E) ORC (CCC 2317.41(A))
ORC:2917.41.variant: FAIL TO COMPLY WITH TRANSIT OFFICER’S ORDER – M1
ORC:2917.41.text: _____________ did fail to comply with the lawful order of a public transportation system police officer, to wit: (NAME OFFICER AND DESCRIBE BEHAVIOR), in violation of Section 2917.41(E) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree or in violation of Section 2317.41(A) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.41.notes: NOTE: See definition of public transportation system listed at beginning of Section 2917.41.

ORC:2917.41.heading: MISCONDUCT INVOLVING A PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM 2917.41(E) ORC (CCC 2317.41(A))
ORC:2917.41.text: _____________ did (resist or obstruct or abuse) a public transportation system officer in the performance of the officer’s duties, to wit: (NAME OFFICER AND DESCRIBE ACT), in violation of Section 2917.41(E) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree or in violation of Section 2317.41(A) of the Columbus City Code, misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2917.41.notes: NOTE: See definition of public transportation system listed at beginning of Section 2917.41.

CCC:2317.41.heading: MISCONDUCT INVOLVING A PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM CCC 2317.41(E)
CCC:2317.41.variant: THROWING OBJECTS AT, WITHIN, OR FROM PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION – M1
CCC:2317.41.text: _____________ did throw a (rock, stone, bottle, missile, projectile, snowball, or other hard substance) (at, within, or from) a public transportation system, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2317.41(E) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
CCC:2317.41.notes: NOTE: See definition of public transportation system listed at beginning of Section 2917.41.

CCC:2317.41.heading: MISCONDUCT INVOLVING A PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM CCC 2317.41(F)
CCC:2317.41.text: _____________ did knowingly (strike or push or shove or assault or unlawfully touch) a public transportation system (driver or operator), to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME, IDENTIFY TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM AND DESCRIBE ACT), in violation of Section 2317.41(F) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
CCC:2317.41.notes: NOTE: See definition of public transportation system listed at beginning of Section 2917.41.

CCC:2317.41.heading: MISCONDUCT INVOLVING A PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM CCC 2317.41(G)
CCC:2317.41.variant: TAMPER WITH PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION EQUIPMENT – M1
CCC:2317.41.text: _____________ did, without privilege to do so, knowingly tamper with (equipment or accessories or operator’s controls) on a public transportation system vehicle, to wit: (IDENTIFY TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM AND DESCRIBE ACT), in violation of Section 2317.41(G) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
CCC:2317.41.notes: NOTE: See definition of public transportation system listed at beginning of Section 2917.41.

CCC:2317.41.heading: MISCONDUCT INVOLVING A PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM CCC 2317.41(H)
CCC:2317.41.variant: CAUSE PASSENGER, DRIVER, OPERATOR TO FEAR PHYSICAL HARM – M1
CCC:2317.41.text: _____________ did knowingly cause a (passenger or driver or operator) of a public transportation system vehicle, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME AND IDENTIFY TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM) to believe that the offender, to wit: (STATE OFFENDER’S NAME) will cause physical harm to said (passenger or driver or operator), in violation of Section 2317.41(H) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
CCC:2317.41.notes: NOTE: See definition of public transportation system listed at beginning of Section 2917.41.

CCC:2317.41.heading: MISCONDUCT INVOLVING A PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM CCC 2317.41(I)
CCC:2317.41.variant: FAIL OR REFUSE TO LEAVE – M1
CCC:2317.41.text: _____________ did, without privilege to do so, and while on a public transportation system vehicle, negligently (fail or refuse) to leave such vehicle, to wit: (IDENTIFY TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM) upon being notified to do so by (the driver or operator or an authorized agent) of the public transportation system, to wit: (STATE NAME), in violation of Section 2317.41(I) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
CCC:2317.41.notes: NOTE: See definition of public transportation system listed at beginning of Section 2917.41.

CCC:2317.41.heading: MISCONDUCT INVOLVING A PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM CCC 2317.41(J)(1)
CCC:2317.41.text: _____________ did, cause (inconvenience or annoyance or alarm) to (an operator or a driver or a passenger) on a public transportation system vehicle, to wit: (NAME PERSON AND IDENTIFY TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM), by engaging in (fighting or threatening harm to persons or threatening harm to property or engaging in violent behavior or engaging in turbulent behavior), to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT), in violation of Section 2317.41(J)(1) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
CCC:2317.41.notes: NOTE: See definition of public transportation system listed at beginning of Section 2917.41.

CCC:2317.41.heading: MISCONDUCT INVOLVING A PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM CCC 2317.41(J)(2)
CCC:2317.41.text: _____________ did, cause (inconvenience or annoyance or alarm) to (an operator or a driver or a passenger) on a public transportation system vehicle, to wit: (STATE NAME), by (insulting or taunting or challenging) a person, to wit: (STATE NAME) under circumstances where such conduct was likely to provoke a violent response or breach of the peace, to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT), in violation of Section 2317.41(J)(2) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
CCC:2317.41.notes: NOTE: See definition of public transportation system listed at beginning of Section 2917.41.

CCC:2317.41.heading: MISCONDUCT INVOLVING A PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM CCC 2317.41(J)(3)
CCC:2317.41.text: _____________ did, cause (inconvenience or annoyance of alarm) to another, to wit: (STATE NAME) by purposely (hindering or preventing) the (ingress or egress or movement) of (an operator or a driver or a passenger) on a public transportation system vehicle, to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT AND NAME TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM), so as to interfere with the rights of others, in violation of Section 2317.41(J)(3) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
CCC:2317.41.notes: NOTE: See definition of public transportation system listed at beginning of Section 2917.41.

CCC:2317.41.heading: MISCONDUCT INVOLVING A PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM CCC 2317.41(K)
CCC:2317.41.text: _____________ did enter or remain inside a public transportation system vehicle while (voluntarily intoxicated, or under the influence of alcohol or a drug of abuse), to wit: (DESCRIBE) and (engage in conduct likely to be offensive or cause inconvenience, annoyance, or alarm) to (the driver, operator, or any passenger) of a public transportation system vehicle, to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT), in violation of Section 2317.41(K) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
CCC:2317.41.notes: NOTE: See definition of public transportation system listed at beginning of Section 2917.41.

CCC:2317.41.heading: MISCONDUCT INVOLVING A PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM CCC 2317.41(M)
CCC:2317.41.variant: ENTRY AFTER NOTICE OF UNAUTHORIZED ACCESS PREVIOUSLY GIVEN TO OFFENDER – M1
CCC:2317.41.text: _________ did enter upon a public transportation system vehicle, to wit: (NAME VEHICLE AND TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM) as to which notice against unauthorized (access or presence) is given by actual communication to the offender, to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT OF OFFENDER AND SPECIFICS OF ACTUAL COMMUNICATION GIVEN AGAINST UNAUTHORIZED ACCESS – INCLUDE COURT CASE/NUMBER IF APPLICABLE), in violation of Columbus City Code 2317.41(M), a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2917.46.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE BLOCK PARENT SYMBOL 2917.46(A) ORC
ORC:2917.46.text: _____________ did, with intent to identify a home or building as a block parent building, to wit: (DESCRIBE ADDRESS OR LOCATION OR STRUCTURE), display the block parent symbol as adopted by the state Board of Education without being authorized as required under the Ohio Revised Code, in violation of Section 2917.46(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor.
ORC:2917.46.notes: NOTE: Proper authorization is pursuant to Sections 3301.076 or 3313.204 ORC.

ORC:2917.46.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE BLOCK PARENT SYMBOL 2917.46(B) ORC
ORC:2917.46.text: _____________ did, with intent to identify a building as a block parent home or building, to wit: (DESCRIBE ADDRESS OR LOCATION OF STRUCTURE), display a symbol that falsely gives the appearance of being the block parent symbol adopted by the board of education, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE FALSE SYMBOL), in violation of Section 2917.46(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor.

ORC:2917.46.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE MCGRUFF HOUSE SYMBOL 2917.46(C) ORC
ORC:2917.46.text: _____________ did, with intent to identify a home or building as a McGruff House Program home or building, to wit: (DESCRIBE ADDRESS OR LOCATION OF STRUCTURE), display the McGruff House symbol as adopted by the Division of Criminal Justice Services in the state Department of Public Safety without being authorized as required under the Ohio Revised Code, in violation of Section 2917.46(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor.
ORC:2917.46.notes: NOTE: Proper authorization is pursuant to Sections 3313.206 or 5502.62 ORC.

ORC:2917.46.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE MCGRUFF HOUSE SYMBOL 2917.46(D) ORC
ORC:2917.46.text: _____________ did, with intent to identify a home or building as a McGruff House Program home or building, to wit: (DESCRIBE ADDRESS OR LOCATION OF STRUCTURE), display a symbol that falsely gives the appearance of being the McGruff House symbol as adopted by the Division of Criminal Justice Services in the state Department of Public Safety, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE FALSE SYMBOL), in violation of Section 2917.46(D) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor.
ORC:2917.46.notes: NOTE: Proper authorization is pursuant to Sections 3313.206 or 5502.62 ORC.

ORC:2917.47.heading: IMPROPERLY HANDLING INFECTIOUS AGENTS 2917.47(A) ORC
ORC:2917.47.text: _____________ did, knowingly, without being permitted by state or federal law, (possess or send or receive) (an isolate or a derivative of an isolate) of an infectious agent, to wit: (NAME AGENT AND DESCRIBE CONDUCT), in violation of Section 2917.47(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2917.47.heading: IMPROPERLY HANDLING INFECTIOUS AGENTS 2917.47(A) ORC
ORC:2917.47.variant: CAUSE THE SENDING OR RECEIVING – F2
ORC:2917.47.text: _____________ did, without being permitted by state or federal law, cause to be (sent or received) (an isolate or a derivative of an isolate) of an infectious agent, to wit: (NAME AGENT AND DESCRIBE CONDUCT), in violation of Section 2917.47(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.

CCC:2317.48.heading: SOLICITING BUSINESS FOR BONDSMEN CCC 2317.48
CCC:2317.48.text: _____________ did, with purpose to solicit business for bail bondsmen, to wit: (NAME BAIL BONDSMEN/COMPANY AND DESCRIBE CONDUCT) loiter (in or around) a (court or public place), to wit: (NAME LOCATION), in violation of Section 2317.48 of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the third degree.

ORC:2919.01.heading: BIGAMY 2919.01(A) ORC
ORC:2919.01.text: _____________ did, while being married to (STATE NAME OF SPOUSE), marry another, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON MARRIED), in the State of Ohio, on (STATE SPECIFIC DATE OF SECOND MARRIAGE), in violation of Section 2919.01(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.01.notes: NOTE: It is an affirmative defense if the violator’s spouse was absent for five continuous years and not known to be alive.

ORC:2919.01.heading: BIGAMY 2919.01(A) ORC
ORC:2919.01.variant: MARRY AND COHABIT WITH ANOTHER PERSON – M1
ORC:2919.01.text: _____________ did, while being married to (STATE NAME OF SPOUSE), marry another and continue to cohabit with such other person in the State of Ohio, to wit: (STATE NAME AND DATE OF SECOND MARRIAGE), in violation of Section 2919.01(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.01.notes: NOTE: It is an affirmative defense if the violator’s spouse was absent for five continuous years and not known to be alive. DEFINITION – ABORTION 2919.11 ORC The purposeful termination of a human pregnancy by any person, including the pregnant woman herself, with an intention other than to produce a live birth or to remove a dead fetus or embryo. Abortion is the practice of medicine or surgery for the purposes of Section 4731.41 of the Revised Code.

ORC:2919.12.heading: UNLAWFUL ABORTION 2919.12(A) ORC
ORC:2919.12.variant: WITHOUT CONSENT OF PREGNANT WOMAN – M1
ORC:2919.12.text: _____________ did (perform or induce) an abortion, to wit: (DESCRIBE MEANS), without the informed consent of the pregnant woman, to wit: (STATE NAME OF WOMAN), in violation of Section 2919.12(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2919.12.heading: UNLAWFUL ABORTION 2919.12(A) ORC
ORC:2919.12.variant: WITHOUT CONSENT OF PREGNANT WOMAN PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F4
ORC:2919.12.text: _____________ did (perform or induce) an abortion, to wit: (DESCRIBE MEANS), without the informed consent of the pregnant woman, to wit: (STATE NAME OF WOMAN) and having been previously convicted of Section 2919.12 of the ORC, on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT), in violation of Section 2919.12(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2919.12.heading: UNLAWFUL ABORTION 2919.12(B) ORC
ORC:2919.12.variant: MINOR WITHOUT NOTIFICATION OR COURT ORDER OR WRITTEN CONSENT – M1
ORC:2919.12.text: _____________ did knowingly (perform or induce) an abortion upon an unmarried, unemancipated, pregnant woman who was under the age of eighteen years, to wit: (STATE NAME AND AGE), without the required actual or constructive notification being given to a person designed under the law or without the written consent of the woman’s parent, guardian or custodian or without a proper court order or constructive court order, in violation of Section 2919.12(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.12.notes: NOTE: The law requires one of the following conditions complied with prior to the performance of an abortion upon an unmarried woman under 18 years of age. The conditions are as follows: (A) Actual notification (24 hours prior to abortion) or constructive notification by certified and regular mail (48 hours prior to abortion) to the woman’s parent, guardian, or custodian or in lieu of a parent then the same notification to a specified brother, sister, stepparent or grandparent who is over 21 years of age and when proper affidavits are filed with juvenile court; (B) Written consent from one of the woman’s parents, guardian or custodian; (C) A court order issued by the juvenile court authorizing the abortion (Section 2151.85 ORC); (D) Constructive authorization by inaction of juvenile court or the court of appeals pursuant to Section 2151.85 (B)(1) or 2505.07.3 (A) ORC; (E) Parent, guardian, custodian, or specified relative notified in accordance with the statute clearly and unequivocally expresses he or she does not wish to consult with the woman; (F) Reasonable efforts to give actual notice to appropriate person has failed, and 48 hours constructive notice has been given in manner specified in statute. NOTE: It is an affirmative defense under this section if an abortion is immediately necessary because of a serious risk to the woman’s life or if the woman has provided misleading or incorrect information about herself or the people to be notified. “UNEMANCIPATED” means a woman unmarried; under 18; not in the armed services; not employed and self-subsisting; and not otherwise independent of parent’s, guardian’s, or custodian’s care and control.

ORC:2919.12.heading: UNLAWFUL ABORTION 2919.12(B) ORC
ORC:2919.12.variant: MINOR WITHOUT NOTIFICATION OR COURT ORDER OR WRITTEN CONSENT – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F5
ORC:2919.12.text: _____________ did knowingly (perform or induce) an abortion upon an unmarried, unemancipated, pregnant woman who was under the age of eighteen years, to wit: (STATE NAME AND AGE), without the required actual or constructive notification being given to a person designated under the law or without the written consent of the woman’s parent, guardian or custodian or without a proper court order or constructive court order, and being previously convicted of Section 2919.12 ORC on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT), in violation of Section 2919.12(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2919.121.heading: UNLAWFUL ABORTION 2919.121 ORC
ORC:2919.121.text: ______________ did, knowingly, perform or induce an abortion upon a pregnant minor, in violation of Section 2919.12.1 of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.121.notes: EXCEPTION: One of the following exceptions must be made: (A) The attending physician has secured the informed written consent of the minor and one parent, guardian, or custodian; or (B) The minor is emancipated and the attending physician has received her written informed consent; or (C) The minor has been authorized to consent to the abortion by a court order issued pursuant to division C of this section, and the attending physician has received her informed written consent; or (D) The court has given its consent in accordance with Division C of this section and the minor is having the abortion willingly. NOTE: A minor shall be considered emancipated if the minor has married, entered the armed services of the United States, become employed and self-subsisting, or has otherwise become independent from the care and control of her parent, guardian or custodian. It is an affirmative defense under this section if an abortion is immediately necessary because of a serious risk to the woman’s life or physical health from the continuation of her pregnancy.

ORC:2919.121.heading: UNLAWFUL ABORTION 2919.121 ORC
ORC:2919.121.text: _____________ did, knowingly, perform or induce an abortion upon a pregnant minor, the said (STATE ACCUSED’S NAME) having previously been convicted of an offense of Unlawful Abortion, to wit: on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT), in violation of Section 2919.12.1 of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2919.123.heading: UNLAWFUL DISTRIBUTION OF ABORTION-INDUCING DRUG 2919.123(A) ORC
ORC:2919.123.text: _____________ did knowingly (give, sell, dispense, administer, otherwise provide, or prescribe) RU-486 (mifepristone) to another, to wit: (NAME), for the purpose of inducing an abortion in any person or enabling the other person to induce an abortion in any person and said offender is not a physician who has satisfied all the criteria established by federal law in order to provide RU- 486 for inducing abortions, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE), in violation of Section 2919.123(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2919.123.heading: UNLAWFUL DISTRIBUTION OF ABORTION-INDUCING DRUG 2919.123(A) ORC
ORC:2919.123.text: _____________ did knowingly (give, sell, dispense, administer, otherwise provide, or prescribe) RU-486 (mifepristone) to another, to wit: (NAME), for the purpose of inducing an abortion in any person or enabling the other person to induce an abortion in any person and said offender is not a physician who has satisfied all the criteria established by federal law in order to provide RU-486 for inducing abortions, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE), and (STATE OFFENDER’S NAME) having been previously convicted of violating (this section or section 2919.12, 2919.121, 2919.13, 2919.14, 2919.151, 2919.17, or 2919.18 of the Revised Code), to wit: on (STATE DATE), in (STATE NAME OF COURT) (STATE CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2919.123(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2919.123.heading: UNLAWFUL DISTRIBUTION OF ABORTION-INDUCING DRUG 2919.123(B) ORC
ORC:2919.123.variant: FAIL TO COMPLY WITH FEDERAL LAW – F4
ORC:2919.123.text: _____________, a physician who provided RU-486 (mifepristone) to another, to wit: (NAME), for the purpose of inducing an abortion, did knowingly fail to comply with the applicable requirements of a federal law that pertains to follow-up examinations or care for persons to whom or for whom RU-486 (mifepristone) is provided for the purpose of inducing an abortion, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE AND FEDERAL LAW VIOLATED), in violation of Section 2919.123(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2919.123.heading: UNLAWFUL DISTRIBUTION OF ABORTION-INDUCING DRUG 2919.123(B) ORC
ORC:2919.123.variant: FAIL TO COMPLY WITH FEDERAL LAW – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F3
ORC:2919.123.text: _____________, a physician who provided RU-486 (mifepristone) to another, to wit: (NAME), for the purpose of inducing an abortion, did knowingly fail to comply with the applicable requirements of a federal law that pertains to follow-up examinations or care for persons to whom or for whom RU-486 (mifepristone) is provided for the purpose of inducing an abortion, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE AND FEDERAL LAW VIOLATED), and (STATE OFFENDER’S NAME) having been previously convicted of violating (this section or section 2919.12, 2919.121, 2919.13, 2919.14, 2919.151, 2919.17, or 2919.18 of the Revised Code), to wit: on (STATE DATE), in (STATE NAME OF COURT) (STATE CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2919.123(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2919.123.heading: UNLAWFUL DISTRIBUTION OF ABORTION-INDUCING DRUG 2919.123(C) (2) ORC
ORC:2919.123.text: _____________, a physician who provided RU-486 (mifepristone) to another, to wit: (NAME) for the purpose of inducing an abortion, did knowingly fail to file a report required under Section 2919.123(C)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE), in violation of Section 2919.123(C)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2919.123.heading: UNLAWFUL DISTRIBUTION OF ABORTION-INDUCING DRUG 2919.123(C) (2) ORC
ORC:2919.123.variant: FAIL TO REPORT – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F3
ORC:2919.123.text: _____________, a physician who provided RU-486 (mifepristone) to another, to wit: (NAME) for the purpose of inducing an abortion, did knowingly fail to file a report required under Section 2919.123(C)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE), and (STATE OFFENDER’S NAME) having been previously convicted of violating (this section or section 2919.12, 2919.121, 2919.13, 2919.14, 2919.151, 2919.17, or 2919.18 of the Revised Code), to wit: on (STATE DATE), in (STATE NAME OF COURT) (STATE CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2919.123(C)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2919.13.heading: ABORTION MANSLAUGHTER 2919.13(A) ORC
ORC:2919.13.text: _____________ did purposely take the life of a child born by an attempted abortion to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), which child was alive when removed from the uterus of a pregnant woman, to wit: (STATE NAME OF WOMAN), in violation of Section 2919.13(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the first degree.

ORC:2919.13.heading: ABORTION MANSLAUGHTER 2919.13(B) ORC
ORC:2919.13.text: _____________ did perform an abortion, to wit: (DESCRIBE MEANS), and failed to take measures required by the exercise of medical judgment, in light of the attending circumstances, to preserve the life of a child who was alive when removed from the uterus of a pregnant woman, to wit: (STATE NAME OF WOMAN AND DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2919.13(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the first degree.

ORC:2919.14.heading: ABORTION TRAFFICKING 2919.14 ORC
ORC:2919.14.variant: EXPERIMENT UPON OR SELL HUMAN CONCEPTION – M1
ORC:2919.14.text: _____________ did (experiment upon or sell) the product of human conception which has been aborted, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2919.14 of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.14.notes: NOTE: Experiment as used in this section does not apply to autopsies made pursuant to Section 313.13 and 2108.50 of the Ohio Revised Code.

ORC:2919.151.heading: PARTIAL BIRTH FETICIDE 2919.151 ORC
ORC:2919.151.text: _____________ did knowingly perform a partial birth feticide, when the fetus was viable, on a pregnant woman when the procedure was not necessary, in reasonable medical judgment, to preserve the life or health of the mother as a result of the mother’s life or health being endangered by a serious risk of the substantial and irreversible impairment of a major bodily function, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2919.151 of the Ohio Revised Code – a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2919.151.heading: PARTIAL BIRTH FETICIDE 2919.151 ORC
ORC:2919.151.text: _____________ did knowingly perform a partial birth feticide, when the fetus was not viable, on a pregnant woman when the procedure was not necessary, in reasonable medical judgment, to preserve the life or health of the mother as a result of the mother’s life or health being endangered by serious risk of the substantial and irreversible impairment of a major bodily function, to wit: DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2919.151 of the Ohio Revised Code – a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2919.151.notes: DEFINITIONS 2919.16 FERTILIZATION – the fusion of a human spermatozoon with a human ovum. GESTATIONAL AGE OR GESTATION – the age of an unborn child as calculated from the first day of the last menstrual period of a pregnant woman HEALTH CARE FACILITY – a hospital, clinic, ambulatory surgical treatment center, other center, medical school, office of a physician, infirmary, dispensary, medical training institution, or other institution or location in or at which medical care, treatment, or diagnosis. HOSPITAL – public health centers and general, tuberculosis, mental, chronic disease, and other types of hospitals, and related facilities, such as laboratories, outpatient departments, nurses’ home facilities, extended care facilities, self-care units and central service facilities operated in connection with hospitals, and also includes education and training facilities for health professions personnel operated as an integral part of a hospital, but does not include any hospital furnishing primarily domiciliary care. LIVE BIRTH – the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of human conception that after such expulsion or extraction breathes or shows any other evidence of life such as beating of the heart, pulsation of the umbilical cord, or definite movement of voluntary muscles, whether or not the umbilical cord has been cut or the placenta is attached. MEDICAL EMERGENCY – a condition that, in the physician’s good faith and medical judgment, based upon the facts known to the physician at that time, so complicates the woman’s pregnancy as to necessitate the immediate performance or inducement of an abortion in order to prevent the death of the pregnant woman or to avoid a serious risk of the substantial and irreversible impairment of a major bodily function of the pregnant woman that delay in the performance or inducement of the abortion would create. PHYSICIAN – any person who is licensed to practice medicine and surgery or osteopathic medicine and surgery by the state medical board. PREGNANT – the human female reproductive condition, that commences with fertilization, of having a developing fetus. PREGNANCY – the condition of being pregnant PREMATURE INFANT – a human whose live birth occurs prior to thirty-eight weeks of gestational age SERIOUS RISK OF THE SUBSTANTIAL AND IRREVERSIBLE IMPAIRMENT OF A MAJOR BODILY FUNCTION – any medically diagnosed condition that so complicates the pregnancy of the woman as to directly or indirectly cause the substantial and irreversible impairment of a major bodily function. A medically diagnosed condition that constitutes a “serious risk of the substantial and irreversible impairment of a major bodily function” includes pre-eclampsia, inevitable abortion, and premature rupture of the membranes, may include, but is not limited to, diabetes and multiple sclerosis, and does not include a condition related to the woman’s mental health. UNBORN CHILD – any individual organism of the species homo sapiens from fertilization until live birth VIABLE – the stage of development of a human fetus at which in the determination of a physician, based on the particular facts of a woman’s pregnancy that are known to the physician and in light of medical technology and information reasonably available to the physician, there is a realistic possibility of the maintaining and nourishing of a life outside of the womb with or without temporary artificial life-sustaining support.

ORC:2919.17.heading: TERMINATING OR ATTEMPTING TO TERMINATE HUMAN PREGNANCY AFTER VIABILITY 2919.17 ORC
ORC:2919.17.variant: INDUCE AN ABORTION IF UNBORN HUMAN IS VIABLE – F4
ORC:2919.17.text: _____________ did purposely perform or induce or attempt to perform or induce an abortion upon a pregnant woman when the unborn human was viable, in violation of Section 2919.17 of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2919.17.notes: EXCEPTION: If the abortion is performed or induced or attempted to be performed or induced by a physician and that physician determines, in good faith and in the exercise of reasonable medical judgment that the abortion is necessary to prevent the death of the pregnant woman or a serious risk of the substantial and irreversible impairment of a major bodily function of the pregnant woman or after making a determination relative of the viability of the unborn human in conformity with Division A of Revised Code Section 2919.18 that the unborn human is not viable.

ORC:2919.17.heading: TERMINATING OR ATTEMPTING TO TERMINATE HUMAN PREGNANCY AFTER VIABILITY 2919.17 ORC
ORC:2919.17.variant: INDUCE AN ABORTION IF UNBORN HUMAN IS VIABLE – F4
ORC:2919.17.text: _____________ did, being a physician, purposely perform or induce or attempt to perform or induce an abortion upon a pregnant woman when the unborn human was viable, in violation of Section 2919.17 of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2919.17.notes: EXCEPTION: Each of the following conditions must be satisfied (A) the physician certifies in writing that he has determined, in good faith, and the exercise of reasonable medical judgment, that the abortion is necessary to prevent the death of the pregnant woman or a serious risk of the substantial and irreversible impairment of a major bodily function of the pregnant woman; and (B) the determination referred to above is concurred in by at least one other physician who certifies in writing that the concurring physician has determined, in good faith and the exercise of reasonable medical judgment, and following a review of the available medical records of and any available test results pertaining to the pregnant woman, that the abortion is necessary to prevent the death of the pregnant woman or a serious risk of the substantial and irreversible impairment of a major bodily function of the pregnant woman; and (C) the abortion is performed or induced or attempted to be performed or induced in a health care facility that has or has access to appropriate neonatal services for premature infants; and (D) the physician who performs or induces or attempts to perform or induce the abortion terminates or attempts to terminate the pregnancy in the manner that provides the best opportunity for the unborn human to survive, unless that physician determines, in good faith and in the exercise of reasonable medical judgment, that the termination of the pregnancy in that manner poses a significant greater risk of the death of the pregnant woman or serious risk of the substantial and irreversible impairment of a major bodily function of the pregnant woman than would other available methods of abortion; and (E) the physician who performs or induces or attempts to perform or induce the abortion has arranged for the attendance in the same room in which the abortion is to be performed or induced or attempted to be performed or induced of at least one other physician who is to take control of, provide immediate medical care for, and take all reasonable steps necessary to preserve the life and health of the unborn human immediately upon the unborn human’s complete expulsion or extraction from the pregnant woman.

ORC:2919.18.heading: FAILURE TO PERFORM VIABILITY TESTING 2919.18(A) ORC
ORC:2919.18.variant: AFTER TWENTIETH WEEK OF GESTATION – M4
ORC:2919.18.text: _____________ did, being a physician, perform or induce or attempt to perform or induce, an abortion, upon a pregnant woman after the beginning of her twentieth week of gestation, in violation of Section 2919.18(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2919.18.notes: EXCEPTION: Unless the physician determines in good faith medical judgment, that the unborn child is not viable, and the physician makes that determination after performing a medical examination of the pregnant woman and after performing or causing the performance of those tests for assessing gestational age, weight, lung maturity, or other tests that the physician believes are necessary to determine whether an unborn child is viable.

ORC:2919.18.heading: FAILURE TO PERFORM VIABILITY TESTING, 2919.18(B) ORC
ORC:2919.18.variant: AFTER TWENTIETH WEEK OF GESTATION – M4
ORC:2919.18.text: _____________ did, being a physician, perform or induce or attempt to perform or induce an abortion, upon a pregnant woman after the beginning of her twentieth week of pregnancy without first entering the determination described in Division (A)and the associated findings of the medical examination and tests in the medical record of the woman, in violation of Section 2919.18(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2919.18.notes: NOTE: Divisions (A) and (B) do not prohibit a physician from performing or inducing or attempting to perform or induce an abortion on a pregnant woman after the beginning of her twentieth week of pregnancy if a medical emergency exists.

ORC:4731.41.heading: PRACTICE OF MEDICINE OR SURGERY WITHOUT A CERTIFICATE 4731.41 ORC
ORC:4731.41.text: _____________ did practice (medicine or surgery), to wit: did perform an abortion, upon (STATE NAME OF WOMAN), by means of (DESCRIBE MEANS), without a certificate from a state medical board, in violation of Section 4731.41 of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:4731.41.notes: NOTE: Also consult Section 4731.41 ORC for the unlicensed advertising or opening of an office to perform abortions.

ORC:4731.41.heading: PRACTICE OF MEDICINE OR SURGERY WITHOUT A CERTIFICATE 4731.41 ORC
ORC:4731.41.variant: PERFORM AN ABORTION – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F4
ORC:4731.41.text: _____________ did practice (medicine or surgery), to wit: did perform an abortion upon (STATE NAME OF WOMAN) by means of (DESCRIBE MEANS), without a certificate from a state medical board, and having been previously convicted of Section 4731.41 ORC, on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT), in violation of Section 4731.41 of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:4731.41.notes: NOTE: Section 2919.11 ORC states that an abortion is the practice of medicine or surgery for the purposes of Section 4731.41 of the Ohio Revised Code. NOTE: Section 4731.41 applies to any unlicensed person who performs an abortion, including a self-induced abortion by a pregnant woman.

ORC:2919.201.heading: ABORTION PROHIBITED WHEN PROBABLE POST-FERTILIZATION AGE OF UNBORN CHILD IS TWENTY WEEKS OR GREATER 2919.201(A) ORC
ORC:2919.201.variant: TERMINATING PREGNANCY OF PAIN-CAPABLE UNBORN CHILD – F4
ORC:2919.201.text: _____________ did purposely (perform, induce, attempt to perform, or attempt to induce) an abortion on a pregnant woman when the probable post-fertilization age of the unborn child is twenty weeks or greater, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES AND PERSONS INVOLVED), in violation of Section 2919.201(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2919.201.notes: NOTE: It is an affirmative defense to a charge under this section that the abortion was purposely performed or induced, or purposely attempted to be performed or induced, by a physician and that the physician determined in the physician’s reasonable medical judgment, based on the facts known to the physician at that time, that either of the following applied: (A) The probable post-fertilization age of the unborn child was less than twenty weeks. (B) The abortion was necessary to prevent the death of the pregnant woman or a serious risk of the substantial and irreversible impairment of a major bodily function of the pregnant woman. (1) No abortion shall be considered necessary on the basis of a claim or diagnosis that the pregnant woman will engage in conduct that would result in the pregnant woman’s death or a substantial and irreversible impairment of a major bodily function of the pregnant woman or based on any reason related to the woman’s mental health. NOTE: A pregnant woman on whom an abortion is purposely performed or induced, or purposely attempted to be performed or induced, in violation of division (A) of this section is not guilty of violating division (A) of this section or of attempting to commit, conspiring to commit, or complicity in committing a violation of division (A) of this section. NOTE: Refer to ORC 2919.20 for definitions.

ORC:2919.21.heading: NONSUPPORT OF DEPENDENTS 2919.21(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2919.21.text: _____________ did (abandon or fail to provide adequate support to) (his or her) spouse, to wit: (NAME OF SPOUSE), as required by law, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2919.21(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.21.notes: NOTE: It is an affirmative defense if the violator is unable to provide support, or provides all support he or she is able to provide because of his ability or means.

ORC:2919.21.heading: NONSUPPORT OF DEPENDENTS 2919.21(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2919.21.text: _____________ did (abandon or fail to provide adequate support to) (his or her) (child under 18 or mentally handicapped child under 21 or physically handicapped child under 21), to wit: (NAME OF CHILD AND DESCRIBED CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2919.21(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.21.notes: NOTE: It is an affirmative defense if the violator is unable to provide support or provides all support he or she is able to provide because of his ability or means.

ORC:2919.21.heading: NONSUPPORT OF DEPENDENTS 2919.21(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2919.21.text: _____________ did (abandon or fail to provide adequate support to) (his or her) (child under 18 or mentally handicapped child under 21 or physically handicapped child under 21), to wit: (NAME OF CHILD AND DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES) and having been previously convicted of Section 2919.21(A) (2) of the Ohio Revised code, to wit: (NAME OF COURT) on (DATE OF CONVICTION OR COURT FINDING), in violation of Section 2919.21(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2919.21.notes: NOTE: Same affirmative defense as stated above.

ORC:2919.21.heading: NONSUPPORT OF DEPENDENTS 2919.21(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2919.21.variant: ABANDON CHILD – PREVIOUS FELONY CONVICTION – F4
ORC:2919.21.text: _____________ did (abandon or fail to provide adequate support to) (his or her) (child under 18 or mentally handicapped child under 21 or physically handicapped child under 21), to wit: (NAME OF CHILD AND DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES) and having been previously convicted of a felony of Section 2919.21(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised code, to wit: (NAME OF COURT) on (DATE OF CONVICTION), in violation of Section 2919.21(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2919.21.notes: NOTE: Same affirmative defense as stated above.

ORC:2919.21.heading: NONSUPPORT OF DEPENDENTS 2919.21(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2919.21.variant: ABANDON CHILD – 26 WEEKS OUT OF 104 CONSECUTIVE WEEKS – F5
