ORC:2919.21.text: _____________ did (abandon or fail to provide adequate support to) (his or her) (child under 18 or mentally handicapped child under 21 or physically handicapped child under 21), to wit: (NAME OF CHILD AND DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES) and being found by a court to have failed to provide support under Section 2912.21(A)(2) for an accumulated period of 26 weeks out of 104 consecutive weeks) by (NAME OF COURT) on (DATE OF COURT FINDING), in violation of Section 2919.21(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2919.21.notes: NOTE: Same affirmative defense as stated above.

ORC:2919.21.heading: NONSUPPORT OF DEPENDENTS 2919.21(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2919.21.text: _____________ did (abandon or fail to provide adequate support to) (his or her) (aged or infirm) (parent or adoptive parent), to wit: (NAME OF PARENT) who from lack of ability and means was unable to provide adequately for (his or her) own support, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2919.21(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.21.notes: NOTE: It is an affirmative defense if the violator is unable to provide support or provides all support he or she is able to provide because of his ability or means; or the person not supported failed to provide support to the violator when he or she was under 18 or handicapped and under 21.

ORC:2919.21.heading: NONSUPPORT OF DEPENDENTS 2919.21(B)(1)(a) ORC
ORC:2919.21.variant: ABANDONMENT OF A DEPENDENT BY LAW – M1
ORC:2919.21.text: _____________ did (abandon or fail to provide adequate support to) a person, to wit: (NAME PERSON), whom (by law or by court order or by court decree), to wit: (STATE THE LAW OR DECREE) (STATE ACCUSED’S NAME) was legally obligated to support, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2919.21(B)(1)(a) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.21.notes: NOTE: It is an affirmative defense if the violator is unable to provide support or provides all support he or she is able to provide because of his ability or means. However, it is no defense that the person who a court has ordered the accused to support is being adequately supported by someone other than the accused.

ORC:2919.21.heading: NONSUPPORT OF DEPENDENTS 2919.21(B)(1)(a) ORC
ORC:2919.21.variant: ABANDONMENT OF A DEPENDENT BY LAW – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F5
ORC:2919.21.text: _____________ did (abandon or fail to provide adequate support to) a person, to wit: (NAME PERSON), whom by law or by court decree), to wit: (STATE THE LAW OR DECREE) (STATE ACCUSED’S NAME) was legally obligated to support, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), and having been previously convicted of Section 2919.21 [B] of the Ohio Revised code, to wit: (NAME OF COURT) on (DATE OF CONVICTION), in violation of Section 2919.21(B)(1) (a) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2919.21.heading: NONSUPPORT OF DEPENDENTS 2919.21(B)(1)(a) ORC
ORC:2919.21.variant: ABANDONMENT OF A DEPENDENT BY LAW – 26 WEEKS OUT OF 104 CONSECUTIVE WEEKS – F5
ORC:2919.21.text: _____________ did (abandon or fail to provide adequate support to) a person, to wit: (NAME PERSON), whom by law or by court decree), to wit: (STATE THE LAW OR DECREE) (STATE ACCUSED’S NAME) was legally obligated to support, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), and being found by a court to have failed to provide support under Section 2912.21 [B] for an accumulated period of 26 weeks out of 104 consecutive weeks) by (NAME OF COURT) on (DATE OF COURT FINDING), in violation of Section 2919.21(B) (1)(a) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2919.21.heading: NONSUPPORT OF DEPENDENTS 2919.21(B)(1)(a) ORC
ORC:2919.21.variant: ABANDONMENT OF A DEPENDENT BY LAW – PREVIOUS FELONY CONVICTION – F4
ORC:2919.21.text: _____________ did (abandon or fail to provide adequate support to) a person, to wit: (NAME PERSON), whom by law or by court decree), to wit: (STATE THE LAW OR DECREE) (STATE ACCUSED’S NAME) was legally obligated to support, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), and having been previously convicted of a felony of Section 2919.21 [B] of the Ohio Revised code, to wit: (NAME OF COURT) on (DATE OF CONVICTION), in violation of Section 2919.21(B)(1)(a) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2919.21.heading: NONSUPPORT OF DEPENDENTS 2919.21(B)(1)(b) ORC
ORC:2919.21.variant: ABANDONMENT OF A DEPENDENT BY LAW WHEN SUPPORT REMAINS UNPAID – M1
ORC:2919.21.text: _____________ did (abandon or fail to provide adequate support to) a person, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON), whom (by law or by court order or by court decree), to wit: (STATE THE LAW OR DECREE AND NAME OF ACCUSED) was legally obligated to support and an amount for support was due and owing prior to the date the person’s duty to pay current support terminated and remained unpaid, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2919.21(B)(1)(b) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.21.notes: NOTE: It is an affirmative defense if the violator is unable to provide support or provides all support he or she is able to provide because of his or her ability or means. However, it is no defense that the person who a court has ordered the accused to support is being adequately supported by someone other than the accused.

ORC:2919.21.heading: NONSUPPORT OF DEPENDENTS 2919.21(B)(1)(b) ORC
ORC:2919.21.variant: ABANDONMENT OF A DEPENDENT BY LAW WHEN SUPPORT REMAINS UNPAID – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F5
ORC:2919.21.text: _____________ did (abandon or fail to provide adequate support to) a person, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON), whom (by law or by court order or by court decree), to wit: (STATE THE LAW OR DECREE AND NAME OF ACCUSED) was legally obligated to support and an amount for support was due and owing prior to the date the person’s duty to pay current support terminated and remained unpaid, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), and having been previously convicted of ORC 2919.21(B) to wit: (STATE NAME OF COURT, CASE NUMBER AND DATE OF CONVICTION), in violation of Section 2919.21(B)(1)(b) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2919.21.notes: NOTE: It is an affirmative defense if the violator is unable to provide support or provides all support he or she is able to provide because of his or her ability or means. However, it is no defense that the person who a court has ordered the accused to support is being adequately supported by someone other than the accused.

ORC:2919.21.heading: NONSUPPORT OF DEPENDENTS 2919.21(B)(1)(b) ORC
ORC:2919.21.variant: ABANDONMENT OF A DEPENDENT BY LAW WHEN SUPPORT REMAINS UNPAID – 26 WEEKS OUT OF 104 CONSECUTIVE WEEKS – F5
ORC:2919.21.text: _____________ did (abandon or fail to provide adequate support to) a person, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON), whom (by law or by court order or by court decree), to wit: (STATE THE LAW OR DECREE AND NAME OF ACCUSED) was legally obligated to support and an amount for support was due and owing prior to the date the person’s duty to pay current support terminated and remained unpaid, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES) and having been found by a court to have failed to provide support under ORC 2919.21 for an accumulated period of 26 weeks out of 104 consecutive weeks by (STATE NAME OF COURT AND DATE OF COURT FINDING), in violation of Section 2919.21(B)(1)(b) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2919.21.notes: NOTE: It is an affirmative defense if the violator is unable to provide support or provides all support he or she is able to provide because of his or her ability or means. However, it is no defense that the person who a court has ordered the accused to support is being adequately supported by someone other than the accused.

ORC:2919.21.heading: NONSUPPORT OF DEPENDENTS 2919.21(B)(1)(b) ORC
ORC:2919.21.variant: ABANDONMENT OF A DEPENDENT BY LAW WHEN SUPPORT REMAINS UNPAID – PREVIOUS FELONY CONVICTION – F4
ORC:2919.21.text: _____________ did (abandon or fail to provide adequate support to) a person, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON), whom (by law or by court order or by court decree), to wit: (STATE THE LAW OR DECREE AND NAME OF ACCUSED) was legally obligated to support and an amount for support was due and owing prior to the date the person’s duty to pay current support terminated and remained unpaid, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), and having been previously convicted of a felony of ORC 2919.21(B) to wit: (STATE NAME OF COURT, CASE NUMBER AND DATE OF CONVICTION), in violation of Section 2919.21(B)(1)(b) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2919.21.notes: NOTE: It is an affirmative defense if the violator is unable to provide support or provides all support he or she is able to provide because of his or her ability or means. However, it is no defense that the person who a court has ordered the accused to support is being adequately supported by someone other than the accused.

ORC:2919.21.heading: CONTRIBUTING TO THE NONSUPPORT OF DEPENDENTS 2919.21(C) ORC
ORC:2919.21.text: _____________ did (aid or abet or induce or cause or encourage or contribute to) a (child or ward of juvenile court), to wit: (NAME CHILD OR PERSON AND AGE), to become (a dependent child as defined in Section 2151.04 of the Ohio Revised Code or a neglected child as defined in Section 2151.03 of the Ohio Revised Code), to wit: (DESCRIBE INDUCEMENT AND NATURE OF DEPENDENCY OR NEGLECT), in violation of Section 2919.21(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.21.notes: NOTE: Each day of violation of Division (C) of this section is a separate offense. NOTE: (A) A dependent child is one: (1) who is homeless or destitute or without proper care or support, through no fault of his or her parents, guardian or custodian; (2) who lacks proper care or support because of parent, guardian or custodian’s physical or mental condition; (3) whose condition or environment is such as to warrant the state, in the interests of the child, in assuming his guardianship (Section 2151.04 ORC) (B) A neglected child is one whose parents, guardian or custodian: (1) abandon the child; (2) because of their faults or habits fail to provide proper parental care; (3) neglect or refuse to provide proper or necessary subsistence, education, medical or surgical care, or other care necessary for the child’s health, morals, or well being; (4) neglect or refuse to provide the special care made necessary by the child’s mental condition; (5) placed or attempted to place child in violation of Section 5103.16 and 5103.17 ORC NOTE: Spiritual treatment through prayer alone in accordance with the tenets of an established religious body is not considered to be a neglected child.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(A) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: PARENT VIOLATING DUTY OF CARE – M1
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did recklessly, while being the (parent or guardian or custodian or person having custody or person having control or person in loco parentis) of a child (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (STATE NAME OF CHILD), create a substantial risk to the (health or safety) of such child by violating a duty of (care or protection or support), to wit: (DESCRIBE WHAT WAS DONE AND CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2919.22(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.22.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply if a child is treated by spiritual means through prayer alone in accordance with the tenets of a recognized religious body.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(A) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: PARENT VIOLATING DUTY OF CARE – RESULTING IN SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM – F3
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did recklessly, while being the (parent or guardian or custodian or person having custody or person having control or person in loco parentis) of a child (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (STATE NAME OF CHILD), create a substantial risk to the (health or safety) of such a child by violating a duty of (care, or protection, or support), which resulted in serious physical harm to the child, to wit: (DESCRIBE WHAT WAS DONE AND CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2919.22(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2919.22.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply if a child is treated by spiritual means through prayer alone in accordance with the tenets of a recognized religious body.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(A) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: PARENT VIOLATING DUTY OF CARE – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F4
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did recklessly, while being the (parent or guardian or custodian or person having custody or person having control or person in loco parentis) of a child (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (STATE NAME OF CHILD), create a substantial risk to the (health or safety) of such child, by violating a duty of (care or protection or support), to wit: (DESCRIBE WHAT WAS DONE AND CIRCUMSTANCES), and (STATE ACCUSED’S NAME) having previously been convicted of violating (Section 2919.22 Revised Code or an offense of neglect of a child or an offense of abandonment of a child or an offense contributing to the delinquency of a child or an offense of physical abuse of a child) on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT) (CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2919.22(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2919.22.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply if a child is treated by spiritual means through prayer alone in accordance with the tenets of a recognized religious body.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: ABUSE CHILD – M1
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did abuse a child (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (NAME OF CHILD AND AGE), by means of (DESCRIBE MANNER OF ABUSE), in violation of Section 2919.22(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.22.notes: NOTE: Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: ABUSE CHILD RESULTING IN SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM – F2
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did abuse a child (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (NAME OF CHILD AND AGE), by means of (DESCRIBE MANNER OF ABUSE), which resulted in serious physical harm to the child, to wit: (DESCRIBE WHAT WAS DONE AND CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2919.22(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2919.22.notes: NOTE: Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: ABUSE CHILD – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F4
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did abuse a child (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (NAME OF CHILD AND AGE), by means of (DESCRIBE MANNER OF ABUSE), and (STATE ACCUSED’S NAME) being previously convicted of violating (Section 2919.22 ORC or an offense of neglect of a child or an offense of abandonment of a child or an offense contributing to the delinquency of a child or an offense of physical abuse of a child) on (DATE OF CONVICTION) (CASE NUMBER), in (NAME OF COURT), in violation of Section 2919.22(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2919.22.notes: NOTE: Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: TORTURING A CHILD – F3
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did (torture or cruelly abuse), to wit: (DESCRIBE MEANS), a child (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (NAME OF CHILD), in violation of Section 2919.22(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2919.22.notes: NOTE: Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: TORTURING A CHILD RESULTING IN SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM – F2
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did (torture or cruelly abuse), to wit: (DESCRIBE MEANS), a child (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (NAME OF CHILD), which resulted in serious physical harm to the child, to wit: (DESCRIBE WHAT WAS DONE AND CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2919.22(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2919.22.notes: NOTE: Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: TORTURING A CHILD – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F2
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did (torture or cruelly abuse), to wit: (DESCRIBE MEANS), a child (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (NAME OF CHILD), and (STATE ACCUSED’S NAME) having been previously convicted of violating (Section 2919.22 Revised Code or an offense of neglect of a child or an offense of abandonment of a child or an offense contributing to the delinquency of a child or an offense of physical abuse of a child) in (NAME OF COURT) (CASE NUMBER) on (DATE OF CONVICTION), in violation of Section 2919.22(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2919.22.notes: NOTE: Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(3) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: EXCESSIVE PUNISHMENT OF A CHILD – F3
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did (administer corporal punishment to or administer physical disciplinary measures to or physically restrain) a child (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (NAME OF CHILD), (in a cruel manner or for a prolonged period) which (punishment or discipline, or restraint) was excessive under the circumstances and created a substantial risk of serious physical harm to the child, to wit: (DESCRIBE PUNISHMENT AND CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2919.22(B)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2919.22.notes: NOTE: Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(3) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: EXCESSIVE PUNISHMENT OF A CHILD RESULTING IN SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM – F2
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did (administer corporal punishment to or administer physical disciplinary measures to or physically restrain) a child (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (NAME OF CHILD), (in a cruel manner or for a prolonged period) which (punishment or discipline, or restrain) was excessive under the circumstances and resulted in serious physical harm to the child involved, to wit: (DESCRIBE PUNISHMENT AND CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2919.22(B) (3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2919.22.notes: NOTE: Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(3) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: EXCESSIVE PUNISHMENT OF A CHILD – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F2
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did (administer corporal punishment to or administer physical disciplinary measures to or physically restrain) a child (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 years or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (NAME OF CHILD), (in a cruel manner or for a prolonged period) which (punishment or discipline or restraint) was excessive under the circumstances and (STATE ACCUSED’S NAME) having been previously convicted of violating (Section 2919.22 Revised Code or an offense of neglect of a child or an offense of abandonment of a child or an offense contributing to the delinquency of a child or an offense of physical abuse of a child) on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT) (CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2919.22(B)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2919.22.notes: NOTE: Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(4) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: UNWARRANTED DISCIPLINE CREATING RISK OF RETARDATION – F3
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did repeatedly administer unwarranted disciplinary measures to a child (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (NAME OF CHILD) which, if continued, created a substantial risk that such conduct would seriously (impair or retard) the child’s (mental health or development), to wit: (DESCRIBE MEANS OF DISCIPLINE AND CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2919.22(B)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2919.22.notes: NOTE: Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(4) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: UNWARRANTED DISCIPLINE CREATING RISK OF RETARDATION AND RESULTING IN SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM – F2
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did repeatedly administer unwarranted disciplinary measures to a child (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (NAME OF CHILD) which, if continued, created a substantial risk that such conduct would seriously (impair or retard) the child’s (mental health or development) and did result in serious physical harm to the child involved, to wit: (DESCRIBE MEANS OF DISCIPLINE AND CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2919.22(B)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2919.22.notes: NOTE: Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(4) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: UNWARRANTED DISCIPLINE CREATING RISK OF RETARDATION – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F2
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did recklessly and repeatedly administer unwarranted disciplinary measures to a child (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (NAME OF CHILD) which, if continued, created a substantial risk that such conduct would seriously (impair or retard) the child’s (mental health or development), to wit: (DESCRIBE MEANS OF DISCIPLINE AND CIRCUMSTANCES) and (STATE ACCUSED’S NAME) having been previously convicted of violating (Section 2919.22 Revised Code or an offense of neglect of a child or an offense of abandonment of a child or an offense contributing to the delinquency of a child or an offense of physical abuse of a child) on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT) (CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2919.22(B) (4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2919.22.notes: NOTE: Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(5) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: PARTICIPATION IN OBSCENE PRODUCTIONS OR MATERIAL – F2
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did recklessly (entice or coerce or permit or encourage or compel or hire or employ or use or allow) a child, (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (STATE NAME), to (act in or model for or participate in or be photographed for) the (production or presentation or dissemination or advertisement) of any obscene (material or performance), to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES INCLUDING HOW THE CHILD WAS MADE TO PERFORM AND WHAT THE CHILD DID AS WELL AS FOR WHOM IT WAS DONE), when the said (material or performance) (depicts or describes) sexual activity, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in a patently offensive way and the said material taken as a whole appeals to a prurient interest in sex as judged by the average person applying contemporary community standards and does not have a serious literary, artistic, political or scientific value, in violation of Section 2919.22(B)(5) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2919.22.notes: NOTE: A judge should determine the question of obscenity before filing and this section does not apply if for a bona fide medical, scientific, educational, religious, governmental, judicial purpose or any other proper purpose by or to a physician, psychologist, sociologist, scientist, teacher, librarian, clergyman, prosecutor, judge, or person having a property interest or pursuing a bona fide study or research. NOTE: Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(5) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: PARTICIPATING IN NUDITY-ORIENTED MATERIAL – F2
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did recklessly, (entice or coerce or permit or encourage or compel or hire or employ or use or allow) a child, (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (STATE NAME), to (act in or model for or participate in or be photographed for) the (production or presentation or dissemination or advertisement) of a nudity-oriented matter in a (material or performance), to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES INCLUDING HOW THE CHILD WAS MADE TO PERFORM AND WHAT THE CHILD DID AS WELL AS THE NAME OF THE PERFORMANCE OR MATERIAL), when the said (material or performance) (depicts or describes) a minor in a state of nudity and when taken as a whole it would be judged by the average person applying contemporary community standards to appeal to a prurient interest in sex, in violation of Section 2919.22(B)(5) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2919.22.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply if for a bona fide medical, scientific, educational, religious, governmental, judicial purpose or any other proper purpose by or to a physician, psychologist, sociologist, scientist, teacher, librarian, clergyman, prosecutor, judge or person having a proper interest or pursuing a bona fide study or research. NOTE: Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(5) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: PARTICIPATING IN SEXUALLY-ORIENTED MATERIAL – F2
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did recklessly, (entice or coerce or permit or encourage or compel or hire or employ or use or allow) a child, (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (STATE NAME), to (act in or model for or participate in or be photographed for) the (production or presentation or dissemination or advertisement) of a sexually-oriented matter in a (material or performance), to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES INCLUDING HOW THE CHILD WAS MADE TO PERFORM AND WHAT THE CHILD DID AS WELL AS THE NAME OF THE PERFORMANCE OR MATERIAL), when the said (material or performance) (depicts or describes) a minor participating or engaging in sexual activity, masturbation, or bestiality, in violation of Section 2919.22(B)(5) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2919.22.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply if for a bona fide medical, scientific, educational, religious, governmental, judicial purpose or any other proper purpose by or to a physician, psychologist, sociologist, scientist, teacher, librarian, clergyman, prosecutor, judge or person having a proper interest or pursuing a bona fide study or research. NOTE: Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(6) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: SAME PARCEL AS DRUG MANUFACTURING – SINGLE-UNIT HOUSING – F3
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did knowingly allow a child, (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (STATE NAME AND AGE), to be on the same parcel of real property, to wit: (ADDRESS), and within one hundred feet of an act in violation of section 2925.04 or 2925.041 of the Revised Code when (SUSPECT) knew that the act is occurring, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE), in violation of Section 2919.22(B) (6) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(6) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: SAME PARCEL AS DRUG MANUFACTURING – SINGLE-UNIT HOUSING – RESULTING IN SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM – F2
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did knowingly allow a child, (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (STATE NAME AND AGE), to be on the same parcel of real property, to wit: (ADDRESS), and within one hundred feet of an act in violation of section 2925.04 or 2925.041 of the Revised Code when (SUSPECT) knew that the act is occurring, which resulted in serious physical harm to the child, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE), in violation of Section 2919.22(B)(6) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(6) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: SAME PARCEL AS DRUG MANUFACTURING – SINGLE-UNIT HOUSING – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F2
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did knowingly allow a child, (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (STATE NAME AND AGE), to be on the same parcel of real property, to wit: (ADDRESS), and within one hundred feet of an act in violation of section 2925.04 or 2925.041 of the Revised Code when (SUSPECT) knew that the act is occurring, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE), and (STATE ACCUSED’S NAME) having been previously convicted of violating (Section 2919.22 of the Revised Code or an offense of neglect of a child or an offense of abandonment of a child or an offense contributing to the delinquency of a child or an offense of physical abuse of a child) on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT) (CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2919.22(B)(6) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(6) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: SAME UNIT AS DRUG MANUFACTURING – MULTI-UNIT HOUSING – F3
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did knowingly allow a child, (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (STATE NAME AND AGE), to be in the same housing unit, and within one hundred feet of, an act in violation of section 2925.04 or 2925.041 of the Revised Code when (SUSPECT) knew that the act is occurring, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE), in violation of Section 2919.22(B)(6) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(6) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: SAME UNIT AS DRUG MANUFACTURING – MULTI-UNIT HOUSING – RESULTING IN SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM – F2
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did knowingly allow a child, (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (STATE NAME AND AGE), to be in the same housing unit, and within one hundred feet of, an act in violation of section 2925.04 or 2925.041 of the Revised Code when (SUSPECT) knew that the act is occurring, which resulted in serious physical harm to the child, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE), in violation of Section 2919.22(B)(6) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(B)(6) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: SAME UNIT AS DRUG MANUFACTURING – MULTI-UNIT HOUSING – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F2

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(C)(1) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: OPERATING VEHICLE WHILE INTOXICATED WITH CHILD ON BOARD – M1
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did, while operating a (vehicle or streetcar or trackless trolley) within the State of Ohio, to wit: (STATE LOCATION) and being in violation of ORC Section 4511.19(A) when (one or more) child(ren) under eighteen years of age, to wit: (STATE NUMBER, NAMES AND AGES) are in said (vehicle or streetcar or trackless trolley), in violation of Section 2919.22(C)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(C)(1) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: OPERATING VEHICLE WHILE INTOXICATED WITH CHILD ON BOARD – SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM – F5
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did while operating a (vehicle or streetcar or trackless trolley) within the State of Ohio, to wit: (STATE LOCATION) and being in violation of ORC Section 4511.19(A) when (one or more) child(ren) to wit: (STATE NUMBER, NAMES AND AGES) are in said (vehicle or streetcar or trackless trolley) and such operation resulted in serious physical harm to the child, to wit: (DESCRIBE PHYSICAL HARM, CAUSE AND CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2919.22(C)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(C)(1) ORC

ORC:2919.22.heading: ENDANGERING CHILDREN 2919.22(C)(1) ORC
ORC:2919.22.variant: OPERATING VEHICLE WHILE INTOXICATED WITH CHILD ON BOARD – SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM AND PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F4
ORC:2919.22.text: _____________ did while operating a (vehicle or streetcar or trackless trolley) within the State of Ohio, to wit: (STATE LOCATION) and being in violation of ORC Section 4511.19(A) when (one or more) child(ren) under eighteen years of age, to wit: (STATE NUMBER, NAMES AND AGES) are in said (vehicle or streetcar or trackless trolley) and such operation resulted in serious physical harm to the child, to wit: (DESCRIBE PHYSICAL HARM, CAUSE AND CIRCUMSTANCES) and (STATE ACCUSED’S NAME) having been previously convicted of violating (Section 2919.22(C), or 2903.06, or 2903.08, or 2903.07 before March 23, 2000, or 2903.04) on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT), in violation of Section 2919.22(C)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2919.222.heading: PARENTAL EDUCATION NEGLECT 2919.222 ORC
ORC:2919.222.text: _____________ did, being required, fail to attend a parental education or training program pursuant to a policy adopted under Section 3313.663(A) or (B), in violation of Section 2919.222 of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2919.224.heading: MISREPRESENTATION BY CHILD CARE PROVIDER 2919.224(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2919.224.variant: TO PARENT, GUARDIAN OR CUSTODIAN RECEIVING CHILD CARE – M1
ORC:2919.224.text: _____________, a child care provider, did knowingly misrepresent any factor or condition that relates to the provision of child care and that substantially affects the health or safety of any child, to wit: (NAME CHILD), in that provider’s facility or receiving child care from that provider to the (parent, guardian, custodian, or other person responsible for the care) of said child, to wit: (STATE MISREPRESENTATION AND PERSON IT WAS MADE TO), in violation of Section 2919.224(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.224.notes: NOTE: For the purposes of this section, “any factor or condition that relates to the provision of child care” includes, but is not limited to, the following: (A) The person or persons who will provide child care to the child of the parent, guardian, custodian, or other person responsible for the care of the child, or to the children in general. (B) The qualifications to provide child care of the child care provider, of a person employed by the provider, or of a person who provides child care as a volunteer. (C) The number of children to whom child care is provided at one time or the number of children receiving child care in the child care facility at one time. (D) The conditions or safety features of the child care facility. (E) The area of the child care facility in which child day-care is provided.

ORC:2919.224.heading: MISREPRESENTATION BY CHILD CARE PROVIDER 2919.224(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2919.224.variant: TO PARENT, GUARDIAN OR CUSTODIAN CONSIDERING PROVIDER – M1

ORC:2919.224.notes: NOTE: For the purposes of this section, “any factor or condition that relates to the provision of child care” includes, but is not limited to, the following: (A) The person or persons who will provide child care to the child of the parent, guardian, custodian, or other person responsible for the care of the child, or to the children in general. (B) The qualifications to provide child care of the child care provider, of a person employed by the provider, or of a person who provides child care as a volunteer. (C) The number of children to whom child care is provided at one time or the number of children receiving child care in the child care facility at one time. (D) The conditions or safety features of the child care facility. (E) The area of the child care facility in which child day-care is provided.

ORC:2919.225.heading: FAILURE OF FAMILY DAY-CARE HOME TO DISCLOSE DEATH OR SERIOUS INJURY OF CHILD 2919.225(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2919.225.text: _____________, an (owner, provider, or administrator) of a (type A or type B) family day-care home, to wit: (NAME AND ADDRESS OF HOME), knowing that a child (died while under the care of the home or while receiving child care from the owner, provider, or administrator; or died as a result of injuries suffered while under the care of the home or while receiving child care from the owner, provider, or administrator), to wit: (DESCRIBE INCIDENT, INCLUDING NAME OF CHILD AND DATE OF DEATH), did accept a child, to wit: (NAME OF CHILD) into that home without first disclosing to the parent, guardian, custodian, or other person responsible for the care of that child that said death had occurred, in violation of Section 2919.225(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2919.225.notes: NOTE: This section does not require more than one person to make disclosures to the same parent, guardian, custodian, or other person responsible for the care of a child regarding any single injury or death for which disclosure is required.

ORC:2919.225.heading: FAILURE OF FAMILY DAY-CARE HOME TO DISCLOSE DEATH OR SERIOUS INJURY OF CHILD 2919.225(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2919.225.variant: SERIOUS INJURY OF CHILD WITHIN 10 YEARS – M4
ORC:2919.225.text: _____________, an (owner, provider, or administrator) of a (type A or type B) family day-care home, to wit: (NAME AND ADDRESS OF HOME), knowing that within the preceding ten years, a child suffered injuries while (under the care of the home or while receiving child care from the owner, provider, or administrator), and those injuries led to said child being hospitalized for more than twenty-four hours, to wit: (DESCRIBE INCIDENT, INCLUDING NAME OF CHILD AND DATE OF INJURY), did accept a child, to wit: (NAME OF CHILD), into that home without first disclosing to the parent, guardian, custodian, or other person responsible for the care of that child that said injuries had occurred, in violation of Section 2919.225(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2919.225.notes: NOTE: This section does not require more than one person to make disclosures to the same parent, guardian, custodian, or other person responsible for the care of a child regarding any single injury or death for which disclosure is required.

ORC:2919.225.heading: FAILURE OF FAMILY DAY-CARE HOME TO DISCLOSE DEATH OR SERIOUS INJURY OF CHILD 2919.225(B)(1)(a) ORC
ORC:2919.225.variant: DEATH OF CHILD – TO PARENT, GUARDIAN OR CUSTODIAN OF OTHER CHILDREN – M4
ORC:2919.225.text: _____________, an (owner, provider, or administrator) of a (type A or type B) family day-care home, did fail to provide notice within 48 hours after the death of a child who (is under the care of the home or dies as a result of injuries suffered while under the care of the home or while receiving child day-care from the owner, provider, or administrator), to wit: (DESCRIBE INCIDENT, INCLUDING NAME OF CHILD AND DATE OF DEATH), to the parent, guardian, custodian, or other person responsible for the care of a child, to wit: (NAME OF CHILD), who is receiving or is enrolled to receive child care at the home or from the owner, provider, or administrator at the time of said death, in violation of Section 2919.225(B)(1)(a) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2919.225.notes: NOTE: This section does not require more than one person to give notices to the same parent, guardian, custodian, other person responsible for the care of the child, public children services agency, peace officer, or child fatality review board regarding any single injury or death for which disclosure is required.

ORC:2919.225.heading: FAILURE OF FAMILY DAY-CARE HOME TO DISCLOSE DEATH OR SERIOUS INJURY OF CHILD 2919.225(B)(1)(a) ORC
ORC:2919.225.variant: DEATH OF CHILD – TO PUBLIC CHILDREN SERVICES AGENCY – M4
ORC:2919.225.text: _____________, an (owner, provider, or administrator) of a (type A or type B) family day-care home, did fail to provide notice within 48 hours after the death of a child who (is under the care of the home or dies as a result of injuries suffered while under the care of the home), to wit: (DESCRIBE INCIDENT, INCLUDING NAME OF CHILD AND DATE OF DEATH), to (the public children services agency of the county in which the home is located or the child care was given, a municipal or county peace officer in the county in which the child resides or in which the home is located or the child care was given, or the child fatality review board appointed under section 307.621 of the Revised Code that serves the county in which the home is located or the child care was given), in violation of Section 2919.225(B)(1)(a) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2919.225.notes: NOTE: This section does not require more than one person to give notices to the same parent, guardian, custodian, other person responsible for the care of the child, public children services agency, peace officer, or child fatality review board regarding any single injury or death for which disclosure is required.

ORC:2919.225.heading: FAILURE OF FAMILY DAY-CARE HOME TO DISCLOSE DEATH OR SERIOUS INJURY OF CHILD 2919.225(B)(1)(b) ORC
ORC:2919.225.variant: SERIOUS INJURY OF CHILD – TO PARENT, GUARDIAN OR CUSTODIAN OF OTHER CHILDREN – M4
ORC:2919.225.text: _____________, an (owner, provider, or administrator) of a (type A or type B) family day-care home, did fail to provide notice within 48 hours of injuries suffered by a child while under care of the home that resulted in said child being hospitalized for more than 24 hours, to wit: (DESCRIBE INCIDENT, INCLUDING NAME OF CHILD AND DATE), to the (parent, guardian, custodian, or other person responsible for the care of a child) of a child, to wit: (NAME OF CHILD) who was receiving or is enrolled to receive child care at the home or from the owner, provider, or administrator at the time of said injury, in violation of Section 2919.225(B)(1)(b) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2919.225.notes: NOTE: This section does not require more than one person to give notices to the same parent, guardian, custodian, other person responsible for the care of the child, public children services agency, peace officer, or child fatality review board regarding any single injury or death for which disclosure is required.

ORC:2919.227.heading: FAILURE OF CHILD CARE CENTER TO DISCLOSE DEATH OR SERIOUS INJURY OF A CHILD 2919.227(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2919.227.variant: FAIL TO DISCLOSE INJURIES WITHIN PREVIOUS TWO YEARS – M4
ORC:2919.227.text: _____________, a child care center licensee, to wit: (STATE NAME AND ADDRESS OF CHILD CARE CENTER), did accept a child, to wit: (NAME OF CHILD) into that center without first providing, upon request of the (parent, guardian, custodian, or other person responsible for the care) of said child, the number and types of injuries to children, as reported in accordance with Revised Code 5104.015, that occurred at the center within the previous two years, to wit: (DESCRIBE OFFENSE), in violation of Section 2919.227(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2919.227.heading: FAILURE OF CHILD CARE CENTER TO DISCLOSE DEATH OR SERIOUS INJURY OF A CHILD 2919.227(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2919.227.variant: FAIL TO DISCLOSE DEATH WITHIN PREVIOUS FIFTEEN YEARS – M4
ORC:2919.227.text: _____________, a child care center licensee, to wit: (STATE NAME AND ADDRESS OF CHILD CARE CENTER), did accept a child, to wit: (NAME OF CHILD) into that center without first providing to the (parent, guardian, custodian, or other person responsible for the care) of said child, a notice that states (a child died while under the care of the center or while receiving child care from the owner, provider, or administrator of the center; or a child died as a result of injuries suffered while under the care of the center or while receiving child care from the owner, provider, or administrator of the center) within the previous fifteen years, to wit: (DESCRIBE INCIDENT, INCLUDING NAME OF CHILD AND DATE), in violation of Section 2919.227(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2919.227.heading: FAILURE OF CHILD CARE CENTER TO DISCLOSE DEATH OR SERIOUS INJURY OF A CHILD 2919.227(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2919.227.variant: FAIL TO KEEP RECORDS FOR THREE YEARS – M4
ORC:2919.227.text: _____________, a child care center licensee, to wit: (STATE NAME AND ADDRESS OF CHILD CARE CENTER), did fail to keep on file at the center a copy of the information provided under Revised Code 2919.227 for at least three years after providing the information, to wit: (DESCRIBE OFFENSE INCLUDING INFORMATION NOT KEPT), in violation of Section 2919.227(A) (3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2919.227.heading: FAILURE OF CHILD CARE CENTER TO DISCLOSE DEATH OR SERIOUS INJURY OF A CHILD 2919.227(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2919.227.variant: FAIL TO DISCLOSE DEATH OF A CHILD WITHIN 48 HOURS – M4
ORC:2919.227.text: _____________, a child care center licensee, to wit: (STATE NAME AND ADDRESS OF CHILD CARE CENTER), did fail to provide notice within 48 hours after the death of a child who (is under the care of the center or is receiving child care from the owner, provider, or administrator of the center OR dies as a result of injuries suffered while under the care of the center or while receiving child care from the owner, provider, or administrator), to wit: (DESCRIBE INCIDENT, INCLUDING NAME OF CHILD AND DATE OF DEATH), to (the parent, guardian, custodian, or other person responsible for the care of each child who, at the time of the death for which notice is required, is receiving or is enrolled to receive child care from the center OR the public children services agency of the county in which the center is located or the child care was given OR a municipal or county peace officer in the county in which the child resides or in which the center is located or the child care was given OR the child fatality review board that serves the county in which the center is located or the child care was given), in violation of Section 2919.227(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2919.23.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH CUSTODY 2919.23(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2919.23.text: _____________ did (knowing he was without privilege to do so or being reckless in that regard), (entice or take or keep or harbor) a child (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (STATE NAME OF CHILD), from that child’s (parent or guardian or custodian), to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES) in violation of Section 2919.23(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.23.notes: NOTE: It is an affirmative defense if a person who entices or takes a child reasonably believed it was necessary for the child’s health and safety or if reasonable notice was given to law enforcement or judicial authorities after keeping or harboring.

ORC:2919.23.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH CUSTODY 2919.23(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2919.23.variant: TAKING CHILD FROM PARENT/GUARDIAN – REMOVAL FROM STATE – F5
ORC:2919.23.text: _____________ did (knowing he was without privilege to do so or being reckless in that regard), (entice or take or keep or harbor) a child (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (STATE NAME OF CHILD), from that child’s (parent or guardian or custodian), to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES) and removed said child from the State of Ohio, in violation of Section 2919.23(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2919.23.notes: NOTE: It is an affirmative defense if a person who entices or takes a child reasonably believed it was necessary for the child’s health and safety or if reasonable notice was given to law enforcement or judicial authorities after keeping or harboring.

ORC:2919.23.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH CUSTODY 2919.23(A)(1) ORC (CCC 2319.23)
ORC:2919.23.variant: TAKING CHILD FROM PARENT/GUARDIAN – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F5
ORC:2919.23.text: _____________ did (knowing he was without privilege to do so or being reckless in that regard), (entice or take or keep or harbor) a child (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (STATE NAME OF CHILD), from that child’s (parent or guardian or custodian), to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES) and (STATE ACCUSED’S NAME) having been previously convicted of violating this Section on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT), in violation of Section 2919.23(A) (1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2919.23.notes: NOTE: It is an affirmative defense if a person who entices or takes a child reasonably believed it was necessary for the child’s health and safety or if reasonable notice was given to law enforcement or judicial authorities after keeping or harboring.

ORC:2919.23.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH CUSTODY 2919.23(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2919.23.variant: TAKING CHILD FROM PARENT/GUARDIAN – PHYSICAL HARM – F4
ORC:2919.23.text: _____________ did (knowing he was without privilege to do so or being reckless in regard to knowing he was without privilege to do so), (entice or take or keep or harbor) a child (under 18 or mentally handicapped under 21 or physically handicapped under 21) years of age, to wit: (STATE NAME OF CHILD), from that child’s (parent or guardian or custodian), to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES) and, said child having suffered physical harm as a result, in violation of Section 2919.23(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2919.23.notes: NOTE: It is an affirmative defense if a person who entices or takes a child reasonably believed it was necessary for the child’s health and safety or if reasonable notice was given to law enforcement or judicial authorities after keeping or harboring.

ORC:2919.23.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH CUSTODY 2919.23(A)(2) ORC (CCC 2319.23(A)(2))
ORC:2919.23.text: _____________ did (knowing he was without privilege to do so or being reckless in that regard), (entice or take or keep or harbor) a person, to wit: (NAME OF PERSON), who had been committed by law on (DATE OF COMMITMENT) by (NAME OF COURT) to an institution for (delinquent or abused or unruly or neglected or dependent) children, to wit: (NAME OF INSTITUTION), from the said institution, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2919.23(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the third degree.
ORC:2919.23.notes: NOTE: It is an affirmative defense if a person gives reasonable notice to law enforcement or judicial authorities after keeping or harboring.

ORC:2919.23.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH CUSTODY 2919.23(A)(3) ORC (CCC 2319.23(A)(3))
ORC:2919.23.variant: TAKING PERSON FROM MENTAL INSTITUTION – M3
ORC:2919.23.text: _____________ did (knowing he was without privilege to do so or being reckless in that regard), (entice or keep or take or harbor) a person, to wit: (NAME OF PERSON), who had been committed by law on (DATE OF COMMITMENT) by (NAME OF COURT) to an institution for the (mentally ill or mentally retarded), to wit: (NAME OF INSTITUTION), from the said institution to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2919.23(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the third degree.
ORC:2919.23.notes: NOTE: For additional section, see Section 2321.01 Columbus City Code and Child Enticement Section 2321.08 Columbus City Code. Also, it is an affirmative defense if a person gives reasonable notice to law enforcement or judicial authorities after keeping or harboring.

ORC:2919.23.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH CUSTODY 2919.23(B) ORC (CCC 2319.23(B))
ORC:2919.23.variant: ENCOURAGE COMMITTED CHILD OR WARD – M1
ORC:2919.23.text: _____________ did (aid or abet or induce or cause or encourage) a (child or ward of the juvenile court), to wit: (STATE NAME) who was committed to the custody of a (person or department or public institution or private institution), to wit: (NAME PERSON OR INSTITUTION), to leave the custody of the said (person or department or institution) without legal consent, to wit: (DESCRIBE MANNER OF INDUCEMENT OR ENCOURAGEMENT), in violation of Section 2919.23(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.23.notes: NOTE: Each day of violation of 2919.23(B) is a separate offense.

ORC:2919.231.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH ACTION TO ISSUE OR MODIFY SUPPORT ORDER 2919.231 ORC
ORC:2919.231.text: _____________ did by (physical harassment or threats of violence) against another person, to wit: (STATE PERSON’S NAME AND NATURE OF HARASSMENT OR THREATS), interfere with said person’s (initiation or continuance) of, or attempt to prevent the other person from (initiating or continuing) an action to (issue or modify) a support order under (Chapter 3115 or Section 2151.23, 2151.231, 2151.232, 2151.33, 2151.36, 2151.49, 3105.18, 3105.21, 3109.05, 3109.19, 3111.13, 3113.04, 3113.07, or 3113.31 of the Ohio Revised Code), in violation of Section 2919.231 of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2919.231.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH ACTION TO ISSUE OR MODIFY SUPPORT ORDER 2919.231 ORC
ORC:2919.231.text: _____________ did, by (physical harassment or threats of violence) against another person, to wit: (STATE PERSON’S NAME AND NATURE OF HARASSMENT OR THREATS), interfere with said person’s (initiation or continuance) of, or attempt to prevent the other person from (initiating or continuing) an action to (issue or modify) a support order under (Chapter 3115 or Section 2151.23, 2151.231, 2151.232, 2151.33, 2151.36, 2151.49, 3105.18, 3105.21, 3109.05, 3109.19, 3111.13, 3113.04, 3113.07, or 3113.31 of the Ohio Revised Code) and (STATE ACCUSED’S NAME) having been previously convicted of violating (Section 2919.231 Revised Code or Section 3111.29 Revised Code) on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT), in violation of Section 2919.231 of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2919.231.notes: DEFINITIONS 2919.24 ORC: DELINQUENCY – The violation of a law which constitutes a crime if committed by an adult except for a traffic violation (2152.02 ORC). UNRULY – Means any of the following: (1) Child not subject to reasonable control of parents, teachers, guardians, or custodian because of being wayward or habitually disobedient; (2) Child habitually truant from home or school; (3) Child who behaves so as to injure or endanger his or her health or morals or others; (4) Child who attempts to marry anywhere without parental consent or other legal authority; (5) Child found in a disreputable place, visits or patronizes a place prohibited by law, or associates with vagrant, vicious, criminal, notorious or immoral persons; (6) Child engaging in illegal occupation or in a situation dangerous to life or limb or injurious to his or her health or morals or that of others; (7) Child who has violated a law applicable to a child.

ORC:2919.24.heading: CONTRIBUTING TO UNRULINESS OR DELINQUENCY OF A CHILD 2919.24(B)(1) ORC (CCC 2319.24(A)(1))
ORC:2919.24.text: _____________ did (aid or abet or induce or cause or encourage or contribute to) a (child or ward of juvenile court), to wit: (NAME CHILD OR PERSON AND AGE), to become (an unruly child as defined in Section 2151.022 ORC or delinquent child as defined in Section 2152.02 ORC, to wit: (DESCRIBE INDUCEMENT AND NATURE OF UNRULY OR DELINQUENT BEHAVIOR), in violation of Section 2919.24(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.24.notes: NOTE: Each day of violation of this section is a separate offense. NOTE: See definitions cited at beginning of Section 2919.24 ORC.

ORC:2919.24.heading: CONTRIBUTING TO UNRULINESS OR DELINQUENCY OF A CHILD 2919.24(B)(2) ORC (CCC 2319.24(A)(2))
ORC:2919.24.variant: TENDING TO CAUSE CHILD TO BECOME UNRULY OR DELIQUENT– M1
ORC:2919.24.text: _____________ did act in a way that tended to cause a (child or ward of the juvenile court), to wit: (NAME CHILD OR PERSON AND AGE), to become (an unruly child as defined in Section 2151.022 ORC or a delinquent child as defined in Section 2152.02 ORC), to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT AND BEHAVIOR OF CHILD AS A RESULT OF SAID CONDUCT) in violation of Section 2919.24(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.24.notes: NOTE: Each day of violation of this section is a separate offense. NOTE: See definitions cited at beginning of Section 2919.24 ORC.

ORC:2919.24.heading: CONTRIBUTING TO UNRULINESS OR DELINQUENCY OF A CHILD 2919.24(B)(3) ORC
ORC:2919.24.variant: CONTRIBUTING TO CHILD BEING ADJUDICATED A HABITUAL TRUANT – M1
ORC:2919.24.text: _____________ did act in a way that contributes to a child, to wit: (NAME CHILD AND AGE) to be adjudicated as a delinquent child as defined in Section 2152.02 ORC based on the violation of a court order, to wit: (INDICATE COURT ORDER CASE NUMBER, JUDGE, COURT OF ISSUE AND DATE OF ISSUANCE) adjudicating the child an unruly child for being an habitual truant, by means of (DESCRIBE CONDUCT OF PERSON AND BEHAVIOR OF CHILD AS A RESULT OF SAID CONDUCT), in violation of Section 2919.24(B)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.24.notes: NOTE: Each day of violation of this section is a separate offense NOTE: See definitions cited at beginning of Section 2919.24 ORC.

ORC:2919.24.heading: CONTRIBUTING TO UNRULINESS OR DELINQUENCY OF A CHILD 2919.24(B)(4) ORC
ORC:2919.24.variant: FAIL TO ENSURE CHILD COMPLIES WITH SEX OFFENDER REGISTRATION DUTY – M1
ORC:2919.24.text: _____________, the (parent, guardian, or custodian) of an unemancipated child who has the duty under Chapters 2152 and 2950 of the Revised Code to (register, register a new residence address, periodically verify a residence address, or to send a notice of intent to reside), to wit: (NAME OF CHILD), did fail to ensure said child complies with said duty, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE, INCLUDING FAILED DUTY), in violation of Section 2919.24(B)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.24.notes: NOTE: Each day of violation of this section is a separate offense NOTE: See definitions cited at beginning of Section 2919.24 ORC. DEFINITIONS 2919.25 ORC: FAMILY OR HOUSEHOLD MEMBER – Any of the following who is residing or has resided with the offender: (A) Spouse, a person living as a spouse, or a former spouse of the offender; (B) Parent, foster parent, or a child of the offender, or another person related by consanguinity or affinity to the offender; (C) Parent or a child of a spouse, person living as a spouse, or former spouse of the offender, or another person related by consanguinity or affinity to a spouse, person living as a spouse, or former spouse of the offender; (D) Natural parent of any child of whom the offender is the other natural parent or is the putative other natural parent. PERSON LIVING AS A SPOUSE – Any person who is living or has lived with the offender in a common law marital relationship, who otherwise is cohabiting with the offender, or who otherwise has cohabited with the offender within five years prior to the date of the alleged commission of the act in question.

ORC:2919.25.heading: DOMESTIC VIOLENCE 2919.25(A) ORC
ORC:2919.25.variant: CAUSE OR ATTEMPT TO CAUSE PHYSICAL HARM – M1
ORC:2919.25.text: _____________ did knowingly (cause or attempt to cause) physical harm, to wit: (DESCRIBE HARM AND MEANS), to a family or household member, to wit: (STATE NAME AND RELATIONSHIP TO THE OFFENDER), in violation of Section 2919.25(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.25.notes: NOTE: See definitions cited at beginning of Section 2919.25 ORC.

ORC:2919.25.heading: DOMESTIC VIOLENCE 2919.25(A) ORC
ORC:2919.25.variant: CAUSE OR ATTEMPT TO CAUSE PHYSICAL HARM – PREGNANT VICTIM – F5
ORC:2919.25.text: _____________ did knowingly (cause or attempt to cause) physical harm, to wit: (DESCRIBE HARM AND MEANS), to a family or household member, to wit: (STATE NAME AND RELATIONSHIP TO THE OFFENDER), knowing said family or household member was pregnant, in violation of Section 2919.25(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2919.25.notes: NOTE: See definitions cited at beginning of Section 2919.25 ORC.

ORC:2919.25.heading: DOMESTIC VIOLENCE 2919.25(A) ORC
ORC:2919.25.variant: CAUSE OR ATTEMPT TO CAUSE PHYSICAL HARM – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F4
ORC:2919.25.text: _____________ did knowingly, (cause or attempt to cause), physical harm, to wit: (DESCRIBE HARM AND MEANS), to a family or household member, to wit: (STATE NAME AND RELATIONSHIP TO OFFENDER), and having been previously convicted of (DOMESTIC VIOLENCE, SECTION 2919.25 ORC; or Felonious Assault, Section 2903.11 ORC Involving family or Household Member; or Aggravated Assault, Section 2903.12 ORC Involving Family or Household Member; or Assault, Section 2903.13 ORC Involving Family or Household Member; or Menacing by Stalking, Section 2903.211 ORC Involving Family or Household Member; or, Aggravated Trespass, Section 2911.211 ORC Involving Family or Household Member), or Aggravated Menacing, Section 2903.21 ORC Involving Family or Household Member; or Menacing, Section 2903.22 ORC Involving Family or Household Member; or Endangering Children, Section 2919.22 ORC Involving Family or Household Member; or Negligent Assault, Section 2903.14 ORC Involving Family or Household Member), in (NAME OF COURT), ON (TYPE OF CONVICTION AND DATE), in violation of Section 2919.25(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2919.25.notes: NOTE: Violation is an F3 if the offender has two prior convictions. Both convictions must be listed in the complaint.

ORC:2919.25.heading: DOMESTIC VIOLENCE 2919.25(B) ORC
ORC:2919.25.variant: RECKLESSLY CAUSE SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM – M1
ORC:2919.25.text: _____________ did recklessly cause serious physical harm, to wit: (DESCRIBE HARM AND MEANS), to a family or household member, to wit: (STATE NAME AND RELATIONSHIP TO OFFENDER), in violation of Section 2919.25(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2919.25.notes: NOTE: See definitions cited at beginning of Section 2919.25 ORC.

ORC:2919.25.heading: DOMESTIC VIOLENCE 2919.25(B) ORC
ORC:2919.25.variant: RECKLESSLY CAUSE SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM – PREGNANT VICTIM – F5
ORC:2919.25.text: _____________ did recklessly cause serious physical harm, to wit: (DESCRIBE HARM AND MEANS), to a family or household member, to wit: (STATE NAME AND RELATIONSHIP TO OFFENDER), knowing said family or household member was pregnant, in violation of Section 2919.25(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2919.25.notes: NOTE: See definitions cited at beginning of Section 2919.25 ORC.

ORC:2919.25.heading: DOMESTIC VIOLENCE 2919.25(B) ORC
ORC:2919.25.variant: RECKLESSLY CAUSE SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F4
ORC:2919.25.text: _____________ did recklessly, cause serious physical harm to wit: (DESCRIBE HARM AND MEANS), to a family or household member, to wit: (STATE NAME AND RELATIONSHIP TO OFFENDER), and having been previously convicted of (Domestic Violence, Section 2919.25 ORC; or Felonious Assault, Section 2903.11 ORC Involving Family or Household Member; or Aggravated Assault, Section 2903.12 ORC Involving Family or Household Member; or Assault, Section 2903.13 ORC Involving Family or Household Member; or Menacing by Stalking, Section 2903.211 ORC Involving Family or Household Member; or Aggravated Trespass, Section 2911.211 ORC Involving Family or Household Member); or Aggravated Menacing, Section 2903.21 ORC Involving Family or Household Member; or Menacing, Section 2903.22 ORC Involving Family or Household Member; or Endangering Children, Section 2919.22 ORC Involving Family or Household Member; or Negligent Assault, Section 2903.14 ORC Involving Family or Household Member), in (NAME OF COURT) on (TYPE OF CONVICTION AND DATE) in violation of Section 2919.25(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2919.25.notes: NOTE: Violation is an F3 if the offender has two prior convictions. Both convictions must be listed in the complaint.

ORC:2919.25.heading: DOMESTIC VIOLENCE 2919.25(C) ORC
ORC:2919.25.text: _____________ did, by threat of force, knowingly cause a family or household member, to wit: (STATE NAME AND RELATIONSHIP TO THE OFFENDER), to believe that the offender will cause imminent physical harm to the said family or household member by, to wit: (DESCRIBE HARM AND MEANS), in violation of Section 2919.25(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2919.25.heading: DOMESTIC VIOLENCE 2919.25(C) ORC
ORC:2919.25.variant: THREAT OF IMMINENT HARM – PREGNANT VICTIM – M3
ORC:2919.25.text: _____________ did, by threat of force, knowingly cause a family or household member, to wit: (STATE NAME AND RELATIONSHIP TO THE OFFENDER), to believe that the offender will cause imminent physical harm to the said family or household member by, to wit: (DESCRIBE HARM AND MEANS), knowing said family or household member was pregnant, in violation of Section 2919.25(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the third degree.

ORC:2919.25.heading: DOMESTIC VIOLENCE 2919.25(C) ORC
ORC:2919.25.variant: THREAT OF IMMINENT HARM – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – M2
ORC:2919.25.text: _____________ did, by threat of force, knowingly cause a family or household member, to wit: (STATE NAME AND RELATIONSHIP TO OFFENDER), to believe that the offender will cause imminent physical harm to the said family or household member by, to wit: (DESCRIBE HARM AND MEANS), and having been previously convicted of (Domestic Violence, Section 2919.25 ORC; or Felonious Assault, Section 2903.11 ORC Involving Family or Household Member; or Aggravated Assault, Section 2903.12 ORC Involving Family or Household member; or Assault, Section 2903.13 ORC Involving Family or Household Member; or Menacing by Stalking, Section 2903.211 ORC Involving Family or Household Member; or Trespass, Section 2911.211 ORC; or Aggravated Menacing, Section 2903.21 ORC Involving Family or Household Member; or Menacing, Section 2903.22 ORC Involving Family or Household Member; or Endangering Children, Section 2919.22 ORC Involving Family or Household Member; or Negligent Assault, Section 2903.14 ORC Involving Family or Household Member), in (NAME OF COURT) on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in violation of Section 2919.25(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.
ORC:2919.25.notes: NOTE: Violation is an M1 if the offender has two prior convictions. Both convictions must be listed in the complaint. DEFINITIONS 2319.25 CCC: FAMILY OR HOUSEHOLD MEMBER – Any of the following who is residing or has resided with the offender: (A) Spouse, a person living as a spouse, or a former spouse of the offender; (B) Parent, foster parent, or a child of the offender, or another person related by consanguinity or affinity to the offender; (C) Parent or a child of a spouse, person living as a spouse, or former spouse of the offender, or another person related by consanguinity or affinity to a spouse, person living as a spouse, or former spouse of the offender; (D) Natural parent of any child of whom the offender is the other natural parent or is the putative other natural parent. PERSON LIVING AS A SPOUSE – Any person who is living or has lived with the offender in a common law marital relationship, who otherwise is cohabiting with the offender, or who otherwise has cohabited with the offender within five years prior to the date of the alleged commission of the act in question. INTIMATE PARTNER – A person with whom the offender is or has been in a dating relationship but who does not meet the definition of a family or household member. DATING RELATIONSHIP – A relationship between individuals who have, or have had, a relationship of a romantic or intimate nature. “Dating relationship” does not include a casual acquaintanceship or ordinary fraternization in a business or social context. NOTE: If the offender had a firearm or dangerous ordnance on or about the offender’s person or under the offender’s control at the time of the commission of the offense in violation of the Columbus City Code, the firearm or dangerous ordnance shall be seized and is subject to forfeiture under Chapter 2981 of the Ohio Revised Code. Refer to the complaint language cited in Chapter 2927 of the Criminal Complaint Manual.

CCC:2319.30.heading: MINOR’S CURFEW 2319.30(A) CCC
CCC:2319.30.text: _____________ did, being under the age of thirteen, to wit: (STATE AGE), (loiter or idle or wander or stroll or play) (in or upon) (the public streets or a public place or a place of amusement or a place of entertainment or a vacant lot or an other unsupervised place) to wit: (STATE LOCATION), between the hours of one hour after sunset and 4:30 am of the following day, in violation of Section 2319.30 of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the third degree.

CCC:2319.30.heading: MINOR’S CURFEW 2319.30(B) CCC
CCC:2319.30.text: _____________ did, being thirteen years of age or older, to wit: (STATE AGE), (loiter or idle or wander or stroll or play) (in or upon) (the public streets or a public place or a place of amusement or a place of entertainment or a vacant lot or an other unsupervised place) to wit: (STATE LOCATION), between the hours of midnight and 4:30 am of the following day, in violation of Section 2319.30 of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the third degree.
CCC:2319.30.notes: NOTE: Use official City time. No violation exists if the minor is a member of the United States Military or a registered full-time student at a business school or institution of higher learning.

CCC:2319.30.heading: MINOR’S CURFEW 2319.30(B) CCC
CCC:2319.30.variant: MINOR OVER 13 YEARS OF AGE – M3
CCC:2319.30.text: _____________, a minor thirteen years of age or older, to wit: (DOB), did (loiter or idle or wander or stroll or play) upon the public streets, other public places, places of amusement and entertainment, vacant lots or other unsupervised places, between the hours of midnight and 4:30 am of the following day, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION, INCLUDING PLACE AND TIME), and said minor is not a member of the United States Military or a registered full-time student at a business school or institution of higher learning, in violation of Section 2319.30(B) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the third degree.
CCC:2319.30.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to a minor accompanied by his parents, guardian or other adult person having the care and custody of the minor, or where the minor is upon an emergency errand or legitimate business directed by his parents, guardian, or other adult person having the care and custody of the minor.

CCC:2319.31.heading: PARENTAL NEGLECT 2319.31 CCC
CCC:2319.31.text: _____________ did, being the (parent or guardian or person having legal custody and control) of a minor, to wit: (NAME MINOR AND STATE AGE), negligently allow said minor to violate Section 2319.30 of the Columbus City Code, to wit: (STATE CIRCUMSTANCES, INCLUDE TIME OF THE CURFEW VIOLATION AND PLACE), in violation of Section 2319.31 of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the third degree.

CCC:2319.32.heading: ALLOWING A MINOR TO SELL GOODS 2319.32 CCC
CCC:2319.32.text: _____________ did, being the (parent or guardian or person having legal custody and control) of a child under the age of eight years, to wit: (NAME MINOR AND STATE AGE), knowingly (cause or induce or permit or allow) said child to (sell or barter or exchange) (newspapers or literature or gum or other wares and merchandise), to wit: (NAME PRODUCT), (on a public street or in a public place), to wit: (GIVE LOCATION), in violation of Section 2319.32 of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the third degree.

ORC:2921.02.heading: BRIBERY 2921.02(A) ORC
ORC:2921.02.variant: PURPOSE TO CORRUPT A PUBLIC OFFICIAL – F3
ORC:2921.02.text: _____________ did, with purpose to corrupt a (public servant or party official), to wit: (STATE OFFICIAL’S NAME AND DESCRIBE CORRUPTION) (before or after) (his or her) (election or appointment or qualification or employment or summoning or swearing in), (promise or offer or give) a valuable (thing or benefit), to wit: (DESCRIBE THING OR BENEFIT, INCLUDE VALUE), in violation of Section 2921.02(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2921.02.variant: IMPROPER INFLUENCE OF A PUBLIC OFFICIAL – F3
ORC:2921.02.text: _____________ did, with purpose to improperly influence a (public servant or party official) with respect to the discharge of official duties, to wit: (STATE OFFICIAL’S NAME AND DESCRIBE THE IMPROPER INFLUENCE OF OFFICIAL DUTIES) (before or after) (his or her) (election or appointment or qualification or employment or summoning or swearing in), (promise or offer or give) a valuable (thing or benefit), to wit: (DESCRIBE THING OR BENEFIT, INCLUDE VALUE), in violation of Section 2921.02(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2921.02.heading: BRIBERY 2921.02(B) ORC
ORC:2921.02.variant: SOLICIT VALUE FOR SELF BY PUBLIC OFFICIAL – F3
ORC:2921.02.text: _____________ did, either (before or after) (his or her) (election or appointment or qualification or employment or summoning or swearing in) as a (public servant or party official), to wit: (STATE OFFICIAL’S NAME) , knowingly (solicit or accept) a valuable (thing or benefit), to wit: (DESCRIBE THING OR BENEFIT, INCLUDE VALUE), to (corrupt or improperly influence) action in respect to the discharge of official duties, to wit: (DESCRIBE OFFICIAL DUTIES CORRUPTED OR INFLUENCED), in violation of Section 2921.02(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2921.02.heading: BRIBERY 2921.02(B) ORC
ORC:2921.02.variant: SOLICIT VALUE FOR ANOTHER PUBLIC OFFICIAL – F3
ORC:2921.02.text: _____________ did, either (before or after) (his or her) (election or appointment or qualification or employment or summoning or swearing in) as a (public servant or party official), to wit: (STATE OFFICIAL’S NAME) , knowingly (solicit or accept) a valuable (thing or benefit), to wit: (DESCRIBE THING OR BENEFIT, INCLUDE VALUE), to (corrupt or improperly influence) action in respect to the discharge of official duties of another (public servant or party official), to wit: (STATE NAME OF OFFICIAL AND DESCRIBE OFFICIAL DUTIES CORRUPTED OR INFLUENCED), in violation of Section 2921.02(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2921.02.heading: BRIBERY 2921.02(C) ORC
ORC:2921.02.text: _____________ did, with purpose to (corrupt or improperly influence) a witness, to wit: (STATE WITNESS’S NAME) with respect to the witness’s testimony in an official proceeding, to wit: (DESCRIBE PROCEEDING) (promise or offer or give) a valuable (thing or benefit), to wit: (DESCRIBE THING OR BENEFIT, INCLUDE VALUE) (before or after) said witness was (subpoenaed or sworn), to wit: (EXPLAIN CIRCUMSTANCES OF CORRUPTED OR INFLUENCED TESTIMONY) in violation of Section 2921.02(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2921.02.heading: BRIBERY 2921.02(C) ORC
ORC:2921.02.variant: OF ANOTHER TO INFLUENCE OR CORRUPT A WITNESS – F3
ORC:2921.02.text: _____________ did, with purpose to (corrupt or improperly influence) a witness, to wit: (STATE WITNESS’S NAME) with respect to the witness’s testimony in an official proceeding, to wit: (DESCRIBE PROCEEDING) (promise or offer or give) a valuable (thing or benefit), to wit: (DESCRIBE THING OR BENEFIT, INCLUDE VALUE) (before or after) another, to wit: (STATE NAME) (before or after) said witness was (subpoenaed or sworn), to wit: (EXPLAIN CIRCUMSTANCES OF CORRUPTED OR INFLUENCED TESTIMONY) in violation of Section 2921.02(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2921.02.heading: BRIBERY 2921.02(D) ORC
ORC:2921.02.text: _____________ did, (before or after) being (subpoenaed or sworn) as a witness, knowingly (solicit or accept) for (said witness’s self or another, to wit: (STATE NAME)), a valuable (thing or benefit), to wit: (DESCRIBE THING OR BENEFIT, INCLUDE VALUE), to (corrupt or influence) the witness with respect to testimony in an official proceeding, to wit: (DESCRIBE PROCEEDING) to wit: (EXPLAIN CIRCUMSTANCES OF CORRUPTED OR INFLUENCED TESTIMONY) in violation of Section 2921.02(D) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2921.02.notes: NOTE: A public servant or party official who is convicted of bribery is forever disqualified from holding any public office, employment, or position of trust in the State of Ohio.

ORC:2921.02.heading: BRIBERY 2921.02(E) ORC
