ORC:2921.02.text: _____________ did, with respect to the discharge of the director’s, officer’s, or employee’s duties, (before or after) the (director, officer, or employee) was (appointed or employed) and with purpose to (corrupt or improperly influence), a (director, officer, or employee) of a municipal school district transformation alliance established under section 3311.86 of the Ohio Revised Code, to wit: (STATE NAME AND POSITION OF PERSON), did (promise/offer/give) the (director/officer/employee) a (valuable thing or valuable benefit, to wit: (DESCRIBE THING OR BENEFIT, INCLUDING VALUE, AND DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2921.02(E) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2921.02.notes: NOTE: A public servant or party official, or director, officer, or employee of a municipal school district transformation alliance, who is convicted of bribery is forever disqualified from holding any public office, employment, or position of trust in the State of Ohio.

ORC:2921.02.heading: BRIBERY 2921.02(F) ORC
ORC:2921.02.variant: SOLICITATION FOR PURPOSES OF CORRUPTION OR INFLUENCE – F3
ORC:2921.02.text: _____________ did , (before or after) the person was (appointed or employed) (director, officer, or employee) of a municipal school district transformation alliance established under section 3311.86 of the Revised Code, knowingly (solicit or accept for self or another person) any (valuable thing or valuable benefit), to wit: (DESCRIBE THING OR BENEFIT, INCLUDING VALUE) to (corrupt or improperly influence) the person, to wit: (STATE NAME AND POSITION OF PERSON) with respect to the discharge of the person’s or other director’s, officer’s, or employee’s duties, in violation of Section 2921.02(F) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2921.02.notes: NOTE: A public servant or party official, or director, officer, or employee of a municipal school district transformation alliance, who is convicted of bribery is forever disqualified from holding any public office, employment, or position of trust in the State of Ohio.

ORC:2921.03.heading: INTIMIDATION 2921.03 ORC
ORC:2921.03.variant: ATTEMPT TO INFLUENCE BY THREAT A PUBLIC OFFICIAL OR WITNESS – F3
ORC:2921.03.text: _____________ did, knowingly and by (force or unlawful threat of harm or by filing, recording, or otherwise using a materially false or fraudulent writing with malicious purpose, in bad faith, or in a wanton and reckless manner), to wit: (DESCRIBE THREAT OR HARM), attempt to (influence or intimidate or hinder) a (public servant or party official or witness), to wit: (STATE NAME AND POSITION) in the discharge of official duties, to wit: (DESCRIBE INFLUENCE AND EXPLAIN DUTY INVOLVED), in violation of Section 2921.03 of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2921.04.heading: INTIMIDATION OF A CRIME VICTIM OR A WITNESS 2921.04(A) ORC (CCC 2321.04(A))
ORC:2921.04.text: _____________ did, knowingly attempt to (intimidate or hinder) the victim of a crime or delinquent act, to wit: (STATE NAME), in the (filing or prosecution) of criminal charges or a delinquent child action or proceeding, to wit: (DESCRIBE HINDRANCE OR INTIMIDATION AND THE CRIMINAL OR DELINQUENT CHARGE INVOLVED), in violation of Section 2921.04(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.04.heading: INTIMIDATION OF A CRIME VICTIM OR A WITNESS 2921.04(A) ORC
ORC:2921.04.text: _____________ did, knowingly attempt to (intimidate the witness to a (criminal or delinquent act) by reason of the person being a witness to that act, to wit: (STATE NAME), to wit: (DESCRIBE THE CRIMINAL OR DELINQUENT ACTION AND THE INTIMIDATION), in violation of Section 2921.04(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2921.04.notes: NOTE: “Witness” means any person who has or claims to have knowledge concerning a fact or facts concerning a criminal or delinquent act, whether or not criminal or delinquent child charges are actually filed.

ORC:2921.04.heading: INTIMIDATION OF A CRIME VICTIM OR A WITNESS 2921.04(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2921.04.variant: BY FORCE OR THREAT – CRIME VICTIM – F3
ORC:2921.04.text: _____________ did, knowingly and by (force, unlawful threat of harm to any person or property, or by unlawful threat to commit any offense or calumny against any person), to wit: (DESCRIBE THREAT, FORCE, OR CALUMNY), attempt to (influence or intimidate or hinder), to wit: (STATE NAME), the victim of a (crime or delinquent act), to wit: (STATE NAME), in the (filing or prosecution) of (criminal charges or delinquent child action or proceeding), to wit: (DESCRIBE HINDRANCE OR INTIMIDATION AND THE CRIMINAL OR DELINQUENT CHARGE INVOLVED), in violation of Section 2921.04(B) (1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2921.04.heading: INTIMIDATION OF A CRIME VICTIM OR A WITNESS 2921.04(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2921.04.variant: BY FORCE OR THREAT – WITNESS – F3
ORC:2921.04.text: _____________ did, knowingly and by (force, unlawful threat of harm to any person or property, or by unlawful threat to commit any offense or calumny against any person), to wit: (DESCRIBE THREAT, FORCE, OR CALUMNY), attempt to (influence or intimidate or hinder) the witness to a (criminal or delinquent act), to wit: (STATE NAME), by reason of being a witness to that act, to wit: (DESCRIBE INFLUENCE/INTIMIDATION/HINDERANCE AND THE CRIMINAL OR DELINQUENT CHARGE INVOLVED), in violation of Section 2921.04(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2921.04.notes: NOTE: “Witness” means any person who has or claims to have knowledge concerning a fact or facts concerning a criminal or delinquent act, whether or not criminal or delinquent child charges are actually filed.

ORC:2921.04.heading: INTIMIDATION OF A CRIME VICTIM OR A WITNESS 2921.04(B)(3) ORC
ORC:2921.04.variant: BY FORCE OR THREAT – ATTORNEY – F3
ORC:2921.04.text: _____________ did, knowingly and by (force, unlawful threat of harm to any person or property, or by unlawful threat to commit any offense or calumny against any person), to wit: (DESCRIBE THREAT, FORCE, OR CALUMNY), attempt to (influence or intimidate or hinder) an attorney, to wit: (STATE NAME), by reason of the attorney’s involvement in any (criminal or delinquent child action or proceeding), to wit: (DESCRIBE THE CRIMINAL OR DELINQUENT ACTION), in violation of Section 2921.04(B)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2921.05.heading: RETALIATION 2921.05(A) ORC
ORC:2921.05.variant: AGAINST OFFICIAL, ATTORNEY OR WITNESS – F3
ORC:2921.05.text: _____________ did, purposely and by (force or unlawful threat of harm to a person or unlawful threat of harm to property), to wit: (DESCRIBE FORCE OR THREAT OF HARM AND NAME PERSON OR PROPERTY OWNER AND DESCRIBE PROPERTY INVOLVED), retaliate against (a public servant or a party official or an attorney or a witness), to wit: (STATE NAME AND TITLE) who was involved in a (civil or criminal) (action or proceeding) because said person discharged their official duties, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE ACTION OR PROCEEDING AND DUTIES INVOLVED), in violation of Section 2921.05(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2921.05.heading: RETALIATION 2921.05(B) ORC
ORC:2921.05.text: _____________ did, purposely and by (force or unlawful threat of harm to a person or unlawful threat of harm to property), to wit: (DESCRIBE FORCE OR THREAT OF HARM AND NAME PERSON OR PROPERTY OWNER), retaliate against a victim of crime, to wit: (STATE NAME) because they (filed or prosecuted) criminal charges, to wit: (DESCRIBE ACTION AND CHARGES), in violation of Section 2921.05(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2921.11.heading: PERJURY 2921.11 ORC
ORC:2921.11.text: _____________ did, in an official proceeding, to wit: (STATE PROCEEDING), knowingly (make a false statement under oath or affirm to a false statement or swear to the truth of a previous false statement or affirm to the truth of a previous false statement) to wit: (DESCRIBE STATEMENT AND HOW IT WAS KNOWN TO BE FALSE), when such statement is material, in violation of Section 2921.11 of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2921.11.notes: NOTE: A false statement is material if it can affect the course or outcome of the proceeding regardless if the violator believed it to be immaterial or if the statement is inadmissible as evidence. NOTE: It is not important that the oath or affirmation is improperly administered. NOTE: Contradictory statements as to the same material fact made under oath or affirmation within the period of the statute of limitation for perjury establishes falsity. NOTE: To obtain conviction more than just one witness testifying contradictory to the defendant’s testimony is required.

ORC:2921.12.heading: TAMPERING WITH EVIDENCE 2921.12(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2921.12.variant: ALTER, DESTROY, CONCEAL, REMOVE EVIDENCE – F3
ORC:2921.12.text: _____________ did, knowing that an official (proceeding or investigation) is (in progress or about to be instituted or likely to be instituted), to wit: (DESCRIBE OFFICIAL PROCEEDING OR INVESTIGATION) (alter or destroy or conceal or remove) a (record or document or thing), to wit: (DESCRIBE THE RECORD, DOCUMENT OR THING), with purpose to impair its (value or availability) as evidence in such (proceeding or investigation) in violation of Section 2921.12(A) (1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2921.12.heading: TAMPERING WITH EVIDENCE 2921.12(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2921.12.variant: MAKE, PRESENT, USE FALSE EVIDENCE TO MISLEAD INVESTIGATOR – F3
ORC:2921.12.text: _____________ did, knowing that an official (proceeding or investigation) is (in progress or about to be instituted or likely to be instituted), to wit: (DESCRIBE OFFICIAL PROCEEDING OR INVESTIGATION) (make or present or use) a (record or document or thing), to wit: (DESCRIBE THE RECORD, DOCUMENT OR THING), knowing it to be false and with purpose to mislead a public official, to wit: (STATE OFFICIAL’S NAME) who (is or may be) engaged in such (proceeding or investigation), in violation of Section 2921.12(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2921.12.heading: TAMPERING WITH EVIDENCE 2921.12(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2921.12.variant: MAKE, PRESENT, USE FALSE EVIDENCE TO CORRUPT OUTCOME OF PROCEEDING OR INVESTIGATION – F3
ORC:2921.12.text: _____________ did, knowing that an official (proceeding or investigation) is (in progress or about to be instituted or likely to be instituted), to wit: (DESCRIBE OFFICIAL PROCEEDING OR INVESTIGATION) (make or present or use) a (record or document or thing), to wit: (DESCRIBE THE RECORD, DOCUMENT OR THING), knowing it to be false and with purpose to corrupt the outcome in such (proceeding or investigation), in violation of Section 2921.12(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2921.13.heading: FALSIFICATION 2921.13(A)(1) ORC (CCC 2321.13)
ORC:2921.13.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a false statement or swear to the truth of a false statement previously made or affirm the truth of a false statement previously made) when the statement, to wit: (DESCRIBE STATEMENT), was made in an official proceeding, to wit: (NAME THE PROCEEDING), in violation of Section 2921.13(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.13.heading: FALSIFICATION 2921.13(A)(2) ORC (CCC 2321.13)
ORC:2921.13.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a false statement or swear to the truth of a false statement previously made or affirm the truth of a false statement previously made) when the statement, to wit: (DESCRIBE STATEMENT), was made with the purpose to incriminate another, to wit: (NAME PERSON), in violation of Section 2921.13(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.13.heading: FALSIFICATION 2921.13(A)(3) ORC (CCC 2321.13)
ORC:2921.13.variant: TO MISLEAD A PUBLIC OFFICIAL – M1
ORC:2921.13.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a false statement or swear to the truth of a false statement previously made or affirm the truth of a false statement previously made) when the statement, to wit: (DESCRIBE STATEMENT), was made with the purpose to mislead a public official, to wit: (STATE NAME), in the performing of the public official’s official function, to wit: (STATE FUNCTION), in violation of Section 2921.13(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.13.heading: FALSIFICATION 2921.13(A)(4) ORC (CCC 2321.13)
ORC:2921.13.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a false statement or swear to the truth of a false statement previously made or affirm the truth of a false statement previously made) when the statement, to wit: (DESCRIBE STATEMENT), was made with purpose to secure the payment of (unemployment compensation; Ohio works first; prevention, retention, and contingency assistance; disability assistance; retirement benefits; economic development assistance, as defined in Section 9.66 of the Revised Code; or other benefits administered by a governmental agency or a benefit paid out of a public treasury by a governmental agency or a benefit paid out of a public treasury), to wit: (DESCRIBE THE BENEFIT AND AGENCY FROM WHOM IT WAS OBTAINED), in violation of Section 2921.13(A)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.13.heading: FALSIFICATION 2921.13(A)(5) ORC (CCC 2321.13)
ORC:2921.13.variant: TO OBTAIN A GOVERNMENT PERMIT OR LICENSE – M1
ORC:2921.13.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a false statement or swear to the truth of a false statement previously made or affirm the truth of a false statement previously made) when the statement, to wit: (DESCRIBE STATEMENT), was made with purpose to secure the issuance by a governmental agency of (a license or a permit or an authorization or a certificate or a registration or a release or a provider agreement), to wit: (DESCRIBE THE ITEM AND AGENCY INVOLVED), in violation of Section 2921.13(A)(5) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.13.heading: FALSIFICATION 2921.13(A)(6) ORC (CCC 2321.13)
ORC:2921.13.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a false statement or swear to the truth of a false statement previously made or affirm the truth of a false statement previously made) when the statement, to wit: (DESCRIBE STATEMENT), was (sworn or affirmed) before a (notary public or another person empowered to administer oaths), to wit: (NAME PERSON), in violation of Section 2921.13(A)(6) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.13.heading: FALSIFICATION 2921.13(A)(7) ORC (CCC 2321.13)
ORC:2921.13.variant: OF WRITTEN REPORT REQUIRED BY LAW – M1
ORC:2921.13.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a false statement or swear to the truth of a false statement previously made or affirm the truth of a false statement previously made) when the statement, to wit: (DESCRIBE STATEMENT), was in writing (on or in connection with) a (report or return) which was (required or authorized by law), to wit: (DESCRIBE REPORT AND LAW INVOLVED), in violation of Section 2921.13(A)(7) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.13.heading: FALSIFICATION 2921.13(A)(8) ORC (CCC 2321.13)
ORC:2921.13.variant: TO EXTEND CREDIT, BENEFIT, OR HONOR – M1
ORC:2921.13.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a false statement or swear to the truth of a false statement previously made or affirm the truth of a false statement previously made) when the statement, to wit: (DESCRIBE STATEMENT), was in writing and was made with purpose to induce another to wit: (STATE NAME), to (extend credit to or employ or confer a degree to or confer a diploma to or confer a certificate of attainment to or confer an award of excellence to or confer honor to or extend a valuable benefit to or bestow a valuable benefit upon or extend a valuable distinction to or bestow a valuable distinction upon) (STATE DEFENDANT’S NAME), when the person to whom the said statement was directed relied to (his or her) detriment, to wit: (DESCRIBE CREDIT OR BENEFIT OR HONOR), in violation of Section 2921.13(A)(8) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.13.heading: FALSIFICATION TO COMMIT OR FACILITATE THEFT 2921.13(A)(9) ORC
ORC:2921.13.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a false statement or swear to the truth of a false statement previously made or affirm the truth of a false statement previously made) when the statement, to wit: (DESCRIBE STATEMENT), was made with the purpose to (commit or facilitate) the commission of a theft offense, to wit: (DESCRIBE THEFT, INCLUDING SECTION NUMBER VIOLATED), in violation of Section 2921.13(A)(9) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2921.13.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00 – Falsification to Commit or Facilitate a Theft, a misdemeanor of the first degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00 – Falsification to Commit or Facilitate Theft, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00 – Falsification to Commit or Facilitate a Theft, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE AT MORE THAN $150,000.00 – Falsification to Commit or Facilitate a Theft, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2921.13.heading: FALSIFICATION 2921.13(A)(10) ORC
ORC:2921.13.text: _____________ did knowingly, (make a false statement or swear to the truth of a false statement previously made or affirm the truth of a false statement previously made) when the statement, to wit: (DESCRIBE STATEMENT), was knowingly made to a probate court in connection with (an action or proceeding or other matter within its jurisdiction) to wit: (STATE THE ACTION OR PROCEEDING OR MATTER), (orally or in a written document, including, but not limited to, an application, petition, complaint, or other pleading, or an inventory, account or report) to wit: (DESCRIBE ORAL STATEMENT OR WRITTEN DOCUMENT), in violation of Section 2921.13(A)(10) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.13.heading: FALSIFICATION 2921.13(A)(11) ORC
ORC:2921.13.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a false statement or swear to the truth of a false statement previously made or affirm the truth of a false statement previously made) when the statement, to wit: (DESCRIBE STATEMENT) was made on an account, form, record, stamp, label, or other writing required by law, in violation of Section 2921.13(A)(11) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.13.heading: FALSIFICATION TO PURCHASE A FIREARM 2921.13(A)(12) ORC
ORC:2921.13.text: _________ did knowingly, (make a false statement or swear to the truth of a false statement previously made or affirm the truth of a false statement previously made) when the statement, was made in connection with the purchase of a firearm, as defined in Section 2923.11 of the Revised Code, and in conjunction with the furnishing to the seller of the firearm of a fictitious or altered driver’s or commercial driver’s license or permit, a fictitious or altered identification card, or any other document that contains false information about the purchaser’s identity, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.13(A) (12) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2921.13.heading: FALSIFICATION 2921.13(A)(13) ORC
ORC:2921.13.variant: JUDGMENT, LIEN, OR CLAIM OF INDEBTEDNESS – M1
ORC:2921.13.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a false statement or swear to the truth of a false statement previously made or affirm the truth of a false statement previously made) when the statement, was made in a document or instrument of writing that purports to be a judgment, lien, or claim of indebtedness and is filed or recorded with the secretary of state, a county recorder, or the clerk of a court of record, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.13(A)(13) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.13.heading: FALSIFICATION 2921.13(A)(14) ORC
ORC:2921.13.variant: IN APPLICATION TO OBTAIN OR RENEW LICENSE TO CARRY CONCEALED HANDGUN – F4
ORC:2921.13.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a false statement, swear to the truth of a false statement previously made, or affirm the truth of a false statement previously made) when the statement was made (in an application filed with a county sheriff pursuant to Section 2923.125 of the Ohio Revised Code to obtain or renew a concealed handgun license or was made in an affidavit submitted to a county sheriff to obtain a concealed handgun license on a temporary emergency basis pursuant to Section 2923.1213 of the Ohio Revised Code), to wit: (DESCRIBE STATEMENT), in violation of Section 2921.13(A)(14) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2921.13.heading: FALSIFICATION 2921.13(A)(15) ORC
ORC:2921.13.variant: REQUIRED FOR PURCHASE OF CIGARETTES OR TOBACCO – M1
ORC:2921.13.text: _____________ did knowingly (make a false statement, swear to the truth of a false statement previously made, or affirm the truth of a false statement previously made) when the statement was made as required under Section 5743.71) of the Revised Code in connection with the person’s purchase of cigarettes or tobacco products in a delivery sale, to wit: (DESCRIBE STATEMENT), in violation of Section 2921.13(A)(15) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.13.heading: FALSIFICATION TO PURCHASE A FIREARM 2921.13(B) ORC
ORC:2921.13.text: _____________ did knowingly, in connection with the purchase of a firearm, as defined in Section 2923.11 of the Revised Code, furnish to the seller of the firearm a fictitious or altered driver’s or commercial driver’s license or permit, a fictitious or altered identification card, or any other document that contains false information about the purchaser’s identity, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.13(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2921.13.heading: FALSIFICATION TO PURCHASE A FIREARM 2921.13(C) ORC
ORC:2921.13.variant: CARRY CONCEALED WEAPON UNDER ORC 2923.125 OR ORC 2923.1213 – F4
ORC:2921.13.text: _____________ did knowingly, in an attempt to obtain a license to carry a concealed handgun under Section 2923.125 of the Revised Code, present to a sheriff a fictitious or altered document that purports to be certification of the person’s competence in handling a handgun as described in Section 2923.125 of the Revised Code, to wit: (DESCRIBE DOCUMENT), in violation of Section 2921.13(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2921.14.heading: FALSE REPORT OF CHILD ABUSE OR NEGLECT 2921.14 ORC
ORC:2921.14.text: _____________ did knowingly (make or cause another person to make a false report) under division B of Section 2151.421 of the Ohio Revised Code, alleging that any person has committed an act or omission that resulted in a child being an abused child as defined in Section 2151.031 of the Revised Code, or a neglected child as defined in Section 2151.03 of the Revised Code, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE REPORT), in violation of Section 2921.14 of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.15.heading: MAKING A FALSE ALLEGATION OF PEACE OFFICER MISCONDUCT 2921.15(B) ORC
ORC:2921.15.text: _____________ did knowingly file a complaint against a peace officer, to wit: (NAME OFFICER) alleging that the peace officer engaged in misconduct in the performance of the officer’s duties, and the said (NAME PERSON) knowing the allegation to be false, to wit: (DESCRIBE FALSE ALLEGATION), in violation of Section 2921.15(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.21.heading: COMPOUNDING A CRIME 2921.21(A) ORC
ORC:2921.21.text: _____________ did knowingly (demand or accept or agree to accept) anything of value, to wit: (DESCRIBE ITEM) in consideration of (abandoning or agreeing to abandon) a pending criminal prosecution, to wit: (IDENTIFY ACTION, INCLUDING CASE NUMBER AND COURT), in violation of Section 2921.21(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2921.21.notes: NOTE: An affirmative defense exists when the crime being prosecuted is Theft, Passing Bad Checks, Insurance Fraud, or Misuse of Credit Cards and the amount demanded, accepted or agreed to is reasonably believed by the actor to be due him as restitution caused by the offense. Acceptance or agreement to abandon by the witness does not bind the State to abandoning prosecution. DEFINITIONS 2921.22 BURN INJURY – any second or third degree burns, burns to the upper respiratory tract or laryngeal edema due to the inhalation of superheated air, any burn injury or wound that may result in death, or any physical harm to persons caused by or as the result of the use of fireworks, novelties and trick noisemakers, and wire sparklers, as each is defined by Section 3743.01 of the Ohio Revised Code. NOTE: Divisions (A) and (D) of this section do not require disclosure of information, when any of the privileges/circumstances listed in 2921.22(G) exist. NOTE: No disclosure of information pursuant to this section gives rise to any liability or recrimination for a breach of privilege or confidence.

ORC:2921.22.heading: FAILURE TO REPORT A CRIME 2921.22(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2921.22.text: _____________ did knowing that a felony (has been or is being) committed, to wit: (GIVE CIRCUMSTANCES AND STATE FELONY BEING COMMITTED), knowingly fail to report said information to law enforcement authorities, in violation of Section 2921.22(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2921.22.notes: NOTE: No disclosure is required if a privilege exists between parties that would be compromised by such disclosure.

ORC:2921.22.heading: FAILURE TO REPORT A CRIME 2921.22(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2921.22.text: _____________ did knowing that a violation of Section 2913.04(B) of the Revised Code (has been or is being committed or that the person has received information derived) from such a violation, to wit: (GIVE CIRCUMSTANCES AND STATE FELONY BEING COMMITTED), knowingly fail to report said information to law enforcement authorities, in violation of Section 2921.22(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2921.22.heading: FAILURE TO REPORT A CRIME 2921.22(B) ORC
ORC:2921.22.variant: MEDICAL PERSONNEL TO REPORT GUNSHOT AND STAB WOUNDS – M2
ORC:2921.22.text: _____________ did being (a person giving aid to a sick or injured person), to wit: (STATE NAME), negligently fail to report to law enforcement authorities any (gunshot wound or stab wound) that said person (treated or observed), to wit (DESCRIBE WOUND AND CIRCUMSTANCES OF CONTACT), in violation of Section 2921.22(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2921.22.heading: FAILURE TO REPORT A CRIME 2921.22(B) ORC
ORC:2921.22.variant: SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM RESULTING FROM VIOLENCE – M2
ORC:2921.22.text: _____________ did being (a person giving aid to a sick or injured person), to wit: (STATE NAME), negligently fail to report to law enforcement authorities any serious physical harm that said person (knows or has reasonable cause to believe) resulted from an offense of violence, to wit (DESCRIBE SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM, NAME AND RELATIONSHIP OF PERPETRATOR AND CIRCUMSTANCES OF CONTACT), in violation of Section 2921.22(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2921.22.heading: FAILURE TO REPORT KNOWLEDGE OF A DEATH 2921.22(C) ORC
ORC:2921.22.text: _____________ did, (having discovered the body of a person or having acquired the first knowledge of a death of a person), to wit: (STATE NAME OF DECEASED AND CIRCUMSTANCES), fail to report the death immediately to (a physician or advanced practice registered nurse whom the person knows to be treating the deceased for a condition from which at the time such death would not be unexpected, or a law enforcement officer, or an ambulance service, or an emergency squad, or the coroner of the political subdivision in which the body was discovered, or the coroner of the political subdivision in which the death is believe to have occurred or the coroner of the political subdivision in which the knowledge of the death was obtained), in violation of Section 2921.22(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2921.22.notes: NOTE: For purposes of this section, “advanced practice registered nurse” does not include a certified registered nurse anesthetist.

ORC:2921.22.heading: FAILURE TO REPORT KNOWLEDGE OF A DEATH 2921.22(D) ORC
ORC:2921.22.text: _____________ did fail to provide (upon request of the person to whom a report under division (C) was made, or to any law enforcement officer who has reasonable cause to assert the authority to investigate the circumstances surrounding the death) to wit: (STATE NAME OF DECEASED AND CIRCUMSTANCES), any facts within the person’s knowledge that may have a bearing on the facts of the death, to wit: (STATE FACTS WITHIN PERSONS KNOWLEDGE), in violation of Section 2921.22(D) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2921.22.notes: NOTE: No disclosure is required if a privilege exists between parties that would be compromised by such disclosure.

ORC:2921.22.heading: FAILURE TO REPORT A BURN INJURY 2921.22(E)(2) ORC
ORC:2921.22.text: _____________ did negligently, being a (physician, physician assistant, nurse, or limited practitioner) who outside a (hospital, sanitarium, or other medical facility), attended or treated a person who has sustained a burn injury, to wit: (NAME OF BURN VICTIM AND DESCRIBE INJURIES), that is inflicted (by an explosion, by other incendiary device, or that shows evidence of having been inflicted in a violent, malicious, or criminal manner), failed to report the burn injury immediately to the (local arson, or fire and explosion investigation, bureau if one exists in the jurisdiction, or to local law enforcement authorities), to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2921.22(E) (2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor.

ORC:2921.22.heading: FAILURE TO REPORT A BURN INJURY 2921.22(E)(2) ORC
ORC:2921.22.text: _____________ did knowingly, being a (physician, nurse, or limited practitioner) who outside a (hospital, sanitarium, or other medical facility), attended or treated a person who has sustained a burn injury, to wit: (NAME OF BURN VICTIM AND DESCRIBE INJURIES), that is inflicted (by an explosion, by other incendiary device, or that shows evidence of having been inflicted in a violent, malicious, or criminal manner), failed to report the burn injury immediately to the (local arson, or fire and explosion investigation, bureau if one exists in the jurisdiction, or to local law enforcement authorities), to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2921.22(E)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2921.22.heading: FAILURE TO REPORT A BURN INJURY 2921.22(E)(3) ORC
ORC:2921.22.text: _____________ did negligently, being a (manager, superintendent, or other person) in charge of a (hospital, sanitarium, or other medical facility), (which was attended by or treated) a person who has sustained a burn injury, to wit: (NAME OF BURN VICTIM AND DESCRIBE INJURIES), that was inflicted (by an explosion, by other incendiary device, or that shows evidence of having been inflicted in a violent, malicious, or criminal manner), to wit: (DESCRIBE HOW INJURIES WERE INFLICTED), fail to report the burn injury immediately to the (local arson, or fire and explosion investigation, bureau if one exists in the jurisdiction, or to local law enforcement authorities), to wit:(DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2921.22(E)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor.

ORC:2921.22.heading: FAILURE TO REPORT A BURN INJURY 2921.22(E)(3) ORC
ORC:2921.22.text: _____________ did knowingly, being a (manager, superintendent or other person) in charge of a (hospital, sanitarium, or other medical facility), (which was attended by or treated) a person who has sustained a burn injury, to wit: (NAME OF BURN VICTIM AND DESCRIBE INJURIES), that is inflicted (by an explosion, by other incendiary device, or that shows evidence of having been inflicted in a violent, malicious, or criminal manner), to wit: (DESCRIBE HOW INJURIES WERE INFLICTED), fail to report the burn injury immediately to the (local arson, or fire and explosion investigation, bureau if one exists in the jurisdiction, or to local law enforcement authorities), to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2921.22(E)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2921.22.heading: FAILURE TO REPORT A BURN INJURY 2921.22(E)(4) ORC
ORC:2921.22.variant: STATE FIRE MARSHALL REPORT – NEGLIGENTLY – MM
ORC:2921.22.text: _____________ did negligently, being a person required under Ohio Revised Code 2921.22(E)(2) or (3) to report any burn injury, fail to file within three working days after (attending or treating) the victim, to wit: (NAME OF BURN VICTIM AND DESCRIBE INJURIES), a written report of the burn injury with the office of the state fire marshal that complies with the uniform standard pursuant to Ohio Revised Code 3737.22(A)(15), to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2921.22(E)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor.

ORC:2921.22.heading: FAILURE TO REPORT A BURN INJURY 2921.22(E)(4) ORC
ORC:2921.22.variant: STATE FIRE MARSHALL REPORT – KNOWINGLY – M2
ORC:2921.22.text: _____________ did knowingly, being a person required under Ohio Revised Code 2921.22(E)(2) or (3) to report any burn injury, fail to file within three working days after (attending or treating) the victim, to wit: (NAME OF BURN VICTIM AND DESCRIBE INJURIES), a written report of the burn injury with the office of the state fire marshal that complies with the uniform standard pursuant to Ohio Revised Code 3737.22(A)(15), to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2921.22(E)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2921.22.heading: FAILURE TO REPORT A CRIME 2921.22(F)(1) ORC
ORC:2921.22.variant: KNOWING LICENSED MEDICAL PROFESSIONAL COMMITTED OFFENSE – M4
ORC:2921.22.text: _____________ did, being a person who knows that a licensed medical professional has committed an offense under Chapter 2907 of the Ohio Revised Code, a violation of a municipal ordinance substantially equivalent to such an offense, or a substantially equivalent criminal offense in another jurisdiction, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE), fail to report such knowledge to law enforcement authorities within thirty days of obtaining the knowledge, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2921.22(F)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2921.23.heading: FAILURE TO AID A LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER 2921.23(A) ORC (CCC 2321.23)
ORC:2921.23.text: _____________ did negligently (fail or refuse) to aid a law enforcement officer, to wit: (STATE NAME OF OFFICER), when called upon for assistance in (preventing or halting) (the commission of an offense or the apprehension of an offender or the detention of an offender), to wit: (STATE OFFENSE AND DESCRIBE OFFENDER), when such aid could have been given without substantial risk of physical harm to (STATE DEFENDANT’S NAME), to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2921.23(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor.

ORC:2921.24.heading: DISCLOSURE OF CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION 2921.24(A) ORC
ORC:2921.24.text: _____________ did, being an (officer or employee) of a (law enforcement agency or court or clerk of court), to wit: (DESCRIBE AGENCY OR OFFICE) disclose during a pending criminal case the home address of a (peace officer, parole officer, prosecuting attorney, assistant prosecuting attorney, correctional employee, or youth services employee) who was a witness or an arresting officer in the pending criminal case, to wit: (NAME OFFICER AND TO WHOM DISCLOSURE WAS MADE), in violation of Section 2921.24(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2921.24.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply if disclosure is by the officer, attorney, or employee (himself or herself) or pursuant to court order following a good cause hearing. Also Section 2921.25 of the Ohio Revised Code prohibits a judge or mayor in mayor’s court from ordering a peace officer to disclose his or her home address while acting as a witness in a criminal case UNLESS the judge or mayor determines the defendant has a right to such disclosure. There is no penalty for that Section.

ORC:2921.29.heading: FAILURE TO DISCLOSE ONE’S PERSONAL INFORMATION 2921.29(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2921.29.text: _____________ did, while in a public place, to wit: (LOCATION/NAME OF PUBLIC PLACE), refused to disclose (his or her) (NAME OR ADDRESS OR DATE OF BIRTH), when requested to do so by a law enforcement officer, to wit: (NAME OF REQUESTING OFFICER AND OFFICIAL TITLE/ BADGE NUMBER), who reasonably suspected (NAME OF OFFENDER) was (COMMITTING, OR HAD COMMITTED, OR WAS ABOUT TO COMMIT) a criminal offense, to wit: (CRIMINAL OFFENSE AND CODE SECTION FOR WHICH THERE WAS REASONABLE SUSPICION), in violation of Section 2921.29(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2921.29.heading: FAILURE TO DISCLOSE ONE’S PERSONAL INFORMATION 2921.29(A)(2)(a) ORC
ORC:2921.29.variant: WITNESS FELONY OFFENSE OF VIOLENCE – M4
ORC:2921.29.text: _____________ did while in a public place, to wit: (LOCATION/NAME OF PUBLIC PLACE), refused to disclose (his or her) (NAME OR ADDRESS OR DATE OF BIRTH), when requested to do so by a law enforcement officer, to wit: (NAME OF REQUESTING OFFICER AND OFFICIAL TITLE/BADGE NUMBER), who reasonably suspected (NAME OF OFFENDER) had witnessed an offense of violence that would constitute a felony under the laws of this state, to wit: (IDENTIFY THE OFFENSE OF VIOLENCE AND CODE SECTION THAT WOULD CONSTITUTE A FELONY) in violation of Section 2921.29(A)(2)(a) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2921.29.heading: FAILURE TO DISCLOSE ONE’S PERSONAL INFORMATION 2921.29(A)(2)(b) ORC
ORC:2921.29.variant: WITNESS FELONY OFFENSE – SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM – M4
ORC:2921.29.text: _____________ did while in a public place, to wit: (LOCATION/NAME OF PUBLIC PLACE), refused to disclose (his or her) (NAME OR ADDRESS OR DATE OF BIRTH), when requested to do so by a law enforcement officer, to wit: (NAME OF REQUESTING OFFICER AND OFFICIAL TITLE/BADGE NUMBER), who reasonably suspected (NAME OF OFFENDER) had witnessed a felony offense that (CAUSED OR RESULTED IN OR CREATED A SUBSTANTIAL RISK OF SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM TO ANOTHER PERSON OR TO PROPERTY), to wit: (IDENTIFY THE FELONY OFFENSE/CODE SECTION AND DESCRIBE THE RISK OF HARM), in violation of Section 2921.29(A)(2) (b) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2921.29.heading: FAILURE TO DISCLOSE ONE’S PERSONAL INFORMATION 2921.29(A)(2)(c) ORC
ORC:2921.29.variant: WITNESS ATTEMPT, CONSPIRACY, OR COMPLICITY IN COMMITTING FELONY OFFENSE – SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM – M4
ORC:2921.29.text: _____________ did while in a public place, to wit: (LOCATION/NAME OF PUBLIC PLACE), refused to disclose (his or her) (NAME OR ADDRESS OR DATE OF BIRTH), when requested to do so by a law enforcement officer, to wit: (NAME OF REQUESTING OFFICER AND OFFICIAL TITLE/ BADGE NUMBER), who reasonably suspected (NAME OF OFFENDER) had witnessed any (ATTEMPT OR CONSPIRACY TO COMMIT OR COMPLICITY IN COMMITTING) any offense identified in division 2921.29 (A)(2)(b) of the Ohio Revised Code, to wit: (IDENTIFY THE OFFENSE CODE/SECTION), in violation of Section 2921.29(A)(2)(c) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2921.29.heading: FAILURE TO DISCLOSE ONE’S PERSONAL INFORMATION 2921.29(A)(2)(d) ORC
ORC:2921.29.variant: WITNESS CONDUCT INDICATING OFFENSE OF 2921(A)(2)(a), 2921(A)(2)(b), OR 2921(A)(2)(c) ORC – M4
ORC:2921.29.text: (NAME OF WITNESS), while in a public place, to wit: (LOCATION/NAME OF PUBLIC PLACE), refused to disclose (his or her) (NAME OR ADDRESS OR DATE OF BIRTH), when requested to do so by a law enforcement officer, to wit: (NAME OF REQUESTING OFFICER AND OFFICIAL TITLE/BADGE NUMBER), who reasonably suspected (NAME OF WITNESS) had witnessed any conduct reasonably indicating that (ANY OFFENSE IN DIVISION 2921(A)(2)(a) OR (b) OF THE OHIO REVISED CODE, OR ANY ATTEMPT, CONSPIRACY, OR COMPLICITY DESCRIBED IN 2921(A)(2)(c) OF THE OHIO REVISED CODE HAS BEEN, IS BEING, OR IS ABOUT TO BE COMMITTED), to wit: (IDENTIFY THE OFFENSE), in violation of Section 2921.29(A)(2)(d) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2921.31.heading: OBSTRUCTING OFFICIAL BUSINESS 2921.31 ORC (CCC 2321.31)
ORC:2921.31.variant: OBSTRUCT PERFORMANCE OF PUBLIC OFFICIAL – M2
ORC:2921.31.text: _____________ did without privilege to do so and with purpose to (prevent or obstruct or delay) the performance by a public official, to wit: (STATE NAME OF OFFICIAL), of an authorized act which was within the public official’s official capacity, to wit: (DESCRIBE ACT), (hamper or impede) the public official in the performance of the public official’s lawful duties, to wit: (DESCRIBE MANNER IN WHICH DUTIES WERE HAMPERED), in violation of Section 2921.31 of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2921.31.heading: OBSTRUCTING OFFICIAL BUSINESS 2921.31 ORC (CCC 2321.31)
ORC:2921.31.variant: OBSTRUCT PERFORMANCE OF PUBLIC OFFICIAL – RISK OF PHYSICAL HARM – F5
ORC:2921.31.text: _____________ did without privilege to do so and with purpose to (prevent or obstruct or delay) the performance by a public official, to wit: (STATE NAME OF OFFICIAL), of an authorized act which was within the public official’s official capacity, to wit: (DESCRIBE ACT), (hamper or impede) the public official in the performance of the public official’s lawful duties, to wit: (DESCRIBE MANNER IN WHICH DUTIES WERE HAMPERED), and having created a risk of physical harm to any person, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE HARM), in violation of Section 2921.31 of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2921.32.heading: OBSTRUCTING JUSTICE 2921.32(A)(1) ORC (CCC 2321.32)
ORC:2921.32.text: _____________ did (with purpose to hinder the discovery, apprehension, prosecution, conviction, or punishment of another for misdemeanor crime or assist another to benefit from the commission of a misdemeanor crime, or with purpose to hinder the discovery, apprehension, prosecution, adjudication as a delinquent child, or disposition of a child for an act that if committed by an adult would be a misdemeanor crime or to assist a child to benefit from the commission of an act that if committed by an adult would be a misdemeanor crime), (harbor or conceal) the other person or child, to wit: (DESCRIBE ACT, PERSON ASSISTED, CRIME, SECTION NUMBER, AND DEGREE OF OFFENSE COMMITTED), in violation of Section 2921.32(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the ________ degree
ORC:2921.32.notes: NOTE: If the crime committed by the person aided is a misdemeanor or if the act committed by the child aided would be a misdemeanor if committed by an adult, the offense is a misdemeanor of the same degree as the crime committed by the person aided or a misdemeanor of the same degree that the act committed by the child aided would be if committed by an adult.

ORC:2921.32.heading: OBSTRUCTING JUSTICE 2921.32(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2921.32.variant: HARBOR OR CONCEAL – FELONY CRIME – F5
ORC:2921.32.text: _____________ did (with purpose to hinder the discovery, apprehension, prosecution, conviction, or punishment of another for felony crime or assist another to benefit from the commission of a felony crime, or with purpose to hinder the discovery, apprehension, prosecution, adjudication as a delinquent child, or disposition of a child for an act that if committed by an adult would be a felony crime or to assist a child to benefit from the commission of an act that if committed by an adult would be a felony crime), (harbor or conceal) the other person or child, to wit: (DESCRIBE ACT, PERSON ASSISTED, CRIME, SECTION NUMBER, AND DEGREE OF OFFENSE COMMITTED), in violation of Section 2921.32(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2921.32.notes: NOTE: If the crime committed by the person aided is Aggravated Murder, Murder, or a felony of the first or second degree or if the act committed by the child aided would be one of those offenses if committed by an adult and if the offender know or has reason to believe that the crime committed by the person aided is one of those offenses or that the act committed by the child aided would be one of those offenses if committed by an adult, a felony of the third degree. NOTE: If the crime committed by the person aided is Trafficking in Persons or if the act committed by the child would be Trafficking in Persons if the child was an adult, Obstructing Justice is a felony of the second degree. NOTE: If the crime or act committed by the person or child aided is an act of terrorism, obstructing justice is a felony of the second degree. If the act of terrorism resulted in the death of a person who was not a participant in the act of terrorism, it is a felony of the first degree.

ORC:2921.32.heading: OBSTRUCTING JUSTICE 2921.32(A)(2) ORC (CCC 2321.32)
ORC:2921.32.variant: AVOIDING DISCOVERY OR APPREHENSION – MISDEMEANOR CRIME
ORC:2921.32.text: _____________ did (with purpose to hinder the discovery, apprehension, prosecution, conviction, or punishment of another for misdemeanor crime or assist another to benefit from the commission of a misdemeanor crime, or with purpose to hinder the discovery, apprehension, prosecution, adjudication as a delinquent child, or disposition of a child for an act that if committed by an adult would be a misdemeanor crime or to assist a child to benefit from the commission of an act that if committed by an adult would be a misdemeanor crime), (provide the other person or child with money, transportation, a weapon, a disguise, or other means of avoiding discovery or apprehension), to wit: (DESCRIBE ACT, PERSON ASSISTED, CRIME, SECTION NUMBER, AND DEGREE OF OFFENSE COMMITTED), in violation of Section 2921.32(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the ________ degree.
ORC:2921.32.notes: NOTE: If the crime committed by the person aided is a misdemeanor or if the act committed by the child aided would be a misdemeanor if committed by an adult, the offense is a misdemeanor of the same degree as the crime committed by the person aided or a misdemeanor of the same degree that the act committed by the child aided would be if committed by an adult.

ORC:2921.32.heading: OBSTRUCTING JUSTICE 2921.32(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2921.32.variant: AVOIDING DISCOVERY OR APPREHENSION – FELONY CRIME – F5
ORC:2921.32.text: _____________ did (with purpose to hinder the discovery, apprehension, prosecution, conviction, or punishment of another for felony crime or assist another to benefit from the commission of a felony crime, or with purpose to hinder the discovery, apprehension, prosecution, adjudication as a delinquent child, or disposition of a child for an act that if committed by an adult would be a felony crime or to assist a child to benefit from the commission of an act that if committed by an adult would be a felony crime), (provide the other person or child with money, transportation, a weapon, a disguise, or other means of avoiding discovery or apprehension), to wit: (DESCRIBE ACT, PERSON ASSISTED, CRIME, SECTION NUMBER, AND DEGREE OF OFFENSE COMMITTED), in violation of Section 2921.32(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2921.32.notes: NOTE: If the crime committed by the person aided is Aggravated Murder, Murder, or a felony of the first or second degree or if the act committed by the child aided would be one of those offenses if committed by an adult and if the offender know or has reason to believe that the crime committed by the person aided is one of those offenses or that the act committed by the child aided would be one of those offenses if committed by an adult, a felony of the third degree. NOTE: If the crime committed by the person aided is Trafficking in Persons or if the act committed by the child would be Trafficking in Persons if the child was an adult, Obstructing Justice is a felony of the second degree. NOTE: If the crime or act committed by the person or child aided is an act of terrorism, obstructing justice is a felony of the second degree. If the act of terrorism resulted in the death of a person who was not a participant in the act of terrorism, it is a felony of the first degree.

ORC:2921.32.heading: OBSTRUCTING JUSTICE 2921.32(A)(3) ORC (CCC 2321.32)
ORC:2921.32.variant: WARNING OF IMPENDING DISCOVERY OR APPREHENSION – MISDEMEANOR CRIME
ORC:2921.32.text: _____________ did (with purpose to hinder the discovery, apprehension, prosecution, conviction, or punishment of another for misdemeanor crime or assist another to benefit from the commission of a misdemeanor crime, or with purpose to hinder the discovery, apprehension, prosecution, adjudication as a delinquent child, or disposition of a child for an act that if committed by an adult would be a misdemeanor crime or to assist a child to benefit from the commission of an act that if committed by an adult would be a misdemeanor crime), (warn the other person or child of impending discovery or apprehension), to wit: (DESCRIBE ACT, PERSON ASSISTED, CRIME, SECTION NUMBER, AND DEGREE OF OFFENSE COMMITTED), in violation of Section 2921.32(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the ________ degree.
ORC:2921.32.notes: NOTE: If the crime committed by the person aided is a misdemeanor or if the act committed by the child aided would be a misdemeanor if committed by an adult, the offense is a misdemeanor of the same degree as the crime committed by the person aided or a misdemeanor of the same degree that the act committed by the child aided would be if committed by an adult.

ORC:2921.32.heading: OBSTRUCTING JUSTICE 2921.32(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2921.32.variant: WARNING OF IMPENDING DISCOVERY OR APPREHENSION – FELONY CRIME
ORC:2921.32.text: _____________ did (with purpose to hinder the discovery, apprehension, prosecution, conviction, or punishment of another for felony crime or assist another to benefit from the commission of a felony crime, or with purpose to hinder the discovery, apprehension, prosecution, adjudication as a delinquent child, or disposition of a child for an act that if committed by an adult would be a felony crime or to assist a child to benefit from the commission of an act that if committed by an adult would be a felony crime), (warn the other person or child of impending discovery or apprehension), to wit: (DESCRIBE ACT, PERSON ASSISTED, CRIME, SECTION NUMBER, AND DEGREE OF OFFENSE COMMITTED), in violation of Section 2921.32(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2921.32.notes: NOTE: If the crime committed by the person aided is Aggravated Murder, Murder, or a felony of the first or second degree or if the act committed by the child aided would be one of those offenses if committed by an adult and if the offender know or has reason to believe that the crime committed by the person aided is one of those offenses or that the act committed by the child aided would be one of those offenses if committed by an adult, a felony of the third degree. NOTE: If the crime committed by the person aided is Trafficking in Persons or if the act committed by the child would be Trafficking in Persons if the child was an adult, Obstructing Justice is a felony of the second degree. NOTE: If the crime or act committed by the person or child aided is an act of terrorism, obstructing justice is a felony of the second degree. If the act of terrorism resulted in the death of a person who was not a participant in the act of terrorism, it is a felony of the first degree.

ORC:2921.32.heading: OBSTRUCTING JUSTICE 2921.32(A)(4) ORC (CCC 2321.32)
ORC:2921.32.variant: DESTROY OR CONCEAL PHYSICAL EVIDENCE – MISDEMEANOR CRIME
ORC:2921.32.text: _____________ did (with purpose to hinder the discovery, apprehension, prosecution, conviction, or punishment of another for misdemeanor crime or assist another to benefit from the commission of a misdemeanor crime, or with purpose to hinder the discovery, apprehension, prosecution, adjudication as a delinquent child, or disposition of a child for an act that if committed by an adult would be a misdemeanor crime or to assist a child to benefit from the commission of an act that if committed by an adult would be a misdemeanor crime), (destroy or conceal physical evidence of the crime or act, or induce any person to withhold testimony or information or to elude legal process summoning the person to testify or supply evidence), to wit: (DESCRIBE ACT, PERSON ASSISTED, CRIME, SECTION NUMBER, AND DEGREE OF OFFENSE COMMITTED), in violation of Section 2921.32(A)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the ________ degree.
ORC:2921.32.notes: NOTE: If the crime committed by the person aided is a misdemeanor or if the act committed by the child aided would be a misdemeanor if committed by an adult, the offense is a misdemeanor of the same degree as the crime committed by the person aided or a misdemeanor of the same degree that the act committed by the child aided would be if committed by an adult.

ORC:2921.32.heading: OBSTRUCTING JUSTICE 2921.32(A)(4) ORC
ORC:2921.32.variant: DESTROY OR CONCEAL PHYSICAL EVIDENCE – FELONY CRIME – F5
ORC:2921.32.text: _____________ did (with purpose to hinder the discovery, apprehension, prosecution, conviction, or punishment of another for felony crime or assist another to benefit from the commission of a felony crime, or with purpose to hinder the discovery, apprehension, prosecution, adjudication as a delinquent child, or disposition of a child for an act that if committed by an adult would be a felony crime or to assist a child to benefit from the commission of an act that if committed by an adult would be a felony crime), (destroy or conceal physical evidence of the crime or act, or induce any person to withhold testimony or information or to elude legal process summoning the person to testify or supply evidence), to wit: (DESCRIBE ACT, PERSON ASSISTED, CRIME, SECTION NUMBER, AND DEGREE OF OFFENSE COMMITTED), in violation of Section 2921.32(A)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2921.32.notes: NOTE: If the crime committed by the person aided is Aggravated Murder, Murder, or a felony of the first or second degree or if the act committed by the child aided would be one of those offenses if committed by an adult and if the offender know or has reason to believe that the crime committed by the person aided is one of those offenses or that the act committed by the child aided would be one of those offenses if committed by an adult, a felony of the third degree. NOTE: If the crime committed by the person aided is Trafficking in Persons or if the act committed by the child would be Trafficking in Persons if the child was an adult, Obstructing Justice is a felony of the second degree. NOTE: If the crime or act committed by the person or child aided is an act of terrorism, obstructing justice is a felony of the second degree. If the act of terrorism resulted in the death of a person who was not a participant in the act of terrorism, it is a felony of the first degree.

ORC:2921.32.heading: OBSTRUCTING JUSTICE 2921.32(A)(5) ORC (CCC 2321.32)
ORC:2921.32.text: _____________ did (with purpose to hinder the discovery, apprehension, prosecution, conviction, or punishment of another for misdemeanor crime or assist another to benefit from the commission of a misdemeanor crime, or with purpose to hinder the discovery, apprehension, prosecution, adjudication as a delinquent child, or disposition of a child for an act that if committed by an adult would be a misdemeanor crime or to assist a child to benefit from the commission of an act that if committed by an adult would be a misdemeanor crime), (communicate false information to any person), to wit: (DESCRIBE ACT, PERSON ASSISTED, CRIME, SECTION NUMBER, AND DEGREE OF OFFENSE COMMITTED), in violation of Section 2921.32(A)(5) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the ________ degree.
ORC:2921.32.notes: NOTE: If the crime committed by the person aided is a misdemeanor or if the act committed by the child aided would be a misdemeanor if committed by an adult, the offense is a misdemeanor of the same degree as the crime committed by the person aided or a misdemeanor of the same degree that the act committed by the child aided would be if committed by an adult.

ORC:2921.32.heading: OBSTRUCTING JUSTICE 2921.32(A)(5) ORC
ORC:2921.32.variant: COMMUNICATE FALSE INFORMATION – FELONY CRIME – F5
ORC:2921.32.text: _____________ did (with purpose to hinder the discovery, apprehension, prosecution, conviction, or punishment of another for felony crime or assist another to benefit from the commission of a felony crime, or with purpose to hinder the discovery, apprehension, prosecution, adjudication as a delinquent child, or disposition of a child for an act that if committed by an adult would be a felony crime or to assist a child to benefit from the commission of an act that if committed by an adult would be a felony crime), (communicate false information to any person), to wit: (DESCRIBE ACT, PERSON ASSISTED, CRIME, SECTION NUMBER, AND DEGREE OF OFFENSE COMMITTED), in violation of Section 2921.32(A)(5) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2921.32.notes: NOTE: If the crime committed by the person aided is Aggravated Murder, Murder, or a felony of the first or second degree or if the act committed by the child aided would be one of those offenses if committed by an adult and if the offender know or has reason to believe that the crime committed by the person aided is one of those offenses or that the act committed by the child aided would be one of those offenses if committed by an adult, a felony of the third degree. NOTE: If the crime committed by the person aided is Trafficking in Persons or if the act committed by the child would be Trafficking in Persons if the child was an adult, Obstructing Justice is a felony of the second degree. NOTE: If the crime or act committed by the person or child aided is an act of terrorism, obstructing justice is a felony of the second degree. If the act of terrorism resulted in the death of a person who was not a participant in the act of terrorism, it is a felony of the first degree.

ORC:2921.32.heading: OBSTRUCTING JUSTICE 2921.32(A)(6) ORC
ORC:2921.32.variant: PREVENT OR OBSTRUCT BY FORCE – F5
ORC:2921.32.text: _____________ did (prevent or obstruct) any person, by means of (force, intimidation ,or deception), from performing any act to aid in the (discovery, apprehension, or prosecution) of the other person or child, to wit: (DESCRIBE ACT, PERSON ASSISTED, CRIME, SECTION NUMBER, AND DEGREE OF OFFENSE COMMITTED), in violation of Section 2921.32(A)(6) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2921.32.notes: NOTE: If the crime committed by the person aided is Aggravated Murder, Murder, or a felony of the first or second degree or if the act committed by the child aided would be one of those offenses if committed by an adult and if the offender know or has reason to believe that the crime committed by the person aided is one of those offenses or that the act committed by the child aided would be one of those offenses if committed by an adult, a felony of the third degree. NOTE: If the crime committed by the person aided is Trafficking in Persons or if the act committed by the child would be Trafficking in Persons if the child was an adult, Obstructing Justice is a felony of the second degree. NOTE: If the crime or act committed by the person or child aided is an act of terrorism, obstructing justice is a felony of the second degree. If the act of terrorism resulted in the death of a person who was not a participant in the act of terrorism, it is a felony of the first degree.

ORC:2921.32.heading: OBSTRUCTING JUSTICE 2921.32(A)(6) ORC
ORC:2921.32.variant: PREVENT OR OBSTRUCT BY FORCE – MISDEMEANOR CRIME
ORC:2921.32.text: _____________ did (prevent or obstruct) any person, by means of (force, intimidation ,or deception), from performing any act to aid in the (discovery, apprehension, or prosecution) of the other person or child, to wit: (DESCRIBE ACT, PERSON ASSISTED, CRIME, SECTION NUMBER, AND DEGREE OF OFFENSE COMMITTED), in violation of Section 2921.32(A)(6) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the ________ degree.
ORC:2921.32.notes: NOTE: If the crime committed by the person aided is misdemeanor or if the act committed by the child aided would be a misdemeanor if committed by an adult, the offense is a misdemeanor of the same degree as the crime committed by the person aided or a misdemeanor of the same degree that the act committed by the child aided would be if committed by an adult. DEFINITIONS 2921.321 PHYSICAL HARM – any injury, illness, or other physiological impairment, regardless of its gravity or duration. POLICE DOG OR POLICE HORSE – a dog or horse that has been trained, and may be used, to assist law enforcement officer in the performance of their official duties. SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM – any physical harm that carries a substantial risk of death; any physical harm that causes permanent maiming or that involves some temporary, substantial maiming; or, any physical harm that causes acute pain of a duration that results in substantial suffering. HANDICAPPED ASSISTANCE DOG – any dog that serves as a guide or leader for a blind person or as a listener for a deaf person or that provides support or assistance for a mobility impaired person. BLIND – vision twenty-two hundred or less in the better eye with proper correction which contracts the peripheral field so that the diameter of the visual field subtends an angle no greater than twenty degrees. MOBILITY IMPAIRED PERSON – any person, regardless of age, who is subject to a physiological defect or deficiency regardless of its cause, nature, or extent that renders the person unable to move about without the aid of crutches, a wheelchair, or any other form of support, or that limits the person’s functional ability to ambulate, climb, descend, sit, rise, or to perform any related function.

ORC:2921.321.heading: ASSAULTING A POLICE DOG OR POLICE HORSE 2921.321(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2921.321.text: _____________ did knowingly (cause or attempt to cause) physical harm to a police (dog or horse), when the police (dog or horse) was assisting a law enforcement officer in the performance of the officer’s official duties at the time the physical harm was caused or attempted, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.321(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code:

ORC:2921.321.heading: ASSAULTING A POLICE DOG OR POLICE HORSE 2921.321(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2921.321.variant: KNOWN POLICE DOG/POLICE HORSE – NOT ASSISTING
ORC:2921.321.text: _____________ did knowingly (cause or attempt to cause) physical harm to a police (dog or horse), when the police (dog or horse) was not assisting a law enforcement officer in the performance of the officer’s official duties at the time the physical harm was caused or attempted, but the offender having actual knowledge that the (dog or horse) was a police (dog or horse), to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.321(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code.

ORC:2921.321.heading: HARASSING A POLICE DOG OR HORSE 2921.321(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2921.321.text: _____________ did recklessly (taunt or torment or strike) a police (dog or horse), to wit: (DESCRIBE ACTION), in violation of Section 2921.321(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code:

ORC:2921.321.heading: HARASSING A POLICE DOG OR HORSE 2921.321(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2921.321.text: _____________ did recklessly throw an (object or substance) at a police (dog or horse), to wit: (DESCRIBE OBJECT OR SUBSTANCE THROWN), in violation of Section 2921.321(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code:

ORC:2921.321.heading: HARASSING A POLICE DOG OR HORSE 2921.321(B)(3) ORC
ORC:2921.321.text: _____________ did recklessly (interfere with or obstruct a police dog or horse or interfere with or obstruct a law enforcement officer assisted by a police dog or horse), to wit: (DESCRIBE INTERFERENCE), by (inhibiting or restricting the law enforcement officer’s control of the police (dog or horse) or depriving the law enforcement officer of control of the police (dog or horse) or releasing the police (dog or horse) from its area of control or entering the area of control of the police dog or horse without the consent of the law enforcement officer, including placing food or other objects or substances in the area), to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCE), in violation of Section 2921.321(B)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code:

ORC:2921.321.heading: HARASSING A POLICE DOG OR HORSE 2921.321(B)(4) ORC
ORC:2921.321.text: _____________ did recklessly engage in conduct that was likely to cause serious physical injury or death to a police (dog or horse), to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT), in violation of Section 2921.321(B)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code:

ORC:2921.321.heading: HARASSING A POLICE DOG OR HORSE 2921.321(B)(5) ORC
ORC:2921.321.variant: DOG OWNER FAILS TO RESTRAIN DOG FROM HARASSING POLICE ANIMAL
ORC:2921.321.text: _____________ did recklessly (as the owner, keeper, or harborer) of a dog, fail to reasonably restrain the dog from (taunting, tormenting, chasing, approaching in a menacing fashion or apparent attitude of attack, or attempting to bite or otherwise endanger) a police (dog or horse) that at the time of the conduct is assisting a law enforcement officer in the performance of the officer’s duties or that the person knows is a police (dog or horse), to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT), in violation of Section 2921.321(B)(5) of the Ohio Revised Code:

ORC:2921.321.heading: ASSAULTING A HANDICAPPED ASSISTANCE DOG 2921.321(C)(1) ORC
ORC:2921.321.text: _____________ did knowingly (cause or attempt to cause) physical harm to a handicapped assistance dog, when the handicapped assistance dog was assisting a (blind, deaf or hearing impaired, or mobility impaired person) at the time the physical harm was caused or attempted, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.321(C)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code:

ORC:2921.321.heading: ASSAULTING A HANDICAPPED ASSISTANCE DOG 2921.321(C)(2) ORC
ORC:2921.321.text: _____________ did, knowingly (cause or attempt to cause) physical harm to a handicapped assistance dog, when the handicapped assistance dog was not assisting a blind, deaf, hearing impaired, mobility impaired person, or person with a seizure disorder at the time the physical harm was caused or attempted, but the offender having actual knowledge that the dog was a handicapped assistance dog, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.321(C)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code:

ORC:2921.321.heading: HARASSING A HANDICAPPED ASSISTANCE DOG 2921.321(D)(1) ORC
ORC:2921.321.text: _____________ did recklessly (taunt or torment or strike) a handicapped assistance dog, when the handicapped assistance dog was assisting a (blind, deaf or hearing impaired, or mobility impaired person), to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.321(D)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code:

ORC:2921.321.heading: HARASSING A HANDICAPPED ASSISTANCE DOG 2921.321(D)(2) ORC
ORC:2921.321.text: _____________ did recklessly throw an (object or substance) at a handicapped assistance dog, when the handicapped assistance dog was not assisting a (blind, deaf or hearing impaired, or mobility impaired person), to wit: (DESCRIBE OBJECT OR SUBSTANCE THROWN), in violation of Section 2921.321(D) (2) of the Ohio Revised Code:

ORC:2921.321.heading: HARASSING A HANDICAPPED ASSISTANCE DOG 2921.321(D-3) ORC
ORC:2921.321.text: _____________ did recklessly (interfere with or obstruct) a handicapped assistance dog, when the handicapped assistance dog was not assisting a (blind, deaf or hearing impaired, or mobility impaired person), to wit: (DESCRIBE INTERFERENCE), by (inhibiting or restricting the assisted or served person’s control of the handicapped assistance dog or depriving the assisted or served person’s of control of the handicapped assistance dog or releasing the handicapped assistance dog from its area of control or entering the area of control of the handicapped assistance dog without the consent of the assisted or served person, including placing food or other objects or substances in the area or inhibiting or restricting the ability of the handicapped assistance dog to assist the assisted or served person), to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCE), in violation of Section 2921.321(D-3) of the Ohio Revised Code:

ORC:2921.321.heading: HARASSING A HANDICAPPED ASSISTANCE DOG 2921.321(D)(4) ORC
ORC:2921.321.text: _____________ did recklessly engage in conduct that was likely to cause serious physical injury or death to a handicapped assistance dog, to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT), in violation of Section 2921.321(D)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code:

ORC:2921.321.heading: HARASSING A HANDICAPPED ASSISTANCE DOG 2921.321(D)(5) ORC
ORC:2921.321.text: _____________ did recklessly (as the owner, keeper, or harborer) of a dog, fail to reasonable restrain the dog from (taunting, tormenting, chasing, approaching in a menacing fashion or apparent attitude of attack, or attempting to bite or otherwise endanger) a handicapped assistance dog that at the time of the conduct is (assisting or serving a blind, deaf or hearing impaired, or mobility impaired person, or that the person knows is a handicapped assistance dog), to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT), in violation of Section 2921.321(D)(5) of the Ohio Revised Code:

ORC:2921.33.heading: RESISTING ARREST 2921.33(A) ORC (CCC 2321.33)
ORC:2921.33.variant: RESIST OR INTERFERE WITH ARREST – M2
ORC:2921.33.text: _____________ did (recklessly or by force) (resist or interfere with) the lawful arrest of (himself or another, to wit: STATE NAME), in the following manner, to wit: (DESCRIBE ACTIONS), in violation of Section 2921.33(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2921.33.heading: RESISTING ARREST 2921.33(B) ORC
ORC:2921.33.variant: CAUSE PHYSICAL HARM TO A LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER – M1
ORC:2921.33.text: ______________ did (recklessly or by force) (resist or interfere with) the lawful arrest of (himself or another) to wit: (STATE NAME OF OFFENDER) and (during the course of or as a result of the resistance or interference), to wit: (DESCRIBE ACTIONS), did cause physical harm, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE PHYSICAL HARM), to a law enforcement officer, to wit: (NAME OF OFFICER), in violation of Section 2921.33(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.33.heading: RESISTING ARREST 2921.33(C)(1) ORC
ORC:2921.33.variant: CAUSE PHYSICAL HARM BY MEANS OF DEADLY WEAPON – F4
ORC:2921.33.text: _____________ did (recklessly or by force) (resist or interfere with) the lawful arrest of (himself or another), to wit: (STATE NAME OF OFFENDER), when the offender (during the course of the resistance or interference or as a result of the resistance or interference) recklessly caused physical harm, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE PHYSICAL HARM), to a law enforcement officer, to wit: (STATE NAME OF OFFICER), by means of a deadly weapon, to wit: (DESCRIBE WEAPON), in violation of Section 2921.33(C)(1) of the Ohio Revised, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2921.33.heading: RESISTING ARREST 2921.33(C)(2) ORC
ORC:2921.33.text: _____________ did (recklessly or by force) (resist or interfere with) the lawful arrest of (himself or another) to wit: (STATE NAME OF OFFENDER) and (during the course of the resistance or interference), to wit: (DESCRIBE ACTIONS), the offender did brandish a deadly weapon, to wit: (DESCRIBE WEAPON), in violation of Section 2921.33(C)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2921.331.heading: FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH OFFICER’S ORDER OR SIGNAL 2921.331(A) ORC (CCC 2321.331(A))
ORC:2921.331.text: _____________ did fail to comply with a lawful (order or direction) of a police officer who was invested with authority to direct, control or regulate traffic, to wit: (DESCRIBE ORDER AND NON-COMPLIANCE), in violation of Section 2921.331(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.331.heading: FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH OFFICER’S ORDER OR SIGNAL 2921.331(B) ORC
ORC:2921.331.variant: BY FLEEING IN MOTOR VEHICLE – F4
ORC:2921.331.text: _____________ did operate a motor vehicle, to wit: (DESCRIBE VEHICLE) so as willfully to elude or flee a police officer, to wit: (NAME OFFICER) after receiving a (visible or audible) signal from a police officer to bring the motor vehicle to a stop, to wit: (DESCRIBE SIGNAL AND FLEEING CONDUCT), in violation of Section 2921.331(B), of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2921.331.heading: FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH OFFICER’S ORDER OR SIGNAL 2921.331(B) ORC
ORC:2921.331.variant: BY FLEEING IN MOTOR VEHICLE IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE COMMISSION OF A FELONY – F3
ORC:2921.331.text: _____________ did operate a motor vehicle, to wit: (DESCRIBE VEHICLE) so as willfully to elude or flee a police officer, to wit: (NAME OFFICER) after receiving a (visible or audible) signal from a police officer to bring the motor vehicle to a stop, to wit: (DESCRIBE SIGNAL AND FLEEING CONDUCT), and fleeing immediately after the commission of a felony, to wit: (DESCRIBE FELONY COMMITTED) in violation of Section 2921.331(B), of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2921.331.heading: FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH OFFICER’S ORDER OR SIGNAL 2921.331(B) ORC
ORC:2921.331.variant: HAVING CAUSED SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM OR A SUBSTANTIAL RISK OF SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM – F3
ORC:2921.331.text: _____________ did operate a motor vehicle, to wit: (DESCRIBE VEHICLE) so as willfully to elude or flee a police officer, to wit: (NAME OFFICER) after receiving a (visible or audible) signal from a police officer to bring the motor vehicle to a stop, to wit: (DESCRIBE SIGNAL AND FLEEING CONDUCT), and having caused serious physical harm or caused a substantial risk of serious physical harm to persons or property, to wit: (DESCRIBE PHYSICAL HARM OR RISK) in violation of Section 2921.331(B), of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2921.34.heading: ESCAPE 2921.34(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2921.34.text: _____________ did, knowing oneself to be under detention other than supervised release detention or being reckless in that regard, (purposely break or attempt to break the detention, or purposely fail to return to detention), either (following temporary leave granted for a specific purpose or limited period, or at the time required when serving a sentence in intermittent confinement), to wit: (DESCRIBE ACTION), in violation of Section 2921.34(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code: See Degree Listed Below:

ORC:2921.34.heading: ESCAPE 2921.34(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2921.34.text: _____________ knowing oneself to be under a geographic restriction or being reckless in that regard, did (purposely leave the geographic area to which the restriction applies or purposely fail to return to that geographic area following a temporary leave granted for a specific purpose or for a specific period of time), to wit: (DESCRIBE ACTION AND DESCRIBE THE RESTRICTION), in violation of Section 2921.34(A)(2)(b) of the Ohio Revised Code: See Degree Listed Below:
ORC:2921.34.notes: NOTE: This division applies to any person who is sentenced to a prison term pursuant to Ohio Revised Code 2971.03(A)(3) or (B) whose sentence has been modified to restrict such person to a geographic area pursuant to Ohio Revised Code 2971.05. – If the offender, at the time of the commission of the offense, was under detention as an alleged or adjudicated delinquent or unruly child, and if the act for which the offender was under detention would not be a felony if committed by an adult, escape, in violation of Section 2921.34(A)(2), is a misdemeanor of the first degree. – If the offender, at the time of the commission of the offense, was under detention in any other manner or if the offender is a person for whom the requirement that the entire prison term imposed upon the person pursuant to division (A)(3) or (B) of Section 2971.03 of the Revised Code be served in a state correctional institution has been modified pursuant to Section 2971.05 of the Revised Code, when the most serious offense for which the person was under detention or for which the person has been sentenced to the prison term under Division (A)(3), (B)(1)(a), (b), or (c), (B)(2)(a), (b), or (c), or (B)(3)(a), (b), (c), or (d) of Section 2971.03 of the Revised Code is aggravated murder, murder, or a felony of the first or second degree or, if the person was under detention as an alleged or adjudicated delinquent child, when the most serious act for which the person was under detention would be aggravated murder, murder, or a felony of the first or second degree if committed by an adult, escape, in violation of 2921.34(A)(2), is a felony of the second degree. – If the offender, at the time of the commission of the offense, was under detention in any other manner or if the offender is a person for whom the requirement that the entire prison term imposed upon the person pursuant to Division (A)(3) or (B) of Section 2971.03 of the Revised Code be served in a state correctional institution has been modified pursuant to Section 2971.05 of the Revised Code, when the most serious offense for which the person was under detention or for which the person had been sentenced under Division (A)(3), (B)(1)(a), (b), or (c), (B)(2)(a), (b), or (c), or (B)(3)(a), (b), (c), or (d) of Section 2971.03 of the Revised Code is a felony of the third, fourth, or fifth degree or an unclassified felony or, if the person was under detention as an alleged or adjudicated delinquent child, when the most serious act for which the person was under detention would be a felony of the third, fourth, or fifth degree or an unclassified felony if committed by an adult, escape, in violation of 2921.34(A)(2), is a felony of the third degree. – If the offender at the time of the commission of the offense, was under detention in any other manner, for which the most serious offense is a misdemeanor, escape, in violation of 2921.34(A)(2), is a felony of the fifth degree. – If the offender at the time of the commission of the offense, was under detention in any other manner, after being found not guilty by reason of insanity, and the person’s detention consisted of hospitalization, institutionalization, or confinement in a facility under an order made pursuant to or under authority of Section 2945.40, 2945.401, or 2945.402 of the Revised Code, escape, in violation of 2921.34(A)(2), is a felony of the fifth degree. – If the offender at the time of the commission of the offense, was under detention in any other manner, when the most serious offense for which the offender was under detention is a misdemeanor and the offender fails to return to the detention at a specified time following temporary leave granted for a specific purpose or limited period or at the time required when serving a sentence in intermittent confinement, escape, in violation of 2921.34(A) (2), is a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.34.heading: ESCAPE 2921.34(A)(3) ORC
