ORC:2921.34.text: _____________, knowing oneself to be under supervised release detention or being reckless in that regard, did (purposely break or attempt to break the supervised release detention OR purposely fail to return to the supervised release detention), either (following temporary leave granted for a specific purpose or limited period, OR at the time required when serving a sentence in intermittent confinement), to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2921.34(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2921.34.notes: NOTE: If the offender violates division (A)(3) of this section and if, at the time of the commission of the offense, the most serious offense for which the offender was under supervised release detention was aggravated murder, murder, any other offense for which a sentence of life imprisonment was imposed, or a felony of the first or second degree, escape is a felony of the fourth degree. NOTE: As used in this section, “supervised release detention” means detention that is supervision of a person by an employee of the department of rehabilitation and correction while the person is on any type of release from a state correctional institution, other than transitional control under ORC 2967.26 or placement in a community-based correctional facility by the parole board under ORC 2967.28.

ORC:2921.35.heading: AIDING ESCAPE OR RESISTANCE TO AUTHORITY 2921.35(A) ORC
ORC:2921.35.variant: INSTRUMENTS BROUGHT IN TO ASSIST IN ESCAPING – F4
ORC:2921.35.text: _____________ did, with a purpose to promote or facilitate an escape or resistance to lawful authority, (convey into a detention facility or provide to anyone confined therein instruments or things which may be used to escape or resist authority), to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.35(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2921.35.heading: AIDING ESCAPE OR RESISTANCE TO AUTHORITY 2921.35(B) ORC
ORC:2921.35.variant: INSTRUMENT GIVEN TO ANOTHER INMATE TO ASSIST IN ESCAPING – F4
ORC:2921.35.text: _____________ did, being confined in a detention facility, and with purpose to promote or facilitate an escape or resistance to lawful authority, make, procure, conceal, unlawfully possess or give to another inmate, any instrument or thing which may be used for such purposes, with a purpose to promote or facilitate escape or resistance to lawful authority, to wit: (DESCRIBE) in violation of Section 2921.35(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2921.35.notes: DEFINITIONS 2921.36 DEADLY WEAPON – any instrument, device, or thing capable of inflicting death, and designed or specially adapted for use as a weapon, or possessed, carried, or used as a weapon. DANGEROUS ORDNANCE – any automatic or sawed-off firearm, zip-gun, or ballistic knife; any explosive device or incendiary device; any other explosive substance having sufficient brisance or power to be particularly suitable for use as a military explosive, or for use in mining, quarrying, excavating, or demolitions; any firearm, rocket launcher, mortar, artillery piece, grenade, mine, bomb, torpedo, or similar weapon, designed and manufactured for military purposes, and the ammunition for that weapon; any firearm muffler or silencer; any combination of parts that is intended by the owner for use in converting any firearm or other device into a dangerous ordnance. DRUG OF ABUSE – any controlled substance as defined in Section 3719.01 of the Revised Code, any harmful intoxicant as defined in Section 2925.01 of the Revised Code, and any dangerous drug as defined in Section 4729.02 of the Revised Code. INTOXICATING LIQUOR – all liquids and compounds, other than beer as defined in division (B)(2) of Section 4301.01, containing one-half of one per cent or more of alcohol by volume which are fit to use for beverage purposes, from whatever source and by whatever process produced, by whatever name called, and whether the same are medicated, proprietary, or patented. The phrase includes wine, as defined in division (B)(3) of this section even if it contains less than four per cent of alcohol by volume, mixed beverages, as defined in division (B)(4) of this section even if they contain less than four per cent of alcohol by volume, cider, as defined in division (B)(21) of this section, alcohol, and all solids and confections which contain any alcohol.

ORC:2921.36.heading: ILLEGAL CONVEYANCE OF WEAPONS OR PROHIBITED ITEMS ONTO GROUNDS OF DETENTION FACILITY OR INSTITUTION 2921.36(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2921.36.variant: CONVEY OR ATTEMPT TO CONVEY WEAPONS OR DANGEROUS ORDNANCE – F3
ORC:2921.36.text: _____________ did, knowingly convey, or attempt to convey, onto the grounds of (a detention facility, an institution, an office building, or other place), that is under the control of the (department of mental health and addiction services, department of developmental disabilities, department of youth services, or department of rehabilitation and correction), to wit: (NAME THE FACILITY), any deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance, as defined in Section 2923.11 of the Revised Code, or any part of or ammunition for use in such a deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.36(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2921.36.notes: NOTE: If the offender is an officer or employee of the department of rehabilitation and correction, the court shall impose a mandatory prison term. NOTE: It is an affirmative defense to a charge under (A)(1) of this section that the weapon or dangerous ordnance in question was being transported in a motor vehicle for any lawful purpose, that it was not on the actor’s person, and, if the weapon or dangerous ordnance in question was a firearm, that it was unloaded and was being carried in a closed package, box, or case or in a compartment that can be reached only by leaving the vehicle.

ORC:2921.36.heading: ILLEGAL CONVEYANCE OF DRUGS OF ABUSE ONTO THE GROUNDS OF DETENTION FACILITY OR INSTITUTION 2921.36(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2921.36.variant: CONVEY OR ATTEMPT TO CONVEY DRUGS OF ABUSE – F3
ORC:2921.36.text: _____________ did, knowingly convey, or attempt to convey, onto the grounds of (a detention facility, an institution, an office building, or other place), that is under the control of the (department of mental health and addiction services, department of developmental disabilities, department of youth services, or department of rehabilitation and correction), to wit: (NAME THE FACILITY), any drug of abuse, as defined in 3719.011 of the Revised Code, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.36(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2921.36.notes: NOTE: If the offender is an officer or employee of the department of rehabilitation and correction or of the department of youth services, the court shall impose a mandatory prison term.

ORC:2921.36.heading: ILLEGAL CONVEYANCE OF INTOXICATING LIQUOR ONTO THE GROUNDS OF DETENTION FACILITY OR INSTITUTION 2921.36(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2921.36.variant: CONVEY OR ATTEMPT TO CONVEY INTOXICATING LIQUOR – M2
ORC:2921.36.text: _____________ did, knowingly convey, or attempt to convey, onto the grounds of (a detention facility, an institution, an office building, or other place), that is under the control of the (department of mental health and addiction services, department of developmental disabilities, department of youth services, or department of rehabilitation and correction), to wit: (NAME THE FACILITY), any intoxicating liquor, as defined in Section 4301.01 of the Revised Code, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.36(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.
ORC:2921.36.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply if any person conveys or attempts to convey an item onto the grounds of a detention facility or of an institution under the control of the department of mental health and addiction services or the department of developmental disabilities pursuant to the written authorization of the person in charge of the detention facility or the institution and in accordance with the written rules of the detention facility or the institution.

ORC:2921.36.heading: ILLEGAL CONVEYANCE OF WEAPONS ONTO THE GROUNDS OF A DETENTION FACILITY OR INSTITUTION 2921.36(C) ORC
ORC:2921.36.variant: DELIVER OR ATTEMPT TO DELIVER DEADLY WEAPON OR ORDNANCE – F3
ORC:2921.36.text: _____________ did, knowingly (deliver or attempt to deliver) to (any person who is confined in a detention facility, a child confined in a youth services facility, a prisoner who is temporarily released from confinement for a work assignment, any patient in an institution under the control of the department of mental health and addiction services or the department of developmental disabilities), to wit: (NAME THE FACILITY), any deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance, as defined in Section 2923.11 of the Revised Code, or any part of or ammunition for use in such a deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.36(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2921.36.notes: NOTE: If the offender is an officer or employee of the department of rehabilitation and correction, the court shall impose a mandatory prison term.

ORC:2921.36.heading: ILLEGAL CONVEYANCE OF PROHIBITED ITEM ONTO THE GROUNDS OF A DETENTION FACILITY OR INSTITUTION 2921.36(C) ORC
ORC:2921.36.variant: DELIVER OR ATTEMPT TO DELIVER DRUG OF ABUSE – F3
ORC:2921.36.text: _____________ did knowingly (deliver or attempt to deliver) to (any person who is confined in a detention facility, a child confined in a youth services facility, a prisoner who is temporarily released from confinement for a work assignment, any patient in an institution under the control of the department of mental health and addiction services or the department of developmental disabilities), to wit: (NAME THE FACILITY), any drug of abuse, as defined in Section 3719.011 of the Revised Code, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.36(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2921.36.notes: NOTE: If the offender is an officer or employee of the department of rehabilitation and correction or of the department of youth services, the court shall impose a mandatory prison term.

ORC:2921.36.heading: ILLEGAL CONVEYANCE OF PROHIBITED ITEM ONTO THE GROUNDS OF A DETENTION FACILITY OR INSTITUTION 2921.36(C) ORC
ORC:2921.36.variant: DELIVER OR ATTEMPT TO DELIVER INTOXICATING LIQUOR – M2
ORC:2921.36.text: _____________ did knowingly (deliver or attempt to deliver) to (any person who is confined in a detention facility, a child confined in a youth services facility, a prisoner who is temporarily released from confinement for a work assignment, any patient in an institution under the control of the department of mental health and addiction services or the department of developmental disabilities), to wit: (NAME THE FACILITY), intoxicating liquor, as defined in Section 4301.01 of the Revised Code, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.36(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.
ORC:2921.36.notes: NOTE: It is an affirmative defense to a charge under this section that the actor was not otherwise prohibited by law from delivering the item to the confined person or the patient and that either of the following applies: 1. The actor was permitted by the written rules of the detention facility or the institution to deliver the item to the confined person or the patient. 2. The actor was given written authorization by the person in charge of the detention facility or the institution to deliver the item to the confined person or the patient.

ORC:2921.36.heading: ILLEGAL CONVEYANCE OF CASH ONTO THE GROUNDS OF DETENTION FACILITY 2921.36(D) ORC
ORC:2921.36.text: _____________ did knowingly (deliver or attempt to deliver) cash to (any person who was confined in a detention facility, a child confined in a youth services facility, or a prisoner who is temporarily released from confinement for a work assignment), to wit: (DESCRIBE AND NAME THE FACILITY), in violation of Section 2921.36(D) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.36.heading: ILLEGAL CONVEYANCE OF CASH ONTO THE GROUNDS OF DETENTION FACILITY 2921.36(D) ORC
ORC:2921.36.text: _____________ did knowingly (deliver or attempt to deliver) cash to (any person who was confined in a detention facility, a child confined in a youth services facility, or a prisoner who is temporarily released from confinement for a work assignment), to wit: (DESCRIBE AND NAME THE FACILITY), and having previously been convicted of or pleaded guilty to this offense, to wit: (COURT, DATE) in violation of Section 2921.36(D) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2921.36.heading: ILLEGAL CONVEYANCE OF COMMUNICATION DEVICE ONTO THE GROUNDS OF DETENTION FACILITY 2921.36(E) ORC
ORC:2921.36.text: _____________ did knowingly (deliver or attempt to deliver) (a cellular telephone, two-way radio, or other electronic communications device) to (any person who was confined in a detention facility, a child confined in a youth services facility, or a prisoner who is temporarily released from confinement for a work assignment), to wit: (DESCRIBE AND NAME THE FACILITY), in violation of Section 2921.36(E) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.36.heading: ILLEGAL CONVEYANCE OF COMMUNICATION DEVICE ONTO THE GROUNDS OF DETENTION FACILITY 2921.36(E) ORC
ORC:2921.36.variant: DELIVER CELL PHONE – PRIOR CONVICTION – F5
ORC:2921.36.text: _____________ did knowingly (deliver or attempt to deliver) (a cellular telephone, two-way radio, or other electronic communications device) to (any person who was confined in a detention facility, a child confined in a youth services facility, or a prisoner who is temporarily released from confinement for a work assignment), to wit: (DESCRIBE AND NAME THE FACILITY), and having previously been convicted of or pleaded guilty to this offense, to wit: (COURT, DATE) in violation of Section 2921.36(E) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.38.heading: HARASSMENT WITH A BODILY SUBSTANCE 2921.38(A) ORC
ORC:2921.38.text: _____________ did, being confined in a detention facility, to wit: (NAME FACILITY), with intent to harass, annoy, threaten, or alarm another person, to wit: (NAME OF PERSON), cause or attempt to cause the other person to come into contact with blood, semen, urine, feces, or another bodily substance by throwing the bodily substance at the other person, by expelling the bodily substance upon the other person, or in any other manner, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.38(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2921.38.heading: HARASSMENT WITH A BODILY SUBSTANCE 2921.38(B) ORC
ORC:2921.38.variant: EXPELLING BODILY SUBSTANCES UPON A LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER – F5
ORC:2921.38.text: _____________ did, with intent to harass, annoy, threaten, or alarm a law enforcement officer, to wit: (NAME OF OFFICER), cause or attempt to cause the law enforcement officer to come into contact with blood, semen, urine, feces, or another bodily substance by throwing the bodily substance at the law enforcement officer, by expelling the bodily substance upon the law enforcement officer, or in any other manner, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.38(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2921.38.heading: HARASSMENT WITH A BODILY SUBSTANCE 2921.38(C) ORC
ORC:2921.38.variant: EXPELLING BODILY SUBSTANCES – CARRIER OF VIRUS – F3
ORC:2921.38.text: _____________ did, with knowledge that the person is a carrier of the virus that causes acquired immunodeficiency syndrome, is a carrier of a hepatitis virus, or is infected with tuberculosis, and with intent to harass, annoy, threaten, or alarm another person, to wit: (NAME OF PERSON), cause or attempt to cause the other person to come into contact with blood, semen, urine, feces, or another bodily substance by throwing the bodily substance at the other person, by expelling the bodily substance upon the other person, or in any other manner, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.38(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2921.38.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to a person who is hospitalized, institutionalized, or confined in a facility operated by the department of mental health and addiction services or the department of developmental disabilities.

ORC:2921.41.heading: THEFT IN OFFICE 2921.41(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2921.41.text: _____________ did, being a public official or party official, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMPLOYMENT), commit a theft offense, using the offender’s office or permitting its use or assenting to its use in aid of such offense, to wit: (DESCRIBE INCLUDING THE THEFT OFFENSE), in violation of Section 2921.41(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2921.41.notes: – VALUE $1,000.00 OR MORE AND LESS THAN $7,500.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $7,500.00 OR MORE AND LESS THAN $150,000.00, a felony of the third degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE AND LESS THAN $750,000.00, a felony of the second degree. – VALUE $750,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the first degree.

ORC:2921.41.heading: THEFT IN OFFICE 2921.41(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2921.41.text: _____________ did, being a public official or party official, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMPLOYMENT), commit a theft offense, involving property or service owned by this or any state, the United States, a county, municipal corporation, or township, or any political subdivision, department, or agency thereof, or by a political party, or which is part of a political campaign fund, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.41(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2921.41.notes: – VALUE $1,000.00 OR MORE AND LESS THAN $7,500.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE $7,500.00 OR MORE AND LESS THAN $150,000.00, a felony of the third degree. – VALUE $150,000.00 OR MORE AND LESS THAN $750,000.00, a felony of the second degree. – VALUE $750,000.00 OR MORE, a felony of the first degree. NOTE: A person convicted or pleading guilty to this section is forever barred from office of public trust. In addition to any imprisonment or fine, the court shall require restitution. State retirement and deferred compensation benefits may be withheld to effect restitution, and the prosecutor must notify the retirement and deferred compensation systems of the filing of charges.

ORC:2921.42.heading: HAVING AN UNLAWFUL INTEREST IN A PUBLIC CONTRACT 2921.42(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2921.42.text: _____________ did, being a public official, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMPLOYMENT), knowingly authorize or employ the authority or influence of (his or her) office to secure authorization of a public contract in which (he or she), a member of (his or her) family, or any of (his or her) business associates has an interest, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.42(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2921.42.heading: HAVING AN UNLAWFUL INTEREST IN A PUBLIC CONTRACT 2921.42(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2921.42.variant: SECURE INVESTMENT OF PUBLIC FUNDS – F4
ORC:2921.42.text: _____________ did, being a public official, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMPLOYMENT), knowingly authorize or employ the authority or influence of (his or her) office to secure the investment of public funds in any share, bond, mortgage, or other security, with such public official, a member of (his or her) family, or any of (his or her) business associates either has an interest, or is an underwriter, or receives any brokerage, origination, or servicing fees, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.42(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2921.42.heading: HAVING AN UNLAWFUL INTEREST IN A PUBLIC CONTRACT 2921.42(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2921.42.variant: OCCUPY ANY POSITION OF PROFIT IN THE PROSECUTION OF A PUBLIC CONTRACT – M1
ORC:2921.42.text: _____________ did, being or having been a public official, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMPLOYMENT) knowingly, during (his or her) term of office or within one year thereafter, occupy any position of profit in the prosecution of a public contract authorized by (him or her) or by a legislative body, commission, or board of which (he or she) was a member at the time of authorization, unless the contract was let by competitive bidding to the lowest and best bidder, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.42(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.42.heading: HAVING AN UNLAWFUL INTEREST IN A PUBLIC CONTRACT 2921.42(A)(4) ORC
ORC:2921.42.variant: HAVE AN INTEREST IN THE PUBLIC CONTRACT WITH POLITICAL SUBDIVISION OR AGENCY – M1
ORC:2921.42.text: _____________ did, being or having been a public official, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMPLOYMENT), knowingly, have an interest in the profits or benefits of a public contract entered into by or for the use of the political subdivision or governmental agency or instrumentality with which (he or she) is connected, to wit: (DESCRIBE), In violation of Section 2921.42(A)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.42.heading: HAVING AN UNLAWFUL INTEREST IN A PUBLIC CONTRACT 2921.42(A)(5)
ORC:2921.42.variant: HAVING AN INTEREST IN CONTRACT INVOLVING MORE THAN $150 – M1
ORC:2921.42.text: _____________ did, being or having been a public official, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMPLOYMENT), knowingly, have an interest in the profits or benefits of a public contract that is not let by competitive bidding if required by law and that involves more than one hundred fifty dollars ($150.00), to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.42(A)(5) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.43.heading: SOLICITING OR RECEIVING IMPROPER COMPENSATION 2921.43(A) (1) ORC
ORC:2921.43.text: _____________ did knowingly promise or give to a public servant, to wit: (NAME PUBLIC SERVANT) or, being a public servant, knowingly solicit or accept any compensation other than as allowed by law, to perform the public servant’s official duties, or perform any other act in the public servant’s public capacity, or for the general performance of the duties of the public servant’s public compensation, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.43(A) (1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.43.heading: SOLICITING OR RECEIVING IMPROPER COMPENSATION 2921.43(A) (2) ORC
ORC:2921.43.text: _____________ did knowingly promise or give to a public servant, to wit: (NAME PUBLIC SERVANT) or, being a public servant, knowingly solicit or accept additional or greater fees or costs than allowed by law to perform the public servant’s official duties, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.43(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.43.heading: SOLICITING OR RECEIVING IMPROPER COMPENSATION 2921.43(B) (1) ORC
ORC:2921.43.text: _____________ did, for one’s own personal or business use, whether a public servant or not, or for the personal or business use of a public servant or party official, to wit: (NAME PUBLIC SERVANT OR PARTY OFFICIAL), solicit or accept anything of value in consideration of appointing, securing, maintaining, renewing the appointment of anyone to a public office, employment or agency, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.43(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.43.heading: SOLICITING OR RECEIVING IMPROPER COMPENSATION 2921.43(B) (2) ORC
ORC:2921.43.text: _____________ did, for one’s own personal or business use, whether a public servant or not, or for the personal or business use of a public servant or party official, to wit: (NAME PUBLIC SERVANT OR PARTY OFFICIAL), solicit or accept anything of value in consideration of preferring, or maintaining the status of, any public employee with respect to compensation, duties, placement, location, promotion, or other material aspects of employment, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.43(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.43.heading: SOLICITING OR RECEIVING IMPROPER COMPENSATION 2921.43(C) (1) ORC
ORC:2921.43.text: _____________ did, for the benefit of a political party, campaign committee, legislative campaign fund, political action committee, or political contributing entity, to wit: (DESCRIBE), shall coerce any contribution in consideration of appointing or securing, maintaining, or renewing the appointment of any person to any public office, employment or agency, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.43(C)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.43.heading: SOLICITING OR RECEIVING IMPROPER COMPENSATION 2921.43(C) (2) ORC
ORC:2921.43.text: _____________ did, for the benefit of a political party, campaign committee, legislative campaign fund, political action committee, or political contributing entity, to wit: (DESCRIBE) shall coerce any contribution in consideration of preferring, or maintaining the status of, any public employee with respect to compensation, duties, placement, location, promotion, or other material aspects of employment, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.43(C)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2921.43.notes: NOTE: A public servant who is convicted of a violation of this section is disqualified from holding any public office, employment, or position of trust in this state for a period of seven years from the date of conviction. NOTE: This section does not prohibit a person from making voluntary contributions to a political party, campaign committee, legislative campaign fund, political action committee, or political contributing entity or prohibit a political party, campaign committee, legislative campaign fund, political action committee, or political contributing entity from accepting voluntary contributions.

ORC:2921.44.heading: DERELICTION OF DUTY 2921.44(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2921.44.variant: FAIL TO SERVE A TIMELY WARRANT – M2
ORC:2921.44.text: _____________ did, being a law enforcement officer, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMPLOYMENT), negligently fail to serve a lawful warrant without delay, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.44(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2921.44.heading: DERELICTION OF DUTY 2921.44(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2921.44.variant: FAIL TO PREVENT THE COMMISSION OF AN OFFENSE – M2
ORC:2921.44.text: _____________ did, being a law enforcement officer, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMPLOYMENT), negligently fail to prevent or halt the commission of an offense or to apprehend an offender, when it was in the law enforcement officer’s power to do so alone or with available assistance, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.44(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2921.44.heading: DERELICTION OF DUTY 2921.44(B) ORC
ORC:2921.44.variant: FAIL TO PERFORM LAWFUL DUTY IN CRIMINAL CASE – M2
ORC:2921.44.text: _____________ did, being a law enforcement, ministerial, or judicial officer, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMPLOYMENT), negligently fail to perform a lawful duty in a criminal case or proceeding, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.44(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2921.44.heading: DERELICTION OF DUTY 2921.44(C)(1) ORC
ORC:2921.44.variant: FAIL TO KEEP DETENTION FACILITY CLEAN – M2
ORC:2921.44.text: _____________ did, being an officer in charge of a detention facility, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMPLOYMENT), negligently allow the detention facility to become littered or unsanitary, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.44(C) (1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2921.44.heading: DERELICTION OF DUTY 2921.44(C)(2) ORC
ORC:2921.44.variant: FAIL TO PROVIDE FOOD, CLOTHING, SHELTER IN DETENTION FACILITY – M2
ORC:2921.44.text: _____________ did, being an officer in charge of a detention facility, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMPLOYMENT), negligently fail to provide persons confined in the detention facility with adequate food, clothing, bedding, shelter, and medical attention, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.44(C)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2921.44.heading: DERELICTION OF DUTY 2921.44(C)(3) ORC
ORC:2921.44.variant: FAIL TO CONTROL AN UNRULY PRISONER – M2
ORC:2921.44.text: _____________ did, being an officer in charge of a detention facility, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMPLOYMENT), negligently fail to control an unruly prisoner, or to prevent intimidation of or physical harm to a prisoner by another, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.44(C)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2921.44.heading: DERELICTION OF DUTY 2921.44(C)(4) ORC
ORC:2921.44.variant: NEGLIGENTLY ALLOWED A PRISONER TO ESCAPE – M2
ORC:2921.44.text: _____________ did, being an officer in charge of a detention facility, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMPLOYMENT), negligently allow a prisoner to escape, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.44(C)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2921.44.heading: DERELICTION OF DUTY 2921.44(C-5) ORC
ORC:2921.44.variant: FAIL TO OBSERVE REGULATION IN MANAGEMENT OF DETENTION FACILITY – M2
ORC:2921.44.text: _____________ did, being an officer in charge of a detention facility, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMPLOYMENT), negligently fail to observe any lawful and reasonable regulation for the management of the detention facility, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.44(C-5) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2921.44.heading: DERELICTION OF DUTY 2921.44(D) ORC
ORC:2921.44.variant: EXPEND A GREATER SUM THAN WAS APPROPRIATED IN THE DEPARTMENT – M2
ORC:2921.44.text: _____________ did, being a public official of the state, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMPLOYMENT), recklessly create a deficiency, incur a liability, or expend a greater sum than is appropriated by the general assembly for the use in any one year of the department, agency, or institution of the state with which the public official is connected, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.44(D) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2921.44.heading: DERELICTION OF DUTY 2921.44(E) ORC
ORC:2921.44.variant: FAIL TO PERFORM A DUTY IMPOSED BY LAW – M2
ORC:2921.44.text: _____________ did, being a public servant, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMPLOYMENT), recklessly fail to perform a duty expressly imposed by law with respect to the public servant’s office, or recklessly do any act expressly forbidden by law with respect to the public servant’s office, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.44(E) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2921.45.heading: INTERFERING WITH CIVIL RIGHTS 2921.45 ORC
ORC:2921.45.text: _____________ did knowingly, being a public servant, to wit: (DESCRIBE EMPLOYMENT), under color of (his or her) office, employment or authority, deprive or conspire or attempt to deprive any person of a constitutional or statutory right, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2921.45 of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.51.heading: IMPERSONATION OF AN OFFICER 2921.51(B) ORC
ORC:2921.51.variant: PEACE OFFICER, PRIVATE POLICEMAN, OR FEDERAL LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER – M4
ORC:2921.51.text: _____________ did impersonate a (peace officer or private police officer or federal law enforcement officer), to wit: (DESCRIBE IMPERSONATION), in violation of Section 2921.51(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2921.51.notes: NOTE: It is an affirmative defense if the impersonation of a peace officer was for a lawful purpose.

ORC:2921.51.heading: IMPERSONATION OF AN OFFICER 2921.51(C) ORC
ORC:2921.51.variant: ARREST, DETAIN, OR SEARCH ANOTHER – M1
ORC:2921.51.text: _____________ did, by impersonating a (peace officer or private police officer or federal law enforcement officer), to wit: (DESCRIBE IMPERSONATION), (arrest or detain or search or search the property of) another, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES AND NAME OF PERSON DETAINED OR SEARCHED), in violation of Section 2921.51(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.51.heading: IMPERSONATION OF AN OFFICER 2921.51(D) ORC
ORC:2921.51.variant: WITH PURPOSE TO COMMIT A MISDEMEANOR – M1
ORC:2921.51.text: _____________ did, with purpose to (commit or facilitate the commission of) a misdemeanor offense, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE AND SECTION NUMBER), impersonate a (peace officer or private police officer or federal law enforcement officer or an officer of the state or an employee of the state or an agent of the state), to wit: (DESCRIBE IMPERSONATION AND ACTIONS PERFORMED), in violation of Section 2921.51(D) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.51.heading: IMPERSONATION OF AN OFFICER 2921.51(D) ORC
ORC:2921.51.variant: WITH PURPOSE TO COMMIT A FELONY – F4
ORC:2921.51.text: _____________ did, with purpose to (commit or facilitate the commission of) a felony offense, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE AND SECTION NUMBER) impersonate a (peace officer or private police officer or federal law enforcement officer or an officer of the state or an agent of the state or an employee of the state), to wit: (DESCRIBE IMPERSONATION AND ACTIONS PERFORMED), in violation of Section 2921.51(D) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2921.51.heading: IMPERSONATION OF AN OFFICER 2921.51(E) ORC
ORC:2921.51.variant: DURING THE COMMISSION OF A FELONY – F3
ORC:2921.51.text: _____________ did commit a felony offense, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE AND SECTION NUMBER), while impersonating a (police officer or private police officer or federal law enforcement officer or an officer of the state or an agent of the state or an employee of the state), to wit: (DESCRIBE IMPERSONATION AND ACTIONS PERFORMED), in violation of Section 2921.51(E) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2921.52.heading: USING SHAM LEGAL PROCESS 2921.52(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2921.52.variant: ISSUE, DISPLAY, DELIVER, DISTRIBUTE OR USE SHAM LEGAL PROCESS – M4
ORC:2921.52.text: _____________ did, knowing the sham legal process to be sham legal process, knowingly (issue, display, deliver, distribute, or otherwise use sham legal process), to wit: (STATE HOW THE SHAM LEGAL PROCESS WAS USED), in violation of 2921.52(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2921.52.heading: USING SHAM LEGAL PROCESS 2921.52(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2921.52.variant: TO ARREST, DETAIN, SEARCH OR SEIZE PERSON OR PROPERTY – M1
ORC:2921.52.text: _____________ did, knowing the sham legal process to be sham legal process, knowingly use sham legal process to (arrest, detain, search, or seize) any (person or the property of another person), to wit: (STATE HOW THE SHAM LEGAL PROCESS WAS USED), in violation of 2921.52(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2921.52.notes: NOTE: It is an affirmative defense to a charge under sections B-1 and B-2 that the use of sham legal process was for a lawful purpose.

ORC:2921.52.heading: USING SHAM LEGAL PROCESS 2921.52(B)(3) ORC
ORC:2921.52.variant: TO COMMIT OR FACILITATE A MISDEMEANOR – M1
ORC:2921.52.text: _____________ did, knowing the sham legal process to be sham legal process, knowingly (commit or facilitate) the commission of a misdemeanor, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE), using sham legal process, to wit: (STATE HOW THE SHAM LEGAL PROCESS WAS USED), in violation of Section 2921.52(B)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2921.52.heading: USING SHAM LEGAL PROCESS 2921.52(B)(3) ORC
ORC:2921.52.variant: TO COMMIT OR FACILITATE THE COMMISSION OF A FELONY – F4
ORC:2921.52.text: _____________ did, knowing the sham legal process to be sham legal process, knowingly (commit or facilitate) the commission of a felony, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE), using sham legal process, to wit: (STATE HOW THE SHAM LEGAL PROCESS WAS USED), in violation of Section 921.52(B)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2921.52.heading: USING SHAM LEGAL PROCESS 2921.52(B)(4) ORC
ORC:2921.52.text: ____________ did, knowing the sham legal process to be sham legal process, knowingly commit a felony, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE) by using sham legal process, to wit: (STATE HOW THE SHAM LEGAL PROCESS WAS USED), in violation of Section 2921.52(B)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2923.01.heading: CONSPIRACY 2923.01(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2923.01.variant: PLAN OR AID IN PLANNING THE COMMISSION OF ANY SPECIFIED OFFENSE
ORC:2923.01.text: _____________ did, with purpose to (commit, promote, or facilitate) the commission of (aggravated murder, murder, kidnapping, abduction, compelling prostitution, promoting prostitution, trafficking in persons, aggravated arson, arson, aggravated robbery, robbery, aggravated burglary, burglary, trespassing in a habitation when a person is present or likely to be present, engaging in a pattern of corrupt activity, corrupting another with drugs, a felony drug trafficking, manufacturing, processing, or possession offense, theft of drugs, or illegal processing of drug documents, the commission of a felony offense of unauthorized use of a motor vehicle, or the commission of a violation of any provision of Chapter 3734 of the Ohio Revised Code other than Section 3734.18 of the Ohio Revised Code that relates to hazardous wastes), with another person, to wit: (NAME OTHER PERSON(S)), plan or aid in planning the commission of any of the above specified offenses, to wit: (DESCRIBE OFFENSE AND GIVE DETAILS OF PLANNING) in violation of Section 2923.01(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2923.01.notes: NOTE: Whoever violates this section is guilty of conspiracy, which is one of the following: 1. A felony of the first degree, when one of the objects of the conspiracy is aggravated murder, murder, or an offense for which the maximum penalty is imprisonment for life. 2. A felony of the next lesser degree than the most serious offense that is the object of the conspiracy, when the most serious offense that is the object of the conspiracy is a felony of the first, second, third or fourth degree. 3. A felony punishable by a fine of not more than twenty-five thousand dollars or imprisonment for not more than eighteen months, or both when the offense that is the object of the conspiracy is a violation of any provision of Chapter 3734 other than Section 3734.18 of the Ohio Revised Code that relates to hazardous waste. 4. A misdemeanor of the first degree, when the most serious offense that is the object of the conspiracy is a felony of the fifth degree. NOTE: See Section 2923.01 of the Ohio Revised Code for further information and defenses to the offense of Conspiracy.

ORC:2923.01.heading: CONSPIRACY 2923.01(A)(2)
ORC:2923.01.variant: ONE OR MORE PERSONS ENGAGE IN CONDUCT THAT FACILITATES THE COMMISSION OF A SPECIFIED OFFENSE
ORC:2923.01.text: _____________ did, with the purpose to (commit, promote, or facilitate) the commission of (aggravated murder, murder, kidnapping, abduction, compelling prostitution, promoting prostitution, trafficking in persons, aggravated arson, arson, aggravated robbery, robbery, aggravated burglary, burglary, trespassing in a habitation when a person is present or likely to be present, engaging in a pattern of corrupt activity, corrupting another with drugs, a felony drug trafficking, manufacturing, processing, or possession offense, theft of drugs, or illegal processing of drug documents, the commission of a felony offense of unauthorized use of a motor vehicle, or the commission of a violation of any provision of Chapter 3734 of the ORC other than § 3734.18 of the ORC that relates to hazardous wastes), agree with another person or persons, to wit: (NAME PERSON(S)), that one or more of them will engage in conduct that facilitates the commission of any of the specified offenses, to wit: (NAME OFFENSE AND DESCRIBE CONDUCT), in violation of Section 2923.01(A) (2) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2923.01.notes: NOTE: Whoever violates this section is guilty of conspiracy, which is one of the following: 1. A felony of the first degree, when one of the objects of the conspiracy is aggravated murder, murder, or an offense for which the maximum penalty is imprisonment for life. 2. A felony of the next lesser degree than the most serious offense that is the object of the conspiracy, when the most serious offense that is the object of the conspiracy is a felony of the first, second, third or fourth degree. 3. A felony punishable by a fine of not more than twenty-five thousand dollars or imprisonment for not more than eighteen months, or both when the offense that is the object of the conspiracy is a violation of any provision of Chapter 3734 other than 3734.18 that relates to hazardous waste. 4. A misdemeanor of the first degree, when the most serious offense that is the object of the conspiracy is a felony of the fifth degree. NOTE: See Section 2923.01 of the Ohio Revised Code for further information and defenses to the offense of Conspiracy.

ORC:2923.02.heading: ATTEMPT 2923.02(A) ORC
ORC:2923.02.text: _____________ did, (purposely or knowingly), (when purpose or knowledge is sufficient culpability), engage in conduct that if successful would result in an offense, to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT AND ATTEMPTED OFFENSE), in violation of 2923.02(A) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2923.02.notes: 1. An attempt to commit aggravated murder, murder, or an offense for which maximum penalty is life imprisonment, a felony of the first degree; 2. An attempt to commit a drug abuse offense for which the penalty is determined by the amount or number of unit doses of the controlled substance involved in the drug abuse offense is an offense of the same degree as the drug abuse offense attempted would be if that drug abuse offense had been committed and had involved an amount or number of unit doses of the controlled substance that is within the next lower range of controlled substance amounts than was involved in the attempt; 3. An attempt to commit any other offense is an offense of the next lesser degree than offense attempted; 4. An attempt to violate hazardous waste provisions, Ohio Revised Code Chapter 3734, other than Section 3734.18 of the Ohio Revised Code, is a felony punishable by a fine up to $25,000 or imprisonment up to 18 months, or both; 5. An attempt to commit a felony offense not specifically classified, a misdemeanor of the first degree; 6. An attempt to commit a misdemeanor offense not specifically classified, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree; 7. An attempt to commit a minor misdemeanor, or to engage in conspiracy is not an offense; NOTE: See Section 2923.02 of the Ohio Revised Code for further information and defenses.

ORC:2923.03.heading: COMPLICITY 2923.03(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2923.03.variant: SOLICIT OR PROCURE ANOTHER TO COMMIT AN OFFENSE
ORC:2923.03.text: _____________ did, while acting with the kind of culpability required for the commission of an offense, (purposely, knowingly, recklessly or negligently), (solicit or procure) another, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON SOLICITED OR PROCURED) to commit an offense, to wit: (STATE THE OFFENSE AND THE SECTION NUMBER AND DESCRIBE THE CONDUCT), in violation of Section 2923.03(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, (the degree of classification for a complicity offense is the same as the principal offense).
ORC:2923.03.notes: NOTE: A person committing complicity must act with the same degree of mental culpability as is required in the offense being committed. For example, the offense of murder requires a person to PURPOSELY aid or abet in the murder. Therefore, the mental culpability required for the offense of complicity must also be PURPOSELY.

ORC:2923.03.heading: COMPLICITY 2923.03(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2923.03.variant: AID OR ABET ANOTHER IN COMMITTING AN OFFENSE
ORC:2923.03.text: _____________ did, while acting with the kind of culpability required for the commission of an offense, (purposely, knowingly, recklessly or negligently), (aid or abet) another, to wit: (STATE NAME OF OTHER PERSON), in committing an offense, to wit: (STATE THE OFFENSE AND THE SECTION NUMBER) and (DESCRIBE DETAILS OF OFFENDER’S PARTICIPATION), in violation of Section 2923.03(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, (the degree of classification for a complicity offense is the same as the principal offense).
ORC:2923.03.notes: NOTE: A person committing complicity must act with the same degree of mental culpability as is required in the offense being committed. For example, the offense of murder requires a person to PURPOSELY aid or abet in the murder. Therefore, the mental culpability required for the offense of complicity must also be PURPOSELY.

ORC:2923.03.heading: COMPLICITY 2923.03(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2923.03.variant: CONSPIRE WITH ANOTHER TO COMMIT AN OFFENSE
ORC:2923.03.text: _____________ did, while acting with the kind of culpability required for the commission of an offense, (purposely, knowingly, recklessly or negligently), conspire with another, to wit: (STATE NAME OF OTHER PERSON), to commit an offense, to wit: (STATE THE OFFENSE AND SECTION NUMBER) in violation of Section 2923.01 of the Ohio Revised Code and (DESCRIBE DETAILS OF OFFENDER’S PARTICIPATION), in violation of Section 2923.03(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, (the degree of classification for a complicity offense is the same as the principal offense).
ORC:2923.03.notes: NOTE: A person committing complicity must act with the same degree of mental culpability as is required in the offense being committed. For example, the offense of murder requires a person to PURPOSELY aid or abet in the murder. Therefore, the mental culpability required for the offense of complicity must also be PURPOSELY.

ORC:2923.03.heading: COMPLICITY 2923.03(A)(4) ORC
ORC:2923.03.variant: CAUSE AN INNOCENT OR IRRESPONSIBLE PERSON TO COMMIT AN OFFENSE
ORC:2923.03.text: _____________ did, while acting with the kind of culpability required for the commission of an offense, (purposely, knowingly, recklessly or negligently), cause an (innocent or irresponsible) person, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON) to commit an offense, to wit: (STATE THE OFFENSE AND SECTION NUMBER) and (DESCRIBE DETAILS OF OFFENDER’S PARTICIPATION), in violation of Section 2923.03(A)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, (the degree of classification for a complicity offense is the same as the principal offense).
ORC:2923.03.notes: NOTE: A person committing complicity must act with the same degree of mental culpability as is required in the offense being committed. For example, the offense of murder requires a person to PURPOSELY aid or abet in the murder. Therefore, the mental culpability required for the offense of complicity must also be PURPOSELY. NOTE: See Section 2923.03 of the Ohio Revised Code for further information and defenses. DEFINITIONS PERTAINING TO WEAPONS OFFENSES NOTE: REFER TO SECTION 2923.11 FOR ORC OFFENSES OR SECTION 2323.11 FOR CCC OFFENSES. NOTE: For purposes of Section 2923.12, “deadly weapon” or “weapon” does not include any knife, razor, or cutting instrument if the instrument was not used as a weapon.

ORC:2923.12.heading: CARRYING CONCEALED WEAPONS 2923.12(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2923.12.variant: DEADLY WEAPON OTHER THAN A HANDGUN – UNLOADED – M1
ORC:2923.12.text: _____________ did knowingly carry or have, concealed on the person’s person, or concealed ready at hand, a deadly weapon other than a handgun, to wit: (DESCRIBE DEADLY WEAPON AND HOW IT WAS CONCEALED), in violation of Section 2923.12(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2923.12.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to the following: 1. Any officer, agent or employee of Ohio or another state or United States or law enforcement officer authorized to carry concealed weapons or dangerous ordnance, and acting within the scope of their duties. 2. Any person who is employed in this state, who is authorized to carry concealed weapons or dangerous ordnance or is authorized to carry handguns, and who is subject to and in compliance with the requirements of Section 109.801 of the Revised Code (Peace Officer Annual Firearms Requalification), unless the appointing authority of the person has expressly specified that this exemption does not apply to the person. 3. A person’s transportation or storage of a firearm, other than a firearm described in divisions (G) to (M) of Section 2923.11 of the Revised Code, in a motor vehicle for any lawful purpose if the firearm is not on the actor’s person. 4. A person’s storage or possession of a firearm, other than a firearm described in divisions (G) to (M) of Section 2923.11 of the Revised Code, in the actor’s own home for any lawful purpose. NOTE: It is an affirmative defense to a charge for carrying or having control of a weapon other than a handgun and other than dangerous ordnance if person is not otherwise prohibited under the law from having the weapon and any of the following applies: 1. The weapon was carried or kept ready at hand by the actor for defensive purposes, while the actor was engaged in or was going to or from the actor’s lawful business or occupation, which business or occupation was of a character or was necessarily carried on in a manner or at a time or place as to render the actor particularly susceptible to criminal attack, such as would justify a prudent person in going armed. 2. The weapon was carried or kept ready at hand by the actor for defensive purposes, while the actor was engaged in a lawful activity, and had reasonable cause to fear a criminal attack upon the actor, a member of the actor’s family, or the actor’s home, such as would justify a prudent person in going armed. 3. The weapon was carried or kept ready at hand by the actor for any lawful purpose and while in the actor’s own home.

ORC:2923.12.variant: DEADLY WEAPON OTHER THAN A HANDGUN, PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F4
ORC:2923.12.text: _____________ did knowingly carry or have, concealed on the person’s person, or concealed ready at hand, a deadly weapon other than a handgun, to wit: (DESCRIBE DEADLY WEAPON AND HOW IT WAS CONCEALED), having been previously convicted of (violating Revised Code 2923.12 or violating an offense of violence), to wit: (STATE SPECIFIC OFFENSE, SECTION NUMBER) on (DATE) in (STATE NAME OF COURT), (STATE CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2923.12(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2923.12.heading: CARRYING CONCEALED WEAPONS 2923.12(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2923.12.variant: DEADLY WEAPON OTHER THAN A HANDGUN, AIRCRAFT – F3
ORC:2923.12.text: _____________ did knowingly carry or have, concealed on the person’s person, or concealed ready at hand, a deadly weapon other than a handgun, to wit: (DESCRIBE DEADLY WEAPON AND HOW IT WAS CONCEALED), (aboard an aircraft or with purpose to carry the weapon aboard an aircraft), to wit: (DESCRIBE AIRCRAFT AND/OR EVIDENCE OF PURPOSE TO CARRY ABOARD), in violation of Section 2923.12(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2923.12.heading: CARRYING CONCEALED WEAPONS 2923.12(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2923.12.variant: HANDGUN OTHER THAN DANGEROUS ORDNANCE, UNLOADED – M1
ORC:2923.12.text: _____________ did knowingly carry or have, concealed on the person’s person, or concealed ready at hand, a handgun other than dangerous ordnance, to wit: (DESCRIBE HANDGUN AND HOW IT WAS CONCEALED), in violation of Section 2923.12(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2923.12.notes: NOTE: The officer shall not cite or arrest for a violation of 2923.12(A)(2) unless the person is determined not to be a qualified adult or if at the time of the violation the person was knowingly in a place described in division 2923.126(B). NOTE: If a person being arrested for a violation of (A)(2) of this section is an active duty member of the armed forces of the United States and is carrying a valid military identification card and documentation of successful completion of firearms training that meets or exceeds the training requirements described in ORC 2923.125(G)(1) of the Revised Code, and if at the time of the violation the person was not knowingly in a place described in ORC 2923.126(B) of the Revised Code, the officer shall not arrest the person for a violation of this offense. NOTE: If a person being arrested for a violation of ORC 2923.12(A)(2) is knowingly in any premises owned or leased by any public or private college, university, or other institution of higher education, and is not authorized to carry a concealed handgun or have a handgun concealed on the person’s person or concealed ready at hand, the penalty shall be as follows: 1. MM: If the person produces a valid concealed handgun license within ten days after the arrest and has not previously been convicted or pleaded guilty to a violation of division (A)(2) of this section; 2. M4: If the person has one previous conviction for a violation of division (A)(2) of this section; 3. M3: If the person has two previous convictions for violations of division (A)(2) of this section; 4. M2: If the person has three or more previous convictions for violations of division (A)(2) of this section; 5. M2: If the person has a previous conviction for any offense of violence; 6. M2: If the weapon involved is a firearm that is either loaded or for which the offender has ammunition ready at hand; 7. M2: If the weapon involved is a dangerous ordnance. NOTE: This section does not apply to the following: 1. Any officer, agent or employee of Ohio or another state or United States or law enforcement officer authorized to carry concealed weapons or dangerous ordnance, and acting within the scope of their duties. 2. Any person who is employed in this state, who is authorized to carry concealed weapons or dangerous ordnance or is authorized to carry handguns, and who is subject to and in compliance with the requirements of Section 109.801 of the Revised Code (Peace Officer Annual Firearms Requalification), unless the appointing authority of the person has expressly specified that this exemption does not apply to the person. 3. A person’s transportation or storage of a firearm, other than a firearm described in divisions (G) to (M) of Section 2923.11 of the Revised Code, in a motor vehicle for any lawful purpose if the firearm is not on the actor’s person. 4. A person’s storage or possession of a firearm, other than a firearm described in divisions (G) to (M) of Section 2923.11 of the Revised Code, in the actor’s own home for any lawful purpose. 5. A person who is carrying a handgun and either is carrying a valid concealed handgun license, is a qualified adult, or is an active duty member of the armed forces of the United States and is carrying a valid military identification card and documentation of successful completion of firearms training that meets or exceeds the training requirements described in ORC 2923.125(G)(1), unless the person is in a place described in division (B) of Section 2923.126 of the Revised Code. The list of prohibited places described in division (B) of Section 2923.126 of the Revised Code is as follows: A police station, sheriff’s office, highway patrol station, premises controlled by the Bureau of Identification and Investigation, state correctional institutions, jails, workhouses, detention facilities, any area of an airport passenger terminal that is beyond a passenger or property screening checkpoint or to which access is restricted through security measures by the airport authority or a public agency, institutions maintained, operated, managed, and governed pursuant to ORC 5119.14(A) or ORC 5123.03(A)(1) (State Mental Health, and DODD facilities), school safety zone (if the licensee’s carrying the concealed handgun is in violation of Section 2923.122 of the Revised Code), courthouse or other buildings where courtrooms are located in violation of ORC 2923.123, any premises or open air arena for which a D permit has been issued under Chapter 4303 of the Revised Code (if the licensee’s carrying the concealed handgun is in violation of Section 2923.121 of the Revised Code), any premises owned or leased by any public or private college, university, or other institution of higher education (unless handgun is in locked motor vehicle or the licensee is in immediate process of placing the handgun in a locked motor vehicle, or unless the licensee is carrying the concealed handgun pursuant to a written policy, rule, or other authorization that is adopted by the institution’s board of trustees or other governing body and that authorizes specific individuals or classes of individuals to carry a concealed handgun on the premises), any church, synagogue, mosque, or other house of worship unless they post and permit otherwise, any building that is a government facility of this state or a political subdivision of this state and that is not a building that is used primarily as a shelter, restroom, parking facility for motor vehicles, or rest facility and is not a courthouse or other building or structure in which a courtroom is located, unless the governing body with authority over the building has enacted a statute, ordinance, or policy that permits a licensee to carry a concealed handgun into the building, and any place where federal law prohibits the carrying of handguns. The CCW laws thus apply to a licensee if they are in any of the listed places.

ORC:2923.12.heading: CARRYING CONCEALED WEAPONS 2923.12(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2923.12.variant: HANDGUN OTHER THAN DANGEROUS ORDNANCE, LOADED – F4
ORC:2923.12.text: _____________ did knowingly carry or have, concealed on the person’s person, or concealed ready at hand, a handgun other than dangerous ordnance, to wit: (DESCRIBE HANDGUN AND HOW IT WAS CONCEALED), (that was loaded or for which ammunition was ready at hand), in violation of Section 2923.12(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2923.12.notes: NOTE: The officer shall not cite or arrest for a violation of 2923.12(A)(2) unless the person is determined not to be a qualified adult or if at the time of the violation the person was knowingly in a place described in division 2923.126(B). NOTE: If a person being arrested for a violation of (A)(2) of this section is an active duty member of the armed forces of the United States and is carrying a valid military identification card and documentation of successful completion of firearms training that meets or exceeds the training requirements described in ORC 2923.125(G)(1) of the Revised Code, and if at the time of the violation the person was not knowingly in a place described in ORC 2923.126(B) of the Revised Code, the officer shall not arrest the person for a violation of this offense. NOTE: If a person being arrested for a violation of ORC 2923.12(A)(2) is knowingly in any premises owned or leased by any public or private college, university, or other institution of higher education, and is not authorized to carry a concealed handgun or have a handgun concealed on the person’s person or concealed ready at hand, the penalty shall be as follows: 1. MM: If the person produces a valid concealed handgun license within ten days after the arrest and has not previously been convicted or pleaded guilty to a violation of division (A)(2) of this section; 2. M4: If the person has one previous conviction for a violation of division (A)(2) of this section; 3. M3: If the person has two previous convictions for violations of division (A)(2) of this section; 4. M2: If the person has three or more previous convictions for violations of division (A)(2) of this section; 5. M2: If the person has a previous conviction for any offense of violence; 6. M2: If the weapon involved is a firearm that is either loaded or for which the offender has ammunition ready at hand; 7. M2: If the weapon involved is a dangerous ordnance. NOTE: This section does not apply to the following: 1. Any officer, agent or employee of Ohio or another state or United States or law enforcement officer authorized to carry concealed weapons or dangerous ordnance, and acting within the scope of their duties. 2. Any person who is employed in this state, who is authorized to carry concealed weapons or dangerous ordnance or is authorized to carry handguns, and who is subject to and in compliance with the requirements of Section 109.801 of the Revised Code (Peace Officer Annual Firearms Requalification), unless the appointing authority of the person has expressly specified that this exemption does not apply to the person. 3. A person’s transportation or storage of a firearm, other than a firearm described in divisions (G) to (M) of Section 2923.11 of the Revised Code, in a motor vehicle for any lawful purpose if the firearm is not on the actor’s person. 4. A person’s storage or possession of a firearm, other than a firearm described in divisions (G) to (M) of Section 2923.11 of the Revised Code, in the actor’s own home for any lawful purpose. 5. A person who is carrying a handgun and either is carrying a valid concealed handgun license, is a qualified adult, or is an active duty member of the armed forces of the United States and is carrying a valid military identification card and documentation of successful completion of firearms training that meets or exceeds the training requirements described in ORC 2923.125(G)(1), unless the person is in a place described in division (B) of Section 2923.126 of the Revised Code. The list of prohibited places described in division (B) of Section 2923.126 of the Revised Code is as follows: A police station, sheriff’s office, highway patrol station, premises controlled by the Bureau of Identification and Investigation, state correctional institutions, jails, workhouses, detention facilities, any area of an airport passenger terminal that is beyond a passenger or property screening checkpoint or to which access is restricted through security measures by the airport authority or a public agency, institutions maintained, operated, managed, and governed pursuant to ORC 5119.14(A) or ORC 5123.03(A)(1) (State Mental Health, and DODD facilities), school safety zone (if the licensee’s carrying the concealed handgun is in violation of Section 2923.122 of the Revised Code), courthouse or other buildings where courtrooms are located in violation of ORC 2923.123, any premises or open air arena for which a D permit has been issued under Chapter 4303 of the Revised Code (if the licensee’s carrying the concealed handgun is in violation of Section 2923.121 of the Revised Code), any premises owned or leased by any public or private college, university, or other institution of higher education (unless handgun is in locked motor vehicle or the licensee is in immediate process of placing the handgun in a locked motor vehicle, or unless the licensee is carrying the concealed handgun pursuant to a written policy, rule, or other authorization that is adopted by the institution’s board of trustees or other governing body and that authorizes specific individuals or classes of individuals to carry a concealed handgun on the premises), any church, synagogue, mosque, or other house of worship unless they post and permit otherwise, any building that is a government facility of this state or a political subdivision of this state and that is not a building that is used primarily as a shelter, restroom, parking facility for motor vehicles, or rest facility and is not a courthouse or other building or structure in which a courtroom is located, unless the governing body with authority over the building has enacted a statute, ordinance, or policy that permits a licensee to carry a concealed handgun into the building, and any place where federal law prohibits the carrying of handguns. The CCW laws thus apply to a licensee if they are in any of the listed places.

ORC:2923.121.heading: ILLEGAL POSSESSION OF FIREARM IN A LIQUOR PREMISE 2923.121(A) ORC
ORC:2923.121.text: _____________ did possess a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE FIREARM), in a room in which any person is consuming beer or intoxicating liquor in a premises for which a “D” permit issued under 4303 of the Ohio Revised Code, to wit: (DESCRIBE LOCATION), in violation of Section 2923.121(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree
ORC:2923.121.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to the following: 1. Any officer, agent, or employee of Ohio, any other state, or the United States, or law enforcement officers authorized to carry firearms, and acting within the scope of their duties. 2. A law enforcement officer or investigator who is authorized to carry firearms but is not acting within the scope of the officer’s or investigator’s duties, as long as all of the following apply: – The officer or investigator is carrying validating identification. – If the firearm the officer or investigator possesses is a firearm issued or approved by the law enforcement agency served by the officer or by the bureau of criminal identification and investigation with respect to an investigator, the agency or bureau does not have a restrictive firearms carrying policy. – The officer or investigator is not consuming beer or intoxicating liquor and is not under the influence of alcohol or a drug of abuse. 3. Any room used for the accommodation of guests of a hotel as defined in Section 4301.01 of the Ohio Revised Code. 4. The principal holder of a D permit issued for a premises or an open air arena while in the premises or open air arena for which the permit was issued if the principal holder of the D permit also possesses a valid concealed handgun license and as long as the principal holder is not consuming beer or intoxicating liquor or under the influence of alcohol or a drug of abuse. 5. Any agent or employee of that holder who also is a peace officer, as defined in Section 2151.3515 of the Revised Code, who is off duty, and who otherwise is authorized to carry firearms while in the course of the officer’s official duties and while in the premises or open air arena for which the permit was issued and as long as the agent or employee of that holder is not consuming beer or intoxicating liquor or under the influence of alcohol or a drug of abuse. 6. Any person who is carrying a valid concealed handgun license, is a qualified adult, or any person who is an active duty member of the armed forces of the United States and is carrying a valid military identification card and documentation of successful completion of firearms training that meets or exceeds the training requirements described in ORC 2923.125, as long as the person is not consuming beer or intoxicating liquor or under the influence of alcohol or a drug of abuse. 7. A person who is a member of a veteran’s organization, as defined by 2915.01 of the Revised Code, from possessing a rifle in a room in any premises owned, leased, or otherwise under the control of the veteran’s organization, if the rifle is not loaded with live ammunition and if the person is not otherwise prohibited by law from having the rifle. 8. Any person possessing or displaying firearms in any room used to exhibit unloaded firearms for sale or trade in a soldiers’ memorial, pursuant to Chapter 345 of the ORC, in a convention center, or in any other public meeting place, if the person is exhibitor, trader, purchaser, or seller of firearms and is not otherwise prohibited by law from possessing, trading, purchasing, or selling the firearms. NOTE: Affirmative defense applies to a charge for possessing a firearm other than a handgun if person is not otherwise prohibited under the law and either of the following apply: 1. The firearm was carried or kept ready at hand by the actor for defensive purposes, while the actor was engaged in or was going to or from the actor’s lawful business or occupation, which business or occupation was of such character or was necessarily carried on in such manner or at such a time or place as to render the actor particularly susceptible to criminal attack, such as would justify a prudent person in going armed. 2. The firearm was carried or kept ready at hand by the actor for defensive purposes, while the actor was engaged in a lawful activity, and had reasonable cause to fear a criminal attack upon the actor or a member of the actor’s family, or upon the actor’s home, such as would justify a prudent person in going armed.

ORC:2923.122.heading: CONVEYING DEADLY WEAPONS OR DANGEROUS ORDNANCE INTO A SCHOOL SAFETY ZONE 2923.122(A) ORC
ORC:2923.122.text: _____________ did knowingly (convey or attempt to convey) a (deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance), to wit: (DESCRIBE WEAPON OR ORDNANCE AND HOW IT WAS CONVEYED OR ATTEMPTED TO BE CONVEYED) into a school safety zone, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE PROPERTY) in violation of Section 2923.122(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2923.122.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to any of the following: 1. An officer, agent, or employee of this or any other state or the United States who is authorized to carry deadly weapons or dangerous ordnance and is acting within the scope of the officer’s, agent’s, or employee’s duties, a law enforcement officer who is authorized to carry deadly weapons or dangerous ordnance, a security officer employed by a board of education or governing body of a school during the time that the security officer is on duty pursuant to that contract of employment, or any other person who has written authorization from the board of education or governing body of a school to convey deadly weapons or dangerous ordnance into a school safety zone or to possess a deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance in a school safety zone and who conveys or possesses the deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance in accordance with that authorization; 2. Any person who is employed in this state, who is authorized to carry deadly weapons or dangerous ordnance, and who is subject to and in compliance with the requirements of Section 109.801 (Peace Officer Annual Firearms Requalification) of the Revised Code, unless the appointing authority of the person has expressly specified that this exemption does not apply to the person. 3. If the weapon is a handgun and all of the following apply: a. The person is carrying a valid concealed handgun license, is a qualified adult, or the person is an active duty member of the armed forces of the United States and is carrying a valid military identification card and documentation of successful completion of firearms training that meets or exceeds the training requirements described in ORC 2923.125. b. The person leaves the handgun in a motor vehicle. c. The handgun does not leave the motor vehicle. d. If the person exits the motor vehicle; the person locks the motor vehicle. 4. If the weapon is a handgun and all of the following apply: a. The person does not enter into a school building or onto school premises and is not at a school activity. b. The person is carrying a valid concealed handgun license, is a qualified adult, or the person is an active duty member of the armed forces of the United States and is carrying a valid military identification card and documentation of successful completion of firearms training that meets or exceeds the training requirements described in ORC 2923.125. c. The person is in a school safety zone in accordance with 18 USC 922(q)(2)(B). d. The person is not knowingly in a place described in division (B)(1) or (B)(3) to (B)(8) of ORC 2923.126.

ORC:2923.122.heading: ILLEGAL POSSESSION OF AN OBJECT INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A FIREARM IN A SCHOOL SAFETY ZONE 2923.122(C) ORC
ORC:2923.122.text: _____________ did knowingly possess an object indistinguishable from a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE OBJECT), and did (indicate that he or she possessed the object and that it was a firearm OR knowingly displayed and/ or brandished the object and indicated it was a firearm), to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES UNDER WHICH PERSON INDICATED POSSESSION OF OBJECT AS A FIREARM) in a school safety zone, to wit: (DESCRIBE PROPERTY), in violation of Section 2923.122(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2923.122.notes: NOTE: As used in this section, “object that is indistinguishable from a firearm” means an object made, constructed, or altered so that, to a reasonable person without specialized training in firearms, the object appears to be a firearm. ORC:2923.123.heading: CONVEYING DEADLY WEAPONS OR DANGEROUS ORDNANCE INTO COURTHOUSE 2923.123(A) ORC
ORC:2923.123.variant: CONVEY OR ATTEMPT TO CONVEY – F5
ORC:2923.123.text: _____________ did knowingly (convey or attempt to convey) a (deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance), to wit: (DESCRIBE WEAPON OR ORDNANCE AND HOW IT WAS CONVEYED OR ATTEMPTED TO BE CONVEYED) into a (courthouse or into another building or structure in which a courtroom is located) to wit: (DESCRIBE THE LOCATION) in violation of Section 2923.123(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2923.123.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to a person who conveys, attempts to convey, possesses, or has under the person’s control a deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance that is to be used as evidence in a pending criminal or civil action or proceeding. NOTE: This section does not apply to any of the following unless a rule of the Supreme Court of Ohio or a local rule of court prohibits all persons from conveying, attempting to convey, possessing or having under one’s control a deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance in a courthouse or another building or structure in which a courtroom is located: 1. A judge of a court of record of this state or a magistrate. 2. A peace officer, officer of a law enforcement agency, or person who is in either of the following categories: a. A peace officer, or an officer of a law enforcement agency of another state, a political subdivision of another state, or the United States, who is authorized to carry a deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance, who possesses or has under that individual’s control a deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance as a requirement of that individual’s duties, and who is acting within the scope of that individual’s duties at the time of that possession or control. b. A person who is employed in this state, who is authorized to carry a deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance, who possesses or has under that individual’s control a deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance as a requirement of that person’s duties, and who is subject to and in compliance with the requirements of Section 109.801 (Peace Officer Annual Firearms Requalification) of the Revised Code, unless the appointing authority of the person has expressly specified that this exemption does not apply to the person. 3. ORC:2923.13.notes: DEFINITIONS 2323.13 CCC: INTIMATE PARTNER – With respect to a person, the spouse of the person, a former spouse of the person, an individual who is a parent of a child of the person, and an individual who cohabitates or has cohabited with the person. MISDEMEANOR CRIME OF DOMESTIC VIOLENCE – Has the same meaning as used in 18 USC 921(a). NOTE: If the offender had a firearm or dangerous ordnance on or about the offender’s person or under the offender’s control at the time of the commission of the offense in violation of the Columbus City Code, the firearm or dangerous ordnance shall be seized and is subject to forfeiture under Chapter 2981 of the Ohio Revised Code. Refer to the complaint language cited in Chapter 2927 of the Criminal Complaint Manual. NOTE: “Under operation of law or legal process” shall not itself include mere completion, termination, or expiration of a sentence imposed as a result of a criminal conviction. NOTE: “Felonies that are punishable by imprisonment for a term exceeding one year” include ORC felonies of the first, second, third and fourth degrees, but do not include felonies of the fifth degree.
