CCC:2323.13.text: _____________ did knowingly (acquire, or have, or carry, or use) a (firearm or dangerous ordnance), to wit: (DESCRIBE SPECIFIC FIREARM OR DANGEROUS ORDNANCE AND HOW ACQUIRED OR POSSESSED OR CARRIED OR USED), not having been relieved from disability under operation of law or legal process, and being (under indictment for or convicted of, or having been adjudged a delinquent child for the commission of an offense that, if committed by an adult, would have been a felony offense punishable by imprisonment for a term exceeding one year), to wit: (STATE SPECIFIC OFFENSE AND ORC SECTION NUMBER – 2927.11 Desecration, or 2927.12 Ethnic intimidation) on (DATE) by (NAME OF COURT) (STATE CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2323.13(A)(1)(g) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor offense.
CCC:2323.13.notes: NOTE: See definitions cited at beginning of Section 2323.13 CCC.

CCC:2323.13.heading: HAVING WEAPONS WHILE UNDER DISABILITY 2323.13(A)(2) CCC
CCC:2323.13.text: _____________did knowingly (acquire, or have, or carry, or use) a (firearm or dangerous ordnance), to wit: (DESCRIBE SPECIFIC FIREARM OR DANGEROUS ORDNANCE AND HOW ACQUIRED OR POSSESSED OR CARRIED OR USED), not having been relieved from disability under operation of law or legal process, and being (subject to a court order that was issued after a hearing of which such person received actual notice, and at which such person had an opportunity to participate; restrains such person from harassing, stalking, or threatening an intimate partner of such person or child of such intimate partner or person, or engaging in other conduct that would place an intimate partner in reasonable fear of bodily injury to the partner or child; and includes a finding that such person represents a credible threat to the physical safety of such intimate partner or child; or by its terms explicitly prohibits the use, attempted use, or threatened use of physical force against such intimate partner or child that would reasonably be expected to cause bodily injury), to wit: (STATE TYPE OF COURT ORDER AND CODE SECTION IT WAS ISSUED UNDER) on (DATE OF ISSUANCE) by (NAME OF COURT AND JUDGE) (STATE CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2323.13(A) (2) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor offense.
CCC:2323.13.notes: NOTE: See definitions cited at beginning of Section 2323.13 CCC.

CCC:2323.13.heading: HAVING WEAPONS WHILE UNDER DISABILITY 2323.13(A)(3) CCC
CCC:2323.13.variant: PREVIOUS CONVICTION OF A MISDEMEANOR CRIME OF DOMESTIC VIOLENCE – MISDEMEANOR
CCC:2323.13.text: _____________ did knowingly (acquire, or have, or carry, or use) a (firearm or dangerous ordnance), to wit: (DESCRIBE SPECIFIC FIREARM OR DANGEROUS ORDNANCE AND HOW IT WAS ACQUIRED OR POSSESSED OR CARRIED OR USED), not having been relieved from disability under operation of law or legal process, and having been previously convicted of a misdemeanor crime of domestic violence, to wit: (STATE SPECIFIC OFFENSE CONVICTION NAME AND CODE SECTION NUMBER) on (DATE) by (NAME OF COURT) (COURT CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2323.13(A) (3) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor offense.
CCC:2323.13.notes: NOTE: See definitions cited at beginning of Section 2323.13 CCC. NOTE: The offender’s previous conviction for Domestic Violence must have been against a person with whom the offender shared one of the following relationships: 1. Current or former spouse of the victim; 2. Parent or guardian of the victim; 3. Person with whom the victim shares a child in common; 4. Person who is cohabiting with or has cohabited with the victim as a spouse, parent, or guardian, or by a person similarly situated to a spouse, parent, or guardian of the victim.

ORC:2923.15.heading: USING WEAPONS WHILE INTOXICATED 2923.15(A) ORC (CCC 2323.15(A))
ORC:2923.15.text: _____________ did, while under the influence of (alcohol or a drug of abuse), (carry or use) a (firearm or dangerous ordnance), to wit: (DESCRIBE FIREARM OR DANGEROUS ORDNANCE), in violation of Section 2923.15(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2923.15.notes: NOTE: If the offender had a firearm or dangerous ordnance on or about the offender’s person or under the offender’s control at the time of the commission of the offense in violation of the Columbus City Code, the firearm or dangerous ordnance shall be seized and is subject to forfeiture under Chapter 2981 of the Ohio Revised Code. Refer to the complaint language cited in Chapter 2927 of the Criminal Complaint Manual.

ORC:2923.16.heading: IMPROPERLY HANDLING FIREARMS IN A MOTOR VEHICLE 2923.16(A) ORC
ORC:2923.16.text: _____________ did knowingly discharge a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE FIREARM), while (in or on) a motor vehicle, to wit: (DESCRIBE VEHICLE), in violation of Section 2923.16(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2923.16.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to any of the following: 1. Officers, agents, or employees of this or any other state or the United States, or to law enforcement officers, when authorized to carry or have loaded or accessible firearms in motor vehicles and acting within the scope of their duties. 2. Any person who is employed in this state, who is authorized to carry or have loaded or accessible firearms in motor vehicles, and who is subject to and in compliance with the requirements of Section 109.801 (Peace Officer Annual Firearms Requalification) of the Revised Code, unless the appointing authority of the person has expressly specified that this exemption does not apply to the person. 3. A person if all of the following apply: a. The person possesses a valid all-purpose vehicle permit issued under Section 1533.103 of the Revised Code by the chief of the division of wildlife. b. The person discharges a firearm at a wild quadruped or game bird as defined in Section 1531.01 of the Revised Code during the open hunting season for the applicable wild quadruped or game bird. c. The person discharges a firearm from a stationary all-purpose vehicle as defined in Section 1531.01 of the Revised Code from private or publicly owned lands or from a motor vehicle that is parked on a road that is owned or administered by the division of wildlife. d. The person does not discharge the weapon (a) while under the influence of alcohol or drugs of abuse, (b) in the direction of a street, highway or other public or private property used by the public for vehicular traffic or parking, (c) at or into an occupied structure that is a permanent or temporary habitation, or (d) in the commission of any violation of law. 4. A person if all of the following apply: a. The person discharges a firearm from a motor vehicle at a coyote or groundhog, the discharge is not during the deer gun-hunting season and the discharge at the coyote or groundhog is otherwise legal. b. The motor vehicle from which the person discharges the firearm is on real property that is located in an unincorporated area of a township and that either is zoned for agriculture or is used for agriculture. c. The person owns the real property described above, is the spouse or child of another person who owns that real property, is a tenant of another who owns that real property, or is the spouse of a child or a tenant of another who owns that real property. d. The person does not discharge the weapon (a) while under the influence of alcohol or drugs of abuse, (b) in the direction of a street, highway or other public or private property used by the public for vehicular traffic or parking, (c) at or into an occupied structure that is a permanent or temporary habitation, or (d) in the commission of any violation of law.

ORC:2923.16.heading: IMPROPERLY HANDLING FIREARMS IN A MOTOR VEHICLE 2923.16(B) ORC
ORC:2923.16.variant: LOADED FIREARM ACCESSIBLE WITHOUT LEAVING VEHICLE – F4
ORC:2923.16.text: _____________ did knowingly (transport or have) a loaded firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE FIREARM), in a motor vehicle, to wit: (DESCRIBE VEHICLE), in such a manner that it was accessible to (the operator or a passenger) without leaving the vehicle, to wit: (DESCRIBE LOCATION OF FIREARM), in violation of Section 2923.16(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2923.16.notes: NOTE: A person who is carrying a valid concealed handgun license or is a qualified adult may have one or more magazines or speed loaders containing ammunition anywhere in a vehicle without further restriction, as long as no ammunition is in a firearm, other than a handgun, in the vehicle other than as permitted under any provision of this chapter. NOTE: Nothing in this section prohibits or restricts a person from possessing, storing, or leaving a firearm in a locked motor vehicle that is parked in the state underground parking garage at the state capitol building or in the parking garage at the Riffe center for government and the arts in Columbus, if the person’s transportation and possession of the firearm in the motor vehicle while traveling to the premises or facility was not in violation of division (A), (B), (C), (D), or (E) of this section or any other provision of the Revised Code. NOTE: This section does not apply to any of the following: 1. Officers, agents, or employees of this or any other state or the United States, or to law enforcement officers, when authorized to carry or have loaded or accessible firearms in motor vehicles and acting within the scope of their duties. 2. Any person who is employed in this state, who is authorized to carry or have loaded or accessible firearms in motor vehicles, and who is subject to and in compliance with the requirements of Section 109.801 (Peace Officer Annual Firearms Requalification) of the Revised Code, unless the appointing authority of the person has expressly specified that this exemption does not apply to the person. 3. A person if all of the following apply: a. The person was the operator or passenger in the motor vehicle. b. The vehicle was on real property located in an unincorporated area of a township and that either is zoned for agriculture or is used for agriculture. c. The person owns the real property, is the spouse or a child of another who owns the property, is the spouse or a child of a tenant of another who owns the real property. d. The person, prior to arriving at the real property did not transport or possess a firearm in the motor vehicle in a manner prohibited by division (B) or (C) of this section while the motor vehicle was being operated on a street, highway, or other public or private property used by the public for vehicular traffic or parking. 4. If the firearm is a handgun and both of the following apply: a. The person who transports or possesses the handgun is either carrying a concealed handgun license, is a qualified adult, or is an active duty member of the armed forces of the United States and is carrying a valid military identification card and documentation of successful completion of firearms training that meets or exceeds the training requirements described in ORC 2923.125(G)(1). b. The person transporting or possessing the handgun is not knowingly in a place described in division (B) of Section 2923.126 of the Revised Code (see notes for 2923.12(A)(2) for list of prohibited places). 5. A person if all of the following apply: a. The person possesses a valid all-purpose vehicle permit issued under Section 1533.103 of the Revised Code by the chief of the division of wildlife. b. The person is on or in an all-purpose vehicle as defined in Section 1531.01 of the Revised Code or a motor vehicle during the open hunting season for a wild quadruped or game bird. c. The person is on or in an all-purpose vehicle as defined in Section 1531.01 of the Revised Code on private or publicly owned lands or on or in a motor vehicle that is parked on a road that is owned or administered by the division of wildlife. NOTE: The following affirmative defenses apply to this section: 1. If the firearm is other than a handgun or dangerous ordnance and if the actor was not otherwise prohibited by law from having the weapon, it is an affirmative defense to this section if the weapon was carried or kept ready at hand by the actor for defensive purposes, while the actor was engaged in or was going to or from the actor’s lawful business or occupation, which business or occupation was of a character or was necessarily carried on in a manner or at a time or place as to render the actor particularly susceptible to criminal attack, such as would justify a prudent person in going armed, OR, the weapon was carried or kept ready at hand by the actor for defensive purposes, while the actor was engaged in a lawful activity and had reasonable cause to fear a criminal attack upon the actor, a member of the actor’s family, or the actor’s home, such as would justify a prudent person in going armed. 2. It is an affirmative defense to this section if the actor transported or had the firearm in the motor vehicle for any lawful purpose and while the motor vehicle was on the actor’s own property, provided that this affirmative defense is not available unless the person immediately prior to arriving at the actor’s own property did not transport or possess the firearm in a motor vehicle in a manner prohibited by division (B) or (C) of 2923.16, while the vehicle was being operated on a street, highway, or other public or private property used by the public for vehicular traffic. NOTE: For purposes of this section, “unloaded” means any of the following: 1. No ammunition is in the firearm in question, and no magazine or speed loader containing ammunition is inserted into the firearm in question AND either: there is no ammunition in a magazine or speed loader that is in the vehicle in question and that may be used with the firearm in question OR any magazine or speed loader that contains ammunition and that may be used with the firearm in question is stored in a compartment within the vehicle in question that cannot be accessed without leaving the vehicle or is stored in a container that provides complete and separate enclosure. 2. With respect to a firearm employing a percussion cap, flintlock, or other obsolete ignition system, when the weapon is uncapped or when the priming charge is removed from the pan. NOTE: For purposes of this section, “container that provides complete and separate enclosure” includes, but is not limited to, any of the following: 1. A package, box, or case with multiple compartments, as long as the loaded magazine or speed loader and the firearm in question either are in separate compartments within the package, box, or case, or, if they are in the same compartment, the magazine or speed loader is contained within a separate enclosure in that compartment that does not contain the firearm and that closes using a snap, button, buckle, zipper, hook and loop closing mechanism, or other fastener that must be opened to access the contents or the firearm is contained within a separate enclosure of that nature in that compartment that does not contain the magazine or speed loader. 2. A pocket or other enclosure on the person of the person in question that closes using a snap, button, buckle, zipper, hook and loop closing mechanism, or other fastener that must be opened to access the contents. 3. With respect to a firearm employing a percussion cap, flintlock, or other obsolete ignition system, when the weapon is uncapped or when the priming charge is removed from the pan.

The person is on or in an all-purpose vehicle as defined in Section 1531.01 of the Revised Code or a motor vehicle during the open hunting season for a wild quadruped or game bird. c. The person is on or in an all-purpose vehicle as defined in Section 1531.01 of the Revised Code on private or publicly owned lands or on or in a motor vehicle that is parked on a road that is owned or administered by the division of wildlife. NOTE: The following affirmative defenses apply to this section: 1. If the firearm is other than a handgun or dangerous ordnance and if the actor was not otherwise prohibited by law from having the weapon, it is an affirmative defense to this section if the weapon was carried or kept ready at hand by the actor for defensive purposes, while the actor was engaged in or was going to or from the actor’s lawful business or occupation, which business or occupation was of a character or was necessarily carried on in a manner or at a time or place as to render the actor particularly susceptible to criminal attack, such as would justify a prudent person in going armed, OR, the weapon was carried or kept ready at hand by the actor for defensive purposes, while the actor was engaged in a lawful activity and had reasonable cause to fear a criminal attack upon the actor, a member of the actor’s family, or the actor’s home, such as would justify a prudent person in going armed. 2. It is an affirmative defense to this section if the actor transported or had the firearm in the motor vehicle for any lawful purpose and while the motor vehicle was on the actor’s own property, provided that this affirmative defense is not available unless the person immediately prior to arriving at the actor’s own property did not transport or possess the firearm in a motor vehicle in a manner prohibited by division (B) or (C) of 2923.16, while the vehicle was being operated on a street, highway, or other public or private property used by the public for vehicular traffic. NOTE: If firearm is loaded, see 2923.16(B) for a similar charge that in an F5. NOTE: For purposes of this section, “unloaded” means any of the following: 1. No ammunition is in the firearm in question, and no magazine or speed loader containing ammunition is inserted into the firearm in question AND either: there is no ammunition in a magazine or speed loader that is in the vehicle in question and that may be used with the firearm in question OR any magazine or speed loader that contains ammunition and that may be used with the firearm in question is stored in a compartment within the vehicle in question that cannot be accessed without leaving the vehicle or is stored in a container that provides complete and separate enclosure. 2. With respect to a firearm employing a percussion cap, flintlock, or other obsolete ignition system, when the weapon is uncapped or when the priming charge is removed from the pan. NOTE: For purposes of this section, “container that provides complete and separate enclosure” includes, but is not limited to, any of the following: 1. A package, box, or case with multiple compartments, as long as the loaded magazine or speed loader and the firearm in question either are in separate compartments within the package, box, or case, or, if they are in the same compartment, the magazine or speed loader is contained within a separate enclosure in that compartment that does not contain the firearm and that closes using a snap, button, buckle, zipper, hook and loop closing mechanism, or other fastener that must be opened to access the contents or the firearm is contained within a separate enclosure of that nature in that compartment that does not contain the magazine or speed loader. 2. A pocket or other enclosure on the person of the person in question that closes using a snap, button, buckle, zipper, hook and loop closing mechanism, or other fastener that must be opened to access the contents.

The person owns the real property, is the spouse or a child of another who owns the property, is the spouse or a child of a tenant of another who owns the real property. d. The person, prior to arriving at the real property did not transport or possess a firearm in the motor vehicle in a manner prohibited by division (B) or (C) of this section while the motor vehicle was being operated on a street, highway, or other public or private property used by the public for vehicular traffic or parking. 4. If the firearm is a handgun and both of the following apply: a. The person who transports or possesses the handgun is either carrying a concealed handgun license, is a qualified adult, or is an active duty member of the armed forces of the United States and is carrying a valid military identification card and documentation of successful completion of firearms training that meets or exceeds the training requirements described in ORC 2923.125(G)(1). b. The person transporting or possessing the handgun is not knowingly in a place described in division (B) of Section 2923.126 of the Revised Code (see notes for 2923.12(A)(2) for list of prohibited places). 5. A person if all of the following apply: a. The person possesses a valid all-purpose vehicle permit issued under Section 1533.103 of the Revised Code by the chief of the division of wildlife. b. The person is on or in an all-purpose vehicle as defined in Section 1531.01 of the Revised Code or a motor vehicle during the open hunting season for a wild quadruped or game bird. c. The person is on or in an all-purpose vehicle as defined in Section 1531.01 of the Revised Code on private or publicly owned lands or on or in a motor vehicle that is parked on a road that is owned or administered by the division of wildlife. NOTE: The following affirmative defenses apply to this section: 1. If the firearm is other than a handgun or dangerous ordnance and if the actor was not otherwise prohibited by law from having the weapon, it is an affirmative defense to this section if the weapon was carried or kept ready at hand by the actor for defensive purposes, while the actor was engaged in or was going to or from the actor’s lawful business or occupation, which business or occupation was of a character or was necessarily carried on in a manner or at a time or place as to render the actor particularly susceptible to criminal attack, such as would justify a prudent person in going armed, OR, the weapon was carried or kept ready at hand by the actor for defensive purposes, while the actor was engaged in a lawful activity and had reasonable cause to fear a criminal attack upon the actor, a member of the actor’s family, or the actor’s home, such as would justify a prudent person in going armed. 2. It is an affirmative defense to this section if the actor transported or had the firearm in the motor vehicle for any lawful purpose and while the motor vehicle was on the actor’s own property, provided that this affirmative defense is not available unless the person immediately prior to arriving at the actor’s own property did not transport or possess the firearm in a motor vehicle in a manner prohibited by division (B) or (C) of 2923.16, while the vehicle was being operated on a street, highway, or other public or private property used by the public for vehicular traffic. NOTE: If firearm is loaded, see 2923.16(B) for a similar charge that in an F5. NOTE: For purposes of this section, “unloaded” means any of the following: 1. No ammunition is in the firearm in question, and no magazine or speed loader containing ammunition is inserted into the firearm in question AND either: there is no ammunition in a magazine or speed loader that is in the vehicle in question and that may be used with the firearm in question OR any magazine or speed loader that contains ammunition and that may be used with the firearm in question is stored in a compartment within the vehicle in question that cannot be accessed without leaving the vehicle or is stored in a container that provides complete and separate enclosure. 2. With respect to a firearm employing a percussion cap, flintlock, or other obsolete ignition system, when the weapon is uncapped or when the priming charge is removed from the pan. NOTE: For purposes of this section, “container that provides complete and separate enclosure” includes, but is not limited to, any of the following: 1. A package, box, or case with multiple compartments, as long as the loaded magazine or speed loader and the firearm in question either are in separate compartments within the package, box, or case, or, if they are in the same compartment, the magazine or speed loader is contained within a separate enclosure in that compartment that does not contain the firearm and that closes using a snap, button, buckle, zipper, hook and loop closing mechanism, or other fastener that must be opened to access the contents or the firearm is contained within a separate enclosure of that nature in that compartment that does not contain the magazine or speed loader. 2. A pocket or other enclosure on the person of the person in question that closes using a snap, button, buckle, zipper, hook and loop closing mechanism, or other fastener that must be opened to access the contents.

A person if all of the following apply: a. The person was the operator or passenger in the motor vehicle. b. The person owns the real property, is the spouse or a child of another who owns the property, is the spouse or a child of a tenant of another who owns the real property. d. The person, prior to arriving at the real property did not transport or possess a firearm in the motor vehicle in a manner prohibited by division (B) or (C) of this section while the motor vehicle was being operated on a street, highway, or other public or private property used by the public for vehicular traffic or parking. 4. If the firearm is a handgun and both of the following apply: a. The person who transports or possesses the handgun is either carrying a concealed handgun license, is a qualified adult, or is an active duty member of the armed forces of the United States and is carrying a valid military identification card and documentation of successful completion of firearms training that meets or exceeds the training requirements described in ORC 2923.125(G)(1). b. The person transporting or possessing the handgun is not knowingly in a place described in division (B) of Section 2923.126 of the Revised Code (see notes for 2923.12(A)(2) for list of prohibited places). 5. A person if all of the following apply: a. The person possesses a valid all-purpose vehicle permit issued under Section 1533.103 of the Revised Code by the chief of the division of wildlife. b. The person is on or in an all-purpose vehicle as defined in Section 1531.01 of the Revised Code or a motor vehicle during the open hunting season for a wild quadruped or game bird. c. The person is on or in an all-purpose vehicle as defined in Section 1531.01 of the Revised Code on private or publicly owned lands or on or in a motor vehicle that is parked on a road that is owned or administered by the division of wildlife. NOTE: The following affirmative defenses apply to this section: 1. If the firearm is other than a handgun or dangerous ordnance and if the actor was not otherwise prohibited by law from having the weapon, it is an affirmative defense to this section if the weapon was carried or kept ready at hand by the actor for defensive purposes, while the actor was engaged in or was going to or from the actor’s lawful business or occupation, which business or occupation was of a character or was necessarily carried on in a manner or at a time or place as to render the actor particularly susceptible to criminal attack, such as would justify a prudent person in going armed, OR, the weapon was carried or kept ready at hand by the actor for defensive purposes, while the actor was engaged in a lawful activity and had reasonable cause to fear a criminal attack upon the actor, a member of the actor’s family, or the actor’s home, such as would justify a prudent person in going armed. 2. It is an affirmative defense to this section if the actor transported or had the firearm in the motor vehicle for any lawful purpose and while the motor vehicle was on the actor’s own property, provided that this affirmative defense is not available unless the person immediately prior to arriving at the actor’s own property did not transport or possess the firearm in a motor vehicle in a manner prohibited by division (B) or (C) of 2923.16, while the vehicle was being operated on a street, highway, or other public or private property used by the public for vehicular traffic. NOTE: If firearm is loaded, see 2923.16(B) for a similar charge that is an F5. NOTE: For purposes of this section, “unloaded” means any of the following: 1. No ammunition is in the firearm in question, and no magazine or speed loader containing ammunition is inserted into the firearm in question AND either: there is no ammunition in a magazine or speed loader that is in the vehicle in question and that may be used with the firearm in question OR any magazine or speed loader that contains ammunition and that may be used with the firearm in question is stored in a compartment within the vehicle in question that cannot be accessed without leaving the vehicle or is stored in a container that provides complete and separate enclosure. 2. With respect to a firearm employing a percussion cap, flintlock, or other obsolete ignition system, when the weapon is uncapped or when the priming charge is removed from the pan. NOTE: For purposes of this section, “container that provides complete and separate enclosure” includes, but is not limited to, any of the following: 1. A package, box, or case with multiple compartments, as long as the loaded magazine or speed loader and the firearm in question either are in separate compartments within the package, box, or case, or, if they are in the same compartment, the magazine or speed loader is contained within a separate enclosure in that compartment that does not contain the firearm and that closes using a snap, button, buckle, zipper, hook and loop closing mechanism, or other fastener that must be opened to access the contents or the firearm is contained within a separate enclosure of that nature in that compartment that does not contain the magazine or speed loader. 2. A pocket or other enclosure on the person of the person in question that closes using a snap, button, buckle, zipper, hook and loop closing mechanism, or other fastener that must be opened to access the contents.

ORC:2923.16.heading: IMPROPERLY HANDLING FIREARMS IN A MOTOR VEHICLE 2923.16(D)(1) ORC

ORC:2923.16.text: _____________ did knowingly (transport or have) a loaded handgun, to wit: (DESCRIBE HANDGUN), in a motor vehicle, to wit: (DESCRIBE VEHICLE), and at the time of that (transportation or possession) the person was under the influence of (alcohol, or a drug of abuse, or alcohol and a drug of abuse), to wit: (DESCRIBE OFFENDER’S CONDITION), in violation of Section 2923.16(D)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2923.16.heading: IMPROPERLY HANDLING FIREARMS IN A MOTOR VEHICLE 2923.16(D)(1) ORC

ORC:2923.16.heading: IMPROPERLY HANDLING FIREARMS IN A MOTOR VEHICLE 2923.16(E)(1) ORC
ORC:2923.16.variant: FAILURE TO DISCLOSE WHEN ASKED BY OFFICER – M2/MM

ORC:2923.16.notes: NOTE: It is not a violation of this division if the person fails to disclose that fact to the officer during the stop and the person has already notified another officer during that same stop. NOTE: This section does not apply to the following: 1. Officers, agents, or employees of this or any other state or the United States, or to law enforcement officers, when authorized to carry or have loaded or accessible firearms in motor vehicles and acting within the scope of their duties. 2. Any person who is employed in this state, who is authorized to carry or have loaded or accessible firearms in motor vehicles, and who is subject to and in compliance with the requirements of Section 109.801 (Peace Officer Annual Firearms Requalification) of the Revised Code, unless the appointing authority of the person has expressly specified that this exemption does not apply to the person.

NOTE: This section does not apply to the following: 1. Officers, agents, or employees of this or any other state or the United States, or to law enforcement officers, when authorized to carry or have loaded or accessible firearms in motor vehicles and acting within the scope of their duties. 2. ORC:2923.16.heading: IMPROPERLY HANDLING FIREARMS IN A MOTOR VEHICLE 2923.16(E)(3) ORC

ORC:2923.16.text: _____________, having been issued a concealed handgun license or is a qualified adult, or is an active duty member of the armed forces of the United States and is carrying a valid military identification card and documentation or successful completion of firearms training that meets or exceeds the training requirements described in ORC 2923.125(G)(1), and being a (driver or occupant) of a motor vehicle, to wit: (DESCRIBE VEHICLE), and having been stopped for (a traffic stop or for another law enforcement purpose), to wit: (DESCRIBE REASON FOR STOP), and having a loaded handgun in said motor vehicle, to wit: (DESCRIBE HANDGUN), did knowingly fail to (remain in the motor vehicle or remain in the motor vehicle or keep their hands in plain sight) at a time after a law enforcement officer, to wit: (NAME OF OFFICER), began approaching the person and before the law enforcement officer left; to wit: (DESCRIBE OFFENDER’S ACTIONS AND WHEN THE ACTIONS OCCURRED), in violation of Section 2923.16(E)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2923.16.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to the following: 1. Any person who is employed in this state, who is authorized to carry or have loaded or accessible firearms in motor vehicles, and who is subject to and in compliance with the requirements of Section 109.801 (Peace Officer Annual Firearms Requalification) of the Revised Code, unless the appointing authority of the person has expressly specified that this exemption does not apply to the person. 3. If the offender’s failure to remain in the motor vehicle or to keep the person’s hands in plain sight is pursuant to and in accordance with directions given by a law enforcement officer.

ORC:2923.161.heading: IMPROPERLY DISCHARGING A FIREARM AT OR INTO A HABITATION 2923.161(A)(1) ORC
