ORC:2923.161.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to officers, agents, or employees of this or any other state or the United States, or to law enforcement officers, when authorized to carry or have loaded or accessible firearms in motor vehicles and acting within the scope of their duties.

ORC:2923.161.heading: IMPROPERLY DISCHARGING A FIREARM WITH THE INTENT TO CAUSE HARM OR PANIC TO PERSONS IN A SCHOOL, IN A SCHOOL BUILDING, OR AT A SCHOOL FUNCTION OR THE EVACUATION OF A SCHOOL FUNCTION 2923.161(B) ORC
ORC:2923.161.text: _____________ did, without privilege to do so, knowingly discharge a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE SPECIFIC FIREARM), within 1,000 feet of any school building or of the boundaries of any school premises, to wit: (STATE NAME AND LOCATION OF SCHOOL AND OFFENDER’S DISTANCE FROM IT), with the intent to ((cause physical harm to another who is in) or (cause panic or fear of physical harm to another who is in) or (cause the evacuation of)) the school, in the school building, or at a function or activity associated with the school, in violation of Section 2923.161(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2923.161.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to officers, agents, or employees of this or any other state or the United States, or to law enforcement officers, who discharge the firearm while acting within the scope of their duties.

ORC:2923.162.heading: DISCHARGE OF A FIREARM ON OR NEAR PROHIBITED PREMISES 2923.162(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2923.162.text: _____________ did, without permission from the proper officials, discharge a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE SPECIFIC FIREARM) (upon or over a cemetery or within 100 yards of a cemetery), to wit: (NAME OF CEMETERY), in violation of Section 2923.162(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2923.162.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to a person who, while on the person’s own land, discharges a firearm.

ORC:2923.162.heading: DISCHARGE OF A FIREARM ON OR NEAR PROHIBITED PREMISES 2923.162(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2923.162.text: _____________ did discharge a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE SPECIFIC FIREARM) on a lawn, park, pleasure ground, orchard, or other ground appurtenant to a schoolhouse, church, or inhabited dwelling, the property of another, or a charitable institution, to wit: (DESCRIBE TYPE OF GROUNDS), in violation of Section 2923.162(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2923.162.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to a person who owns any type of property described in that division and who, while on the person’s own enclosure, discharges a firearm.

ORC:2923.162.heading: DISCHARGE OF A FIREARM ON OR NEAR PROHIBITED PREMISES 2923.162(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2923.162.variant: OVER A ROAD OR PUBLIC HIGHWAY – M1
ORC:2923.162.text: _____________ did discharge a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE FIREARM), (upon or over) a public road or highway, to wit: (NAME OF ROAD OR HIGHWAY), in violation of Section 2923.162(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2923.162.heading: DISCHARGE OF A FIREARM ON OR NEAR PROHIBITED PREMISES 2923.162(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2923.162.variant: OVER A ROAD OR PUBLIC HIGHWAY – SUBSTANTIAL RISK OF PHYSICAL HARM TO ANY PERSON – F3
ORC:2923.162.text: _____________ did discharge a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE FIREARM), (upon or over) a public road or highway, to wit: (NAME OF ROAD OR HIGHWAY), creating a substantial risk of physical harm to a person, to wit: (STATE PERSON AND RISK OF PHYSICAL HARM), in violation of Section 2923.162(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2923.162.heading: DISCHARGE OF A FIREARM ON OR NEAR PROHIBITED PREMISES 2923.162(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2923.162.variant: OVER A ROAD OR PUBLIC HIGHWAY – SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM TO PROPERTY – F3
ORC:2923.162.text: _____________ did discharge a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE FIREARM), (upon or over) a public road or highway, to wit: (NAME OF ROAD OR HIGHWAY), causing serious physical harm to property, to wit: (STATE PROPERTY AND RISK OF PHYSICAL HARM), in violation of Section 2923.162(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2923.162.heading: DISCHARGE OF A FIREARM ON OR NEAR PROHIBITED PREMISES 2923.162(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2923.162.variant: OVER A ROAD OR PUBLIC HIGHWAY – PHYSICAL HARM TO ANY PERSON – F2
ORC:2923.162.text: _____________ did discharge a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE FIREARM), (upon or over) a public road or highway, to wit: (NAME OF ROAD OR HIGHWAY), causing physical harm to a person, to wit: (STATE PERSON AND PHYSICAL HARM), in violation of Section 2923.162(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2923.162.heading: DISCHARGE OF A FIREARM ON OR NEAR PROHIBITED PREMISES 2923.162(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2923.162.variant: OVER A ROAD OR PUBLIC HIGHWAY – SERIOUS PHYSICAL HARM TO ANY PERSON – F1
ORC:2923.162.text: _____________ did discharge a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE FIREARM), (upon or over) a public road or highway, to wit: (NAME OF ROAD OR HIGHWAY), causing serious physical harm to a person, to wit: (STATE PERSON AND RISK OF PHYSICAL HARM), in violation of Section 2923.162(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the first degree.

ORC:2923.17.heading: UNLAWFUL POSSESSION OF DANGEROUS ORDNANCE 2923.17(A) ORC
ORC:2923.17.text: _____________ did knowingly (acquire or have or carry or use) a dangerous ordnance, to wit: (DESCRIBE DANGEROUS ORDNANCE AND MANNER ACQUIRED OR POSSESSED OR CARRIED OR USED), in violation of Section 2923.17(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2923.17.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to: 1. Officers, agents or employees of any state or the United States; members of the US Armed Forces; members of any state organized militia and law enforcement officers, to extent they are authorized to acquire, have, carry or use a dangerous ordnance and act within the scope of their duties. 2. Importers, manufacturers, dealers and users of explosives with federal license or user permit (18 USC 843) to extent lawful under federal and state law. 3. Importers, manufacturers and dealers with federal license to deal in destructive devices or ammunition (18 USC 923) to extent lawful under federal and state law. 4. Persons with surplus ordnance sold, loaned or given by secretary of the army if properly used (10 USC 4684). 5. Owners of dangerous ordnance registered in national firearms registration and transfer record (26 USC 5841). 6. Transporters of dangerous ordnance in course of lawful business in compliance with federal and state law. 7. Holders of state license or temporary permit issued under Section 2923.18 of the Ohio Revised Code when in compliance with license or permit.

ORC:2923.17.heading: UNLAWFUL POSSESSION OF DANGEROUS ORDNANCE 2923.17(B) ORC
ORC:2923.17.text: _____________ did (manufacture or process) an explosive, to wit: (DESCRIBE EXPLOSIVE) at a location in this state, to wit: (NAME LOCATION WHERE MANUFACTURED OR PROCESSED) without first being issued a (license, or certificate of registration, or permit) from (a fire official of a political subdivision of this state or from the office of the fire marshal), in violation of Section 2923.17(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2923.19.heading: FAILURE TO SECURE DANGEROUS ORDNANCE 2923.19(A)(1) ORC (CCC 2323.19(A)(1))
ORC:2923.19.variant: AGAINST THEFT OR UNAUTHORIZED USE – M2
ORC:2923.19.text: _____________ did, in (acquiring or possessing or carrying or using) a dangerous ordnance, to wit: (DESCRIBE DANGEROUS ORDNANCE), negligently fail to take proper precautions to secure said dangerous ordnance (against theft or against its acquisition or use by an unauthorized or incompetent person, to wit: (DESCRIBE HOW SECURED AND CIRCUMSTANCES OF ACQUISITION OR THEFT AND NAME THE OTHER PERSON), in violation of Section 2923.19(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.
ORC:2923.19.notes: NOTE: For purposes of Section 2323.19 CCC, “dangerous ordnance” has the same meaning as used in Section 2534.01 CCC. NOTE: If the offender had a firearm or dangerous ordnance on or about the offender’s person or under the offender’s control at the time of the commission of the offense in violation of the Columbus City Code, the firearm or dangerous ordnance shall be seized and is subject to forfeiture under Chapter 2981 of the Ohio Revised Code. Refer to the complaint language cited in Chapter 2927 of the Criminal Complaint Manual.

ORC:2923.19.heading: FAILURE TO SECURE DANGEROUS ORDNANCE 2923.19(A)(2) ORC (CCC 2323.19(A)(2))
ORC:2923.19.text: _____________ did, in (acquiring or possessing or carrying or using) a dangerous ordnance, to wit: (DESCRIBE DANGEROUS ORDNANCE), negligently fail to take proper precautions to insure the safety of persons and property, to wit: (DESCRIBE HOW IT WAS NEGLIGENTLY SECURED AND CONSEQUENCES IF ANY), in violation of Section 2923.19(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.
ORC:2923.19.notes: NOTE: For purposes of Section 2323.19 CCC, “dangerous ordnance” has the same meaning as used in Section 2534.01 CCC. NOTE: If the offender had a firearm or dangerous ordnance on or about the offender’s person or under the offender’s control at the time of the commission of the offense in violation of the Columbus City Code, the firearm or dangerous ordnance shall be seized and is subject to forfeiture under Chapter 2981 of the Ohio Revised Code. Refer to the complaint language cited in Chapter 2927 of the Criminal Complaint Manual. DEFINITIONS 2323.191 CCC NOTE: The following criteria apply to this section: 1. Violations are generally a misdemeanor of the fourth degree. a. If a minor gains access to a firearm as a result of an individual’s violation of this section, it is a misdemeanor of the third degree. b. If a minor gains access to a firearm as a result of a violation of this section and uses the firearm to cause any personal injury or death, other than in self-defense, a violation of this section is a misdemeanor of the first degree. 2. It is not a violation if a person stores or leaves a firearm in the person’s residence if the firearm is kept in safe storage as defined in Section 2323.11(O) of the Columbus City Code, the firearm is on one’s person or within one’s immediate control, or if a minor gains access to the firearm as a result of any other person’s unlawful entry into the residence. 3. This section shall not apply if the circumstances indicate that the firearm was unlawfully furnished to the minor. Such a violation should be prosecuted under applicable state law. 4. If the offender had a firearm or dangerous ordnance on or about the offender’s person or under the offender’s control at the time of the commission of the offense in violation of the Columbus City Code, the firearm or dangerous ordnance shall be seized and is subject to forfeiture under Chapter 2981 of the Ohio Revised Code. Refer to the complaint language cited in Chapter 2927 of the Criminal Complaint Manual.

CCC:2323.191.heading: NEGLIGENT STORAGE OF FIREARM 2323.191(A)(1) CCC
CCC:2323.191.variant: MINOR DID NOT GAIN ACCESS – M4
CCC:2323.191.text: _____________ did negligently store or leave a firearm in a manner or location in the person’s residence where the person knows or reasonably should know a minor is able to gain access to the firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE HOW FIREARM WAS NEGLIGENTLY STORED AND AGE OF MINOR), in violation of Section 2323.191(A)(1) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

CCC:2323.191.heading: NEGLIGENT STORAGE OF FIREARM 2323.191(A)(1) CCC
CCC:2323.191.text: _____________ did negligently store or leave a firearm in a manner or location in the person’s residence where the person knows or reasonably should know a minor is able to gain access to the firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE HOW FIREARM WAS NEGLIGENTLY STORED AND AGE OF MINOR), and the minor gained access to the firearm as a result of the person’s negligent storage of the firearm, in violation of Section 2323.191(A)(1) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the third degree.

CCC:2323.191.heading: NEGLIGENT STORAGE OF FIREARM 2323.191(A)(1) CCC
CCC:2323.191.variant: MINOR GAINED ACCESS AND USED FIREARM – M1
CCC:2323.191.text: _____________ did negligently store or leave a firearm in a manner or location in the person’s residence where the person knows or reasonably should know a minor is able to gain access to the firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE HOW FIREARM WAS NEGLIGENTLY STORED AND AGE OF MINOR), and the minor gained access to the firearm as a result of the person’s negligent storage of the firearm, and the minor used the firearm to cause any personal injury or death, other than in self-defense, in violation of Section 2323.191(A) (1) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
CCC:2323.191.notes: DEFINITIONS 2923.20 ORC NOTE: Divisions (A)(3), (A)(4), and (A)(5) do not apply to any of the following: 1. A law enforcement officer who is acting within the scope of the officer’s duties; 2. A person who is acting in accordance with directions given by a law enforcement officer described in division (B)(1) of this section.

ORC:2923.20.heading: UNLAWFUL TRANSACTION IN WEAPONS 2923.20(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2923.20.variant: FURNISH FIREARM TO PERSON UNDER DISABILITY OR INFLUENCE OF DRUG OR ALCOHOL – F4
ORC:2923.20.text: _____________ did recklessly (sell or lend or give or furnish) a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE FIREARM) to a person prohibited by Section (2923.13 or 2923.15 of the Ohio Revised Code) from (acquiring or using) a firearm, to wit: (STATE PERSON RECEIVING FIREARM AND FACTS REGARDING PROHIBITION) in violation of Section 2923.20(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2923.20.heading: UNLAWFUL TRANSACTION IN WEAPONS 2923.20(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2923.20.variant: FURNISH DANGEROUS ORDNANCE TO PERSON UNDER DISABILITY OR INFLUENCE OF DRUG OR ALCOHOL OR NOT LICENSED – F4
ORC:2923.20.text: _____________ did recklessly (sell or lend or give or furnish) a dangerous ordnance, to wit: (DESCRIBE DANGEROUS ORDNANCE) to a person prohibited by Section (2923.13 or 2923.15 or 2923.17) of the Ohio Revised Code from (acquiring or using) a dangerous ordnance, to wit: (STATE PERSON RECEIVING DANGEROUS ORDNANCE AND FACTS REGARDING PROHIBITION) in violation of Section 2923.20(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2923.20.heading: UNLAWFUL TRANSACTION IN WEAPONS 2923.20(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2923.20.variant: DISPOSING OF FIREARM OR DANGEROUS ORDNANCE – F4
ORC:2923.20.text: _____________ did possess any firearm or dangerous ordnance with purpose to dispose of it in violation of Division (A) of this section, to wit: (DESCRIBE FIREARM OR DANGEROUS ORDNANCE AND HOW IT WAS BEING DISPOSED), in violation of Section 2923.20(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2923.20.heading: UNLAWFUL TRANSACTION IN WEAPONS 2923.20(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2923.20.variant: PROCURE, SOLICIT, PERSUADE, ENCOURAGE, OR ENTICE ANOTHER TO TRANSFER FIREARM OR AMMUNITION IN PROHIBITED MANNER – F3
ORC:2923.20.text: _____________ did knowingly (solicit, persuade, encourage, or entice) a (federally licensed firearms dealer or private seller), to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON AND POSITION) to transfer (a firearm or ammunition), to any person, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON AND WHAT WAS TRANSFERRED), in a manner prohibited by state of federal law, to wit: (DESCRIBE HOW DEALER OR SELLER WAS SOLICITED/PERSUADED), in violation of Section 2923.20(A) (3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2923.20.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to any of the following: 1. A law enforcement officer who is acting within the scope of the officer’s duties; 2. A person who is acting in accordance with directions given by a law enforcement officer described in Division (B)(1) of this section.

ORC:2923.20.heading: UNLAWFUL TRANSACTION IN WEAPONS 2923.20(A)(4) ORC
ORC:2923.20.variant: PROVIDE MATERIALLY FALSE INFORMATION TO A FIREARMS DEALER OR PRIVATE SELLER – F3
ORC:2923.20.text: _____________ did, with an intent to deceive, knowingly provide materially false information to a (federally licensed firearms dealer or private seller), to wit: (STATE INTENT, WHAT FALSE INFORMATION WAS PROVIDED AND TO WHOM), in violation of Section 2923.20(A)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2923.20.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to any of the following: 1. A law enforcement officer who is acting within the scope of the officer’s duties; 2. A person who is acting in accordance with directions given by a law enforcement officer described in Division (B)(1) of this section.

ORC:2923.20.heading: UNLAWFUL TRANSACTION IN WEAPONS 2923.20(A)(5) ORC
ORC:2923.20.variant: PROCURE, SOLICIT, PERSUADE, ENCOURAGE, OR ENTICE ANOTHER TO VIOLATE SECTION (A)(3) OR (A)(4) – F3
ORC:2923.20.text: _____________ did, knowingly (procure, solicit, persuade, encourage, or entice) another person, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON) to act in violation of 2923.20(A)(3) or (4), to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2923.20(A)(5) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2923.20.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to any of the following: 1. A law enforcement officer who is acting within the scope of the officer’s duties; 2. A person who is acting in accordance with directions given by a law enforcement officer described in Division (B)(1) of this section.

ORC:2923.20.heading: UNLAWFUL TRANSACTION IN WEAPONS 2923.20(A)(6) ORC
ORC:2923.20.variant: FAIL TO IDENTIFY AUTHORIZATION OF DANGEROUS ORDNANCE – M2
ORC:2923.20.text: _____________ did, when transferring a dangerous ordnance (DESCRIBE DANGEROUS ORDNANCE) to another, to wit: (NAME OTHER PERSON), negligently fail to require the transferee to exhibit such identification, license, or permit showing that person to be authorized to acquire the dangerous ordnance pursuant to Section 2923.17 of the Ohio Revised Code, in violation of Section 2923.20(A)(6) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2923.20.heading: UNLAWFUL TRANSACTION IN WEAPONS 2923.20(A)(6) ORC
ORC:2923.20.variant: FAIL TO RECORD TRANSACTION OF DANGEROUS ORDNANCE – M2
ORC:2923.20.text: _____________ did, when transferring a dangerous ordnance (DESCRIBE DANGEROUS ORDNANCE) to another, negligently fail to take a complete record of the transaction and forthwith forward a copy of that record to the sheriff of the county or safety director or police chief of the municipality where the transaction took place, to wit: (DESCRIBE WHERE TRANSACTION OCCURRED), in violation of Section 2923.20(A)(6) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2923.20.heading: UNLAWFUL TRANSACTION IN WEAPONS 2923.20(A)(7) ORC (CCC 2323.20(B))
ORC:2923.20.variant: FAIL TO REPORT LOSS OR THEFT OF DANGEROUS ORDNANCE – M4
ORC:2923.20.text: _____________ did, knowingly fail to report to law enforcement authorities forthwith the loss or theft of any firearm or dangerous ordnance, to wit: (DESCRIBE FIREARM OR DANGEROUS ORDNANCE), in the person’s possession or under the persons control, in violation of Section 2923.20(A)(7) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2923.20.notes: NOTE: If the offender had a firearm or dangerous ordnance on or about the offender’s person or under the offender’s control at the time of the commission of the offense in violation of the Columbus City Code, the firearm or dangerous ordnance shall be seized and is subject to forfeiture under Chapter 2981 of the Ohio Revised Code. Refer to the complaint language cited in Chapter 2927 of the Criminal Complaint Manual.

CCC:2323.20.heading: UNLAWFUL TRANSACTION IN WEAPONS 2323.20(A)(1) CCC
CCC:2323.20.variant: RECKLESSLY SELL, LEND, GIVE, OR FURNISH FIREARM – M1
CCC:2323.20.text: _____________ did recklessly (sell, lend, give, or furnish a firearm) to another person, (NAME PERSON), when the seller or furnisher knew, or had reason to know, that the person purchasing or attempting to purchase the firearm did so for, on behalf of, or at the request or demand of any other person that meets the criteria of one or more provisions in Section 2923.13 of the Ohio Revised Code or Section 2323.13 of the Columbus City Code pertaining to weapons under disability, in violation of Section 2323.20(A)(1) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
CCC:2323.20.notes: NOTE: If the offender had a firearm or dangerous ordnance on or about the offender’s person or under the offender’s control at the time of the commission of the offense in violation of the Columbus City Code, the firearm or dangerous ordnance shall be seized and is subject to forfeiture under Chapter 2981 of the Ohio Revised Code. Refer to the complaint language cited in Chapter 2927 of the Criminal Complaint Manual.

CCC:2323.20.heading: UNLAWFUL TRANSACTION IN WEAPONS 2323.20(A)(2) CCC
CCC:2323.20.text: _____________ did recklessly (purchase or attempt to purchase) any firearm (DESCRIBE WEAPON) for, on behalf of, or at the request or demand of any other person, (NAME PERSON), knowing or having reasonable cause to believe that such other person meets the criteria of one or more provisions in Section 2923.13 of the Ohio Revised Code or Section 2323.13 of the Columbus City Code pertaining to weapons under disability, in violation of Section 2323.20(A) (2) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
CCC:2323.20.notes: NOTE: If the offender had a firearm or dangerous ordnance on or about the offender’s person or under the offender’s control at the time of the commission of the offense in violation of the Columbus City Code, the firearm or dangerous ordnance shall be seized and is subject to forfeiture under Chapter 2981 of the Ohio Revised Code. Refer to the complaint language cited in Chapter 2927 of the Criminal Complaint Manual.

ORC:2923.201.heading: DEFACING A FIREARM 2923.201(A)(1) ORC (CCC 2323.201(A)(1))
ORC:2923.201.variant: CHANGE, ALTER, REMOVE, OR OBLITERATE IDENTIFICATION MARK OR SERIAL NUMBER – M1
ORC:2923.201.text: _____________ did (change, alter, remove, or obliterate) the (name of the manufacturer, model, manufacturer’s serial number, or other mark of identification) on a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE FIREARM AND HOW IT WAS DEFACED), in violation of Section 2923.201(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2923.201.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to any firearm on which no manufacturer’s serial number was inscribed at the time of its manufacture. NOTE: Section 2323.201(A)(1) CCC shall not apply to circumstances which, by law, constitute felony violations to be prosecuted under either Section 2923.201 ORC or other applicable state law. NOTE: If the offender had a firearm or dangerous ordnance on or about the offender’s person or under the offender’s control at the time of the commission of the offense in violation of the Columbus City Code, the firearm or dangerous ordnance shall be seized and is subject to forfeiture under Chapter 2981 of the Ohio Revised Code. Refer to the complaint language cited in Chapter 2927 of the Criminal Complaint Manual.

ORC:2923.201.heading: DEFACING A FIREARM 2923.201(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2923.201.variant: DEFACE A FIREARM – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F4
ORC:2923.201.text: _____________ did (change, alter, remove, or obliterate) the (name of the manufacturer, model, manufacturer’s serial number, or other mark of identification) on a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE FIREARM AND HOW IT WAS DEFACED), and (STATE OFFENDER’S NAME) having been previously convicted of violating Section 2923.201(A)(1), to wit: on (STATE DATE), in (STATE NAME OF COURT) (STATE CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2923.201(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2923.201.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to any firearm on which no manufacturer’s serial number was inscribed at the time of its manufacture.

ORC:2923.201.heading: DEFACING A FIREARM 2923.201(A)(2) ORC (CCC 2323.201(A)(2))
ORC:2923.201.text: _____________ did possess a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE FIREARM) knowing or having reasonable cause to believe that the (name of the manufacturer, model, manufacturer’s serial number, or other mark of identification) on the firearm has been (changed, altered, removed, or obliterated), to wit: (DESCRIBE HOW THE FIREARM WAS DEFACED), in violation of Section 2923.201(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2923.201.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to any firearm on which no manufacturer’s serial number was inscribed at the time of its manufacture. NOTE: Section 2323.201(A)(2) CCC shall not apply to circumstances which, by law, constitute felony violations to be prosecuted under either Section 2923.201 ORC or other applicable state law. NOTE: If the offender had a firearm or dangerous ordnance on or about the offender’s person or under the offender’s control at the time of the commission of the offense in violation of the Columbus City Code, the firearm or dangerous ordnance shall be seized and is subject to forfeiture under Chapter 2981 of the Ohio Revised Code. Refer to the complaint language cited in Chapter 2927 of the Criminal Complaint Manual.

ORC:2923.201.heading: DEFACING A FIREARM 2923.201(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2923.201.variant: POSSESS A DEFACED FIREARM – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F4
ORC:2923.201.text: _____________ did possess a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE FIREARM) knowing or having reasonable cause to believe that the (name of the manufacturer, model, manufacturer’s serial number, or other mark of identification) on the firearm has been (changed, altered, removed, or obliterated), to wit: (DESCRIBE HOW THE FIREARM WAS DEFACED), and (STATE OFFENDER’S NAME) having been previously convicted of violating Section 2923.201(A)(2), to wit: on (STATE DATE), in (STATE NAME OF COURT) (STATE CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2923.201(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2923.201.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to any firearm on which no manufacturer’s serial number was inscribed at the time of its manufacture.

ORC:2923.21.heading: IMPROPERLY FURNISHING FIREARMS TO A MINOR 2923.21(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2923.21.variant: SELL FIREARM TO PERSON UNDER 18 YEARS – F5
ORC:2923.21.text: _____________ did sell a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE SALE AND FIREARM), to a person, to wit: (STATE NAME OF BUYER), being under eighteen years of age, to wit: (STATE THE AGE OF BUYER), in violation of Section 2923.21(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2923.21.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to the sale or furnishing of a handgun to a person eighteen years or older and under twenty-one years of age if the person eighteen years of age or older and under twenty-one years of age is a law enforcement officer who is properly appointed or employed as a law enforcement officer and has received firearms training approved by the Ohio Peace officer training council or equivalent firearms training. NOTE: This section does not apply to the sale or furnishing of a handgun to an active duty member of the armed forces of the United States who has received firearms training that meets or exceeds the training requirements described in ORC 2923.125(G)(1).

ORC:2923.21.heading: IMPROPERLY FURNISHING FIREARMS TO A MINOR 2923.21(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2923.21.variant: SELL HANDGUN TO PERSON UNDER 21 YEARS – F5
ORC:2923.21.text: _____________ did sell a handgun, to wit: (DESCRIBE SALE AND HANDGUN), to a person, to wit: (STATE NAME OF BUYER), being under twenty-one years of age, to wit: (STATE THE AGE OF THE BUYER), in violation of Section 2923.21(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2923.21.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to the sale or furnishing of a handgun to a person eighteen years or older and under twenty-one years of age if the person eighteen years of age or older and under twenty-one years of age is a law enforcement officer who is properly appointed or employed as a law enforcement officer and has received firearms training approved by the Ohio Peace officer training council or equivalent firearms training. NOTE: This section does not apply to the sale or furnishing of a handgun to an active duty member of the armed forces of the United States who has received firearms training that meets or exceeds the training requirements described in ORC 2923.125(G)(1).

ORC:2923.21.heading: IMPROPERLY FURNISHING FIREARMS TO A MINOR 2923.21(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2923.21.variant: FURNISH FIREARM TO PERSON UNDER 18 WITHOUT ADULT SUPERVISION – F5
ORC:2923.21.text: _____________ did furnish a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE FIREARM) to a person, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON) who was under eighteen years of age, to wit: (STATE AGE OF PERSON), and not being for the purpose of lawful hunting, sporting or educational purposes under the supervision or control of a responsible adult, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2923.21(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2923.21.heading: IMPROPERLY FURNISHING FIREARMS TO A MINOR 2923.21(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2923.21.variant: FURNISH HANDGUN TO PERSON UNDER 21 WITHOUT ADULT SUPERVISION – F5
ORC:2923.21.text: _____________ did furnish a handgun, to wit: (DESCRIBE HANDGUN) to a person, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON) who was under twenty-one years of age, to wit: (STATE AGE OF PERSON) and not being for the purpose of lawful hunting, sporting or educational purposes under the supervision or control of a responsible adult, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCE), in violation of Section 2923.21(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2923.21.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to the sale or furnishing of a handgun to a person eighteen years or older and under twenty-one years of age if the person eighteen years of age or older and under twenty-one years of age is a law enforcement officer who is properly appointed or employed as a law enforcement officer and has received firearms training approved by the Ohio Peace officer training council or equivalent firearms training.

ORC:2923.21.heading: IMPROPERLY FURNISHING FIREARMS TO A MINOR 2923.21(A)(4) ORC
ORC:2923.21.variant: SELL OR FURNISH FIREARM TO PERSON TO SELL TO A PERSON UNDER 18 YEARS OF AGE – F5
ORC:2923.21.text: _____________ did (sell or furnish) a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE FIREARM) to a person, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON) who was eighteen years of age or older, to wit: (STATE AGE OF PERSON) and (knowing or having reason to know) that the person receiving the firearm was purchasing or receiving the firearm for the purpose of ((selling the firearm in violation of 2923.21(A)(1)) or (furnishing the firearm in violation of 2923.21(A)(3)) of the Ohio Revised Code to a person who is under eighteen years of age, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON AND AGE) in violation of Section 2923.21(A)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2923.21.heading: IMPROPERLY FURNISHING FIREARMS TO A MINOR 2923.21(A)(5) ORC
ORC:2923.21.variant: SELL OR FURNISH HANDGUN TO PERSON TO SELL TO A PERSON UNDER 21 YEARS OF AGE – F5
ORC:2923.21.text: _____________ did (sell or furnish) a handgun, to wit: (DESCRIBE HANDGUN) to a person, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON) who was twenty-one years of age or older, to wit: (STATE AGE OF PERSON) and (knowing or having reason to know) that the person receiving the handgun was purchasing or receiving the handgun for the purpose of ((selling the handgun in violation of 2923.21(A)(2)) or (furnishing the handgun in violation of 2923.21(A)(3)) of the Ohio Revised Code to a person who is under twenty-one years of age, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON AND AGE) in violation of Section 2923.21(A)(5) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2923.21.heading: IMPROPERLY FURNISHING FIREARMS TO A MINOR 2923.21(A)(6) ORC
ORC:2923.21.variant: PURCHASE OR ATTEMPT TO PURCHASE A FIREARM WITH INTENT TO SELL OR FURNISH TO PERSON UNDER 18 YEARS – F5
ORC:2923.21.text: _____________ did (purchase or attempt to purchase) a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE FIREARM) with the intent to (sell the firearm in violation of 2923.21(A)(1) or furnish the firearm in violation of 2923.21(A)(3)) to a person, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON) who was under eighteen years of age, to wit: (STATE AGE OF PERSON) in violation of Section 2923.21(A)(6) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2923.21.heading: IMPROPERLY FURNISHING FIREARMS TO A MINOR 2923.21(A)(7) ORC
ORC:2923.21.variant: PURCHASE OR ATTEMPT TO PURCHASE A HANDGUN WITH INTENT TO SELL OR FURNISH TO PERSON UNDER 21 YEARS – F5
ORC:2923.21.text: _____________ did (purchase or attempt to purchase) a handgun, to wit: (DESCRIBE HANDGUN) with the intent to (sell the handgun in violation of 2923.21(A)(2) or furnish the handgun in violation of 2923.21(A)(3)) to a person, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON) who was under twenty-one years of age, to wit: (STATE AGE OF PERSON) in violation of Section 2923.21(A)(7) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2923.211.heading: UNDERAGE PURCHASE OF FIREARM OR HANDGUN 2923.211(A) ORC
ORC:2923.211.variant: PURCHASE OF FIREARM BY PERSON UNDER 18 YEARS – F4
ORC:2923.211.text: _____________ did (purchase or attempt purchase) a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE FIREARM) and was under eighteen years of age, to wit: (STATE AGE) in violation of Section 2923.211(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2923.211.notes: NOTE: The offender being a delinquent child is subject to disposition under Section 2151.355 of the Ohio Revised Code.

ORC:2923.211.heading: UNDERAGE PURCHASE OF FIREARM OR HANDGUN 2923.211(B) ORC (CCC 2323.211(B))
ORC:2923.211.variant: PURCHASE A HANDGUN BY PERSON UNDER 21 YEARS – M2
ORC:2923.211.text: _____________ did (purchase or attempt to purchase) a handgun, to wit: (DESCRIBE HANDGUN) and was under the age of twenty-one years, to wit: (STATE AGE) and (STATE OFFENDER’S NAME) is not a law enforcement officer, or an active, reserve or honorably discharged member of the armed forces of the United States or the Ohio National Guard who has received firearms training, in violation of Section 2923.211(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.
ORC:2923.211.notes: NOTE: If the offender had a firearm or dangerous ordnance on or about the offender’s person or under the offender’s control at the time of the commission of the offense in violation of the Columbus City Code, the firearm or dangerous ordnance shall be seized and is subject to forfeiture under Chapter 2981 of the Ohio Revised Code. Refer to the complaint language cited in Chapter 2927 of the Criminal Complaint Manual.

ORC:2923.24.heading: POSSESSING CRIMINAL TOOLS 2923.24(A) ORC (CCC 2323.24(A))
ORC:2923.24.variant: WITH PURPOSE TO COMMIT OFFENSE OTHER THAN A FELONY – M1
ORC:2923.24.text: _____________ did (have under his or her control or possess) a (substance or device or instrument or article), to wit: (DESCRIBE ITEM), with the purpose to use it criminally, to wit: (DESCRIBE MANNER TOOL WAS POSSESSED AND PURPOSE), in violation of Section 2923.24(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2923.24.notes: NOTE: It is prima facie evidence of “criminal purpose” if any of the following apply: 1. Possession or control of a dangerous ordnance, or materials or parts for making a dangerous ordnance, absent circumstances indicating the dangerous ordnance, materials, or parts are intended for legitimate use; 2. Possession or control of any substance, device, instrument or article designed or specially adapted for criminal use; 3. Possession or control of any substance, device, instrument or article commonly used for criminal purposes, under circumstances indicating the item is intended from criminal use. NOTE: Section 2323.24(A) CCC shall not apply to circumstances which, by law, constitute felony violations to be prosecuted under either Section 2923.24 ORC or other applicable state law. NOTE: If the offender had a firearm or dangerous ordnance on or about the offender’s person or under the offender’s control at the time of the commission of the offense in violation of the Columbus City Code, the firearm or dangerous ordnance shall be seized and is subject to forfeiture under Chapter 2981 of the Ohio Revised Code. Refer to the complaint language cited in Chapter 2927 of the Criminal Complaint Manual.

ORC:2923.24.heading: POSSESSING CRIMINAL TOOLS 2923.24(A) ORC
ORC:2923.24.variant: WITH PURPOSE TO COMMIT A FELONY – F5
ORC:2923.24.text: _____________ did (have under his or her control or possess) a (substance or device or instrument or article), to wit: (DESCRIBE ITEM), with the purpose to use it criminally, to wit: (DESCRIBE MANNER TOOL WAS POSSESSED AND PURPOSE), and the circumstances indicated that the (substance or device or instrument or article) was intended for use in the commission of a felony, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES) in violation of Section 2923.24(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2923.24.notes: NOTE: It is prima facie evidence of “criminal purpose” if any of the following apply: 1. Possession or control of a dangerous ordnance, or materials or parts for making a dangerous ordnance, absent circumstances indicating the dangerous ordnance, materials, or parts are intended for legitimate use; 2. Possession or control of any substance, device, instrument or article designed or specially adapted for criminal use; 3. Possession or control of any substance, device, instrument or article commonly used for criminal purposes, under circumstances indicating the item is intended from criminal use.

ORC:2923.241.heading: DESIGNING HIDDEN COMPARTMENT 2923.241(B) ORC
ORC:2923.241.text: _____________ did knowingly (design, build, construct, or fabricate) a vehicle with a hidden compartment, or modify or alter any portion of a vehicle in order to create or add a hidden compartment, to wit: (DESCRIBE VEHICLE AND HIDDEN COMPARTMENT) with the intent to facilitate the unlawful concealment or transportation of a controlled substance in violation of Section 2923.241(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2923.241.notes: NOTE: “Hidden compartment” means a container, space, or enclosure that conceals, hides, or otherwise prevents the discovery of the contents of the container, space, or enclosure. “Hidden compartment” includes, but is not limited to, any of the following: 1. False, altered, or modified fuel tanks; 2. Any original factory equipment on a vehicle that has been modified to conceal, hide, or prevent the discovery of the modified equipment’s contents; 3. Any compartment, space, box, or other closed container that is added or attached to existing compartments, spaces, boxes, or closed containers integrated or attached to a vehicle. NOTE: This section does not apply to the following: 1. Any law enforcement officer acting in the performance of the law enforcement officer’s duties. 2. Any licensed motor vehicle dealer or motor vehicle manufacturer that in the ordinary course of business repairs, purchases, receives in trade, leases, or sells a motor vehicle. 3. A box, safe, container, or other item added to a vehicle for the purpose of securing valuables, electronics, or firearms as long as the box, safe, container, or other item added to the vehicle does not contain a controlled substance or visible residue of a controlled substance.

ORC:2923.241.heading: DESIGNING HIDDEN COMPARTMENT 2923.241(B) ORC
ORC:2923.241.text: _____________ did knowingly (design, build, construct, or fabricate) a vehicle with a hidden compartment, or modify or alter any portion of a vehicle in order to create or add a hidden compartment, to wit: (DESCRIBE VEHICLE AND HIDDEN COMPARTMENT) with the intent to facilitate the unlawful concealment or transportation of a controlled substance, and having been previously convicted of violating Section 2923.241(B), to wit: on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT AND CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2923.241(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2923.241.heading: OPERATING A VEHICLE WITH A HIDDEN COMPARTMENT 2923.241(C) ORC
ORC:2923.241.text: _____________ did knowingly (operate, possess, or use) a vehicle with a hidden compartment, to wit: (DESCRIBE VEHICLE AND HIDDEN COMPARTMENT) with the knowledge that the hidden compartment is used or intended to be used to facilitate the unlawful concealment or transportation of a controlled substance, in violation of Section 2923.241(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2923.241.heading: OPERATING A VEHICLE WITH A HIDDEN COMPARTMENT 2923.241(C) ORC
ORC:2923.241.text: _____________ did knowingly (operate, possess, or use) a vehicle with a hidden compartment, to wit: (DESCRIBE VEHICLE AND HIDDEN COMPARTMENT) with the knowledge that the hidden compartment is used or intended to be used to facilitate the unlawful concealment or transportation of a controlled substance, and having been previously convicted of violating Section 2923.241(C) or (D), to wit: on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT AND CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2923.241(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2923.241.heading: OPERATING A VEHICLE WITH A HIDDEN COMPARTMENT 2923.241(C) ORC
ORC:2923.241.text: _____________ did knowingly (operate, possess, or use) a vehicle with a hidden compartment, to wit: (DESCRIBE VEHICLE AND HIDDEN COMPARTMENT) with the knowledge that the hidden compartment is used or intended to be used to facilitate the unlawful concealment or transportation of a controlled substance and the hidden compartment contained a controlled substance at the time of the offense, to wit: (DESCRIBE CONTROLLED SUBSTANCE), in violation of Section 2923.241(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.

ORC:2923.241.heading: OPERATING A VEHICLE WITH A HIDDEN COMPARTMENT 2923.241(D) ORC
ORC:2923.241.text: _____________ did (operate, possess, or use) a vehicle with a hidden compartment, to wit: (DESCRIBE VEHICLE AND HIDDEN COMPARTMENT) and has been convicted of or pled guilty to a violation of aggravated trafficking in drugs under Section 2925.03 of the Revised Code, to wit: on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT AND CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2923.241(D) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2923.241.heading: OPERATING A VEHICLE WITH A HIDDEN COMPARTMENT 2923.241(D) ORC
ORC:2923.241.variant: PRIOR AGGRAVATED DRUG TRAFFICKING AND PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F3
ORC:2923.241.text: _____________ did (operate, possess, or use) a vehicle with a hidden compartment, to wit: (DESCRIBE VEHICLE AND HIDDEN COMPARTMENT) and has been convicted of or pled guilty to a violation of aggravated trafficking in drugs under Section 2925.03 of the Revised Code, to wit: on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT AND CASE NUMBER), and having been previously convicted of violating Section 2923.241(C) or (D), to wit: on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT AND CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2923.241(D) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2923.241.heading: OPERATING A VEHICLE WITH A HIDDEN COMPARTMENT 2923.241(D) ORC
ORC:2923.241.variant: PRIOR AGGRAVATED DRUG TRAFFICKING AND DRUGS IN HIDDEN COMPARTMENT – F2
ORC:2923.241.text: _____________ did (operate, possess, or use) a vehicle with a hidden compartment, to wit: (DESCRIBE VEHICLE AND HIDDEN COMPARTMENT) and the hidden compartment contained a controlled substance at the time of the offense, to wit: (DESCRIBE CONTROLLED SUBSTANCE), and has been convicted of or pled guilty to a violation of aggravated trafficking in drugs under Section 2925.03 of the Revised Code, to wit: on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT AND CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2923.241(D) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.

CCC:2323.30.heading: DISCHARGING WEAPONS 2323.30(A) CCC
CCC:2323.30.text: _____________ did (discharge or cause to be discharged) a (firearm, airgun, or other instrument used to explode any cartridge or thing filled with any exploding substance or material), to wit: (DESCRIBE WEAPON), in violation of Section 2323.30(A) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
CCC:2323.30.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to the following: 1. Devices in which paper caps containing 0.25 grains or less of exploding compound are used, (providing they are so constructed that the hand cannot come in contact with the cap when in place for the explosion), and toy pistol paper caps which contain less than 0.20 grains of explosive mixture; 2. A law enforcement officer in the lawful performance of his or her duties; 3. Discharge of a weapon when acting in self-defense or defense of another, including as provided in Section 2901.05 of the Ohio Revised Code; 4. Situations in which the firearm was discharged or was on or about the person or under the control of a person in the commission of a felony for which the Revised Code requires a term of imprisonment; 5. Discharge of a firearm upon or over a public road or highway when the violation created a substantial risk of physical harm, caused harm, or caused serious physical harm to any person; or caused serious physical harm to property violation of which is to be prosecuted under relevant state law. NOTE: If the offender had a firearm or dangerous ordnance on or about the offender’s person or under the offender’s control at the time of the commission of the offense in violation of the Columbus City Code, the firearm or dangerous ordnance shall be seized and is subject to forfeiture under Chapter 2981 of the Ohio Revised Code. Refer to the complaint language cited in Chapter 2927 of the Criminal Complaint Manual.

CCC:2323.32.heading: UNLAWFUL POSSESSION OF LARGE CAPACITY MAGAZINE 2323.32(A) CCC
CCC:2323.32.text: _____________ did knowingly (possess, purchase, keep for sale, offer or expose for sale, transfer, distribute, or import) a large capacity magazine, as defined in Section 2323.11(N) of the Columbus City Code. to wit: (DESCRIBE MAGAZINE AND CAPACITY), in violation of Section 2323.32(A) of the Columbus City Code, an unclassified misdemeanor.
CCC:2323.32.notes: NOTE: This following criteria apply to this section: 1. A “large capacity magazine” is defined in Columbus City Code 2323.11(N) as any magazine, belt, drum, feed strip, clip or other similar device that has the capacity of, or can be readily restored or converted to accept, thirty (30) or more rounds of ammunition for use in a firearm. 2. A “large capacity magazine” does not include any of the following: a. A feeding device that has been permanently altered so that it cannot accommodate thirty or more rounds of ammunition. b. A .22 caliber tube ammunition feeding device. c. A tubular magazine that is contained in a lever-action firearm. d. A magazine that is permanently inoperable. 3. This section does not apply to the following: a. An officer, agent, or employee of Ohio or any state, a political subdivision of Ohio or any other state, or the United States; members of the armed forces of the U.S or the organized militia of Ohio or any other state; and law enforcement officers to the extent that the officer, agent, employee, or member is authorized to possess, purchase, keep for sale, offer or expose for sale, transfer, distribute, or import large capacity magazines and is acting within the scope of the officer’s, agent’s, employee’s, or member’s duties. b. Any person who is employed in Ohio, who is authorized to carry concealed weapons or dangerous ordnance or is authorized to carry handguns, and who is subject to and in compliance with the requirements of Section 109.801 of the Ohio Revised Code, and is acting within the scope of the employee’s duties, unless the appointing authority of the person has expressly specified that the exemption provided in Section 2323.32(B)(1)(b) of the Columbus City Code does not apply to the person. c. The large capacity magazine belongs to a firearm or which is possessed by an owner of a firearm which is registered with federal authorities under the National Firearms Act (26 U.S.C. Secs. 5801-5871). d. A large capacity magazine that has been rendered totally inoperable or inert and the firearm cannot readily be rendered operable or activated and which is kept as a trophy, souvenir, curio, or museum piece. e. Importers, manufacturers, and dealers of large capacity magazines that are federally licensed. f. Carriers, warehouses, and others engaged in the business of transporting or storing firearms for hire, with respect to large capacity magazines lawfully transported or stored in the usual course of business and in compliance with Ohio laws and applicable federal law. 4. The person is immune from prosecution under this section as follows: a. If the person lawfully acquired or possessed a large capacity magazine prior to December 5, 2022, the person is immune from prosecution in accordance with Section 2323.23(E) of the Columbus City Code prior to July 1, 2023, provided the person does one of the following prior to July 1, 2023: (1) Remove the large-capacity magazine from the City limits; or (2) Sell the large-capacity magazine to a licensed firearms dealer located outside of the City limits; or (3) Surrender the large capacity magazine for destruction by reporting the possession of the large capacity magazine to the Columbus Division of Police, describing the large capacity magazine in the person’s possession and where the person may be found, and voluntarily surrendering the large capacity magazine to the Division of Police. b. If the person may not lawfully possess a large-capacity magazine as of December 5, 2022, and fails to dispose of the large capacity magazine by July 1, 2023, in accordance with Section 2323.23(E) of the Columbus City Code, the person is immune from prosecution, provided the person does the following: (1) Surrender the large capacity magazine for destruction by reporting the possession of the large capacity magazine to the Columbus Division of Police, describing the large capacity magazine in the person’s possession and where the person may be found, and voluntarily surrendering the large capacity magazine to the Division of Police. Note: A surrender is not voluntary if it occurs when the person is taken into custody or during a pursuit or attempt to take the person into custody under circumstances indicating that the surrender is made under threat of force. 5. It is an affirmative defense that the person knowingly possessed, kept for sale, transferred, distributed, or imported a large capacity magazine solely for the purpose of transporting the large capacity magazine in a motor vehicle for an otherwise lawful purpose through the municipal limits of the city. This defense only applies if the large capacity magazine is not on the actor’s person or within the passenger area of the motor vehicle. 6. If the offender had a firearm or dangerous ordnance on or about the offender’s person or under the offender’s control at the time of the commission of the offense in violation of the Columbus City Code, the firearm or dangerous ordnance shall be seized and is subject to forfeiture under Chapter 2981 of the Ohio Revised Code. Refer to the complaint language cited in Chapter 2927 of the Criminal Complaint Manual.

ORC:2923.32.heading: ENGAGING IN PATTERN OF CORRUPT ACTIVITY 2923.32(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2923.32.variant: CONDUCT AFFAIRS OF AN ENTERPRISE THROUGH PATTERN OF CORRUPT ACTIVITY – F2
ORC:2923.32.text: _____________ did, while (employed by or associated with) an enterprise, to wit: (NAME THE ENTERPRISE), (conduct or participate) (directly or indirectly) in the affairs of the enterprise through (a pattern of corrupt activity or the collection of an unlawful debt) to wit: (DESCRIBE THE PATTERN OF CORRUPT ACTIVITY OR THE COLLECTION OF DEBT) in violation of Section 2923.32(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2923.32.notes: NOTE: Engaging in a Pattern of Corrupt Activity is a felony of the first degree if at least one of the incidents of corrupt activity is a felony of the first, second, or third degree; aggravated murder or murder under Ohio law or another jurisdiction’s similar law; or if the offense is committed in furtherance of human trafficking. Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking. NOTE: See ORC 2923.32 for further information.

ORC:2923.32.heading: ENGAGING IN PATTERN OF CORRUPT ACTIVITY 2923.32(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2923.32.variant: ACQUIRE INTEREST OR CONTROL OF PROPERTY THROUGH A PATTERN OF CORRUPT ACTIVITY – F2
ORC:2923.32.text: _____________ did, through (a pattern of corrupt activity or the collection of an unlawful debt), to wit: (DESCRIBE THE PATTERN OF CORRUPT ACTIVITY OR THE COLLECTION OF DEBT) (acquire or maintain) (directly or indirectly) any (interest in or control of) an (enterprise or real property), to wit: (NAME THE ENTERPRISE OR DESCRIBE THE PROPERTY) in violation of Section 2923.32(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2923.32.notes: NOTE: Engaging in a Pattern of Corrupt Activity is a felony of the first degree if at least one of the incidents of corrupt activity is a felony of the first, second, or third degree; aggravated murder or murder under Ohio law or another jurisdiction’s similar law; or if the offense is committed in furtherance of human trafficking. Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking. NOTE: See ORC 2923.32 for further information.

ORC:2923.32.heading: ENGAGING IN PATTERN OF CORRUPT ACTIVITY 2923.32(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2923.32.variant: USE PROCEEDS OF CORRUPT ACTIVITY TO INVEST IN PROPERTY OR ENTERPRISE – F2
ORC:2923.32.text: _____________ did, having knowingly received proceeds, to wit: (STATE AMOUNT OF PROCEEDS) derived (directly or indirectly) from (a pattern of corrupt activity or the collection of an unlawful debt), to wit: (DESCRIBE THE PATTERN OF CORRUPT ACTIVITY OR THE COLLECTION OF DEBT) (used or invested) (directly or indirectly) (a part of those proceeds or any proceeds), to wit: (STATE AMOUNT) derived from the (use or investment) of those proceeds in the acquisition of any (title to or any right or interest or equity in) (real property or in the establishment or operation of an enterprise), to wit: (DESCRIBE THE PROPERTY OR ENTERPRISE) in violation of Section 2923.32(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2923.32.notes: NOTE: Engaging in a Pattern of Corrupt Activity is a felony of the first degree if at least one of the incidents of corrupt activity is a felony of the first, second, or third degree; aggravated murder or murder under Ohio law or another jurisdiction’s similar law; or if the offense is committed in furtherance of human trafficking. Add the following at the end of the complaint for HUMAN TRAFFICKING: (OFFICER’S NAME) further finds and specifies that the offender committed the offense in furtherance of human trafficking. NOTE: See ORC 2923.32 for further information. DEFINITIONS: CRIMINAL GANGS, REFER TO SECTION 2923.41 ORC

ORC:2923.42.heading: PARTICIPATING IN CRIMINAL GANG 2923.42 ORC
ORC:2923.42.text: _____________ did, being a person who actively participates in a criminal gang, with knowledge that the criminal gang engages in or has engaged in a pattern of criminal gang activity, to wit: (DESCRIBE GANG ACTIVITY), (purposely promote, further or assist any criminal conduct or purposely commit or engage in any act that constitutes criminal conduct), to wit: (DESCRIBE CRIMINAL CONDUCT AS DEFINED IN DIVISION (C) OF 2923.41 OF THE REVISED CODE), in violation of Section 2923.42 of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2923.42.notes: DEFINITIONS 2323.51 CCC BB DEVICE – Any instrument that expels a projectile, such as a BB or a pellet, through the force of air pressure, gas pressure, or spring action, including any airsoft gun and any spot marker or paintball guns unless specifically exempted under division (B). IMITATION FIREARM – Any BB device, replica of a firearm, or other device that is so substantially similar in coloration and overall appearance to an existing firearm as to lead a reasonable person to perceive that the BB device, replica of a firearm, or other device is a firearm. Does not include a nonfiring, collector replica of an antique firearm developed prior to 1898. PUBLIC PLACE – An area open to the public, including any of the following: 1. A street, alley, sidewalk, driveway, or parking lot; 2. A bridge; 3. A plaza or park; 4. A front yard; 5. A motor vehicle, as defined in Section 4511.01 ORC, whether moving or not; 6. A building open to the general public, including one that serves food or drink or that provides entertainment; 7. A doorway or entrance to a building or dwelling; 8. A school operated by a board of education or a community school established under Chapter 3314 ORC; 9. Any premises owned or leased by a public or private college, university, or other institution of higher education.

CCC:2323.52.heading: UNLAWFUL SALE OF IMITATION FIREARMS TO MINORS 2323.52(B) CCC
CCC:2323.52.variant: GIVE, SELL, OR FURNISH TO MINOR – M1
CCC:2323.52.text: _____________ did knowingly (give, sell, or otherwise furnish) an imitation firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE IMITATION FIREARM AND HOW IT WAS GIVEN, SOLD OR FURNISHED) to any person under the age of eighteen (18) years, to wit: (NAME OTHER PERSON AND STATE AGE), in violation of Section 2323.52(B) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
CCC:2323.52.notes: NOTE: Refer to the definitions cited in 2323.51 CCC. NOTE: This section does not apply to provision of an imitation firearm to a minor in conjunction with the lawful use of an imitation firearm in any theatrical production including any motion picture, video, television, or stage production; or at a certified or regulated public or private shooting range or at a paintball facility. NOTE: This section does not apply where the entire exterior surface of the device is white, bright red, bright orange, bright yellow, bright green, bright blue, bright pink, bright purple, or any other color designated by the US Department of Commerce in regulations promulgated pursuant to 15 USCA Section 5001 either singly or as the predominant color in combination with other colors in any pattern, or where the entire device is constructed of transparent or translucent materials which permits unmistakable observation of the device’s complete contents.

CCC:2323.53.heading: ALTERATION OF AN IMITATION FIREARM 2323.53(A) CCC
CCC:2323.53.text: _____________ did knowingly (change, alter, remove, or obliterate) any (coloration, markings, or bands), to wit: (DESCRIBE CHANGE/ALTERATION AND WHAT WAS ALTERED) that are required by 15 USCA Section 5001 and accompanying federal regulations for any imitation firearm in a way that makes the imitation firearm look more like a firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE EFFECT OF ALTERATION), in violation of Section 2323.53(A) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
CCC:2323.53.notes: NOTE: Refer to the definitions cited in 2323.51 CCC. NOTE: This section does not apply to a lawful use of an imitation firearm in any theatrical production, including any motion picture, video, television, or stage production.

CCC:2323.53.heading: POSSESSION OF AN ALTERED IMITATION FIREARM 2323.53(B) CCC
CCC:2323.53.text: _____________ did knowingly possess an imitation firearm on which the blaze orange tip or other approved marking as described in 15 USCA Section 5001 and accompanying federal regulations has been removed or obscured, to wit: (DESCRIBE IMITATION FIREARM, MARKING AND HOW IT WAS POSSESSED), in violation of Columbus City Code 2323.53(B), a misdemeanor of the first degree.
CCC:2323.53.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to a lawful use of an imitation firearm in any theatrical production, including any motion picture, video, television, or stage production.

CCC:2323.54.heading: ILLEGAL DISPLAY/POSSESSION OF AN IMITATION FIREARM 2323.54(A) CCC
CCC:2323.54.variant: OPEN DISPLAY IN A PUBLIC PLACE – M1
CCC:2323.54.text: _____________ did knowingly (openly display or expose) any imitation firearm in a public place, to wit: (DESCRIBE IMITATION FIREARM, PUBLIC PLACE AND HOW IT WAS DISPLAYED), in violation of Section 2323.54(A) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
CCC:2323.54.notes: NOTE: Refer to the definitions cited in 2323.51 CCC. NOTE: This section does not apply in the following circumstances: 1. The imitation firearm has a blaze orange tip or other approved marking as described in 15 USCA Section 5001 and accompanying federal regulations and the blaze orange tip or marking is not concealed. 2. The imitation firearm is displayed or exposed in the course of commerce, including a commercial film or video production, or for service, repair, or restoration of the imitation firearm. 3. The imitation firearm is used in a theatrical production, including any motion picture, video, television, or stage production. 4. The imitation firearm is used in conjunction with a certified or regulated sporting event or competition. 5. The imitation firearm is used in conjunction with lawful hunting or a lawful pest control activity. 6. The imitation firearm is used or possessed at a certified or regulated public or private shooting range or at a paintball facility. 7. The imitation firearm is used at a fair, exhibition, exposition, or other similar activity for which a permit has been obtained from the City. 8. The imitation firearm is used in a military, civil defense, or civic activity, including a flag ceremony, color guard, parade, award presentation, historical reenactment, or memorial. 9. The imitation firearm is used for a public display authorized by a school or a display that is part of a museum collection. 10. The imitation firearm is used in a parade, ceremony, or other similar activity for which a permit has been obtained from the City. 11. The imitation firearm is displayed on a wall plaque or in a presentation case. 12. The imitation firearm is being used in an area where the discharge of a firearm is lawful or in conjunction with law enforcement training.

CCC:2323.54.heading: ILLEGAL DISPLAY/POSSESSION OF AN IMITATION FIREARM 2323.54(B) CCC
CCC:2323.54.variant: POSSESSION IN A SCHOOL SAFETY ZONE – M1
CCC:2323.54.text: ____________ did knowingly possess an imitation firearm, to wit: (DESCRIBE IMITATION FIREARM) in a school safety zone, to wit: (DESCRIBE SCHOOL SAFETY ZONE) if the person (indicates that the person possesses the object and that it is a firearm, or the person knowingly displays or brandishes the object and indicates that it is a firearm), to wit: (DESCRIBE HOW PERSON POSSESSED OR DISPLAYED OBJECT AND WHAT INDICATIONS WERE MADE), in violation of Section 2323.54(B) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
CCC:2323.54.notes: NOTE: Refer to the definitions cited in 2323.51 CCC. NOTE: This section does not apply in the following circumstances. 1. Premises upon which home schooling is conducted. 2. A school administrator, teacher, or employee who possesses an imitation firearm for legitimate school purposes during the course of employment. 3. A student who uses an imitation firearm under the direction of a school administrator, teacher, or employee. 4. Any other person who, with the express prior approval of a school administrator, possesses an imitation firearm for a legitimate purpose, including the use of the object in a ceremonial activity, a play, reenactment, or other dramatic presentation, school safety training, or a ROTC activity or another similar use of the object. NOTE: If the offender previously has been convicted of a violation of division (B) of this section, illegal possession of an imitation firearm in a school safety zone is a felony to be prosecuted under state law.

ORC:2925.03.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to: 1) Manufacturers, licensed health professionals authorized to prescribe drugs, pharmacists, owners of pharmacies and other persons whose conduct is in accordance with Ohio law; 2) Any person who is conducting or participating in a research project involving the use of an anabolic steroid, if the offense involves an anabolic steroid and if the project has been approved by the United States food and drug administration; or, 3) Any person who sells, offers for sale, prescribes, dispenses, or administers for livestock or other nonhuman species an anabolic steroid that is expressly intended for administration through implants to livestock or other nonhuman species and approved for that purpose under the “Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act,” 52 Stat. 1040 (1938), 21 U.S.C.A. 301, as amended, and is sold, offered for sale, prescribed, dispensed, or administered for that purpose in accordance with that act. ORC:2925.03.heading: AGGRAVATED TRAFFICKING IN DRUGS 2925.03(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2925.03.variant: TRAFFICKING IN FENTANYL-RELATED COMPOUND – SELL OR OFFER TO SELL
ORC:2925.03.text: _____________ did knowingly (sell or offer to sell) a controlled substance included in Schedule II, to wit: (A COMPOUND, MIXTURE, PREPARATION, OR SUBSTANCE CONTAINING A FENTANYL-RELATED COMPOUND, AND TERMS OF SALE) in an amount, to wit: (STATE AMOUNT OF SUBSTANCE), in violation of Section 2925.03(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, THE CHARGE IS AS FOLLOWS:
ORC:2925.03.notes: – An amount less than 10 unit doses or 1 gram, a felony of the fifth degree. – An amount less than 10 unit doses or 1 gram, and the offense was committed in the vicinity of a school, juvenile, or substance addiction services provider or recovering addict, a felony of the fourth degree. – An amount equal to or exceeding 10 unit doses but is less than 50 unit doses, or is equal to or exceeding 1 gram but less than 5 grams, a felony of the fourth degree. – An amount equal to or exceeding 10 unit doses but is less than 50 unit doses, or is equal to or exceeding 1 gram but less than 5 grams, and the offense was committed in the vicinity of a school, juvenile, or substance addiction services provider or recovering addict, a felony of the third degree. – An amount equal to or exceeding 50 unit doses but is less than 100 unit doses or is equal to or exceeding 5 grams but less than 10 grams, a felony of the third degree. – An amount equal to or exceeding 50 unit doses but less than 100 unit doses or is equal to or exceeding 5 grams but less than 10 grams, and the offense was committed in the vicinity of a school, juvenile, or substance addiction services provider or recovering addict, a felony of the second degree. – An amount equal to or exceeding 100 unit doses but is less than 200 unit doses or is equal to or exceeding 10 grams but less than 20 grams, a felony of the second degree. – An amount equal to or exceeding 100 unit doses but is less than 200 unit doses or is equal to or exceeding 10 grams but less than 20 grams, and the offense was committed within the vicinity of a school, juvenile, or substance addiction services provider or recovering addict, a felony of the first degree. – An amount equal to or exceeding 200 unit doses or is equal to or exceeding 20 grams, a felony of the first degree. NOTE: This section does not apply to manufacturers, licensed health professionals authorized to prescribe drugs, pharmacists, owners of pharmacies and other persons whose conduct is in accordance with Ohio law. NOTE: As used in this section, “drug” includes any substances that is represented to be a drug. NOTE: See Section 2925.01(LL) for definition of fentanyl-related compound. NOTE: If the drug involved in the violation is a compound, mixture, preparation or substance that is a COMBINATION of a fentanyl-related compound AND marihuana, the offender shall be charged for trafficking in marihuana. NOTE: If the offender knows or has reason to know that the compound, mixture, preparation, or substance that is the drug involved contains a fentanyl-related compound, the offender shall be charged for trafficking in a fentanyl-related compound. NOTE: See the criteria and definitions listed in Sections 2925.01(QQ), 2925.01(RR), and 2925.01(SS) of the Ohio Revised Code to determine whether the violation was “committed in the vicinity of a substance addiction services provider or a recovering addict.”

ORC:2925.03.heading: AGGRAVATED TRAFFICKING IN DRUGS 2925.03(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2925.03.variant: PREPARE FOR SHIPMENT/TRANSFER FOR RESALE – FENTANYL-RELATED COMPOUND
ORC:2925.03.text: _____________ did knowingly, prepare for shipment, ship, transport, deliver, prepare for distribution or distribute a controlled substance included in Schedule II, to wit: (A COMPOUND, MIXTURE, PREPARATION, OR SUBSTANCE CONTAINING A FENTANYL-RELATED COMPOUND, AND TERMS OF SALE) in an amount, to wit: (STATE AMOUNT OF SUBSTANCE), when the offender knew or had reasonable cause to believe that the controlled substance was intended for sale or resale by the offender or another person, in violation of Section 2925.03(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, THE CHARGE IS AS FOLLOWS:
ORC:2925.03.notes: – An amount less than 10 unit doses or 1 gram, a felony of the fifth degree. – An amount equal to or exceeding 10 unit doses but is less than 50 unit doses, or is equal to or exceeding 1 gram but less than 5 grams, a felony of the fourth degree. – An amount equal to or exceeding 50 unit doses but is less than 100 unit doses or is equal to or exceeding 5 grams but less than 10 grams, a felony of the third degree. – An amount equal to or exceeding 100 unit doses but is less than 200 unit doses or is equal to or exceeding 10 grams but less than 20 grams, a felony of the second degree. – An amount equal to or exceeding 200 unit doses or is equal to or exceeding 20 grams, a felony of the first degree. NOTE: See Section 2925.01(LL) for definition of fentanyl-related compound. NOTE: If the drug involved in the violation is a compound, mixture, preparation or substance that is a COMBINATION of a fentanyl-related compound AND marihuana, the offender shall be charged for trafficking in marihuana. NOTE: If the offender knows or has reason to know that the compound, mixture, preparation, or substance that is the drug involved contains a fentanyl-related compound, the offender shall be charged for trafficking in a fentanyl-related compound.

ORC:2925.03.heading: TRAFFICKING IN HASHISH 2925.03(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2925.03.variant: PREPARE FOR SHIPMENT/DISTRIBUTION – LIQUID FORM
ORC:2925.03.text: _____________ did knowingly, prepare for shipment, ship, transport, deliver, prepare for distribution or distribute a controlled substance included in Schedule I, to wit: (HASHISH OR A COMPOUND, MIXTURE, PREPARATION OR SUBSTANCE CONTAINING HASHISH AND NAME THE TERMS OF SALE) in an amount, to wit: (STATE AMOUNT OF SUBSTANCE), when the offender knew or had reasonable cause to believe that the controlled substance was intended for sale or resale by the offender or another person, in violation of Section 2925.03(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, THE CHARGE IS AS FOLLOWS:
ORC:2925.03.notes: – An amount less than 2 grams in liquid form, a felony of the fifth degree. – An amount equal to or exceeding 2 grams but less than 10 grams in liquid form, a felony of the fourth degree. – An amount equal to or exceeding 10 grams but less than 50 grams in liquid form, a felony of the third degree. – An amount equal to or exceeding 50 grams but less than 200 grams in liquid form, a felony of the third degree. – An amount equal to or exceeding 200 grams in liquid form, a felony of the second degree. NOTE: This section does not apply to manufacturers, licensed health professionals authorized to prescribe drugs, pharmacists, owners of pharmacies and other persons whose conduct is in accordance with Ohio law. NOTE: As used in this section, “drug” includes any substances that is represented to be a drug.

ORC:2925.03.heading: TRAFFICKING IN HASHISH 2925.03(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2925.03.variant: PREPARE FOR SHIPMENT/DISTRIBUTION – LIQUID FORM – WITHIN THE VICINITY OF A SCHOOL OR A JUVENILE
ORC:2925.03.text: _____________ did knowingly, prepare for shipment, ship, transport, deliver, prepare for distribution or distribute a controlled substance included in Schedule I, to wit: (HASHISH OR A COMPOUND, MIXTURE, PREPARATION OR SUBSTANCE CONTAINING HASHISH AND NAME THE TERMS OF SALE) in an amount, to wit: (STATE AMOUNT OF SUBSTANCE), when the offender knew or had reasonable cause to believe that the controlled substance was intended for sale or resale by the offender or another person, within the vicinity of a (school or juvenile), to wit: (STATE NAME AND LOCATION OF SCHOOL OR NAME OF JUVENILE), in violation of Section 2925.03(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, THE CHARGE IS AS FOLLOWS:
ORC:2925.03.notes: – An amount less than 2 grams in liquid form, a felony of the fourth degree. – An amount equal to or exceeding 2 grams but less than 10 grams in liquid form, a felony of the third degree. – An amount equal to or exceeding 10 grams but less than 50 grams in liquid form, a felony of the second degree. – An amount equal to or exceeding 50 grams but less than 200 grams in solid form, a felony of the second degree. – An amount equal to or exceeding 200 grams in liquid form, a felony of the first degree. NOTE: This section does not apply to manufacturers, licensed health professionals authorized to prescribe drugs, pharmacists, owners of pharmacies and other persons whose conduct is in accordance with Ohio law. NOTE: As used in this section, “drug” includes any substances that is represented to be a drug.

ORC:2925.03.heading: TRAFFICKING IN CONTROLLED SUBSTANCE ANALOG 2925.03(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2925.03.variant: PREPARE FOR SHIPMENT/DISTRIBUTION – CONTROLLED SUBSTANCE ANALOG – WITHIN THE VICINITY OF A SCHOOL OR A JUVENILE – F4
ORC:2925.03.text: _____________ did knowingly, prepare for shipment, ship, transport, deliver, prepare for distribution or distribute a controlled substance analog, to wit: (NAME SUBSTANCE AND TERMS OF SALE) when the offender knew or had reasonable cause to believe that the controlled substance analog was intended for sale or resale by the offender or another person, within the vicinity of a (school or juvenile), to wit: (STATE NAME AND LOCATION OF SCHOOL OR NAME OF JUVENILE) in violation of Section 2925.03(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2925.04.heading: ILLEGAL MANUFACTURE OF DRUGS 2925.04(A) ORC

ORC:2925.04.heading: ILLEGAL CULTIVATION OF MARIHUANA 2925.04(A) ORC
ORC:2925.04.variant: AMOUNT EXCEEDING 100 GRAMS BUT LESS THAN 200 GRAMS – M4
ORC:2925.04.text: _____________ did knowingly cultivate Marihuana, to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT), in an amount or exceeding 100 grams but less than 200 grams, to wit: (STATE AMOUNT), in violation of Section 2925.04(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

ORC:2925.04.heading: ILLEGAL CULTIVATION OF MARIHUANA 2925.04(A) ORC
ORC:2925.04.variant: AMOUNT EXCEEDING 100 GRAMS BUT LESS THAN 200 GRAMS – VICINITY OF JUVENILE OR SCHOOL – M3

ORC:2925.04.heading: ILLEGAL CULTIVATION OF MARIHUANA 2925.04(A) ORC
ORC:2925.04.variant: AMOUNT EQUAL TO OR EXCEEDING 200 GRAMS BUT LESS THAN 1,000 GRAMS – F5

ORC:2925.04.heading: ILLEGAL CULTIVATION OF MARIHUANA 2925.04(A) ORC

ORC:2925.04.heading: ILLEGAL CULTIVATION OF MARIHUANA 2925.04(A) ORC
ORC:2925.04.variant: AMOUNT EQUAL TO OR EXCEEDING 1,000 GRAMS BUT LESS THAN 5,000 GRAMS – VICINITY OF JUVENILE OR SCHOOL – F2

ORC:2925.04.heading: ILLEGAL CULTIVATION OF MARIHUANA 2925.04(A) ORC

ORC:2925.041.heading: ILLEGAL ASSEMBLY OR POSSESSION OF CHEMICALS FOR THE MANUFACTURE OF DRUGS 2925.041(A) ORC

ORC:2925.041.heading: ILLEGAL ASSEMBLY OR POSSESSION OF CHEMICALS FOR THE MANUFACTURE OF DRUGS 2925.041(A) ORC

ORC:2925.05.heading: AGGRAVATED FUNDING OF DRUG TRAFFICKING 2925.05(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2925.05.variant: PROVIDING MONEY TO ANOTHER PERSON TO SELL – EQUAL TO OR EXCEEDING BULK AMOUNT – F1
ORC:2925.05.text: _____________ did knowingly provide money or other items of value to another person, to wit: (STATE WHAT WAS PROVIDED AND NAME OF PERSON), with the purpose that the recipient of the (money or items of value) use them to obtain any controlled substance for the purpose of (violating Section 2925.04 of the Ohio Revised Code or of selling or offering to sell the controlled substance) being any compound, mixture, preparation or substance included in Schedule I or II*, equal to or exceeding bulk amount, to wit: (NAME DRUG AND AMOUNT), in violation of Section 2925.05(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the first degree.
ORC:2925.05.notes: NOTE: See Section 2925.05(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code – *with the exception of marihuana, cocaine, LSD, heroin, any fentanyl-related compound, and hashish, or Schedule III, IV, or V.

ORC:2925.05.heading: FUNDING OF DRUG TRAFFICKING 2925.05(A)(1) ORC

ORC:2925.05.heading: AGGRAVATED FUNDING OF DRUG TRAFFICKING 2925.05(A)(3) ORC

ORC:2925.05.heading: AGGRAVATED FUNDING OF DRUG TRAFFICKING 2925.05(A)(5) ORC

ORC:2925.05.heading: AGGRAVATED FUNDING OF DRUG TRAFFICKING 2925.05(A)(6) ORC

ORC:2925.06.heading: ILLEGAL ADMINISTRATION/DISTRIBUTION OF ANABOLIC STEROIDS 2925.06(A) ORC
ORC:2925.06.variant: ADMINISTRATION TO A HUMAN BEING – F4
ORC:2925.06.text: _____________ did knowingly administer to a human being, to wit: (NAME PERSON) an anabolic steroid, to wit: (NAME SUBSTANCE) not approved by the United States food and drug administration for such administering, in violation of Section 2925.06(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2925.06.heading: ILLEGAL ADMINISTRATION/DISTRIBUTION OF ANABOLIC STEROIDS 2925.06(A) ORC
