ORC:2925.09.heading: SALE OR USE OF DRUGS NOT APPROVED BY FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION 2925.09(A) ORC
ORC:2925.09.text: _____________ did (administer or dispense or distribute or manufacture or possess or sell or use) a drug, other than a controlled substance, to wit: (NAME DRUG), that is not approved by the United States (food and drug administration or department of agriculture), and no application has been approved for the investigation of said drug, and said drug was not combined by a licensed health professional or pharmacist to make a single product for medical purposes, in violation of Section 2925.09(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2925.09.notes: NOTE: Subsequent violations of this Section constitute a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2925.09.heading: SALE OR USE OF DRUGS NOT APPROVED BY FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION 2925.09(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2925.09.text: _____________ did (administer or dispense or distribute or manufacture or possess or sell or use) any dangerous drug to or for livestock or any animal that is generally used for food or in the production of food, to wit: (NAME DRUG), in violation of Section 2925.09(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2925.09.notes: NOTE: Subsequent violations of this Section constitute a felony of the fourth degree. NOTE: This is not an offense if the drug is prescribed by a licensed veterinarian by prescription or other written order and the drug is used in accordance with the veterinarian’s order or direction. NOTE: This section does not apply to a licensed manufacturer of dangerous drugs, outsourcing facility, third-party logistics provider, repackager of dangerous drugs, wholesale distributor of dangerous drugs, or terminal distributor of dangerous drugs or to a person who possesses, possesses for sale, or sells, at retail, a drug in accordance with Ohio law.

ORC:2925.12.heading: POSSESSING DRUG ABUSE INSTRUMENTS 2925.12 ORC
ORC:2925.12.text: _____________ did knowingly (make or obtain or possess or use) (an instrument or an article or a thing), to wit: (DESCRIBE INSTRUMENT, ARTICLE OR THING), of which its customary and primary purpose is for the administration of or use of a dangerous drug, to wit: (IDENTIFY DRUG AND DESCRIBE ADMINISTRATION OR USE) when the instrument involved is a hypodermic or syringe, whether or not of crude or extemporized manufacture or assembly and the (instrument or article or thing) involved has been used by the offender, to wit: (STATE NAME), (to unlawfully administer or use a dangerous drug or prepare a dangerous drug or for unlawful administration or for unlawful use), to wit: (DESCRIBE ADMINISTRATION OR USE INCLUDING EVIDENCE), in violation of Section 2925.12 of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.
ORC:2925.12.notes: NOTE: By definition, Marihuana may not be the dangerous drug in this section. NOTE: This section does not apply to manufacturers, licensed health professionals authorized to prescribe drugs, pharmacists, owners of pharmacies, and other persons whose conduct is in accordance with Ohio law. NOTE: Pursuant Section 2925.11(B)(2), this section does not apply when a person seeks or obtains medical assistance for another person who is experiencing a drug overdose, a person experiences a drug overdose and seeks medical assistance for that overdose, or a person is the subject of another person seeking or obtaining medical assistance for that overdose. No person shall be granted immunity under Section 2925.11(B)(2)(b) more than two times.

ORC:2925.12.notes: NOTE: By definition, Marihuana may not be the dangerous drug in this section. NOTE: This section does not apply to manufacturers, licensed health professionals authorized to prescribe drugs, pharmacists, owners of pharmacies, and other persons whose conduct is in accordance with Ohio law. NOTE: Pursuant Section 2925.11(B)(2), this section does not apply when a person seeks or obtains medical assistance for another person who is experiencing a drug overdose, a person experiences a drug overdose and seeks medical assistance for that overdose, or a person is the subject of another person seeking or obtaining medical assistance for that overdose. No person shall be granted immunity under Section 2925.11(B)(2)(b) more than two times.

ORC:3719.172.text: _____________ did, being a manufacturer, distributor, or dealer in hypodermics or medication packaged in hypodermics, or their authorized agents or employees or terminal distributor of dangerous drugs, to wit: (STATE POSITION), display any hypodermic for sale, to wit: (NAME HYPODERMIC FOR SALE), in violation of Section 3719.172(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the third degree.

ORC:3719.172.heading: POSSESSION, SALE, AND DISPOSAL OF HYPODERMICS 3719.172(B) ORC
ORC:3719.172.text: _____________ did, being a manufacturer, distributor, or dealer in hypodermics or medication packaged in hypodermics, or their authorized agents or employees or terminal distributor of dangerous drugs, to wit: (STATE POSITION), display any hypodermic for sale, to wit: (NAME HYPODERMIC FOR SALE), and having previously been convicted of this offense, to wit: (OFFENSE, COURT AND DATE OF CONVICTION), in violation of Section 3719.172(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:3719.172.heading: POSSESSION, SALE, AND DISPOSAL OF HYPODERMICS 3719.172(C) ORC
ORC:3719.172.text: _____________ did, not being a manufacturer, distributor, dealer in hypodermics or medication packaged in hypodermics, or their authorized agents or employees or terminal distributor of dangerous drugs, person under the direct supervision of a pharmacist or licensed health professional authorized to prescribe drugs, to wit: (STATE POSITION), sell or furnish a hypodermic to another, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON AND NAME HYPODERMIC SOLD OR FURNISHED), in violation of Section 3719.172(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:3719.172.heading: POSSESSION, SALE, AND DISPOSAL OF HYPODERMICS 3719.172(C) ORC
ORC:3719.172.text: _____________ did, not being a manufacturer, distributor, dealer in hypodermics or medication packaged in hypodermics, or their authorized agents or employees or terminal distributor of dangerous drugs, person under the direct supervision of a pharmacist or licensed health professional authorized to prescribe drugs, to wit: (STATE POSITION), sell or furnish a hypodermic to another, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON AND NAME HYPODERMIC SOLD OR FURNISHED), and having previously been convicted of this offense, to wit: (OFFENSE, COURT AND DATE OF CONVICTION), in violation of Section 3719.172(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:3719.172.heading: POSSESSION, SALE, AND DISPOSAL OF HYPODERMICS 3719.172(D) ORC
ORC:3719.172.text: _____________ did, sell or furnish a hypodermic to another, to wit: (NAME OTHER PERSON) whom he or she knows or has reasonable cause to believe is not authorized by this section to possess a hypodermic, to wit: (NAME HYPODERMIC SOLD OR FURNISHED), in violation of Section 3719.172(D) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2925.13.heading: PERMITTING DRUG ABUSE 2925.13(A) ORC
ORC:2925.13.variant: VEHICLE USED TO COMMIT FELONY DRUG OFFENSE
ORC:2925.13.text: _____________ did, being the (owner or operator or person in charge) of a (locomotive or watercraft or aircraft or vehicle), to wit: (DESCRIBE THE VEHICLE), knowingly permit said vehicle to be used for the commission of a felony drug abuse offense, to wit: (STATE NAME AND SECTION NUMBER OF OFFENSE), in violation of Section 2925.13(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2925.13.notes: NOTE: If the drug offense in question involves corrupting another with drugs, in violation of Section 2925.02 or the sale of a controlled substance, in violation of Section 2925.03, or the illegal manufacture of drugs or cultivation of marihuana, in violation of Section 2925.04, this offense is a felony of the fifth degree. NOTE: This offense is a felony of the fifth degree if the drug abuse offense in question involves the illegal assembly or possession of chemicals for the manufacture of drugs, in violation of Section 2925.041, and the offender had actual knowledge, at the time the offender permitted the vehicle, premises, or real estate to be used as described in division (A) or (B) of this section, that the person who assembled or possessed the chemicals in question had assembled or possessed them with the intent to manufacture a controlled substance in Schedule I or II in violation of Section 2925.04. NOTE: See Section 4501.01 (A) for definition of vehicle involved in this offense.

ORC:2925.13.heading: PERMITTING DRUG ABUSE 2925.13(B) ORC
ORC:2925.13.variant: PREMISES USED TO COMMIT FELONY DRUG OFFENSE
ORC:2925.13.text: _____________ did, being the (owner or lessee or occupant or person having custody or person having control or person having supervision) of (premises or real estate {including vacant land}), to wit: (DESCRIBE LOCATION), knowingly permit said (premises or real estate {including vacant land}), to be used for the commission of a felony drug abuse offense, to wit: (STATE NAME AND SECTION NUMBER OF OFFENSE), by another person, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON), in violation of Section 2925.13(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree (See note)
ORC:2925.13.notes: NOTE: If the drug offense in question involves corrupting another with drugs, in violation of Section 2925.02 of the Ohio Revised Code or the sale of a controlled substance, in violation of Section 2925.03 of the Ohio Revised Code, this offense is a felony of the fifth degree. NOTE: This section does not apply to manufacturers, licensed health professionals authorized to prescribe drugs, pharmacists, owners of pharmacies, and other persons whose conduct is in accordance with Ohio law.

ORC:2925.14.heading: ILLEGAL USE OR POSSESSION OF DRUG PARAPHERNALIA 2925.14(C) (1) ORC
ORC:2925.14.variant: USE OR POSSESS TO USE – M4
ORC:2925.14.text: _____________ did knowingly (use or possess with purpose to use) drug paraphernalia, to wit: (DESCRIBE SPECIFIC PARAPHERNALIA), in violation of Section 2925.14(C)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2925.14.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to manufacturers, licensed health professionals authorized to prescribe drugs, pharmacists, owners of pharmacies, and other persons whose conduct is in accordance with Ohio law. NOTE: This section does not apply to the possession or use of a hypodermic as authorized by Section 3719.172 of the Revised Code. NOTE: This section does not apply to a person’s use or possession of any drug paraphernalia used with marihuana. NOTE: This section does not apply to a person’s use, or possession with purpose to use, any drug testing strips to determine the presence of fentanyl or a fentanyl-related compound. NOTE: Pursuant Section 2925.11(B)(2), this section does not apply when a person seeks or obtains medical assistance for another person who is experiencing a drug overdose, a person experiences a drug overdose and seeks medical assistance for that overdose, or a person is the subject of another person seeking or obtaining medical assistance for that overdose. No person shall be granted immunity under Section 2925.11(B)(2)(b) more than two times.

ORC:2925.14.heading: DEALING IN DRUG PARAPHERNALIA 2925.14(C)(2) ORC
ORC:2925.14.variant: SELL OR POSSESS FOR SALE – M2
ORC:2925.14.text: _____________ did knowingly (sell or possess with purpose to sell or manufacture with purpose to sell) drug paraphernalia, to wit: (DESCRIBE SPECIFIC PARAPHERNALIA), when (he or she) knew or reasonably should have known the equipment, product, or material would be used as drug paraphernalia, in violation of Section 2925.14(C)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.
ORC:2925.14.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to manufacturers, licensed health professionals authorized to prescribe drugs, pharmacists, owners of pharmacies, and other persons whose conduct is in accordance with Ohio law. NOTE: This section does not apply to the possession or use of a hypodermic as authorized by Section 3719.172 of the Revised Code.

ORC:2925.14.heading: SELLING DRUG PARAPHERNALIA TO JUVENILES 2925.14(C)(2) ORC
ORC:2925.14.variant: SELL OR POSSESS FOR SALE TO A JUVENILE – M1
ORC:2925.14.text: _____________ did knowingly (sell or possess with purpose to sell or manufacturer with purpose to sell) drug paraphernalia, to wit: (DESCRIBE SPECIFIC PARAPHERNALIA), to a juvenile, in violation of Section 2925.14(C)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2925.14.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to manufacturers, licensed health professionals authorized to prescribe drugs, pharmacists, owners of pharmacies, and other persons whose conduct is in accordance with Ohio law. NOTE: This section does not apply to the possession or use of a hypodermic as authorized by Section 3719.172 of the Revised Code.

ORC:2925.14.heading: ILLEGAL ADVERTISING OF DRUG PARAPHERNALIA 2925.14(C)(3) ORC
ORC:2925.14.variant: SELL OR POSSESS FOR SALE – M2
ORC:2925.14.text: _____________ did, place an advertisement in a (newspaper or magazine or handbill or other publication), to wit: (NAME PUBLICATION) that is published and printed and circulates primarily within this state, knowing the purpose of the advertisement is to promote the illegal sale in this state of the (equipment or product or material) that the offender (intended or designed for use) as drug paraphernalia, to wit: (DESCRIBE SPECIFIC PARAPHERNALIA), in violation of Section 2925.14(C)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.
ORC:2925.14.notes: NOTE: The definition, exceptions and relevant factors for determining whether or not an item may be drug paraphernalia should be reviewed before citing this section. [See: 2925.14(A),(B) & (D)]. NOTE: This section does not apply to manufacturers, licensed health professionals authorized to prescribe drugs, pharmacists, owners of pharmacies, and other persons whose conduct is in accordance with Ohio law. NOTE: This section does not apply to the possession or use of a hypodermic as authorized by Section 3719.172 of the Revised Code.

ORC:2925.22.heading: DECEPTION TO OBTAIN A DANGEROUS DRUG 2925.22(A) ORC
ORC:2925.22.text: _____________ did, by deception, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE DECEPTION), procure (the administration of or a prescription for or the dispensing of or possess an uncompleted preprinted prescription blank used for writing a prescription for) a dangerous drug, to wit: (NAME DRUG), in violation of Section 2925.22(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2925.22.notes: NOTE: Deception defined in Section 2913.01 of the Ohio Revised Code.

ORC:2925.22.heading: DECEPTION TO OBTAIN A DANGEROUS DRUG 2925.22(A) ORC
ORC:2925.22.text: _____________ did, by deception, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE DECEPTION), procure (the administration of or a prescription for or the dispensing of or possess an uncompleted preprinted prescription blank used for writing a prescription for) a dangerous drug, to wit: (NAME DRUG), and having been previously convicted of a drug abuse offense, to wit: (ORC SECTION), on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT) (CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2925.22(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2925.22.notes: NOTE: Deception defined in Section 2913.01 of the Ohio Revised Code.

ORC:2925.22.heading: DECEPTION TO OBTAIN A DANGEROUS DRUG 2925.22(A) ORC
ORC:2925.22.variant: SCHEDULE I OR II DRUG – EXCEPT MARIHUANA – LESS THAN BULK AMOUNT – F4
ORC:2925.22.text: _____________ did, by deception, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE DECEPTION), procure (the administration of or a prescription for or the dispensing of or possess an uncompleted preprinted prescription blank used for writing a prescription for) a dangerous drug, and said dangerous drug being included in Schedule I or II, to wit: (NAME DRUG), in an amount less than the bulk amount, to wit: (STATE AMOUNT), in violation of Section 2925.22(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2925.22.notes: NOTE: Deception defined in Section 2913.01 of the Ohio Revised Code.

ORC:2925.22.heading: DECEPTION TO OBTAIN A DANGEROUS DRUG 2925.22(A) ORC
ORC:2925.22.variant: SCHEDULE I OR II DRUG – EXCEPT MARIHUANA – EQUAL TO OR EXCEEDING BULK AMOUNT BUT LESS THAN FIVE TIMES BULK – F3
ORC:2925.22.text: _____________ did, by deception, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE DECEPTION), procure (the administration of or a prescription for or the dispensing of or possess an uncompleted preprinted prescription blank used for writing a prescription for) a dangerous drug, and said dangerous drug being included in Schedule I or II, to wit: (NAME DRUG), in an amount equal to or exceeding the bulk amount but less than five times the bulk amount, to wit: (STATE AMOUNT), in violation of Section 2925.22(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2925.22.notes: NOTE: Deception defined in Section 2913.01 of the Ohio Revised Code.

ORC:2925.22.heading: DECEPTION TO OBTAIN A DANGEROUS DRUG 2925.22(A) ORC
ORC:2925.22.variant: SCHEDULE I OR II DRUG – EXCEPT MARIHUANA – EQUAL TO OR EXCEEDING 5 TIMES BULK AMOUNT BUT LESS THAN 50 TIMES BULK – F2
ORC:2925.22.text: _____________ did, by deception, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE DECEPTION), procure (the administration of or a prescription for or the dispensing of or possess an uncompleted preprinted prescription blank used for writing a prescription for) a dangerous drug, and said dangerous drug being included in Schedule I or II, to wit: (NAME DRUG), in an amount equal to or exceeding 5 times the bulk amount but less than 50 times the bulk amount, to wit: (STATE AMOUNT), in violation of Section 2925.22(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2925.22.notes: NOTE: Deception defined in Section 2913.01 of the Ohio Revised Code.

ORC:2925.22.heading: DECEPTION TO OBTAIN A DANGEROUS DRUG 2925.22(A) ORC
ORC:2925.22.variant: SCHEDULE I OR II DRUG – EXCEPT MARIHUANA – EQUAL TO OR EXCEEDING 50 TIMES BULK AMOUNT – F1
ORC:2925.22.text: _____________ did, by deception, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE DECEPTION), procure (the administration of or a prescription for or the dispensing of or possess an uncompleted preprinted prescription blank used for writing a prescription for) a dangerous drug, and said dangerous drug being included in Schedule I or II, to wit: (NAME DRUG), in an amount equal to or exceeding 50 times the bulk amount, to wit: (STATE AMOUNT), in violation of Section 2925.22(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the first degree.
ORC:2925.22.notes: NOTE: Deception defined in Section 2913.01 of the Ohio Revised Code.

ORC:2925.22.heading: DECEPTION TO OBTAIN A DANGEROUS DRUG 2925.22(A) ORC
ORC:2925.22.variant: SCHEDULE III, IV OR V DRUG – INCLUDING MARIHUANA – LESS THAN BULK AMOUNT – F5
ORC:2925.22.text: _____________ did, by deception, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE DECEPTION), procure (the administration of or a prescription for or the dispensing of or possess an uncompleted preprinted prescription blank used for writing a prescription for) a dangerous drug, and said dangerous drug (being included in Schedule III, IV, V, to wit: (NAME DRUG) or being marihuana), in an amount less than the bulk amount, to wit: (STATE AMOUNT), in violation of Section 2925.22(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2925.22.notes: NOTE: Deception defined in Section 2913.01 of the Ohio Revised Code.

ORC:2925.22.heading: DECEPTION TO OBTAIN A DANGEROUS DRUG 2925.22(A) ORC
ORC:2925.22.variant: SCHEDULE III, IV OR V DRUG – INCLUDING MARIHUANA – EQUAL TO OR EXCEEDING BULK AMOUNT BUT LESS THAN FIVE TIMES BULK – F4
ORC:2925.22.text: _____________ did, by deception, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE DECEPTION), procure (the administration of or a prescription for or the dispensing of or possess an uncompleted preprinted prescription blank used for writing a prescription for) a dangerous drug, and said dangerous drug (being included in Schedule III, IV, V, to wit: (NAME DRUG) or being marihuana), in an amount equal to or exceeding the bulk amount but less than five times the bulk amount, to wit: (STATE AMOUNT), in violation of Section 2925.22(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2925.22.notes: NOTE: Deception defined in Section 2913.01 of the Ohio Revised Code.

ORC:2925.22.heading: DECEPTION TO OBTAIN A DANGEROUS DRUG 2925.22(A) ORC
ORC:2925.22.variant: SCHEDULE III, IV OR V DRUG – INCLUDING MARIHUANA – EQUAL TO OR EXCEEDING 5 TIMES BULK AMOUNT BUT LESS THAN 50 TIMES BULK – F3
ORC:2925.22.text: _____________ did, by deception, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE DECEPTION), procure (the administration of or a prescription for or the dispensing of or possess an uncompleted preprinted prescription blank used for writing a prescription for) a dangerous drug, and said dangerous drug (being included in Schedule III, IV, V, to wit: (NAME DRUG) or being marihuana), in an amount equal to or exceeding five times the bulk amount but less than fifty times the bulk amount, to wit: (STATE AMOUNT), in violation of Section 2925.22(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2925.22.notes: NOTE: Deception defined in Section 2913.01 of the Ohio Revised Code.

ORC:2925.22.heading: DECEPTION TO OBTAIN A DANGEROUS DRUG 2925.22(A) ORC
ORC:2925.22.variant: SCHEDULE III, IV OR V DRUG – INCLUDING MARIHUANA – EQUAL TO OR EXCEEDING 50 TIMES BULK AMOUNT – F2
ORC:2925.22.text: _____________ did, by deception, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE DECEPTION), procure (the administration of or a prescription for or the dispensing of or possess an uncompleted preprinted prescription blank used for writing a prescription for) a dangerous drug, and said dangerous drug (being included in Schedule III, IV, V, to wit: (NAME DRUG) or being marihuana), in an amount equal to or exceeding 50 times the bulk amount, to wit: (STATE AMOUNT), in violation of Section 2925.22(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2925.22.notes: NOTE: Deception defined in Section 2913.01 of the Ohio Revised Code.

ORC:2925.23.heading: ILLEGAL PROCESSING OF DRUG DOCUMENTS 2925.23(A) ORC
ORC:2925.23.text: _____________ did, knowingly, make a false statement in a (prescription or order or report or record) required by (Chapter 3719 or Chapter 4729 of the Ohio Revised Code), to wit: (DESCRIBE FALSE STATEMENT AND IDENTIFY APPROPRIATE CHAPTER), in violation of Section 2925.23(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, if its Schedule I or II (except marihuana), a felony of the fourth degree or if its Schedule III, IV, V or marihuana, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2925.23.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to manufacturers, licensed health professionals authorized to prescribe drugs, pharmacists, owners of pharmacies, and other persons whose conduct is in accordance with Ohio law.

ORC:2925.23.heading: ILLEGAL PROCESSING OF DRUG DOCUMENTS 2925.23(B) ORC
ORC:2925.23.text: _____________ did (intentionally make, utter, or sell or knowingly possess) a false or forged (prescription, uncompleted preprinted prescription blank used for writing a prescription, official written order, license for a manufacturer of dangerous drugs/outsourcing facility/third-party logistics provider/repackager of dangerous drugs/wholesale distributor of dangerous drugs as required by Section 4729.52 of the Ohio Revised Code, or license for a terminal distributor of dangerous drugs as required in Section 4729.60 of the Ohio Revised Code or registration certificate for a wholesale distributor of dangerous drugs as required in section 4729.60 of the Ohio Revised Code), to wit: (NAME FORGED DOCUMENT), in violation of Section 2925.23(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2925.23.heading: ILLEGAL PROCESSING OF DRUG DOCUMENTS 2925.23(B) ORC
ORC:2925.23.variant: SCHEDULE I OR II DRUG – EXCEPT MARIHUANA – F4
ORC:2925.23.text: _____________ did (intentionally make, utter, or sell or knowingly possess) a false or forged (prescription or official written order), to wit: (NAME FORGED DOCUMENT), and the drug involved being a Schedule I or II drug, to wit: (NAME DRUG), in violation of Section 2925.23(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2925.23.heading: ILLEGAL PROCESSING OF DRUG DOCUMENTS 2925.23(B) ORC
ORC:2925.23.variant: SCHEDULE III, IV, OR V OR MARIHUANA – F5
ORC:2925.23.text: _____________ did (intentionally make, utter, or sell or knowingly possess) a false or forged (prescription or official written order), to wit: (NAME FORGED DOCUMENT), and the drug involved being (a dangerous drug or a Schedule III, IV, or V drug, to wit: (NAME DRUG), or marihuana), in violation of Section 2925.23(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2925.23.heading: ILLEGAL PROCESSING OF DRUG DOCUMENTS 2925.23(C) ORC
ORC:2925.23.text: _____________ did, by theft as defined in Section 2913.02 of the Ohio Revised Code, acquire (a prescription, an uncompleted preprinted prescription blank used for writing a prescription, an official written order, or a blank official written order, or a license or blank license for a manufacturer of dangerous drugs/outsourcing facility/third-party logistics provider/repackager of dangerous drugs/wholesale distributor of dangerous drugs as required in Section 4729.52 of the Ohio Revised Code, or a license or blank license for a terminal distributor of dangerous drugs as required in Section 4729.60 of the Ohio Revised Code or a registration certificate or blank registration certificate for a wholesale distributor of dangerous drugs as required in Section 4729.60 of the Ohio Revised Code), in violation of Section 2925.23(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2925.23.heading: ILLEGAL PROCESSING OF DRUG DOCUMENTS 2925.23(C) ORC
ORC:2925.23.variant: SCHEDULE I OR II DRUG – EXCEPT MARIHUANA – F4
ORC:2925.23.text: _____________ did, by theft as defined in Section 2913.02 of the Ohio Revised Code, acquire (a prescription or an official written order), to wit: (NAME DOCUMENT ACQUIRED), and the drug involved being a Schedule I or II drug, to wit: (NAME DRUG), in violation of Section 2925.23(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2925.23.heading: ILLEGAL PROCESSING OF DRUG DOCUMENTS 2925.23(C) ORC
ORC:2925.23.variant: SCHEDULE III, IV, OR V OR MARIHUANA – F5
ORC:2925.23.text: _____________ did, by theft as defined in Section 2913.02 of the Ohio Revised Code, acquire (a prescription or an official written order), to wit: (NAME DOCUMENT ACQUIRED), and the drug involved being (a dangerous drug or a Schedule III, IV, or V drug, to wit: (NAME DRUG), or marihuana), in violation of Section 2925.23(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.

ORC:2925.23.heading: ILLEGAL PROCESSING OF DRUG DOCUMENTS 2925.23(D) ORC
ORC:2925.23.variant: SCHEDULE I OR II DRUG – EXCEPT MARIHUANA – F4
ORC:2925.23.text: _____________ did, knowingly, make or affix any false or forged label to a package or receptacle containing any dangerous drugs, and the drug involved being a Schedule I or II drug, to wit: (NAME DRUG), in violation of Section 2925.23(D) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.
ORC:2925.23.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to manufacturers, licensed health professionals authorized to prescribe drugs, pharmacists, owners of pharmacies, and other persons whose conduct is in accordance with Ohio law.

ORC:2925.23.heading: ILLEGAL PROCESSING OF DRUG DOCUMENTS 2925.23(D) ORC
ORC:2925.23.variant: SCHEDULE III, IV OR V OR MARIHUANA – F5
ORC:2925.23.text: _____________ did, knowingly, make or affix any false or forged label to a package or receptacle containing any dangerous drugs, and the drug involved being (a dangerous drug or a Schedule III, IV, or V drug, to wit: (NAME DRUG), or marihuana), in violation of Section 2925.23(D) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2925.23.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to manufacturers, licensed health professionals authorized to prescribe drugs, pharmacists, owners of pharmacies, and other persons whose conduct is in accordance with Ohio law.

ORC:2925.24.heading: TAMPERING WITH DRUGS 2925.24(A) ORC
ORC:2925.24.text: _____________ did, knowingly adulterate or alter any dangerous drug or substitute any dangerous drug with another substance, to wit: (DESCRIBE DRUG ALTERED OR SUBSTITUTED), in violation of Section 2925.24(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2925.24.notes: NOTE: This statute does not apply to manufacturers, practitioners, pharmacists, owners of pharmacies, nurses, and other persons, when the conduct of the manufacturer, practitioner, pharmacist, owner of a pharmacy, nurse, or other person is in accordance with Chapters 3719, 4715, 4723, 4729, 4731, or 4741 of the Ohio Revised Code. NOTE: It is an affirmative defense to a charge under this section alleging that a person altered a dangerous drug that the dangerous drug the person allegedly altered was lawfully prescribed for the person’s personal use and that the person did not sell or transfer or intend to sell or transfer the dangerous drug to another person.

ORC:2925.24.heading: TAMPERING WITH DRUGS 2925.24(A) ORC
ORC:2925.24.text: _____________ did, knowingly adulterate or alter any dangerous drug or substitute any dangerous drug with another substance, to wit: (DESCRIBE DRUG ALTERED OR SUBSTITUTED), and physical harm being suffered as a result, to wit: (DESCRIBE PHYSICAL HARM), in violation of Section 2925.24(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2925.24.notes: NOTE: This statute does not apply to manufacturers, practitioners, pharmacists, owners of pharmacies, nurses, and other persons, when the conduct of the manufacturer, practitioner, pharmacist, owner of a pharmacy, nurse, or other person is in accordance with Chapters 3719, 4715, 4723, 4729, 4731, or 4741 of the Ohio Revised Code. NOTE: It is an affirmative defense to a charge under this section alleging that a person altered a dangerous drug that the dangerous drug the person allegedly altered was lawfully prescribed for the person’s personal use and that the person did not sell or transfer or intend to sell or transfer the dangerous drug to another person.

ORC:2925.24.heading: TAMPERING WITH DRUGS 2925.24(B) ORC
ORC:2925.24.text: _____________ did, knowingly adulterate or alter any package or receptacle containing any dangerous drug or substitute any package or receptacle containing any dangerous drug with another package or receptacle, to wit: (DESCRIBE RECEPTACLE OR PACKAGE ALTERED OR SUBSTITUTED), in violation of Section 2925.24(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2925.24.notes: NOTE: This statute does not apply to manufacturers, practitioners, pharmacists, owners of pharmacies, nurses, and other persons, when the conduct of the manufacturer, practitioner, pharmacist, owner of a pharmacy, nurse, or other person is in accordance with Chapters 3719, 4715, 4723, 4729, 4731, or 4741 of the Ohio Revised Code. NOTE: It is an affirmative defense to a charge under this section alleging that a person altered a dangerous drug that the dangerous drug the person allegedly altered was lawfully prescribed for the person’s personal use and that the person did not sell or transfer or intend to sell or transfer the dangerous drug to another person.

ORC:2925.24.heading: TAMPERING WITH DRUGS 2925.24(B) ORC
ORC:2925.24.text: _____________ did, knowingly adulterate or alter any package or receptacle containing any dangerous drug or substitute any package or receptacle containing any dangerous drug with another package or receptacle, to wit: (DESCRIBE RECEPTACLE OR PACKAGE ALTERED OR SUBSTITUTED), and physical harm being suffered as a result, to wit: (DESCRIBE PHYSICAL HARM), in violation of Section 2925.24(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the second degree.
ORC:2925.24.notes: NOTE: This statute does not apply to manufacturers, practitioners, pharmacists, owners of pharmacies, nurses, and other persons, when the conduct of the manufacturer, practitioner, pharmacist, owner of a pharmacy, nurse, or other person is in accordance with Chapters 3719, 4715, 4723, 4729, 4731, or 4741 of the Ohio Revised Code. NOTE: It is an affirmative defense to a charge under this section alleging that a person altered a dangerous drug that the dangerous drug the person allegedly altered was lawfully prescribed for the person’s personal use and that the person did not sell or transfer or intend to sell or transfer the dangerous drug to another person.

ORC:2925.31.heading: ABUSING HARMFUL INTOXICANTS 2925.31(A) ORC
ORC:2925.31.text: _____________ did (obtain or possess or use) a harmful intoxicant, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES AND NAME OF INTOXICANT), with the purpose to induce (intoxication or physiological effects similar to intoxication), in violation of Section 2925.31(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2925.31.notes: NOTE: Section does not apply to lawful research, clinical, medical, dental or veterinary purposes.

ORC:2925.31.heading: ABUSING HARMFUL INTOXICANTS 2925.31(A) ORC
ORC:2925.31.text: _____________ did (obtain or possess or use) a harmful intoxicant, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES AND NAME OF INTOXICANT) with the purpose to induce (intoxication or physiological effects similar to intoxication) and having been previously convicted of a drug abuse offense, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE AND SECTION NUMBER), on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT), in violation of Section 2925.31(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2925.31.notes: NOTE: Section does not apply to lawful research, clinical, medical, dental, or veterinary purposes.

ORC:2925.32.heading: TRAFFICKING IN HARMFUL INTOXICANTS 2925.32(A)(1) ORC

ORC:2925.32.heading: TRAFFICKING IN HARMFUL INTOXICANTS 2925.32(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2925.32.text: _____________ did knowingly (dispense or distribute) a harmful intoxicant, to wit: (DESCRIBE INTOXICANT), to a person eighteen years of age or older, to wit: (STATE NAME AND AGE), (knowing or having reason to believe) that the harmful intoxicant will be used for the purpose of inducing (intoxication or physiological effects similar to intoxication) as prohibited in Section 2925.31 of the Ohio Revised Code, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), and having been previously convicted of a drug abuse offense, to wit: (STATE OFFENSE AND SECTION NUMBER) on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT), in violation of Section 2925.32(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2925.32.heading: TRAFFICKING IN HARMFUL INTOXICANTS 2925.32(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2925.32.text: _____________ did, knowingly (dispense or distribute) a harmful intoxicant, to wit: (DESCRIBE INTOXICANT), to a person under eighteen years of age, to wit: (STATE NAME AND AGE), (knowing or having reason to believe) that the harmful intoxicant will be used for the purpose of inducing (intoxication or physiological effects similar to intoxication) as prohibited in Section 2925.31 of the Ohio Revised Code, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2925.32(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2925.32.notes: NOTE: This division does not prohibit dispensing or distributing a harmful intoxicant to a person under 18 if a written order from the juvenile’s parent or guardian is provided to the dispenser or distributor or dispensing or distributing gasoline or diesel fuel to a person under 18 if the dispenser or distributor does not know or have reason to believe the product will be used in violation of Section 2925.31 of the Ohio Revised Code. A person is not required to obtain a written order from the parent or guardian of a person under age 18 in order to distribute or dispense gasoline or diesel fuel to the person.

ORC:2925.34.heading: SALE OF PURE CAFFEINE PRODUCT 2925.34(B) ORC
ORC:2925.34.variant: SELL OR OFFER TO SELL – MM
ORC:2925.34.text: ___________ did knowingly (sell or offer for sale) a pure caffeine product, to wit: (DESCRIBE PRODUCT, NAME SELLER AND BUYER, AND CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2925.34(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor.
ORC:2925.34.notes: NOTE: Nothing in this section prohibits either of the following: 1. Possession of a product manufactured in a unit-dose form such as a pill, tablet, or caplet, but only if each unit dose of the product contains not more than two hundred fifty milligrams of caffeine. 2. Possession of a pure caffeine product by any of the following: a. A food processing establishment, as defined in Section 3715.021 of the Revised Code; b. A manufacturer of a drug that is available without a prescription; c. A laboratory that holds a current, valid category III terminal distributor of dangerous drugs license issued by the state board of pharmacy under Section 4729.54 of the Revised Code; d. A laboratory of any agency or department of this state that performs testing, analysis, and other laboratory services on behalf of the state; e. A postal or delivery service that transports or delivers a pure caffeine product to an entity specified in divisions (D)(2)(a) to (d) of this section.

ORC:2925.37.notes: DEFINITIONS UNLAWFUL PURCHASE OF A PSEUDOEPHEDRINE/EPHEDRINE PRODUCT 2925.55 ORC PSEUDOEPHEDRINE – means any material, compound, mixture, or preparation that contains any quantity of pseudoephedrine, any of its salts, optical isomers, or salts of optical isomers. PSEUDOEPHEDRINE PRODUCT – means a consumer product that contains pseudoephedrine. CONSUMER PRODUCT – means any food or drink that is consumed or used by humans and any drug, including a drug that may be provided legally only pursuant to a prescription, that is intended to be consumed or used by humans. EPHEDRINE – means any material, compound, mixture, or preparation that contains any quantity of ephedrine, any of its salts, optical isomers, or salts of optical isomers EPHEDRINE PRODUCT – means a consumer product that contains ephedrine.

ORC:2925.55.heading: UNLAWFUL PURCHASE OF A PSEUDOEPHEDRINE/EPHEDRINE PRODUCT 2925.55(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2925.55.text: _____________ did knowingly (purchase, receive, or otherwise acquire) an amount of (pseudoephedrine product/ephedrine product) that is greater than (three and six tenths grams within a period of a single day OR nine grams within a period of thirty consecutive days), to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION, INCLUDING QUANTITY, NAME OF PRODUCT AND TIME PERIOD), and said product was not dispensed by a pharmacist pursuant to a valid prescription issued by a licensed health professional authorized to prescribe drugs, in violation of Section 2925.55(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2925.55.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to an employee of a retailer or terminal distributor of dangerous drugs who accepts from the retailer or terminal distributor of dangerous drugs the pseudoephedrine product in a sealed container in connection with manufacturing, warehousing, placement, stocking, bagging, loading, or unloading of the product. NOTE: The limits specified in this section apply to the total amount of base pseudoephedrine or base ephedrine in the pseudoephedrine product or ephedrine product, respectively. The limits do not apply to the product’s overall weight.

ORC:2925.55.heading: UNDERAGE PURCHASE OF A PSEUDOEPHEDRINE/EPHEDRINE PRODUCT 2925.55(C)(1) ORC
ORC:2925.55.text: _____________, an individual under eighteen years of age, to wit: (STATE AGE), did knowingly (purchase, receive, or otherwise acquire) a pseudoephedrine product or ephedrine product, to wit: (STATE PRODUCT), and said product was not dispensed by a pharmacist pursuant to a valid prescription issued by a licensed health professional authorized to prescribe drugs, in violation of Section 2925.55(C)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2925.55.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to an individual who purchases, receives, or otherwise acquires a pseudoephedrine or ephedrine product from any of the following: 1. A licensed health professional authorized to prescribe drugs or pharmacist who dispenses, sells, or otherwise provides the pseudoephedrine or ephedrine product to that individual and whose conduct is in accordance with Ohio law; 2. A parent or guardian of that individual who provides the pseudoephedrine or ephedrine product to the individual; 3. A person, as authorized by that individual’s parent or guardian, who dispenses, sells, or otherwise provides the pseudoephedrine or ephedrine product to the individual; 4. A retailer or terminal distributor of dangerous drugs who provides the pseudoephedrine or ephedrine product to that individual if the individual is an employee of the retailer or terminal distributor of dangerous drugs and the individual receives or accepts the pseudoephedrine or ephedrine product in a sealed container in connection with manufacturing, warehousing, placement, stocking, bagging, loading, or unloading of the product.

ORC:2925.55.heading: USING FALSE INFORMATION TO PURCHASE A PSEUDOEPHEDRINE/ EPHEDRINE PRODUCT 2925.55(D) ORC
ORC:2925.55.text: _____________, an individual under eighteen years of age, to wit: (STATE AGE), did knowingly show or give false information concerning the individual’s name, age or other identification for the purpose of (purchasing, receiving, or otherwise acquiring) a pseudoephedrine product or ephedrine product, to wit: (DESCRIBE PRODUCT AND VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2925.55(D) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2925.55.heading: IMPROPER PURCHASE OF A PSEUDOEPHEDRINE/EPHEDRINE PRODUCT 2925.55(E) ORC

ORC:2925.56.heading: UNLAWFULLY SELLING A PSEUDOEPHEDRINE/EPHEDRINE PRODUCT 2925.56(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2925.56.text: _____________, a retailer or terminal distributor of dangerous drugs or an employee of a retailer or terminal distributer of dangerous drugs, did knowingly (sell/offer to sell/hold for sale/deliver, or otherwise provide) to any individual, an amount of (pseudoephedrine product/ephedrine product) that is greater than (three and six tenths grams within a period of a single day OR nine grams within a period of thirty consecutive days), to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION, INCLUDING QUANTITY, NAME OF PRODUCT AND TIME PERIOD), and said product was not dispensed by a pharmacist pursuant to a valid prescription issued by a licensed health professional authorized to prescribe drugs, in violation of Section 2925.56(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2925.56.notes: NOTE: The maximum amounts specified apply to the total amount of base ephedrine or base pseudoephedrine in the product. The maximum amounts do not apply to the product’s overall weight. NOTE: This section does not apply to any quantity of pseudoephedrine or ephedrine product dispensed by a pharmacist pursuant to a valid prescription issued by a licensed health professional authorized to prescribe drugs if the conduct of the pharmacist and the licensed health professional authorized to prescribe drugs is in accordance with Ohio law. NOTE: This section does not apply to a retailer, terminal distributor of dangerous drugs, or an employee of either who provides to an individual more than nine grams of any pseudoephedrine or ephedrine product within a period of thirty consecutive days if the individual is an employee of the retailer or terminal distributor of dangerous drugs, and the employee receives or accepts the pseudoephedrine or ephedrine product in a sealed container in connection with manufacturing, warehousing, placement, stocking, bagging, loading, or unloading of the product. NOTE: This section does not apply when a stop-sale alert is issued after the submission of information to the national precursor log exchange if the retailer/terminal distributor was unable to complete an information submission previously due to experiencing mechanical or electronic failure of the equipment needed to submit the information. “Stop-sale alert” means a notification sent from the national precursor log exchange to a retailer or terminal distributor of dangerous drugs indicating that the completion of a sale of a pseudoephedrine product or ephedrine product would result in a violation of division (A)(1) of section 2925.56 of the Revised Code or federal law.

ORC:2925.56.heading: UNLAWFULLY SELLING A PSEUDOEPHEDRINE/EPHEDRINE PRODUCT TO A MINOR 2925.56(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2925.56.text: _____________, (a retailer or terminal distributor of dangerous drugs or an employee of a retailer or terminal distributor of dangerous drugs, to wit: (STATE EMPLOYER)), did knowingly (sell, offer to sell, hold for sale, deliver, or otherwise provide) a pseudoephedrine or ephedrine product to an individual who is under eighteen years of age, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION, INCLUDING NAME OF PRODUCT AND NAME AND AGE OF MINOR), in violation of Section 2925.56(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
ORC:2925.56.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to any of the following: 1. A licensed health professional authorized to prescribe drugs or pharmacist who dispenses, sells, or otherwise provides a pseudoephedrine or ephedrine product to an individual under eighteen years of age and whose conduct is in accordance with Ohio law; 2. A parent or guardian of an individual under eighteen years of age who provides a pseudoephedrine or ephedrine product to the individual; 3. A person who, as authorized by that individual’s parent or guardian, dispenses, sells, or otherwise provides the pseudoephedrine or ephedrine product to an individual under eighteen years of age; 4. The provision by a retailer, terminal distributor of dangerous drugs, or employee of either of a pseudoephedrine or ephedrine product in a sealed container to an employee of the retailer or terminal distributor of dangerous drugs who is under eighteen years of age in connection with manufacturing, warehousing, placement, stocking, bagging, loading, or unloading of the product. NOTE: It is an affirmative defense to this section that all of the following occurred: 1. A card holder attempting to purchase or receive a pseudoephedrine or ephedrine product presented a driver’s or commercial driver’s license or an identification card. 2. A transaction scan of the driver’s or commercial driver’s license or identification card that the card holder presented indicated that the license or card was valid. 3. The pseudoephedrine or ephedrine product was sold, given away, or otherwise distributed to the card holder in a reasonable reliance upon the identification presented and the completed transaction scan.

ORC:2925.56.heading: IMPROPER SALE OF A PSEUDOEPHEDRINE/EPHEDRINE PRODUCT 2925.56(C) ORC
ORC:2925.56.text: _____________, a retailer or terminal distributor of dangerous drugs that sells, offers to sell, holds for sale, delivers, or otherwise provides a pseudoephedrine or ephedrine product to the public, did fail to (maintain a log book of all purchases of pseudoephedrine/ephedrine products or require each purchaser to sign an entry in a log book or determine whether a name signed in an entry in a log book corresponds with the name on a government-issued identification card or retain the log book for a minimum of one year after the date of the last purchase recorded in the log book or include the required statement in a conspicuous location in a log book) as required by Revised Code 3715.05(C) (2), to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2925.56(C) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2927.01.heading: ABUSE OF A CORPSE 2927.01(A) ORC
ORC:2927.01.text: _____________ did, not being authorized by law, treat a human corpse, to wit: (STATE DECEDENT’S NAME), in a way that the person knew would outrage the reasonable family sensibilities, to wit: (DESCRIBE MANNER), in violation of Section 2927.01(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2927.01.heading: GROSS ABUSE OF A CORPSE 2927.01(B) ORC
ORC:2927.01.text: _____________ did, not being authorized by law, treat a human corpse, to wit: (STATE DECEDENT’S NAME), in a way that the person knew would outrage the reasonable community sensibilities, to wit: (DESCRIBE MANNER), in violation of Section 2927.01(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2927.01.notes: DEFINITIONS 2927.02 ORC ALTERNATIVE NICOTINE PRODUCT - An electronic cigarette or any other product or device that consists of or contains nicotine that can be ingested into the body by any means, including, but not limited to, chewing, smoking, absorbing, dissolving, or inhaling. ALTERNATIVE NICOTINE PRODUCT - does not include any of the following: Any cigarette or other tobacco product; Any product that is a “drug” as that term is defined in 21 U.S.C. 321(g)(1); Any product that is a “device” as that term is defined in 21 U.S.C. 321(h); Any product that is a “combination product” as described in 21 U.S.C. 353(g). CIGARETTE – Clove cigarettes and hand-rolled cigarettes. DISTRIBUTE – To furnish, give, or provide cigarettes, other tobacco products, alternative nicotine products, or papers used to roll cigarettes to the ultimate consumer of the cigarettes, other tobacco products, alternative nicotine products, or papers used to roll cigarettes. ELECTRONIC CIGARETTE - Any electronic product or device that produces a vapor that delivers nicotine or any other substance to the person inhaling from the device to simulate smoking and that is likely to be offered to or purchased by consumers as an electronic cigarette, electronic cigar, electronic cigarillo, or electronic pipe. PROOF OF AGE – A driver’s license, commercial driver’s license, military identification card, passport, or an identification card issued under Sections 4507.50 to 4507.52 of the Ohio Revised Code that shows that a person is eighteen years of age or older. TOBACCO PRODUCT – Any product that is made from tobacco, including, but not limited to, a cigarette, a cigar, pipe tobacco, chewing tobacco, or snuff.

ORC:2927.02.notes: NOTE: The following are affirmative defenses to this section: 1. The person under twenty-one years of age was accompanied by a parent, spouse who is twenty-one years of age or older, or legal guardian of the person under twenty-one years of age; or 2. NOTE: It is not a violation of this section for a person to give or otherwise distribute to a person under twenty-one years of age cigarettes, other tobacco products, alternative nicotine products, or papers used to roll cigarettes while the person under twenty-one years of age is participating in a research protocol if all of the following apply: 1. The parent, guardian, or legal custodian of the person under twenty-one years of age has consented in writing to the person under twenty-one years of age participating in the research protocol; 2. An institutional human subjects protection review board, or an equivalent entity, has approved the research protocol; and 3. The person under twenty-one years of age is participating in the research protocol at the facility or location specified in the research protocol.

NOTE: It is an affirmative defense if the child was accompanied by a parent, spouse who is eighteen years of age or older, or legal guardian of the child; or the person who gave, sold, or distributed cigarettes, alternative nicotine products, other tobacco products or papers used to roll cigarettes to a child under division (B)(1) of this section is a parent, spouse who is eighteen years of age or older, or legal guardian of the child. DEFINITIONS 2329.14 CCC ELECTRONIC SMOKING DEVICE – means any device that can be used to deliver aerosolized or vaporized nicotine to the person inhaling from the device, including, but not limited to, an e-cigarette, e-cigar, e-pipe, vape pen, or e-hookah. 1. Includes any component, part, or accessory of such a device, whether or not sold separately, and includes any substance intended to be aerosolized or vaporized during the use of the device. 2. Does not include drugs, devices, or combination products authorized for sale by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, as those terms are defined in the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act. PRODUCT PARAPHERNALIA – means any product that is used to assist in chewing, smoking, absorbing, dissolving, inhaling, or any other consumption of tobacco product to include, but not limited to, pipes, rolling papers, and electronic smoking devices. PROOF OF AGE – means a driver’s license, a commercial driver’s license, a military identification card, a passport, or an identification card issued under Sections 4507.50 to 4507.52 of the Ohio Revised Code demonstrating that the recipient or purchaser is at least 21 years of age. 1. No such verification is required for a recipient over the age of thirty (30). 2. That a person appeared to be over the age of thirty (30) shall not constitute a defense to a violation of this section. TOBACCO PRODUCT – means any product that is made from or derived from tobacco, and is intended for human consumption or is likely to be consumed, whether smoked, heated, chewed, absorbed, dissolved, inhaled, or ingested by any other means, including, but not limited to, a cigarette, a cigar, pipe tobacco, chewing tobacco, snuff, or snus. 1. Also includes an electronic smoking device and any component or accessory used in the consumption of a tobacco product, such as filters, rolling papers, pipes, or liquids used in electronic smoking devices, whether or not they contain nicotine. 2. Does not include drugs, devices, or combination products authorized for sale by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, as those terms are defined in the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act. VENDING MACHINE – means any mechanical or electronic device designed to do both of the following: 1. Receive a coin, bill, token, or credit card, including, but not limited to, a card, code, device, or other means of access to a customer’s account, made for that purpose; 2. In return for the insertion or deposit of a coin, bill, token, or credit card, automatically dispense property, provide a service, or grant a license.

ORC:2151.87.notes: NOTE: It is not a violation of this section if the child possesses, purchases or attempts to purchase, orders, pays for, shares the cost of, or accepts or receives cigarettes, other tobacco products, alternative nicotine products, or papers used to roll cigarettes while participating in an inspection or compliance check conducted by a federal, state, local, or corporate entity at a location at which cigarettes, other tobacco products, alternative nicotine products, or papers used to roll cigarettes are sold or distributed. ORC:2151.87.heading: CHILD PROHIBITED FROM POSSESSING, USING, PURCHASING, OR RECEIVING CIGARETTES OR OTHER TOBACCO PRODUCTS 2151.87(B)(4) ORC
ORC:2151.87.text: _____________, a child, to wit: (DOB), not accompanied by a parent, spouse who is eighteen years of age or older, or legal guardian, did (accept or receive) (cigarettes or tobacco products or alternative nicotine products or papers used to roll cigarettes), to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2151.87(B)(4) of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor.
ORC:2151.87.notes: NOTE: It is not a violation of this section if the child possesses, purchases or attempts to purchase, orders, pays for, shares the cost of, or accepts or receives cigarettes, other tobacco products, alternative nicotine products, or papers used to roll cigarettes while participating in an inspection or compliance check conducted by a federal, state, local, or corporate entity at a location at which cigarettes, other tobacco products, alternative nicotine products, or papers used to roll cigarettes are sold or distributed. NOTE: It is not a violation of this section for a child to accept or receive cigarettes, other tobacco products, alternative nicotine products, or papers used to roll cigarettes if the child is required to do so in the performance of the child’s duties as an employee of that child’s employer and the child’s acceptance or receipt of cigarettes, other tobacco products, alternative nicotine products, or papers used to roll cigarettes occurs exclusively within the scope of the child’s employment. NOTE: A child alleged or found to have violated this section shall not be detained under any provision of this chapter or any other provision of the Revised Code.

ORC:2151.87.notes: NOTE: A child alleged or found to have violated this section shall not be detained under any provision of this chapter or any other provision of the Revised Code.

CCC:2329.13.heading: ILLEGAL DISTRIBUTION OF TOBACCO PRODUCTS 2329.13(A) CCC

CCC:2329.14.heading: ILLEGAL DISTRIBUTION OF TOBACCO PRODUCTS 2329.14(A)(1) CCC
CCC:2329.14.variant: DISTRIBUTION TO PERSON UNDER THE AGE OF 21 – M4
CCC:2329.14.text: ___________ did, while being a (manufacturer, producer, distributor, wholesaler, or retailer or any agent, employee, or representative of a manufacturer, producer, distributor, wholesaler, or retailer) of (cigarettes or other tobacco products or product paraphernalia), to wit: (DESCRIBE NAME OF COMPANY) did (give, sell, or distribute) cigarettes, other tobacco products, or product paraphernalia, to wit: (DESCRIBE PRODUCT) to any person under twenty-one (21) years of age, to wit: (STATE NAME AND AGE OF PERSON), in violation of Section 2329.14(A)(1) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

CCC:2329.14.heading: ILLEGAL DISTRIBUTION OF TOBACCO PRODUCTS 2329.14(A)(1) CCC

CCC:2329.14.heading: ILLEGAL DISTRIBUTION OF TOBACCO PRODUCTS 2329.14(A)(2) CCC
CCC:2329.14.variant: DISTRIBUTION TO PERSON UNDER THE AGE OF 21 WITHOUT CONSPICUOUS SIGN POSTED – M4
CCC:2329.14.text: ___________ did, while being a (manufacturer, producer, distributor, wholesaler, or retailer or any agent, employee, or representative of a manufacturer, producer, distributor, wholesaler, or retailer) of (cigarettes, other tobacco products or product paraphernalia) to wit: (DESCRIBE NAME OF COMPANY) did (give, sell, or otherwise distribute) cigarettes, other tobacco products, or product paraphernalia, to wit: (DESCRIBE PRODUCT) to any person under twenty-one (21) years of age, to wit: (STATE NAME OF PERSON AND AGE), in any place that does not have posted in a conspicuous place a sign stating that giving, selling, or otherwise distributing cigarettes, other tobacco products or product paraphernalia to a person under twenty-one (21) years of age is prohibited by law, to wit: (DESCRIBE PLACE) in violation of Section 2329.14(A)(2) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

CCC:2329.14.heading: ILLEGAL DISTRIBUTION OF TOBACCO PRODUCTS 2329.14(A)(2) CCC
CCC:2329.14.variant: DISTRIBUTION TO PERSON UNDER THE AGE OF 21 WITHOUT CONSPICUOUS SIGN POSTED – PREVIOUS CONVICTION – M3

CCC:2329.14.heading: ILLEGAL DISTRIBUTION OF TOBACCO PRODUCTS 2329.14(A)(3) CCC

ORC:2927.11.heading: DESECRATION 2927.11(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2927.11.variant: UNITED STATES OR OHIO FLAG – M2
ORC:2927.11.text: _____________ did, without privilege to do so, purposely (deface or damage or pollute or physically mistreat) the flag of the (United States or the State of Ohio), to wit: (DESCRIBE ITEM AND WHAT WAS DONE TO IT), in violation of Section 2927.11(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.
ORC:2927.11.notes: NOTE: When burning of a flag is political expression, it is not a crime.

ORC:2927.11.heading: DESECRATION 2927.11(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2927.11.text: _____________ did, without privilege to do so, purposely (deface or damage or pollute or physically mistreat) a public monument, to wit: (DESCRIBE MONUMENT, ITS LOCATION AND WHAT WAS DONE TO IT), in violation of Section 2927.11(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2927.11.heading: DESECRATION 2927.11(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2927.11.text: _____________ did, without privilege to do so, purposely (deface or damage or pollute or physically mistreat) a (historical marker or commemorative marker or structure or Indian mound or earthwork, cemetery, thing or site of great historical or archaeological interest), to wit: (DESCRIBE ITEM, LOCATION AND WHAT WAS DONE TO IT), in violation of Section 2927.11(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.

ORC:2927.11.heading: DESECRATION 2927.11(A)(4) ORC

ORC:2927.11.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $5,000.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $5,000.00 AND $100,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE MORE THAN $100,000.00, a felony of the third degree. NOTE: Penalty includes a fine of up to $2,500.00

ORC:2927.11.heading: DESECRATION 2927.11(A)(6) ORC

CCC:2331.08.heading: ETHNIC INTIMIDATION 2331.08 CCC
CCC:2331.08.variant: VICTIM’S ETHNICITY MOTIVE/REASON/PURPOSE FOR COMMISSION OF OFFENSE – M1
CCC:2331.08.text: _____________ did violate Columbus City Code section (2303.13, 2303.22, 2307.06, 2309.06, 2309.07, 2311.21, 2313.02, 2313.03, 2313.04, 2317.03, 2317.11, 2317.12, 2323.30, or 2329.01) (STATE OFFENSE), by means of (DESCRIBE FACTS AND HOW OFFENSE COMMITTED), by reason of or where one of the motives, reasons or purposes for the commission of the offense is the victim’s (race, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, familial status, or military status), to wit: (DESCRIBE WHAT SUSPECT DID/SAID THAT SHOWS MOTIVE/REASON/ PURPOSE AND STATE VICTIM’S NAME) in violation of section 2331.08 of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
CCC:2331.08.notes: NOTE: In a prosecution under this section the offender’s motive, reason, or purpose for the commission of the offense may be shown by the offender’s temporarily related conduct or statements before, during, or after the offense, including ethnic, sexual orientation, religious, or racial slurs, and by the totality of the facts, circumstances, and conduct surrounding the commission of the offense. NOTE: This section does not apply if the facts alleged in the complaint would constitute a felony under Section 2927.12, Ohio Revised Code.

ORC:2927.13.heading: SELLING OR DONATING CONTAMINATED BLOOD 2927.13(A) ORC
ORC:2927.13.text: _____________ did, knowing that (he or she) is a carrier of a virus that causes acquired immune deficiency syndrome, to wit: (STATE BASIS FOR KNOWLEDGE) (sell or donate) (blood, plasma, or a product of said person’s blood) when (he or she) (has knowledge or should have had knowledge) that the (blood, plasma, or blood product) is being accepted for the purpose of transfusion to another person, to wit: (STATE FACTS ESTABLISHING THE REQUISITE KNOWLEDGE, INCLUDING NAME AND LOCATION OF THE PLACE TAKING THE BLOOD AND/OR THE NAME OF THE PROSPECTIVE TRANSFUSEE), in violation of Section 2927.13(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2927.15.heading: UNLAWFUL COLLECTION OF BODILY SUBSTANCE 2927.15(A) ORC
ORC:2927.15.text: _____________ did knowingly collect any (blood, urine, tissue, or other bodily substance) of another person, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME), without privilege or consent to do so, to wit: (DESCRIBE OFFENSE), in violation of Section 2927.15(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2927.15.heading: UNLAWFUL COLLECTION OF BODILY SUBSTANCE 2927.15(A) ORC
ORC:2927.15.text: _____________ did knowingly collect any (blood, urine, tissue, or other bodily substance) of another person, to wit: (STATE VICTIM’S NAME), without privilege or consent to do so, to wit: (DESCRIBE OFFENSE), having been previously convicted of violating Ohio Revised Code 2927.15(A), to wit: on (DATE OF CONVICTION) in (NAME OF COURT) (CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2927.15(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fifth degree.
ORC:2927.15.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply to any of the following: 1. The collection of any bodily substance of a person by a law enforcement officer, or by another person pursuant to the direction or advice of a law enforcement officer, for purposes of a chemical test or tests of the substance under division (A)(1) of section 1547.111 or division (A)(2) of section 4511.191 of the Revised Code to determine the alcohol, drug, controlled substance, metabolite of a controlled substance, or combination content of the bodily substance; 2. The collection of any bodily substance of a person by a peace officer, or by another person pursuant to the direction or advice of a peace officer, for purposes of a test or tests of the substance as provided in division (A) of section 4506.17 of the Revised Code to determine the person’s alcohol concentration or the presence of any controlled substance or metabolite of a controlled substance. 3. This section shall not be construed as implying that the persons identified above do not have privilege to collect the bodily substance of another person as described in those divisions or as limiting the definition of “privilege” set forth in section 2901.01 of the Revised Code. DEFINITIONS 2927.21 (ORC) OFFENSE SUBJECT TO FORFEITURE PROCEEDINGS – means any of the following: 1. A violation of Section 2903.01, 2903.02, 2903.03, 2903.04, 2903.041, 2903.05, 2903.06, 2903.08, 2903.09, 2903.11, 2903.12, 2903.13, 2903.14, 2903.15, 2903.16, 2903.21, or 2903.211 of the Ohio Revised Code; 2. A violation of Section 2905.01, 2905.02, 2905.03, 2905.05, 2905.11, 2905.32, or 2905.33 of the Ohio Revised Code; 3. A violation of Section 2907.02, 2907.03, 2907.04, 2907.05, 2907.06, 2907.07, 2907.19, 2907.21, 2907.22, 2907.321, 2907.322, or 2907.323 of the Ohio Revised Code; 4. A violation of Section 2909.02, 2909.03, 2909.22, 2909.23, 2909.24, 2909.26, 2909.27, 2909.28, or 2909.29 of the Ohio Revised Code; 5. A violation of Section 2911.01, 2911.02, 2911.11, 2911.12, or 2911.13 of the Ohio Revised Code; 6. A violation of Section 2915.02, 2915.03, 2915.04, or 2915.05 of the Ohio Revised Code; 7. A violation of Section 2921.02, 2921.03, 2921.04, 2921.05, 2921.11, 2921.12, or 2921.41 of the Ohio Revised Code; 8. A violation of Section 2925.02, 2925.03, 2925.04, 2925.041, 2925.05, 2925.06, 2925.09, or 2925.11 of the Ohio Revised Code; 9. A conspiracy or attempt to commit, or complicity in committing, any offense delineated above. PROCEEDS – means both of the following as outlined in Section 2981.01(B)(11) of the Ohio Revised Code: 1. In cases involving unlawful goods, services, or activities, “proceeds” means any property derived directly or indirectly from an offense. “Proceeds” may include, but is not limited to, money or any other means of exchange. “Proceeds” is not limited to the net gain or profit realized from the offense. “Proceeds” does not include property, including money or other means of exchange, if all of the following apply to that property: a. It is held under clear title by a law enforcement agency; b. It is used or may be used to purchase contraband for the purpose of investigating any drug abuse offense, as defined in section 2925.01 of the Revised Code; c. If it is used to purchase contraband under division (B)(11)(a)(ii) of this section, the property continues to be considered the property of the law enforcement agency if the agency establishes a clear chain of custody of it. 2. In cases involving lawful goods or services that are sold or provided in an unlawful manner, “proceeds” means the amount of money or other means of exchange acquired through the illegal transactions resulting in the forfeiture, less the direct costs lawfully incurred in providing the goods or services. The lawful costs deduction does not include any part of the overhead expenses of, or income taxes paid by, the entity providing the goods or services. The alleged offender or delinquent child has the burden to prove that any costs are lawfully incurred. VEHICLE – has the same meaning as in Section 4501.01 of the Ohio Revised Code.

ORC:2927.21.heading: OFFENSE SUBJECT TO FORFEITURE PROCEEDINGS 2927.21(B) ORC
ORC:2927.21.variant: RECEIVE, RETAIN, POSSESS, OR DISPOSE OF PROCEEDS – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00 – M1
ORC:2927.21.text: ___________ did (receive, retain, possess, or dispose of) proceeds, to wit: (DESCRIBE PROCEEDS) knowing or having reasonable cause to believe that the proceeds were derived from the commission of an offense subject to forfeiture proceedings, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES, OFFENSE, AND VALUE OF PROCEEDS), in violation of Section 2927.21(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2927.21.notes: NOTE: It is not a defense to a charge of receiving proceeds of an offense subject to forfeiture proceedings in violation of this section that the proceeds were derived by means other than the commission of an offense subject to forfeiture proceedings if the property was explicitly represented to the accused person as having been derived from the commission of an offense subject to forfeiture proceedings. NOTE: A person shall be considered to have received, retained, possessed, or disposed of proceeds if the proceeds are found anywhere in a vehicle, and the person was the last person who operated the vehicle immediately prior to the search of the vehicle by the law enforcement officer who found the proceeds.
