ORC:2927.24.heading: CONTAMINATING SUBSTANCE FOR HUMAN CONSUMPTION OR USE 2927.24(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2927.24.variant: PLACE IN FOOD OR DRUG – F1
ORC:2927.24.text: _____________ did knowingly mingle a (poison or hazardous chemical, biological, or radioactive substance or harmful substance), to wit: (NAME SUBSTANCE) with a (food or drink or nonprescription drug or prescription drug or pharmaceutical product), to wit: (NAME SUBSTANCE MEANT FOR HUMAN CONSUMPTION) (knowing or having reason to know that) such item may be (ingested or used) by another person, to wit: (STATE CIRCUMSTANCES GIVING RISE TO SUCH KNOWLEDGE AND/OR STATE NAME OF VICTIM, IF IDENTIFIABLE), in violation of Section 2927.24(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the first degree.
ORC:2927.24.notes: NOTE: For purposes of this section a person does not know or have reason to know that water may be ingested or used by another if it is disposed as waste into a household drain including a drain of a toilet, sink, tub, or floor. NOTE: A person may mingle a drug with a food or drink for the purpose of causing the drug to be ingested or used in the quantity described by its labeling or prescription. NOTE: This section shall not be applied in a manner that conflicts with any other state or federal law or rule relating to substances permitted to be applied to or present in any food, raw or processed, any milk or milk product, any meat or meat product, any type of crop, water, or alcoholic or nonalcoholic beverage.

ORC:2927.24.heading: CONTAMINATING SUBSTANCE FOR HUMAN CONSUMPTION OR USE 2927.24(B)(1) ORC
ORC:2927.24.text: _____________ did knowingly place a (poison or hazardous chemical, biological, or radioactive substance or harmful substance, to wit: (NAME SUBSTANCE) in a (spring or well or reservoir or public water supply ), to wit: (NAME SUPPLY AND LOCATION) (knowing or having reason to know that) said water may be (ingested or used) by another person, to wit: (STATE CIRCUMSTANCES GIVING RISE TO SUCH KNOWLEDGE AND/OR STATE NAME OF VICTIM, IF IDENTIFIABLE), in violation of Section 2927.24(B)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the first degree.
ORC:2927.24.notes: NOTE: For purposes of this section a person does not know or have reason to know that water may be ingested or used by another if it is disposed as waste into a household drain including a drain of a toilet, sink, tub, or floor. NOTE: A person may place a poison or other harmful substance in a spring, well, reservoir, or public water supply in such quantity as is necessary to treat the spring, well, reservoir, or water supply to make it safe for human consumption and use. NOTE: This section shall not be applied in a manner that conflicts with any other state or federal law or rule relating to substances permitted to be applied to or present in any food, raw or processed, any milk or milk product, any meat or meat product, any type of crop, water, or alcoholic or nonalcoholic beverage.

ORC:2927.24.heading: CONTAMINATION WITH A HAZARDOUS CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, OR RADIOACTIVE SUBSTANCE 2927.24(B)(2) ORC
ORC:2927.24.variant: RELEASE INTO AIR, LEAVE IN PUBLIC PLACE, OR EXPOSE ONE OR MORE PERSONS – F1
ORC:2927.24.text: _____________ did knowingly (release into the air or leave in any public place or expose one or more persons to) a hazardous chemical, biological, or radioactive substance, to wit: (NAME SUBSTANCE), with the intent to cause, or create a risk of, death or serious physical harm to any person, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2927.24(B)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the first degree.
ORC:2927.24.notes: NOTE: This section shall not be applied in a manner that conflicts with any other state or federal law or rule relating to substances permitted to be applied to or present in any food, raw or processed, any milk or milk product, any meat or meat product, any type of crop, water, or alcoholic or nonalcoholic beverage.

ORC:2927.24.heading: SPREADING FALSE REPORT OF CONTAMINATION 2927.24(C)(1) ORC
ORC:2927.24.variant: FALSE REPORT OF VIOLATION OF REVISED CODE 2927.24(B)(1) – F4
ORC:2927.24.text: _____________ did inform another person, to wit: (STATE NAME AND POSITION) that a (poison or hazardous chemical, biological, or radioactive substance or harmful substance) (has been or will be) placed in (a food or a drink or a nonprescription drug or a prescription drug or a pharmaceutical product or a spring or a well or a reservoir or a public water supply), to wit: (IDENTIFY SUBSTANCE AND LOCATION), and the placement of such (poison or substance) would be a violation of Revised Code 2927.24(B)(1) if true, and knowing the information was false and likely to be disseminated to the public, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2927.24(C)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2927.24.heading: SPREADING FALSE REPORT OF CONTAMINATION 2927.24(C)(2) ORC
ORC:2927.24.variant: FALSE REPORT OF VIOLATION OF REVISED CODE 2927.24(B)(2) – F4
ORC:2927.24.text: _____________ did inform another person, to wit: (STATE NAME AND POSITION) that (a hazardous chemical, biological, or radioactive substance (has been or will be) released into the air or a hazardous chemical, biological, or radioactive substance (has been or will be) left in a public place or that one or more persons (has been or will be) exposed to a hazardous chemical, biological, or radioactive substance), to wit: (IDENTIFY SUBSTANCE AND LOCATION), and the (release or leaving or exposure) of the hazardous chemical, biological, or radioactive substance would be a violation of Revised Code 2927.24(B)(2), and knowing the information was false and likely to be disseminated to the general public, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION) in violation of Section 2927.24(C)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2927.27.heading: ILLEGAL BAIL BOND AGENT PRACTICES 2927.27(A) ORC
ORC:2927.27.text: _____________ did, not being a law enforcement officer, (apprehend, detain or arrest) a principal on bond, where ever issued, to wit: (STATE ILLEGAL BOND PRACTICE), by failing to meet the standard criteria:
ORC:2927.27.notes: – Qualified, licensed, and appointed as a surety bail bond agent under Sections 3905.83 – 3905.95 of the Ohio Revised Code, or – Licensed as a surety bail bond agent by the state where the bond was written, or – Licensed as a private investigator under Section 4749 of the Ohio Revised Code, or – An off-duty peace officer as defined in Section 2921.51 of the Ohio Revised Code, or – The person, prior to apprehending, detaining, or arresting the principal, entered into a written contract with the surety or with a licensed surety bail bond agreement appointed by the surety and the contract sets forth the name of the principal who is to be apprehended, detained or arrested, or – The person, prior to apprehending, detaining, or arresting the principal, has notified the local law enforcement agency having jurisdiction over the area in which such activities will be performed and has provided any form of identification or other information requested by the law enforcement agency, or – Licensed as a private investigator by the state where the bond was written, in violation of Section 2927.27(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2927.27.heading: ILLEGAL BAIL BOND AGENT PRACTICES 2927.27(A) ORC
ORC:2927.27.text: _____________ did, not being a law enforcement officer, (apprehend, detain or arrest) a principal on bond, where ever issued, to wit: (STATE ILLEGAL BOND PRACTICE), and the offender previously has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to two or more violations of this section by failing to meet the standard criteria:
ORC:2927.27.notes: – Qualified, licensed, and appointed as a surety bail bond agent under Sections 3905.83 – 3905.95 of the Ohio Revised Code, or – Licensed as a surety bail bond agent by the state where the bond was written, or – Licensed as a private investigator under Section 4749 of the Ohio Revised Code, or – An off-duty peace officer as defined in Section 2921.51 of the Ohio Revised Code, or – The person, prior to apprehending, detaining, or arresting the principal, entered into a written contract with the surety or with a licensed surety bail bond agreement appointed by the surety and the contract sets forth the name of the principal who is to be apprehended, detained or arrested, or – The person, prior to apprehending, detaining, or arresting the principal, has notified the local law enforcement agency having jurisdiction over the area in which such activities will be performed and has provided any form of identification or other information requested by the law enforcement agency or – Licensed as a private investigator by the state where the bond was written, in violation of Section 2927.27(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2927.27.heading: ILLEGAL BAIL BOND AGENT PRACTICES 2927.27(B) ORC
ORC:2927.27.text: _____________ did represent the person’s self to be a bail enforcement agent or bounty hunter, or claim any similar title, in this state, to wit: (STATE REPRESENTATION), in violation of Section 2927.27(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2927.27.heading: ILLEGAL BAIL BOND AGENT PRACTICES 2927.27(B) ORC
ORC:2927.27.text: _____________ did represent the person’s self to be a bail enforcement agent or bounty hunter, or claim any similar title, in this state, to wit: (STATE REPRESENTATION), and the offender previously has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to two or more violations of this section In violation of Section 2927.27(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2933.52.heading: INTERCEPTION OF WIRE, ORAL, OR ELECTRONIC COMMUNICATION 2933.52(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2933.52.text: _____________ did purposely (intercept or attempt to intercept or procure any other person to intercept or attempt to intercept) any (wire communication or oral communication or electronic communication), to wit: (DESCRIBE COMMUNICATION THAT WAS INTERCEPTED), in violation of Section 2933.52(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2933.52.heading: INTERCEPTION OF WIRE, ORAL, OR ELECTRONIC COMMUNICATION 2933.52(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2933.52.text: _____________ did purposely (use, attempt to use, or procure another person to use or attempt to use) an interception device to intercept any (wire communication or oral communication electronic communication), to wit: (DESCRIBE COMMUNICATION THAT WAS INTERCEPTED), when the interception device (is affixed to, or otherwise transmits a signal through a wire, cable, satellite, microwave, or other similar method of connection used in wire communications or transmits communications by radio, or interferes with the transmission of communications by radio), to wit: (DESCRIBE COMMUNICATION THAT WAS INTERCEPTED), in violation of Section 2933.52(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2933.52.heading: INTERCEPTION OF WIRE, ORAL, OR ELECTRONIC COMMUNICATION 2933.52(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2933.52.text: _____________ did purposely (use or attempt to use) the contents of a (wire communication or oral communication or electronic communication), to wit: (DESCRIBE COMMUNICATION THAT WAS USED), knowing or having reason to know that the contents were obtained through the interception of a wire communication or oral communication or electronic communication, to wit: (DESCRIBE), in violation of Section 2933.52(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the fourth degree.

ORC:2933.59.heading: PRESENTING ALTERED RECORD OF INTERCEPTED COMMUNICATION 2933.59 ORC
ORC:2933.59.text: _____________ did, with intent to present the altered recording or resume (in any judicial proceeding or in any proceeding under oath or affirmation), to wit: (DESCRIBE PROCEEDING), purposefully (edit or alter or tamper with or attempt to alter, edit or tamper with) (any recording or resume of any intercepted wire or oral communication or present or permit presentation of any altered recording or resume) in any judicial proceeding or in any proceeding under oath or affirmation without fully indicating the nature of the changes made, to wit: (DESCRIBE ALTERED OATH OR AFFIRMATION), in violation of Section 2933.59 of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2933.59.notes: DEFINITIONS 2950.035 ORC CAPACITY AFFORDING EXTENSIVE CONTACT WITH MINOR CHILDREN – any capacity in which a person would be working directly and in an unaccompanied setting with minor children on more than an incidental and occasional basis or would have supervision or disciplinary power over minor children. PROSECUTING AUTHORITY – the prosecuting attorney, village solicitor, city or township director of law, similar chief legal officer of a municipal corporation or township, or official designated as a prosecutor in a municipal corporation that has jurisdiction over the place at which a person serves in a position in violation of division (A)(1) or (2) of this section. WORKING DIRECTLY AND IN AN UNACCOMPANIED SETTING – includes, but is not limited to, providing goods or services to minors. NOTE: A violation of 2950.035(A)(1) ORC without injunctive relief is not a criminal offense. NOTE: A violation of 2950.035(A)(2) ORC is a criminal offense and is subject to the penalties specified in 2950.99 ORC

ORC:2950.035.heading: UNLAWFUL WORK WITH OR SUPERVISION OF MINORS 2950.035(A) (2) ORC
ORC:2950.035.text: _____________, who is in a restricted offender category, did violate division (A)(1) of this section at any time after an injunction was obtained against the person under division (B)(2) of this section with respect to a violation of division (A)(1) of this section, to wit: (STATE ISSUING COURT AND DATE OF INJUNCTION), and commenced service in a position as a volunteer with any person, group, or organization, in a capacity affording extensive contact with minor children on or after April 3, 2023 (or at any time after July 3, 2023, if the offender was in the position prior to April 3, 2023), to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT), in violation of Section 2950.035(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:2950.035.notes: NOTE: A violation of division (A)(1) of this section that is not also a violation of division (A) (2) of this section is subject to injunctive relief as described in division (B)(2) of this section. If a law enforcement agency, based on a report made to the agency by any person or based on its own investigation, finds that a person to whom division (A) of this section applies is violating that division, the agency shall report that finding to the prosecuting authority. Under (B)(2), a prosecuting authority, upon receipt of a report under division (B)(1) of this section, has a cause of action for injunctive relief against the person for the violation if the violation is of division (A)(1) of this section and may bring an action to obtain the injunctive relief. The plaintiff shall not be required to prove irreparable harm in order to obtain the relief. A prosecuting authority, upon receipt of a report under division (B)(1) of this section, may proceed with a criminal prosecution for the violation if the violation is of division (A) (2) of this section. NOTE: See additional information at the beginning of Section 2950.035 of this manual.

ORC:2950.035.heading: UNLAWFUL WORK WITH OR SUPERVISION OF MINORS 2950.035(A) (2) ORC
ORC:2950.035.text: _____________, who is in a restricted offender category, did violate division (A)(1) of this section at any time after an injunction was obtained against the person under division (B)(2) of this section with respect to a violation of division (A)(1) of this section, to wit: (STATE ISSUING COURT AND DATE OF INJUNCTION), and commenced service in a position as a volunteer with any person, group, or organization, in a capacity affording extensive contact with minor children on or after April 3, 2023 (or at any time after July 3, 2023, if the offender was in the position prior to April 3, 2023), to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT), and having been previously convicted of violating Section 2950.035(A)(2), to wit: (STATE ISSUING COURT, DATE OF CONVICTION, AND CASE NUMBER), in violation of Section 2950.035(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the third degree.
ORC:2950.035.notes: NOTE: See additional information at the beginning of Section 2950.035 of this manual.

ORC:2950.035.heading: UNLAWFUL WORK WITH OR SUPERVISION OF MINORS 2950.035(A) (2) ORC
ORC:2950.035.variant: EXTENSIVE CONTACT – TWO OR MORE PREVIOUS CONVICTION – F1
ORC:2950.035.text: _____________, who is in a restricted offender category, did violate division (A)(1) of this section at any time after an injunction was obtained against the person under division (B)(2) of this section with respect to a violation of division (A)(1) of this section, to wit: (STATE ISSUING COURT AND DATE OF INJUNCTION), and commenced service in a position as a volunteer with any person, group, or organization, in a capacity affording extensive contact with minor children on or after April 3, 2023 (or at any time after July 3, 2023, if the offender was in the position prior to April 3, 2023), to wit: (DESCRIBE CONDUCT), and having been previously convicted of violating Section 2950.035(A)(2) two or more times, to wit: (STATE ISSUING COURTS, DATES OF CONVICTION, AND CASE NUMBERS), in violation of Section 2950.035(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a felony of the first degree.
ORC:2950.035.notes: NOTE: See additional information at the beginning of Section 2950.035 of this manual.

ORC:2950.17.heading: POSSESSION OF PHOTOGRAPH OF VICTIM OF SEXUALLY ORIENTED OFFENSE OR CHILD-VICTIM ORIENTED OFFENSE PROHIBITED WHILE PERSON SERVING TERM OF CONFINEMENT IMPOSED FOR OFFENSE 2950.17(A) ORC
ORC:2950.17.text: _____________, a person who (was convicted of, or plead guilty to, OR is or has been adjudicated a delinquent child for committing) a sexually oriented offense or a child-victim oriented offense, to wit: (STATE DATE, CHARGE, COURT, AND CASE NUMBER OF CONVICTION) did possess a photograph of the victim of the sexually oriented offense or child-victim oriented offense while the person is serving any (prison term, jail term, community residential sanction, or other term of confinement) imposed on the offender for the offense, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 2950.17(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2950.17.heading: POSSESSION OF PHOTOGRAPH OF ANY MINOR CHILD PROHIBITED 2950.17(B) ORC
ORC:2950.17.text: _____________, a person who (was convicted of, or plead guilty to, OR is or has been adjudicated a delinquent child for committing) a sexually oriented offense or a child-victim oriented offense, to wit: (STATE DATE, CHARGE, COURT, AND CASE NUMBER OF CONVICTION) did possess a photograph of any minor child while the person is serving any prison term, jail term, community residential sanction, or other term of confinement imposed on the offender for the offense, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2950.17(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:2981.07.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH OR DIMINISHING FORFEITABLE PROPERTY 2981.07(A)(1) ORC
ORC:2981.07.variant: PURPOSE TO PREVENT OR IMPAIR STATE’S OR POLITICAL SUBDIVISION’S LAWFUL AUTHORITY TO TAKE THE PROPERTY INTO ITS CUSTODY
ORC:2981.07.text: _____________, did destroy, damage, remove, or transfer property that is subject to forfeiture or otherwise take any action in regard to property that is subject to forfeiture with purpose to prevent or impair the state’s or political subdivision’s lawful authority to take the property into its custody or control under ORC Chapter 2981 or to continue holding the property under its lawful custody or control, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2981.07(A)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2981.07.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE MORE THAN $150,000.00, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2981.07.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH OR DIMINISHING FORFEITABLE PROPERTY 2981.07(A)(2) ORC
ORC:2981.07.variant: PURPOSE TO IMPAIR OR DEFEAT THE COURT’S CONTINUING JURISDICTION OF THE PERSON AND PROPERTY
ORC:2981.07.text: _____________, did destroy, damage, remove, or transfer property that is subject to forfeiture or otherwise take any action in regard to property that is subject to forfeiture with purpose to impair or defeat the court’s continuing jurisdiction over the person and property, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2981.07(A)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2981.07.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE MORE THAN $150,000.00, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:2981.07.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH OR DIMINISHING FORFEITABLE PROPERTY 2981.07(A)(3) ORC
ORC:2981.07.text: _____________, did destroy, damage, remove, or transfer property that is subject to forfeiture or otherwise take any action in regard to property that is subject to forfeiture with purpose to devalue property that the person knows, or has reasonable cause to believe, is subject to forfeiture proceedings under ORC Chapter 2981, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 2981.07(A)(3) of the Ohio Revised Code:
ORC:2981.07.notes: – VALUE LESS THAN $1,000.00, a misdemeanor of the first degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $1,000.00 AND $7,500.00, a felony of the fifth degree. – VALUE BETWEEN $7,500.00 AND $150,000.00, a felony of the fourth degree. – VALUE MORE THAN $150,000.00, a felony of the third degree.

ORC:3716.11.heading: ADULTERATED FOOD 3716.11(A) ORC
ORC:3716.11.variant: PLACE HAZARDOUS OBJECT IN FOOD – M1
ORC:3716.11.text: _____________ did, (knowing or having reasonable cause to believe) that a person would (suffer physical harm or be seriously inconvenienced or annoyed) place a (pin or needle or razor blade or glass or laxative or drug of abuse or a harmful/hazardous object or a harmful/hazardous substance) to wit: (DESCRIBE OBJECT), in a (food or confection), to wit: (DESCRIBE FOOD), in violation of Section 3716.11(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:3716.11.heading: ADULTERATED FOOD 3716.11(B) ORC
ORC:3716.11.variant: FURNISH FOOD HAVING HAZARDOUS OBJECT IN IT – M1
ORC:3716.11.text: _____________ did, (knowing or having reasonable cause to believe) that a person would (suffer physical harm or be seriously inconvenienced or be annoyed) furnish a person, to wit: (STATE NAME), a (food or confection), to wit: (DESCRIBE FOOD), which had been adulterated with a hazardous (object or substance), to wit: (DESCRIBE OBJECT OR SUBSTANCE), in violation of Section 3716.11(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:3719.32.heading: REGULATING THE SALE OF POISONS 3719.32 ORC
ORC:3719.32.text: _____________ did knowingly, sell or deliver (to any person other than in the manner prescribed by law or to a minor under 16 in the manner prescribed by law but without written order of an adult or any of the substances listed in this section or any poisonous compounds, combinations, or preparations thereof), to wit: (DESCRIBE POISON/SUBSTANCE AND PERSON TO WHOM IT WAS DELIVERED), in violation of Section 3719.32 of the Ohio Revised Code, a minor misdemeanor.

CCC:2329.01.heading: LITTERING 2329.01(A) CCC
CCC:2329.01.text: _____________ did (deposit litter or cause litter to be deposited), to wit: (DESCRIBE LITTER), upon any (public property or private property not owned by the offender or in waters owned by the city or on waters owned by the city), to wit: (DESCRIBE LOCATION) in violation of Section 2329.01(A) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor to the third degree.
CCC:2329.01.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply if any of the following apply: 1. The person is directed to deposit litter by a public official as part of a litter collection drive; 2. Except as provided in 2329.01(B), the person deposits the litter in a litter receptacle in a manner that prevents its being carried away by the elements; 3. The person is issued a permit or license covering the litter pursuant Chapter 3734 or 6111 of the Revised Code.

CCC:2329.01.heading: LITTERING 2329.01(B) CCC
CCC:2329.01.text: _____________ did, without privilege to do so, knowingly (deposit litter or cause litter to be deposited), to wit: (DESCRIBE), in a litter receptacle located on any (public property, or any private property not owned by) (him or her), to wit: (DESCRIBE LOCATION) and does not fall under any of the exceptions listed in 2329.01(B)(1)(4) in violation of Section 2329.01(B) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor to the third degree.
CCC:2329.01.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply if any of the following apply: 1. The litter was generated or located on the property on which the litter receptacle is located. 2. The person is directed to deposit litter by a public official as part of a litter collection drive. 3. The person is directed to deposit litter by a person whom he reasonably believes to have the privilege to use the litter receptacle. 4. The litter consists of any of the following: a. The contents of a litter bag or container of a type and size customarily carried and used in a motor vehicle; b. The contents of an ash tray of a type customarily installed or carried and used in a motor vehicle; c. Beverage containers and food sacks, wrappings, and containers of a type and in an amount that reasonably may be expected to be generated during routine commuting or business or recreational travel by a motor vehicle; d. Beverage containers, food sakes, wrappings, containers, and other materials of a type and in an amount that reasonably may be expected to be generated during a routine day by a person and deposited in a litter receptacle by a casual passerby. DEFINITIONS 2333.01 CCC DISTRIBUTION – An exchange or an attempt to exchange a physical item between two or more individuals. NOTE: This section shall not apply to persons possessing a permit issued pursuant to CCC 525.24. NOTE: Violations (A)-(D) are strict liability offenses. NOTE: If a person has been previously convicted of a violation of 2333.01 or any other substantially similar statute or municipal ordinance, Distribution in a Right-of-Way is a misdemeanor of the third degree. Prior convictions must be alleged on the complaint with the following information: case number of prior conviction, court in which conviction occurred, date of conviction, and offense code section of conviction.

CCC:2333.01.heading: DISTRIBUTION IN A RIGHT-OF-WAY 2333.01(A) CCC
CCC:2333.01.variant: PEDESTRIAN INTERFERENCE: VEHICLE NOT LAWFULLY STOPPED/ STANDING/PARKED – M4
CCC:2333.01.text: _____________ did engage in distribution with the (driver/occupant) of a vehicle in a right-of-way, to wit: (DESCRIBE VEHICLE AND LOCATION) when the vehicle was not lawfully (stopped/standing/parked) in compliance with ORC 4511, by means of: (DESCRIBE BEHAVIOR), in violation of 2333.01(A) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
CCC:2333.01.notes: NOTE: See definitions listed at beginning of Section 2333.01. NOTE: A person may engage in distribution with the occupant of a vehicle in a right-of-way so long as the person remains on the surrounding sidewalks and not in or on the right-of-way itself, including medians or traffic islands within the right-of-way.

CCC:2333.01.heading: DISTRIBUTION IN A RIGHT-OF-WAY 2333.01(B) CCC
CCC:2333.01.variant: PEDESTRIAN INTERFERENCE: VEHICLE OBEYING TRAFFIC SIGNAL – M4
CCC:2333.01.text: _____________ did, while being within the right-of-way, to wit: (DESCRIBE LOCATION) engage in distribution with the (driver/occupant) of a vehicle stopped in a right-of-way in obedience to a traffic control signal, by means of: (DESCRIBE VEHICLE AND BEHAVIOR), in violation of 2333.01(B) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
CCC:2333.01.notes: NOTE: See definitions listed at beginning of Section 2333.01. NOTE: A person may engage in distribution with the occupant of a vehicle in a right-of-way so long as the person remains on the surrounding sidewalks and not in or on the right-of-way itself, including medians or traffic islands within the right-of-way.

CCC:2333.01.heading: DISTRIBUTION IN A RIGHT-OF-WAY 2333.01(C) CCC
CCC:2333.01.variant: DRIVER/OCCUPANT INTERFERENCE: VEHICLE NOT LAWFULLY STOPPED/STANDING/PARKED – M4
CCC:2333.01.text: _____________ did, while being the (driver/occupant) of a vehicle in the right-of-way, to wit: (DESCRIBE VEHICLE AND LOCATION) engage in distribution with another who is not an occupant of the vehicle, to wit: (DESCRIBE OTHER PERSON) when the vehicle was not lawfully (stopped/standing/parked) in compliance with ORC 4511, by means of: (DESCRIBE BEHAVIOR), in violation of 2333.01(C) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
CCC:2333.01.notes: NOTE: See definitions listed at beginning of Section 2333.01. NOTE: A driver or occupant of a vehicle stopped in a right-of-way may engage in distribution with another who is not an occupant of the vehicle so long as the person remains on the surrounding sidewalks and not in the right-of-way itself, including any medians or traffic islands within the right-of-way.

CCC:2333.01.heading: DISTRIBUTION IN A RIGHT-OF-WAY 2333.01(D) CCC
CCC:2333.01.variant: DRIVER/OCCUPANT INTERFERENCE: VEHICLE OBEYING TRAFFIC SIGNAL – M4
CCC:2333.01.text: _____________ did, while being the (driver/occupant) of a vehicle stopped in a right-of-way in obedience to a traffic control signal, to wit: (DESCRIBE VEHICLE AND LOCATION) engage in distribution with another who is not an occupant of the vehicle, to wit: (DESCRIBE OTHER PERSON AND BEHAVIOR), in violation of 2333.01(D) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
CCC:2333.01.notes: NOTE: See definitions listed at beginning of Section 2333.01. NOTE: A driver or occupant of a vehicle stopped in a right-of-way may engage in distribution with another who is not an occupant of the vehicle so long as the person remains on the surrounding sidewalks and not in the right-of-way itself, including any medians or traffic islands within the right-of-way.

CCC:2333.02.heading: AGGRESSIVE DISTRIBUTION 2333.02(A)(1) CCC
CCC:2333.02.text: _____________ did engage or attempt to engage in distribution by knowingly (touching/grabbing) another person or that person’s property, to wit: (DESCRIBE OTHER PERSON OR PROPERTY) without that person’s consent, by means of: (DESCRIBE BEHAVIOR AND CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of 2333.02(A) (1) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.
CCC:2333.02.notes: NOTE: “Distribution” means an exchange or an attempt to exchange a physical item between two or more individuals. NOTE: If a person has been previously convicted of a violation of 2333.02 or any other substantially similar statute or municipal ordinance, Aggressive Distribution is a misdemeanor of the first degree. Prior convictions must be alleged on the complaint with the following information: case number of prior conviction, court in which conviction occurred, date of conviction, and offense code section of conviction.

CCC:2333.02.heading: AGGRESSIVE DISTRIBUTION 2333.02(A)(2) CCC
CCC:2333.02.variant: FOLLOWING PERSON UNWILLING/UNABLE TO ENGAGE IN DISTRIBUTION – M2
CCC:2333.02.text: _____________ did knowingly follow another person, to wit: (DESCRIBE OTHER PERSON) and continue to (engage or attempt to engage) in distribution with that person, by means of (DESCRIBE BEHAVIOR) after that person has made an affirmative communication, to wit: (DESCRIBE COMMUNICATION) that the person is (unwilling or unable) to engage in distribution, in violation of 2333.02(A)(2) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the second degree.
CCC:2333.02.notes: NOTE: “Distribution” means an exchange or an attempt to exchange a physical item between two or more individuals. NOTE: If a person has been previously convicted of a violation of 2333.02 or any other substantially similar statute or municipal ordinance, Aggressive Distribution is a misdemeanor of the first degree. Prior convictions must be alleged on the complaint with the following information: case number of prior conviction, court in which conviction occurred, date of conviction, and offense code section of conviction.

CCC:2333.03.heading: ATM PRIVACY 2333.03 CCC
CCC:2333.03.text: _____________ did knowingly approach within three (3) feet of any person, to wit: (DESCRIBE PERSON) who is actively using an automated teller machine without that person’s consent, to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES AND BEHAVIOR), in violation of 2333.03 of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
CCC:2333.03.notes: NOTE: “Automated teller machine” means a fixed device linked to a financial institution’s account records which is able to carry out transactions, including by not limited to, account transfers, deposits, withdrawals, balance inquiries, and mortgage and loan payments. NOTE: If a person has been previously convicted of a violation of 2333.03 or any other substantially similar statute or municipal ordinance, Violating ATM privacy is a misdemeanor of the third degree. Prior convictions must be alleged on the complaint with the following information: case number of prior conviction, court in which conviction occurred, date of conviction and offense code section of conviction.

CCC:2333.04.heading: OBSTRUCTING CITY RIGHT-OF-WAY 2333.04(A)(1) CCC
CCC:2333.04.text: _____________ did, without legal privilege or authority to do so, recklessly obstruct a (highway, street, sidewalk, railway, waterway, elevator, aisle, hallway, entrance, or exit) to which the public or a substantial group of the public has access to wit: (DESCRIBE LOCATION AND PUBLIC ACCESS) or any other place used for the passage of (persons, vehicles, or conveyances), regardless of the means of creating the obstruction and whether the obstruction arose from the person’s acts alone or from the person’s acts and the acts of others, by means of: (DESCRIBE OBSTRUCTION AND OTHER PLACE IF APPLICABLE), in violation of 2333.04(A)(1) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
CCC:2333.04.notes: NOTE: “Obstruct” means to render impassable or to render passage unreasonably inconvenient or hazardous. NOTE: If a person has been previously convicted of a violation of 2333.04 or any other substantially similar statute or municipal ordinance, Obstructing the Right-of-Way is a misdemeanor of the third degree. Prior convictions must be alleged on the complaint with the following information: case number of prior conviction, court in which conviction occurred, date of conviction and offense code section of conviction.

CCC:2333.04.heading: OBSTRUCTING CITY RIGHT-OF-WAY 2333.04(A)(2) CCC
CCC:2333.04.variant: RECKLESSLY DISOBEY REASONABLE REQUEST/ORDER TO MOVE – M4
CCC:2333.04.text: _____________ did, without legal privilege or authority to do so, recklessly disobey a reasonable (request or order to move), to wit: (DESCRIBE REQUEST), issued by a person the actor knows to be or is informed is, a (peace officer or a person with the authority to control the use of the premises), to wit: (DESCRIBE PEACE OFFICER OR PERSON WITH AUTHORITY AND WHAT AUTHORITY S/HE HAS) when the request/order is made in order to prevent the obstruction of a (highway or any of the areas mentioned in subsection (1)), to wit: (DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES AND LOCATION), in violation of 2333.04(A)(2) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
CCC:2333.04.notes: NOTE: “Obstruct” means to render impassable or to render passage unreasonably inconvenient or hazardous. NOTE: If a person has been previously convicted of a violation of 2333.04 or any other substantially similar statute or municipal ordinance, Obstructing the Right-of-Way is a misdemeanor of the third degree. Prior convictions must be alleged on the complaint with the following information: case number of prior conviction, court in which conviction occurred, date of conviction and offense code section of conviction. DEFINITIONS 525.23 CCC CHARITABLE – Any benevolent, philanthropic, patriotic, or educational purpose. CONTRIBUTION – The promise or grant of any money or property of any kind or value. SOLICIT/SOLICITATIONS – The request, either directly or indirectly, for money or financial assistance on the plea or representation that such money or financial assistance will be used for a charitable purpose. A “solicitation” as defined herein, shall be deemed completed when made, whether or not the person making the same receives any contribution or makes any sale. NOTE: The requirements of this section and Section 525.24 shall not apply to any employee of the division of fire, provided the chief of the division of police has received prior written notice of the date, time, and locations or intersections for charitable contributions solicitation, and provided the employee is in uniform while on the street, highway, or roadway, and provided the employee has received permission from the chief of the division of fire.

CCC:525.23.heading: SOLICITING CHARITABLE CONTRIBUTIONS IN ROADWAY WITHOUT PERMIT 525.23(A) CCC
CCC:525.23.text: _____________ did knowingly solicit charitable contributions on a (street or highway or roadway) from the driver or occupants of a vehicle without first having obtained a permit pursuant to Section 525.24 of this code, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION), in violation of Section 525.23(A) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the third degree.

CCC:2501.985.heading: OPEN BURNING 2501.985 CCC
CCC:2501.985.text: _____________ did knowingly violate a provision of Ohio Fire Code, to wit: (Section F-403.1 – cause or allow opening burning, as incorporated into the Columbus Fire Prevention Code by Columbus City Code 2594.01) by means of: (DESCRIBE DEFENDANT’S CONDUCT) at (STATE LOCATION), in violation of Section 2501.985 of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:4301.69.heading: OFFENSES INVOLVING UNDERAGE PERSONS 4301.69(A) ORC
ORC:4301.69.text: _____________ did sell (beer or intoxicating liquor), to wit: (DESCRIBE), to an underage person, to wit (NAME, DOB, AND DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 4301.69(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor.
ORC:4301.69.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply if given by a physician in the regular line of the physician’s practice, given for established religious purposes, or the underage person is supervised by a parent, spouse who is not an underage person, or legal guardian.

ORC:4301.69.heading: OFFENSES INVOLVING UNDERAGE PERSONS 4301.69(A) ORC
ORC:4301.69.text: _____________ did furnish (beer or intoxicating liquor), to wit: (DESCRIBE), to an underage person, to wit (NAME, DOB, AND DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 4301.69(A) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor,.
ORC:4301.69.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply if the given by a physician in the regular line of the physician’s practice, given for established religious purposes, or the underage person is supervised by a parent, spouse who is not an underage person, or legal guardian.

ORC:4301.69.heading: OFFENSES INVOLVING UNDERAGE PERSONS 4301.69(B) ORC
ORC:4301.69.variant: ALLOW UNDERAGE PERSON TO REMAIN IN OR ON PROPERTY WHILE POSSESSING/CONSUMING ALCOHOL – M1
ORC:4301.69.text: _____________ did, being the owner or occupant of any public or private place, to wit (DESCRIBE), knowingly allow any underage person, to wit (NAME AND DOB), to remain in or on the place while (possessing or consuming) (beer or intoxicating liquor), to wit: (DESCRIBE ALCOHOL AND CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 4301.69(B) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:4301.69.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply if the alcohol is given by a parent, a spouse who is not an underage person, or legal guardian and the other party is present at the time of the underage person’s possession or consumption.

ORC:4301.69.heading: OFFENSES INVOLVING UNDERAGE PERSONS 4301.69(C)(1) ORC
ORC:4301.69.variant: ENGAGE/USE ACCOMMODATIONS KNOWING UNDERAGE DRINKING WOULD OCCUR – M1
ORC:4301.69.text: _____________ did engage or use accommodations at a (hotel, inn, cabin, campground, or restaurant), to wit: (DESCRIBE LOCATION), knowing or having reason to know that (beer or intoxicating liquor) would be consumed by an underage person on the premises, to wit (NAME, DOB, AND DESCRIBE CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 4301.69(C)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:4301.69.notes: NOTE: This section does not apply if the person engaging or using the accommodations is the spouse of an underage person and is not underage, or is the parent or legal guardian of all of the underage persons who consume on the premises. The other party must be present at the time of possession or consumption.

ORC:4301.69.heading: OFFENSES INVOLVING UNDERAGE PERSONS 4301.69(C)(2) ORC
ORC:4301.69.variant: ENGAGE/USE ACCOMMODATIONS KNOWING UNDERAGE DRUG ABUSE WOULD OCCUR – M1
ORC:4301.69.text: _____________ did engage or use accommodations at a (hotel, inn, cabin, campground, or restaurant), to wit: (DESCRIBE LOCATION), knowing or having reason to know that a drug of abuse, to wit: (DESCRIBE DRUG), would be consumed on the premises by any person who did not obtain the drug pursuant to a prescription or does not have the drug in the original container, to wit: (DESCRIBE PERSON AND CIRCUMSTANCES), in violation of Section 4301.69(C)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:4301.69.heading: OFFENSES INVOLVING UNDERAGE PERSONS 4301.69(D)(2) ORC
ORC:4301.69.variant: UNDERAGE PERSON PRESENTING FALSE IDENTIFICATION FOR OVERNIGHT ACCOMMODATIONS – M1
ORC:4301.69.text: _____________ did, being underage, to wit: (DOB), knowingly engage or attempt to engage accommodation at any (hotel, inn, cabin, or campground), to wit: (DESCRIBE), by presenting identification that falsely indicates (he or she) is 21 years of age or older, to wit: (DESCRIBE IDENTIFICATION), in violation of Section 4301.69(D)(2) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.

ORC:4301.69.heading: OFFENSES INVOLVING UNDERAGE PERSONS 4301.69(E)(1) ORC
ORC:4301.69.variant: UNDERAGE PERSON ATTEMPTING TO PURCHASE, POSSESS, OR CONSUME ALCOHOL – M3
ORC:4301.69.text: _____________ did, being underage, to wit: (DOB), knowingly (order, pay for, share the cost of, attempt to purchase, possess, or consume) any (beer or intoxicating liquor) in any public or private place, to wit: (DESCRIBE ALCOHOL AND PLACE), in violation of Section 4301.69(E)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the third degree.

ORC:4301.69.heading: OFFENSES INVOLVING UNDERAGE PERSONS 4301.69(E)(1) ORC
ORC:4301.69.variant: UNDERAGE PERSON UNDER THE INFLUENCE IN PUBLIC – M3
ORC:4301.69.text: _____________ did, being underage, to wit: (DOB), knowingly be under the influence of any (beer or intoxicating liquor) in any public place, to wit: (DESCRIBE ALCOHOL AND PLACE), in violation of Section 4301.69(E)(1) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the third degree.
ORC:4301.69.notes: NOTE: Section (E)(1) does not apply if the underage person is supervised by a parent, spouse who is not an underage person, or legal guardian, or the alcohol is given by a physician in the regular line of the physician’s practice, or given for established religious purposes.

ORC:4301.69.heading: OFFENSES INVOLVING UNDERAGE PERSONS 4301.69(F) ORC
ORC:4301.69.variant: PARENT/GUARDIAN PERMITTING MINOR TO VIOLATE 4301.69, 63, 633, OR 634 OF THE OHIO REVISED CODE – M1
ORC:4301.69.text: _____________ did, being the (parent, spouse who is not an underage person, or legal guardian), of a minor, to wit: (NAME, DOB), knowingly permit the minor to violate Section (4301.69, 4301.63, 4301.633, or 4301.634) of the Ohio Revised Code, to wit: (DESCRIBE THE VIOLATIONS), in violation of Section 4301.69(F) of the Ohio Revised Code, a misdemeanor of the first degree.
ORC:4301.69.notes: NOTE: All exceptions to Section 4301.69 of the Ohio Revised Code still apply.

CCC:2321.021.heading: SCHOOL ATTENDANCE 2321.021(A) CCC
CCC:2321.021.text: _____________, a person between the ages of six and under the age of eighteen years, to wit: (DOB), did be upon or about the public streets, public places, commercial establishments or places of amusement or entertainment within the city during the hours of 9:00 am and 3:30 pm, to wit: (DESCRIBE VIOLATION, INCLUDING PLACE AND TIME), and the child did not have written proof from school authorities excusing (him or her) from school attendance at that particular time; the child was not accompanied by a parent, guardian or person having legal custody and control of that child; the child was required by law to be in school; the child was not employed pursuant to ages and schooling certificate, during actual working hours or travelling directly to or from the job site; and the child was not on an emergency errand, in violation of Section 2321.021(A) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.

CCC:2329.11.heading: COMMUNITY NOISE 2329.11(C)(1) CCC
CCC:2329.11.variant: UNREASONABLY LOUD AND/OR RAUCOUS NOISE – MM
CCC:2329.11.text: _____________ did make or allow to be made an unreasonably loud and/ or raucous noise, to wit: (DESCRIBE NOISE) in such a manner or at such volume, to wit: (DESCRIBE INTENSITY, CHARACTER AND DURATION OF THE NOISE) as to annoy or disturb the quiet, comfort, or repose of a person of ordinary sensibilities, to wit: (COMPLAINANT’S NAME) in violation of Section 2329.11(C)(1) of the Columbus City Code, a minor misdemeanor.
CCC:2329.11.notes: NOTE: See definitions listed at end of Section 2329.11. NOTE: This section does not apply to the following: 1. The emission of sound for the purpose of alerting persons to the existence of an emergency, or the emission of sound in the performance of emergency work. 2. Warning devices necessary for the protection of public safety. 3. Outdoor gatherings, public dances, shows, sporting events, concerts, entertainment events, and other temporary events that may emanate noise in violation of this chapter, provided these events are conducted pursuant to a permit or license issued by the License Section of the Department of Building and Zoning Services or the Special Events Section of the Department of Recreation and Parks. 4. Public works projects as authorized by the state and/or other political subdivisions. 5. The emission of sound that is periodically generated by activities required to maintain the property in compliance with housing, building, zoning, fire, safety, health or sanitation codes and which occurs between the hours of 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.

CCC:2329.11.variant: UNREASONABLY LOUD AND/OR RAUCOUS NOISE – PRIOR WARNING WITHIN 12 HOURS – M4
CCC:2329.11.text: _____________ did make or allow to be made an unreasonably loud and/ or raucous noise, to wit: (DESCRIBE NOISE) in such a manner or at such volume, to wit: (DESCRIBE INTENSITY, CHARACTER AND DURATION OF THE NOISE) as to annoy or disturb the quiet, comfort, or repose of a person of ordinary sensibilities, to wit: (COMPLAINANT’S NAME), and did persist in making or allowing to be made unreasonably loud and raucous noise after receiving a reasonable warning or request to desist within the prior 12 hours, to wit: (DESCRIBE WHO GAVE THE WARNING/REQUEST TO DESIST, IN WHAT MANNER THE WARNING WAS GIVEN AND AT WHAT TIME IT WAS GIVEN), in violation of Section 2329.11(C)(1) of the Columbus City Code, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
